It's good out of the bag and should be a nice treat on top of yogurt or ice cream.The price per ounce is quite a good value and less than what I pay here at the store.It's not sweet.  I would say the dominant flavor is the oats, and they are listed number one in ingredients, with evaporated cane juice, soy oil, spelt, dark chocolate chunks, flax seeds, dried coconut, cocoa, freeze-dried berries, rice starch, sea salt, natural chocolate flavor, natural vanilla flavor and tocopherols (Natural vitamin E) following.  I'm not a health-food nut, so I cannot comment on any of the ingredients.I could not taste the coconut.  I could taste the cocoa slightly, especially with the first taste.I would have to say, though, that after naming their product flavor as "Dark Chocolate and Red Berries," the manufacturers were too stingy with the berries.  The berry bits are too small, too few and too far between.  Any granola needs something to liven it up.I would recommend this product.  Add more berries and it would even better.

I like the flavor of this granola. It has just enough chocolate to really enhance the flavor but not feel like a dessert. I barely noticed the berry flavor. The granola is very crunchy, but not hard. I put it in small ziplock baggies and carry them around for snacking.I like that it's certified organic. The serving size is listed as ¼ of cup.  It is 140 calories per serving.  It contains 14 grams of whole grains per serving.  I'm trying to incorporate more whole grains into my diet and this is a great way to do this.

Nature's Path Love Crunch Premium Organic Granola, Dark Chocolate and Red Berries 11.5-Ounce (Pack of 6)I haven't had granola in quite a while. The calorie count for the amount, perceived or real, is on the high side. This product is 140 for ¼ cup at just over an ounce. I don't tend to measure my cereal. I use bowls with known capacity. Larger bowls for the puffy type cereal, smaller bowls for the dense cereals. Well even my smallest bowl make ¼ cup look puny. Grape Nuts runs into that same problem. That said, it's a delicious cereal or snack.The clusters have a great taste and nice bite. They hold up to milk well, but will sog out if you're a slow eater. I'm not, and they stay crunchy-bity throughout my meal. I like the bits of chocolate and freeze dried berry in the mix. I do wish there was more berries but other than that this is good stuff. The ingredients list doesn't have any red flags to my knowledge. No weird oils of unnatural stuff. Still it's a high calorie treat if you don't measure carefully. But who's really looking, enjoy!

I've never met a combination of dark chocolate and raspberries that I didn't like, and Love Crunch does not disappoint. This new Nature's Path blend is a really tasty combination of sweetened rolled oats, tart freeze-dried strawberry and raspberry bits, and chunks of high quality dark chocolate. The granola is not too sweet, perfectly crunchy, and ideal for eating straight out of the bag, on top of yogurt, or even ice cream. For whatever reason, it doesn't seem to chew up the roof of my mouth the way other granolas have in the past. I do wish there were more berries -- good thing the granola has plenty of character and flavor on its own. Each 30g serving has 14g of whole grains and a modest 6g of sugars (the 'evaporated cane juice' listed second in the ingredients is basically sugar, by the way).If you're the crunchy type (and I am), you'll be glad to know that Love Crunch is certified organic and has a very clean ingredient list. I'd love it even more if the bag were recyclable / compostable and the chocolate were fair trade, but am happy to find that Nature's Path donates to food banks for every bag purchased, up to $1 million. I'm not usually a big granola eater, but I'd happily buy more Love Crunch.

column9: Very, very good! Organic!  Non-GMO! But not enough berries or chocolate
column10: This granola is great. Very tasty, organic & non-GMO. The bits of dried raspberries & strawberries that are added to this granola have a tangy/tart flavor...but there's not many pieces in the bag. I love the dark chocolate pieces that are added  too.  But, I've had 3  servings that haven't had any fruit or chocolate in them & there's still half a bag left. I could even do without more chocolate added if there were lots more berries in the bag. (And no, none of my family members have been selectively picking out the berries & chocolate)Nutrition Facts:Serving Size 1/4 cup (30 g); Calories 140, Calories from fat: 55Total Fat 6g, Saturated Fat 1g, Trans Fat 0, Polyunsaturated Fat 3g, Monounsaturated Fat 1.5gCholesterol 0Sodium 55mgPotassium 105mgTotal Carbohydrate 20gDietary Fiber 2gSugars 6gProtein 2gVitamin A & Calcium 0%Vitamin C 2%Iron 4%Ingredients:Rolled oats*, evaporated cane juice*, soy oil*, spelt*, dark chocolate chunks*, flax seeds*, dried coconut*, cocoa* freeze-dried berry blend*, rice starch*, sea salt, natural chocolate flavor, natural vanilla flavor, natural vitamin E*OrganicContains Soy. Produced in a facility that uses dairy, peanuts & tree nuts.Very, very, very good!If it had more berries, I'd change the star rating to 5. (It needs a little more chocolate too, but I'd be satisfied with more of those tangy berries)

column9: Very tasty, but not as chocolately as expected
column10: This granola is great -it has a fun theme (raspberries and chocolate), nice packaging, a delicious taste, and an inviting crunch.It didn't have a high chocolate ratio (as I might have expected with the packaging), but when considering that this product really is trying to be granola, and not a candy crunch dessert (like a chocolate covered granola bar), then it is fine.  The chocolate bits were small squares, and they seemed to be of good quality (and not chalky like some cheaper candies).I was impressed with the maker of this product, Nature's Path, and I will definitely be seeking out their other creations.Oh yeah, three more things to like: it contains flax seeds (which are one of the best way to get Omega-3 oils without eating fish), it is completely organic, and the company gives an equivalent amount of food to food banks for every product purchased.  If this is true it gives me one more reason to like them.Highly Recommended.

Who knew that granola could be described as decadent? I sure didn't, until I tried this one. The dark chocolate flavor combined with the berries and the crunchy granola....yummy! My problem is not knowing when to stop eating it, I finished this off (myself) in two days, 98% of the granola I ate straight out of the bag. I tried a handful tossed in low fat vanilla yogurt, not quite as good as eating it plain IMHO.One thing you need to watch - if you order this in hot weather, the chocolate will melt; it was 74 degrees the day this arrived, not really all that hot, and when I opened the bag it was pretty messy from the melted chocolate.

This stuff is really addictive.  I usually don't have time to eat during work.  I like to take granola to pour into a cup and gulp down as I work.  I can't stop eating it.  The granola by itself is great.  Add the dark chocolate (just the right amount of sweetness) and strawberries and it's awesome.

I'll be fully frank: I'm not a health food fan. I tend to avoid things that say "organic" on them like the plague. Not that I eat only junk, but in my experience a lot of things that are labeled as health food simply don't taste edible.I was very skeptical that this granola would be healthy and delicious, but I was wrong! How good is Love Crunch? I had to pry it away from my kids AND my husband just to get a taste!!What sets Love Crunch apart is two things: the fruit bits and the chocolate bits. The chocolate is delicious! Dark chocolate pieces that taste as chocolate should. Very yummy! The fruit pieces shocked me because many of them are tiny, but they pack a huge punch when you put one in your mouth.The only downside to this bag is that both my husband and I wished for more chocolate and more fruit pieces. The granola was delicious, however, and almost tasted like it was a crunchy no-bake chocolate cookie that had been smashed up.We were definitely surprised by this granola and are going to be ordering more!

column9: Delicious Granola From a Good Company
column10: Before opening the bag, I read the back and I like what I read. Organic and non-GMO from a company that gives back.That's a good start, but means nothing if the resulting product is inferior. Nature's Path got this one right. This is one of the best granolas I've tasted! The clusters and loose bits of granola have nice crunchy chocolate flavor without being overpowering. The real chocolate bits are of a good quality, and while small, they compliment the crunchy bits perfectly. The only minus is that the freeze-dried red berries are few and far between, and the bits that are there are small.I snacked on it dry and mixed it with yogurt, so it lasted for almost two days. With my morning yogurt alone I might get four servings from a bag, but as a snack I would say there was one serving per bag. It's that addicting. They don't even need the "Best By" date on the back of the bag...it will never last that long!I feel that, at just under four bucks a bag here on Amazon as of this writing, this is a guilty pleasure I can indulge in now and again.Final Score: 4.75 (Rounded up to 5)

column9: Great taste, low sodium, and organic, could use a little more chocolate and berries
column10: This is good tasting granola. The granola itself is crunchy but not too dry by granola standards, and filling. The dark chocolate is very good quality. The berries are tasty and not sweet at all but add a little acid.If you get a handfull of granola with both together that is a good combo. But the bag is mostly granola and that doesn't happen too often. Nonetheless, the overal product is still very good, healthy, and good value for organic and low sodium. A good snack to try that you can feel good about. Recommended.

It tastes as good as the packaging makes it look! I love that there is a mission behind the brand to provide for food banks. I usually don't like dark chocolate so I was surprised that I like the chocolate squares so much. Maybe I've been eating the wrong dark chocolate. The strawberries didn't do much for me but that's ok. The only thing I didn't like was that more than half of the granola on the bottom of the bag was crushed and no longer in bite size pieces. This may have just been from all of the shipping though. Overall very good, tastes great.

column9: Delicious, wholesome food with a conscience
column10: I love, love, love this granola.  It tastes so sinful, but it's actually good for you.  (But one caution, a serving size of ¼ cup is 140 calories, and it's easy to get carried away eating this!) It's the perfect snack for when your sweet tooth is acting up.  The granola itself has a hint of cocoa and a soft whisper of coconut which is tasty, but not overpowering.  The berries add a tiny bit of tartness that balances well with the sweet richness of the chocolate.  I did wish that there had been more dark chocolate chunks, but this is more reflective of my own chocolate addiction than any deficit in the product.  It's delicious eaten plain, but would also be great over ice cream or yogurt.I also really like to know that I'm eating something from a company that grows organically, and donates to food banks with each purchase.  The ingredients are all natural, I know what everything is in the ingredient list and can pronounce it all.  Good, nutritious food from a socially and environmentally responsible company--I'm sold.

Our office has a rotation schedule of weekly treats.  I used this Love Crunch granola to top some fruit and yogurt parfaits.  I couldn't have been more pleased.  The granola added the perfect crunch and the dark chocolate chunks added a touch of decadence to my healthy snack.  A bonus was that it didn't contain any raisins, so commonly found in granola. Raisins send one of my bosses screaming for the hills due to some deep seated childhood incident.  But I digress....Anyway the parfaits were a total hit, being described as "rockin' good" and "best treat ever".  Thanks, Nature's Path for helping me suck up to my bosses!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

column9: One of the best tasting granolas I have tried (dark chocolate and red berries)
column10: Received the dark chocolate and red berries version. From a nutritional standpoint it was a good choice having very low sugar amounts compared to a lot of granola and cereal products (6 grams). The fat content is up a bit a 6 grams as well but only 1 of those is saturated. Everything is listed as being organic and chemical free.Tastewise this version is outstanding. In milk it reminds me of chocolate oatmeal christmas cookies. The chocolate chunks taste great and the berries are slightly noticeable and add great flavor. This is by far the best bagged granola I have ever tried and I go through a lot (I like to put them in plain greek yogurt as well as in milk).It is priced very competatively as well.Fat: 6g (1g saturated, 3g poly unsaturated, 1.5 grams monunsaturated)Cholesterol: 0mgSodium: 55mgPotassium: 105mgTotal Carbohydrates: 20g (Fiber 2g, Sugars 6g)Protein: 2g

column9: Real berries and real chocolate - delicious!
column10: I fell in love with Love Crunch at the first bite!  I have had many flavored granola products and some even contained bits of berries, but I have never before had one that contained whole dried berries as well as actual chunks of chocolate.  The taste was so great that I was absolutely sure it had to be terrible for me, but that isn't the case at all.  For Dark Chocolate and Red Berries blend, the serving size is 1/4 cup and each serving has 140 calories (55 from fat), 6g fat (1g saturated), 0mg cholesterol, 55mg sodium, 105mg potassium, 20g carbs, and 2g protein.  It felt very decadent on yogurt or even just eaten alone.  Altogether it was an excellent treat!

column9: Yummy snack with everything I want...
column10: Love Crunch is just delicious. Granola bits with dried strawberries and chunks of chocolate -- I don't know really how healthy it is, but it makes an excellent snack. Forgot breakfast? Love Crunch. Have coffee but nothing to eat with it except dried apricots? Love Crunch. Need something to keep in your car so you don't starve during a day at school? Love Crunch.I would caution against using it as a cereal, though. I tried, with Soy Milk, and it tasted pretty good at first, but you've got to be quick because once those strawberries get wet... they just don't taste very good. The texture is a bit slimy. Of course you can pick out the strawberries and throw them in as you go.Trying it with ice cream is certainly going to be my next step, though yoghurt sounds pretty good too. The combination of elements makes the treat interesting, you get soft and chewy, slight bitter slight sweet, fruity and chocolate. It's one of the best dried snacks I've had.

For something 'organic' and 'granola', this seems much too good and tasty to be healthy for you.  The granola has a great, chocolate taste without being too sweet, as well as a satisfactory crunch to it without being too hard on the teeth.  I'd say that Nature's Path did indeed come up with a 'unique marriage of taste and health' with this blend - everyone I had try it loved the flavor!  There are nice sized chunks of yummy dark chocolate in the tasty granola, and the only complaint I have about this blend is the red berries - I don't know if it's the bag I received or not, but they were a bit missing compared to everything else, just a few tiny pieces here and there.  Yet the granola is still delicious and I didn't really feel it lacking for their tiny presence (the chocolate more than made up for them), just be aware if you're hoping for nice big chunks in yours.

I think the makers of this granola intended to have this be cereal, but I ate it as snack. This product is delicious and lower calories than most granola. The dark chocolate gives the crunch just enough sweetness. The berries don't really add a lot of flavor. I also used this with yogurt which was yummy. I think the dark chocolate bites really preclude this from being a breakfast cereal for most adults, but I am sure some will find this much more appetizing than other grains.For the price, this a good value and as I said the 3.5 g of fat per serving is lower than most granola.  The manufacturer is also donating proceeds to food banks. So besides being organic, good to eat, there is also a charitable element to buying this food.I know I will buy more of it.

Unlike other berry-flavored cereals, this organic granola from Nature's Path contains real freeze-dried strawberries and raspberries.  There is no weird artificial aftertaste or sticky sweetness associated with added flavors.  The dark chocolate bits are visible and melt slowly in your mouth and if taken with milk melt easily to make a slightly chocolate-y milk.Pros:+ Organic+ real freeze-dried berries+ real dark chocolate+ No artificial flavoringsCons:- product breaks easily during shipment, leaving lots of tiny bits and small clusters.- Pricey- chocolate could melt easily during shipment during hotter months.Overall, highly recommended for those who like real berries (and hate artificial berry-flavor) and real dark chocolate.

I'm normally not a fan of dark chocolate, but this granola is really understated and not the least bit bitter.  It's also not the type of granola that's so sharp and hard that it could sandpaper a wall!  It's crunchy, yet breaks apart easily while chewing and is really satisfying and delicious.  I'm not sure about buying 6 packs at a time, as packaged here on Amazon.  But I really liked it and would probably pick up a bag here and there at my local grocery store.  Definitely interested in the other flavors too.  Wish Amazon offered a variety pack instead; 2 bags of each of the 3 flavors.  Now that's something I would buy for sure.  We love it in our morning oatmeal -- YUM! :oD

column9: Yummy, though the serving size is rather small
column10: I like to eat granola as a snack and this granola is delicious. At 1/4 cup for a serving size, it's far too easy to eat more than one serving size. A serving has 140 calories (calories from fat is 55); 6 g of fat of which 1 g is saturated fat; dietary fiber is 2 g and sugar is 6 g.The oats are sweet, but not overly sweet. I loved the dark chocolate and the berries were nice and tart and the mix of chocolate, berries, and granola is perfect. I would have liked more berries (strawberries and raspberries) as the pieces are very small (or maybe larger pieces) but overall this is great granola.

This granola is really quite good. In fact, it may be one of my favorite commercial granolas (sometimes I buy, sometimes I make my own) and it may be my new go-to brand when I do buy granola. It's rich and full of flavor and not overly sweet. The sweetness level is perfect (and the sugars weigh in at 6 g per serving, which isn't too shabby for granola - sometimes it can be loaded with sugar). The chocolate is dark and rich (my favorite kind) and the berries are a nice addition. So why not 5 stars? Well, the berries are my only gripe - there aren't enough of them! I snagged some Just Tomatoes Organic Just Strawberries, 1.2 Ounce  Pouch (Pack of 4) to mix in and now it's perfect. I know those berries are pricey, so I get it, but it does feel a little lacking.I would like to try the other varieties of granola in this line. I'm sure they are tasty. Really, I haven't had anything made by Nature's Path that I didn't really like.

column9: Rich Granola would make a better snack
column10: I was so excited to try this granola. Who doesn't like cereal, really?It's definitely chocolatey! I would not imagine I'd like to eat this first thing in the morning, but it would be a good little snack, or lunch even. There aren't many berries, and the pieces are very little, but the flavor is there. There was just the right number/size of chocolate pieces. The bag is also a little small, but then granola bags tend to be as they are very dense. It's very rich, and I was not tempted to go back for a second bowl (in a row).It is all organic and non-GMO, which is really nice. It doesn't have that much fat (for granola-notoriously unhealthy), and has 2g fiber and protein each. Only 6 gm sugar, which seems very low to me (luckily!)It's got a lot of whole grains and omega-3s too, which is supposed to be good for me.Overall this was a fine cereal, I will definitely save it for a snacktime treat again.

column9: Delicious by the handful, or as a cereal.
column10: Dark chocolate and berries is one of my favorite flavor combinations.  I have a weakness for healthy snacks like granola and trail mix.  Except they aren't so healthy when you finish a whole bag in a single day, a handful here, a handful there.  I decided to avoid doing that with the Love Crunch Granola by treating it like cereal.I served myself 1/3 cup of granola (which is more than a serving) and poured a little 1% milk on it.  It's perfect!  There is a good balance of smaller crumbles and larger chunks in the chocolate-flavored granola.  The dark chocolate squares and dried berries are just right ... enough to be savored without overpowering the granola.  The granola stays crunchy in the milk without being difficult to chew. (I have TMJ and sometimes crunchy granolas are hard and bother my jaw.)It was a decadent snack and I will enjoy the bag.  Hopefully I can savor it over the course of several days and don't give into my compulsion to sneak handfuls throughout the day.  Hopefully I can enjoy at least one more bowl before my teenage daughter discovers it's open and finishes it off for me.This granola did not disappoint me in any way.  It was deliciously perfect!

I'm a fan of Nature's Crossing products and when I had the chance to try and review  their new organic granola, I jumped at it. With each bag you're getting 11.5 ounces of high quality goodness.What's in "Love Crunch?" Well it's mostly road oats and chunks of dark chocolate, but you also get dried strawberries, dried raspberries (hence the "red berries"), dried coconut, some flaw seed and a bit of vanilla. It's all very tasty. Although I know granola isn't everyone's go-to snack food (It isn't even mine), thiis is a really tasty mix and I'm even snacking on it while I write this review. If you're looking to get your kids to eat something healthy or trying to ease out of processed sweets, you should definitely consider Love Crunch (although the name is kind of dippy).Each serving is 140 calories and contains 9% of your RDAs of fat. Unfortunately a serving is only 1/4th of a cup. That's a lot of fat and calories for such a small serving - which is why I knocked a star off. There's only 1 gram of saturated fat per serving at least. It's also cholestrol free and very low in sodium. So it might not be the be the best granola for you, but it's still healthier than a candy bar or a piece of cake.I was also happy to see that for every bag of Love Crunch purchases, Nature's Crossing donates a bag to a food shelf/food bank. That means in purchasing this, you're also giving a high quality organic product to those who are in need and/or otherwise couldn't afford the extra cost of going organic. This is a really nice thing to do and it definitely helps encourage me to want to purchase more. Think of it as a "Buy 1, Someone Else Gets 1 Free."All in all Love Crunch is one of the tastier granolas that I've tried. I've had better and I've had worse, but this is still a great little granola I can happily recommend even to people who normally pass up this type of snack.

This granola in one word? AMAZING. This stuff rocks. It's a perfect snack (though a little high in calories at 140 for 1/4 cup) full of cocoa, coconut, berries, oats and chunks of chocolate. I love that it's organic too. The only thing I didn't like is that there are an awful lot of small crumbs at the bottom of the bag from the larger chunks falling apart (due to shipping?). Love it and can't wait to get more.

I really like granola, especially the Nature Valley bars, but this Love Crunch Chocolate Berry mix is beyond delicious!!  It is so good, it can be very, very dangerous for those (like me) trying to watch their weight.  Granola is good for you, but can also be high in calories, which makes moderation key.  This product is kind've high in calories considering the serving.  It's 140 calories a serving, but a serving is only 1/4 cup (30 grams).  Please see my pictures of an actual serving of this granola.  That's not very much when it comes down to it.  Thankfully, it packs a lot of flavor, so a small amount goes a long way in yogurt, cereal, or pudding.  I can't wait to mix some with Chobani.  I think this would also be great in baked goods likes muffins or breads.  It wasn't dry, like many granola mixes I have tried. And I was pleasantly surprised at the amount of chocolate pieces.  There are plenty so that you really do get some in every serving.  I would have liked to have more fruit pieces, but there was enough in the bag to give a noticeable fruity flavor boost and a good contrasting texture.  I truly wish they offered this in a single-serve size bar.The bag is a good sized 11.5 ounces, and the Amazon price for 6 bags is quite reasonable (less than $4 a bag as of this writing).  Having 6 bags in the house would be torture for me, so I'll stick to buying this one bag at a time in a supermarket.  But, I WILL buy it.  For a family, the bulk option is a good deal. The bag is also ziplock, which is great for staying fresh longer.  I keep mine in the freezer to maintain freshness, and because chocolate is just so much better cold :-)  Overall, highly recommended!As reviewer D.A.J. noted:140 calories per serving55 calories from fat6g total fat2 g dietary fiber6g sugars2 gram protein

column9: Great snack, didn't use it as cereal.
column10: This was a great snack food.  Excellent taste and pretty healthy.I woudn't recommend it as a breakfast cereal, we had some very large chunks in our bag, not something you'd grab with a spoon.Love the dark chocolate bits too, wish there was more in there.Overall... Great food!

It's organic. It's not genetically modified. It has 0 transfat. It's not surprisingly cholesterol free. It's only 140 calories per 1/4 cup serving, but try limiting yourself to such a stingy sized serving. I couldn't and didn't.One morning I found myself with no bread for toast and only a box of Raisin Bran in the cupboard. On the counter was my unopened bag of Love  Crunch granola. Not wanting to dilute its taste with milk, I sampled this tasty treat right out of the bag. The resealable bag resisted tearing at 6 in the morning, but I did magage to make a crooked tear across the top and gain access to my treasure. As far as granola goes, this is as good as it gets with the merging of crunch, exquisite flavor, wholesome grains, and a hint of fruit.With six grams of fat per decadent serving, it's probably best not to eat this heavenly food out of the bag as I did and am doing at this very moment. Many large, finger-plucking chunks of granola and chocolate are in the bag, but there are also small, sunflower seed-sized pieces that tend to slip through the fingers and fall on one's lap, desk, or keyboard. Luckily I've got a couple small vacuums within reach.The price here for a six bag order seems reasonable. I just don't know if someone like this Potato Head with so little will power could resist the temptation of all that goodness so near and so accessible.

Tasty, delicious, chocolaty, great oats and not overly sweet. Love the taste!But 140 calories (55 from fat) in a 1/4 of cup? Who eats 1/4 of cup for breakfast? Because I eat cup or more..So this is pure indulgence, treat.Also 1 bag lasted me 4 breakfasts, I guess I will stick to regular oatmeal;)

column9: Tastes great, but serving size is ridiculous
column10: Despite looking good "on paper," this granola isn't very nutritious.  The recommended serving size (there must be some government regulation that pegs cereal servings at around 1 ounce) is only 1/4 cup!  Who is going to sit down and have just 1/4 cup of cereal for breakfast?  I'm thinking more like 3/4 cup.  This will put you at 500 calories if you add a cup of (skim) milk.  And most of the protein will be coming from the milk, since even three "servings" of this granola will only give you 6g.  (See the pictures I uploaded for a closeup of the Nutrition Facts label and what one serving looks like.)But if you do go and have yourself a 500-calorie bowl of cereal (570 if you're using whole milk), it's actually pretty filling.  With 18g of sugar in a 3/4-cup triple serving, you're going to be feeling kind of guilty, but the triple serving would have 6g of fiber, so at least that will help slow down the sugar spike.The taste is pretty good.  It's kind of like you went for a hike with a chocolate bar and some trail mix and they melted together.  Can't go wrong with that!  With the notes of coconut, it kind of reminded me of German chocolate icing.I didn't think I'd like the berries, but I do, and I actually wish the mix had more (and bigger pieces of them; these are minuscule).  Watch out if you order online and the weather is hot.  My bag arrived kind of melty (made me feel like I'd been hiking!), but I take that as a sign of the chocolate's quality.If this weren't so carby (and expensive), I could happily sit down and eat it every morning.  But it is, so I won't.

column9: Is organic the new junk food?
column10: Ah granola, I am slowly beginning to develop a love-hate relationship with it.  Love because it is very versatile and tasty.  Hate because many times granola is promoted as a healthy food and I have discovered (many times) it is not.  Therefore, I find myself on a pilgrimage to find the best tasting and most healthy granola out there.This brings us to Nature's Path Love Crunch Granola.  This product is a certified organic food with no trans fat and whole grains.  Unfortunately the serving size betrays the calorie count.  So while this product is made with healthy ingredients, the serving size betrays the portions.  Which I find odd because this granola has chocolate and freeze dried raspberries in it.  I have to tell you, I had to dig, no exaggeration for chocolate, excuse me Italian chocolate and raspberries.  Again if there aren't chunks of chocolate (or even raspberries) how is this so high in calories?As for the taste, I must confess that it is pleasant.  Nevertheless, it isn't anything to become too excited over.  I have tasted granola that is half the price that has tasted better.  I have only eaten the granola by itself, I am sure in yogurt, over a salad or ice cream and as a cereal it might elevate the taste.  I will eat this granola, but it will not be something I would attain again.  Under the assumption a person is searching for organic and/or vegetarian granola, you might have found your match.  I for one find organic products, in many cases, as a marketing ploy.  As for finding a great tasting and healthy granola, it still hasn't happened.

This granola tastes great, if you like Chocolate. but if you like chocolate covered berries, this really isn't the thing.because there is hardly any berry flavor. The chocolate over powers it.it tastes good but just not Chocolate and red berries. It's more like Chocolate and a hint of red berries.
Chocolate, raspberries, strawberries, and organic to boot. What's not to like?  Okay, the package is too small.  This is awesome stuff.  I love it.

This product is pretty much exactly what it promises.  Granola, dried strawberries, and little bars of dark chocolate.  I definitely agree with the name "Love Crunch" because I loved it and it crunched.  But, wow, 10 servings per bag?  I read this after I had eaten about half the bag in 30 seconds.  So, at 140 calories per serving, this bag is 1400 calories.  Yikes.  I had to immediately introduce my underweight kids to it to get it out of my house because I would have eaten the other 700 calories within the hour if I hadn't.  Lucky for me, they loved it too and polished off the bag.  Whew!  Crisis averted!  But, if you need high calories or have way more self control than me, it is absolutely delicious!

column9: Is there such a thing as too chocolaty? Yes.
column10: I love chocolate. If a manufacturer wants to guarantee that I'll toss a box of their product into the basket at the grocery store, just add some chocolate. Well, unless it's bacon, bacon doesn't need chocolate.When I saw this Nature's Path, I thought it would be a great replacement for my typical evening treat of Cocoa Krispies. And health-wise, it is a step in the right direction. A definite plus, because I can now say "healthy" and "chocolate cereal" in the same sentence.Unfortunately, I have finally found something that I consider too rich and chocolaty. The actual cocoa-saturated oat clusters are very good, not too sweet, just the right amount of crunch (if you eat fast enough). If they'd added more than a thimbleful of the dried strawberries, I think the taste would be darned near irresistible. Unfortunately, there's not enough of the tangy berry to offset the very rich and sweet chocolate. The addition of actual chunks of dark chocolate just really take it over the top.This does make me want to try some of Nature's Path other cereal offerings, the quality of the product is very good, and the ingredients are healthy.

Actually, this granola has freeze-dried strawberries which are quite tasty...but the manufacturer is very stingy with them. I'd guess that an entire bag has the equivalent of one strawberry sliced, diced, and dried. I definitely wanted more! The chocolate chunks are also tasty but sort of few and far between. The granola itself is quite good (albeit a little oatmeal-cookie sweet). But if Love Crunch is going to make chocolate and red berries so prominent on the packaging, they really should make sure that not a mouthful will go by in which you don't get at least a taste of one of those extras. As those components are obviously added after the fact (they're not embedded in the granola itself) they really should be a little more generous.

This granola tastes amazing, especially if you are a chocolate lover and I most definitely am! The red berries give it a light and sweet taste and is the perfect accent to this treat. I was curious about the name and the history behind this granola is that it was created by a couple for their wedding. I thought that was so cute, but even more impressive is that they contribute a portion of their proceeds to charity. So thoughtful! Anyway, it is very tasty and I will be buying this granola because not only do I like it but my kids do, too. And the kids rule this roost! ;)

column9: I usually don't like stuff like this,
column10: but I really enjoyed this. Other granolas have been too sweet, and this one wasn't. The taste of the dark chocolate and the dried cranberries were a good counterpoint to the grain. Why not five stars? Because there wasn't enough of the dark chocolate and dried cranberries! Other than that, this was very enjoyable.

If you can keep it in the house without overeating it, this stuff is great.  However, it's like dessert. It's so good, you just keep going back for more, and it's really high in calories. I love it, but I don't think I'll repurchase it until I get more willpower.

column9: Very good if it's what you're looking for!
column10: I tried the Dark Chocolate and Red Berries flavor, and it tasted good, with just a little chocolate, and some berries (but not as many as I'd expected, compared to other cereals with berries).  From some of the other reviews it seems like the proportions of the different ingredients might vary somewhat from bag to bag for whatever reason.  Hopefully they can get that sorted out, but otherwise I think this is a great product IF you're looking for natural/organic/non-GMO and want to help support a good cause at the same time.I end up rating a lot of products 4 stars because there's no 3 1/2 or 4 1/2 and a product has to be pretty close to what I consider perfect to get 5 stars from me.  The seeming lack of berries (maybe just a result of variation from one bag to another), and the price prevent me from being able to give this 5 stars, but I do certainly like the taste, and I like the idea of supporting companies that are responsible and willing to give back to the community.If I had the time I'd make my own granola more often, as that allows me to choose exactly what goes into it, and save some money too, but since I don't, this will do fine for those "granola mornings" or as a snack.

This granola has a great taste.  It also came to me in bigger chunks, which was good for snacking.  Other granola sometimes is too small to eat like that.  It is good with milk as a cereal or in oatmeal as a topping.  It's a bit pricey, but it is tasty for what it is.
Tastes great, serving size is only 1/4 cup...this is anything but good for a diet!  Also, when delivered, all white chocolate was melted...

There's a difference between all-natural and organic.  Poisonous mushrooms are all-natural, proving that foods that boast about naturalness aren't necessarily all that impressive.  Organic means that the food is made from some of the healthiest ingredients available, and this granola is organic.Now, while we've established that this granola is healthy, there's still the issue of taste.  Too often, organic food is extraordinarily healthy but tastes like cardboard coated with mud.  Thankfully, that is not the case with Love Crunch!  My taste buds tingled with every tantalizing bite of this delectable granola, and I could rest assured that I was getting a good source of fiber and many other nutrients.  There were chunks of dark chocolate and berries mingling with the granola clusters that would excite my tongue even more when I would munch on one of those.Some other reviewers have stated that they found this to be more of a snack food than a breakfast food; honestly, I would use it for both.  I found that I was reaching for this in the morning more often than my Cheerios Honey Nut Cereal, however, there were also times when I would be snacking on it in the afternoon.  It's so good for any time of the day or any type of preparation.  If you like your granola with milk or yogurt, this will work very well for that.  I ate it plain most of the time, but it really can be used any way you would normally use granola, except for maybe baking.Overall, I love this stuff, and I will most likely be buying more soon.  It's probably most comparable to Special K Chocolatey Delight Cereal but with healthier and more delicious ingredients (and granola instead of cereal flakes).  I highly recommend this to granola/chocolate enthusiasts.  It's organic, but it's also good.

Upon opening the bag, the wonderful aroma of chocolate was the first thing I noticed. With chunks of chocolate, dried raspberries and strawberries, it was impossible to not want to sample immediately. The flavor reminded me of those no-bake chocolate oatmeal cookies that everyone's grandma makes, but with added chunks of chocolate, coconut and berries. Delicious!Although too sweet for my taste as a cereal, this makes a delightful, healthy and satisfying snack, making it perfect for those days when you want something sweet or chocolaty. It is fantastic used as a topping for yogurt or added to hot cereal to give it a little sparkle.Perfect for gift-giving, "Love Crunch" will be a welcomed gift for any occasion. Instead of sending a gift basket to the college student, consider sending them this healthy alternative. It's organic and full of heart-healthy ingredients that will give you the satisfaction of sending something good for them. They on the other hand will be thrilled you sent them something chocolate that certainly can't be healthy!

column4: Mark P. Sadler "Reviewed by Mark P Sadler"
column10: This is the best cereal I ever tasted. All that chocolate and good for you too; only 6g of sugar. Since it is not in my local grocer I'm happy there is a QR Code on the pacakge so I can research how to find this product one line... did I mention the way it turns the milk all chocolatly!

column9: Review for Nature's Path Love Crunch Granola (Dark Chocolate and Red Berries flavor)
column10: I thought this granola tasted pretty good. It is crunchy and not overly sweet. I wish there were more dried berries though. Also, for people who hate coconut, there is coconut in this granola and the flavor is subtle but there. I tried this with milk (like cereal) but liked it better without the milk. There were some chunks that were a bit too big to eat with a spoon, but I'm sure it's easy to smash them into smaller chunks in the bag. It's also filling enough that I can eat it for breakfast and not get hungry too soon.

I'm not generally a fan of store-bought granola, and usually make my own instead. But I have to admit that this one is just as good. It has tiny chocolate chunks and freeze-dried strawberries, and just the right quantity of small clumps. The label also has less "bad news" than I'd expect--far less sugar than most breakfast cereals (6 grams per serving), is relatively low in fat unlike other granolas (55 calories out of 140), and no trans fat. The latter being more surprising because of the chocolate chunks. As a bonus, I recognize all of the ingredients too--no chemical cocktail here. It's not often you can find something packaged that isn't also heavily processed, but this seems to fit the bill.Incidentally, in three-plus years of getting free items from teh Amazon Vine program, this is the first item I have subsequently decided to purchase with my own money.
This granola is addictive! It is so refreshing and it is also organic.  I used it for cereal when the granola got to small and it tastes great!

If you want a snack which is both delicious and healthy, this works. As for it stating, "love at first bite," I can't say that. The berries were freeze dried which really didn't add much to the mix, taste-wise. Plus, the cost might be prohibitive for some, though for a special occasion, it probably would be a welcome change-of-pace treat. So, overall, it pleases just fine.

Nature's Path Love Crunch is delicious granola with the addition of chocolate and strawberry flavors.  The granola is quite tasty and is sure to please anyone who prefers a sweeter granola.  There's a bit more fat in this granola than others I've tried, but that's the price you pay for the flavor.The following nutrition facts are from the package: For a 1/4 cup serving -- 140 calories; 6g/9% total fat (1g/5% saturated fat, 0g trans fat); 0mg cholesterol; 55mg/2% sodium;  20g/7% total carbohydrate; 6g sugars; 2g/8% dietary fiber.

This Love Crunch is quite a treat! Plus, I don't have to feel bad about eating it because it is organic and reasonably healthy, too. I can taste the chocolate and the berries in just about every bite.

This Nature's Path Love Crunch organic granola is healthy and tastes great.  You could mix it in with plain Greek yogurt for a protein-filled power snack.  Or you can just enjoy it as we did- plain out of the bag.  Each 1/4th cup is 140 calories and contains 6 grams of sugar, so try not to get too carried away- you could do some serious damage to the bag in one sitting (it's that tasty).The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because the amount of dark chocolate and red berries in the bag is actually very small.  You have to dig around for them.  If you buy this granola, be prepared for the lack of these treats.

I was pleasantly surprised by the bag of granola from Nature's Path.1/4 cup (30 grams) is 140 calories, with 6 grams of sugar (or 1/5, 20% of the serving).20 grams of carbs, and 2 grams of fiber.  A touch of salt, and 6 grams of fat, another 20% of the serving.Everything in the product is Organic, other than the salt (can that even be not organic?).Anyways, this is a nice topper to sugar free cereals or low sugar cereals.  And also it is a nice with sugar free almond milk.I can highly recommend this sweet indulgence, in moderation.  The dark chocolate is a teeny bit bitter, which I like, and the strawberries add even more love.
This snack is a great introduction to the world of organic treats.  The clusters are the perfect size and the flavor is divine.

column9: NO ONE can eat just 1/4 cup of this!!! <;-D
column10: I just consumed, in one sitting, about 1,120 calories of this elixir of the granola gods - and I'm not done yet -- there is a VERY good chance that in the next 30 minutes, I will have consumed another 280 calories and then the bag will be empty.There are ten servings in this bag  -- 1/4 cup each is 140 calories. I doubt that anyone other than perhaps someone with extreme willpower and self-control (but why!!??) would limit themselves to a 1/4 cup of this wonderful (AND it's organic and NON GMO!) granola.I ate a few handfuls (then a few/many more) -- I put it in a WHOLE (9 ounce) cup and added hot coffee (yumyumyum!) then tried it in a cup of hot water. Then I poured this granola into another cup into which I added cold water -- you get the idea-- I have been eating many servings of Nature's Path Love Crunch Premium Organic Granola (Dark Chocolate and Berries) nonstop all day at my desk in my humble cubicle and it has been a INTENSE and wonderful experience. The only thing(s) I did NOT do were to add cream and then at the next sitting, to add soy (only because they were unavailable - my office mates use that powdery fake "stuff") -- but I have NO DOUBT that either addition would have been embraced by the subtle, chocolate-ness and taste-bud-embracing crunchiness of this delightful concoction. Try it atop ice cream with WHIPPED CREAM! Try it in your Yogurt!!!Could I taste the berries? No, not really  -- peering into the bag gave me a good look at them -- they are there -- but I have no doubt that they too contributed to the excellence of this Granola Nirvana.Could I taste the delightful chocolate squares that are interspersed among the chocolate-y graola chunks in this bag? Yes, when eating out of hand they were smooth and melted in my mouth for intense chocolate flavor -- it was almost a sacrilege to pour hot water on them in the cup, but (sigh) for the sake of this review process, I did.I could see the little flax seeds swimming around in there -- and as for the coconut, I could barely taste it, and since I have this small problem with coconut (not really a fan of it), I was very happy to realize that it DID not impact my enjoyment of this granola -- so THAT is GOODAs in any granola, there are alot of calories from fat (55 calories -- about 39% of the total calories are fat). NO Cholesterol, low sodium, some fiber (of course, the coconut and the flax seeds and the oats, maybe even the fruits).Since this Granola was created for a wedding, then the calories should not really be a problem -- for what is a wedding but a joyful occasion where many calories are burned off? So I would suggest that this Granola not only be enjoyed as a breakfast cereal for those who are embarking on the usual stressful commute (think "run for bus" "run for train" etc etc) but also for lunchbox treats, and definitely camping and hiking. It WILL give your day a Lift.So what's NOT to LOVE about this? Those who have allergies should read the label -- "contains soy", and "produced in a facility that uses dairy, peanuts and tree nuts".PS-- So why did I not add milk to this LOVElLY Granola? Because I am lactose Intolerant. "Then why add Cream, Ace?" you might say. Well, because cream has alot of little fat globs in it and that makes it digest slower -- ergo I rarely have trouble digesting cream (or whipped cream either, to my delight).

I usually make my own granola by Alton Brown, too, but this is decent.  My husband hates coconut so this is a good cereal for him.I agree that 1/4 cup sounds like not very much but granola sticks to you better than flakes and is usually the amount I eat with milk, anyway.  It doesn't get soggy but isn't so firm that you need to see the dentist after eating it.It's great as a snack, but you could easily polish it off at one sitting if you eat it while watching a movie or driving so portion it out.  Absolutely yummy!

column4: Wandrwoman "Wise as Aphrodite, Beautiful as A...
column10: This "Love Crunch" is a curious product....organic dark chocolate granola. More of a deconstructed trail bar than a breakfast cereal, it tastes pretty good, as well it should. In addition to tiny dark chocolate chunks, it contains rolled oats, flax seeds, dried coconut, cocoa, tiny bits of freeze dried strawberries and raspberries, rice starch, sea salt, and natural flavors.Tipping the scales at 140 calories for a 1/4 cup, even before you add milk, this is not to be consumed daily by dieters. Those watching their carbohydrate intake should also beware as 1/4 cup contains 20g of carbs and only 2g of protein. On the good side, the granola is low sodium, contains 0g trans fat, and is cholesterol free.This product is Certified Organic; guaranteed to be grown without chemical herbicides or pesticides, or synthetic preservatives and additives. It is also Non-GMO certified, which means that the ingredients are guaranteed not to be genetically modified.For every bag of "Love Crunch" sold, Nature's Path Organic, the manufacturer, "will donate an equal amount in food or cash, up to $1 million".

This Love Crunch taste's so good it's kind of hard to keep in mind its on the better side of snack foods.  This is a very tasty trail mix right out of the pouch.  It's loaded with all the ingredients listed without being bogged down with peanuts or some other cheap filler like other mixes.  And no doubt its made up of quality stuff all the way through.  Even the small morsels of chocolate have a rich creamy taste worthy of being called gourmet.  Add milk or cream and you have a truly delicious concoction one could really get used too in the morning, or as a healthy snack any time.  It may be a little pricey, but the taste and quality well make up for it.  Fresh, delicious, and recommended...: )
i have ordered love crunch - dark chocolate and red berries, yet i received aloha blend. well, my sweetheart likes it but i am not happy because i received the wrong item.

column9: Too Much of a Good Thing
column10: It's a challenge to review food, since so much of it is a matter of taste.  Although I think some people will like this granola a lot, it wasn't for me.This is a high-quality granola, flavored with cocoa and coconut, with chunks of dark chocolate and freeze dried strawberries and berries.  The texture is excellent, and contrasts well with milk or yogurt.Unfortunately, I thought there was way too much chocolate.  The dominant flavor is cocoa, followed by the oats, then the chunks of chocolate.  The berries are pretty sparse, and I couldn't detect the coconut.  As I said, it might be right for some people, but I found the cocoa aftertaste to be offputting and am not a fan.

The package states that there are "chocolate chunks" and "tangy" red berries within this granola.  Well,neither I or any of my friends could taste anything but a dry rolled oats concoction.  The fact that the company states it will donate an equal amount of money to a food bank for every bag purchased is exemplary but will not make any difference to me as the lack of taste will make certain that I do not purchase this product.

I love granola, so I was thrilled to try this product.  I eat as a snack (i.e., right out of the bag) rather than a cereal.  Before I even tasted it, I checked out the nutritional profile, and I was extremely pleased.  Compared to other granolas, "Love Crunch" (love the name!) is relatively love in fat (6 grams overall, 1 gram saturated) and quite low in sugar (6 grams, just slightly over a teaspoon--most granolas are loaded with added sugar!).  The also are 2 grams of protein (a bit on the low side since this granola doesn't contain nuts), 2 grams of fiber, and 14 grams whole grains per serving.Of course, a serving size is only 1/4 cup, which is quite small--and that's where the problem comes in.  When I first tried the granola, I'm sure I ate WAY more than a serving; I could have easily finished off half the bag if I hadn't stopped myself!  (For reference, the bag actually contains about TEN servings.)  This granola has a GREAT taste: it is surprisingly sweet given the lack of added sugar (it's sweetened with evaporated cane juice), but it is also nicely oat-y, with a bit of a chocolate flavor as well (from the added cocoa).  The granola has little bits of dried berries--these kind of get lost in there, but what you DEFINITELY notice is the tiny little chunks of dark chocolate!  Finally, I also loved the texture of the granola, which included plenty of big clumps.Frankly, I can't imagine anyone who likes granola and chocolate NOT liking this product--highly recommended!

All natural ingredients, most of which we'd consider wholesome. Great mouth feel & crunch, fabulous taste. I mean the chocolate pieces were good enough to pick them out an eat them all by themselves. (not that I did that....much).But, to me this is more of a healthy snack than a breakfast food. Look, for a snack, it's amazingly nutritional, and way better than almost any other snack food. It's tasty, easy to eat, has fiber, good nutrients, and not a lot of fat.However, for a breakfast cereal, I'd want something less sweet, with less fat and more fiber.  Of course, personal tastes differ on this.  Some folks still eat Coco-puffs for breakfast.I got the Dark Chocolate and Red Berries version. Score!However, as a snack I give this two thumbs up!Edited to add: I passed around the rest of the package on Game nite. Everyone agreed- super tasty, great as a snack. But several others also had reservations about it for breakfast. On the other hand, one of is a Father of some young boys, and they eat tons of over-sweet cereal.  The Dad thought this might be a good way to wean them away from junk-food cereals, he's going to order some and give it a try.

After learning the joys of homemade granola from Alton Brown, I have avoided most store-bought types.  However, it is convenient sometimes and fun to try new flavors.  The Love Crunch variety is surprising in how much it tastes like homemade, likely due both to the organic ingredients and the way it is made.With dried fruit, there is always the risk of the texture being too chewy or hard.  Thankfully, the berries were of the melt-in-your-mouth texture and good without milk.  The chocolate pieces are small enough to add chocolate flavor, but not weigh things down.Overall, this granola has a carefully thought out ratio of flavors, while avoiding the artificial texture and flavor of some competitors.  I don't know about romantic, but it is yummy.
This is seriously amazing granola. I usually homemake my own, so I am kind of a granola snob. It is seriously so good!

column9: Very goood, much better than expected
column10: I was really pleasantly surprised with how good this granola was. I am not usually a granola eater. Yes, I know it is supposed to be good for you - but whenever I had eaten it in the past granola just tasted dry. Tasting this and wow - this taste really good! The rolled oats have a nutty flavor with just enough spice. Okay - evaporated cane juice is the second ingredient on the label - so I am sure the sweet flavor is what is really doing it for me.The dark chocolate chunks have a really good flavor - not as bitter a taste as I normally find with dark chocolate.The freeze dried fruit has a nice sharp taste, but this is where my only complaint comes into play - there just aren't many of the fruit chunks in the bag. I was surprised that there were more chocolate chunks than fruit chunks - almost at a ratio of 3 to 1. While this doesn't kill the product for me, the nice contrast you get with the fruit chunks is nice so having more would be good. My young kids also like the sour "pop" they get from the fruit chunks so having more for them to munch on would be a bonus.A serving size is 1/4 cup (a little small, this is good and I can eat it by the handful)140 calories per serving55 calories from fat6g total fat2 g dietary fiber6g sugars2 gram proteinNothing in the ingredients worries me - I can pronounce all the words and even the oils and sweetners are okay in my book (evaporated cane juice, soy oil). In addition to the rolled oats there is also spelt, flax seeds, and dried coconuts - things I just wouldn't eat otherwise. Another bonus - Non GMO verified which I am very happy about.The bags are a good size (11.5 oz) with about 10 servings per bag. Since you get 6 packs I would think it would take you a while to get through all of these unless you eat it every single day. I think the price is fair for what you get and I would actually purchase these for the family and feel good eating them. I must admit, I am still shocked about liking granola!

This is the first time I have ever ordered this product and really enjoyed it.It is great on many different types of food, ice cream, oat meal, differet kinds of cold cereal and yougart.  Or it is good eaten by itself.there are a variety of tastes in this granola.  I enjoy eating it very much.  I would recommended it for my friends.  The amount of granola you get is amazing.  It is well worth the price.

Yummy in my tummy! :) Nature's Path Love Crunch Premium Organic Granola, with dark chocolate and red berries is both healthy and nutritious. Check this out:Low sodium0g trans fatCholesterol free14g whole grains per 30g servingExcellent source of omega-3140 calories per serving (serving size is only 1/4 cup- but what a great healthy snack)Filled with healthy organic ingredients such as: chocolate, flax seeds, coconut and red berries.But it is the taste that does it for me! I am not a huge chocolate lover but this super sweet mix is just the right combination of dark chocolate and sweet but tangy berries. After 1 handful I was sold and added it to my daily routine of breakfast of flax seed wheat bread and egg whites. It gives me that kick of snaking but I don't feel the guilt because of all the healthy goodness that I am eating. The only true problem that I have is that I want more then my serving size! Even my picky hubby has fallen in love Nature's Path and he shuns granola likes its the plague. Funny thing is he asked me if he could make this into a cereal, I told him to go for it, and another time he asked me if I could make these into cookies for him. I am not sure about the cookie factor for I think that would defeat the purpose of eating healthy granola but you can really see that he has fallen for it and would love to try it different ways.Pick up bag and enjoy a special treat without the guilt!

column9: Great as yogurt topper & base for snack mix but needs some extra OOMPH
column10: If you are looking for a lower fat and lower sugar Yummy granola-based yogurt topper or snack base, this might just be up your alley.  We found the fat & sugar content to be better than most grocery store options but an area where they can still imrpove.  therefore, we limit our enjoyment of this admittitedly delicious product for use as a topping on our own homemade yogurt and as the base upon which we build our dry snacks.  WE found there weren't enough dehydrated fruit bits for the fruit taste to come through so we add some more of our own Harmony House Foods Freeze-Dried Strawberries, whole (2 oz, Quart Size Jar) as well as some conventionally dried golden raisins.  That works nicely as a yogurt topping and also as good topping for either store bought or homemade icrecream of soft-serve.  If we want to eat it as a cereal, we find we need to add some more home-toasted rolled oats - any brand will do, the cheaper the better just make sure you give them a light toast on a Cookie Sheet.  it brings out the nuttiness in the flavor.  I'd say for each Cereal serving we add maybe another tablespeoon of dehydrated berries, 4 or 5 chopped golden raisins and an extra scant handful of toasted rolled oats.This is not to say that the Nature's Path Love Crunch Dark Chocolate & Red Berries Granola doesn't taste great AS IS, it's just we were expecting more of a berry ZING given the description.  When we eat it plain as a cereal, we want to taste more berry so that's why we left off 1 star.  As a yogurt topping, it also works fine on it's own but adding the extra dehydrated berries, like you find in the Special K Red Berries Cereal, 16.7 Ounce Box (Pack of 3),  adds even more crunch.  Some people have also said they don't find the chocolate taste coming through but I found the taste of it as a Cereal of Yogurt topper to be just fine.  if I were going to have this as a Snack, I recommend, a few inexpensive addtions to stretch the item out and add a little more of a nutritional boost:To make the Snack Mix that our family loves to pack in lunches, also known as "How to Hack your Storebought granola into a snack mix"  -- we have added some home toasted almond slivers and to augment the admittedly small amounts of chocolate pieces in the mix, we toss in a healtheir choice than plain chocolate and use some Nibbles Organic Dark Chocolate Cacao Nibs that have a slightly sweetened dark chocolate covering over the naturally crunchy and unsweetened Cocao Nib in the middle. That punches up the Chocolate quotient nicely without adding too much to the sugar load.  To this we then add even more of the toasted rolled oats mentioned above, which are cheaper than dirt.  Oats are a whole grain, good fuel for on-the-go kids and they hardly notice when it's mixed into a "store bought fancy Granola" alone with the extra berries and Cocao Nibs!  If you still need to stretch it further or just want some variety, we have tried adding some slightly crushed whole wheat pretzels we get locally that are only lightly salted with sea salt, some toasted pepitos (pumpkin seeds), and some generic cornflakes.  That makes up quite a goodly amount of snack mix with enough crunch and taste to satisfy every snacker in our household.As I mentioned above, I liked this Brand and Flavor right out of the bag and could have eaten the entire thing as a snack but after one or two bite, I did want more crunch and more of a Berry/Chocolate thing going on.  The simplest fix is to find the cheapest Dehydrated Strawberries you can on Amazon or locally AND  a Cocao Nib NOT covered in dark chocolate since that will save you a little bit in the sugar to carbs ratio and the calroies from fat area without sacrificing any crunch or chocolate and berry flavor.  In fact, the SIMPLEST fix is to just add more dehydrated strawberries and this would be a 5-star item.I've written to the company to sugest that and also suggest they consider adding plain Cacao Nibs to their forumla since those are actually a formerly under-appreciated by-product of the chocolate making  process and can be sourced cheaply if purchased in large enough quantities.  I believe those 2 rather minor tweaks to the recipe coul make Love Crunch fly off the shelves!

I found this to be a yummy premium chocolate granola. The somewhat sparse pieces of strawberry and raspberry add extra accents of flavor. It makes a nice addition to plain or vanilla yogurt, or even ice cream. Perhaps it is from being shipped, but there is a good bit of the granola that was crushed and crumbled, taking away from the enjoyable mouth feel and texture evident in the larger chunks.Love Crunch does not quite have the 'crunch' I would expect for a quality granola, and the chocolate flavor is muted somehow. The small chunks of dark chocolate seem to be of good quality however. It is fairly healthy when limited to the 1/4 cup size, though it's hard to stop munching after those significant 140 calories.This is a satisfying cereal that I would consider more of a dessert than a breakfast food. See if you can purchase it locally to minimize the amount of crushing I experienced. 3.4 stars, rounding down.~ Kort

I have to admit I never tasted Granola before in my 63 years. But after a heart attack I had spent the past 2-3 years as an avid juicer, plus bought a Vitamix & use it faithfully as well. Now this isn't the most healthy of snacks given its 140 calories in a single serving size of 1/4 cup.....but that 1/4 cup goes a LONG way in satisfying any "treat" cravings you may have. In the long run it will SAVE you calories as it honestly stops a lot of cravings. I have my serving with a cup of decaf coffee and find I don't even feel the need for breakfast, PLUS feel like I just plain start my morning on the right foot. Kind of nice to begin my day every single day rewarding myself and not feeling like I do it with junk food.  If it had not been for the Vine program I admit I would have gone to my grave never having ever even tasted granola. Now as it turns out I will be ordering this and plan to continue using it as my guilty free snack. Not sure why but I never feel like I am forced to watch my portions since while 1/4 cup sounds small in theory, when eaten it completely satisfies and I never feel like I "need" more. This is now one of about a dozen items I have tried on Vine that I end up buying on my own to continue. Even more rare, it EARNS an honest 5 out of 5 stars.

column9: On the 8th day (because peanut butter was created on the 7th)
column10: God created Carrot Cake Granola. I can eat this all day every day. That is my review. Buy this, eat this, and be happy.

I'm not always crazy about granola, but this mix is sweet enough to hold my interest, and my taste buds. I exclusively ate this by the handful as a snack and did not try it as a cereal. My biggest complaint, and the thing keeping it from getting five starts, would be the lack of red berry and chocolate chunks. I rarely grabbed a handful that had both berries and chocolate mixed in with the granola, and often my handfuls had neither berry or chocolate. I assume the low amount of chocolate is for nutritional reasons, but the only reason I can come up with for them to be so stingy on the berries is cost.

Nature's Path Love Crunch, Premium Organic Granola, with dark chocolate and red berries is both healthy and nutritious.  How does this sound:  - 14g whole grains per 30g serving  - Excellent source of ala omega-3  -Low sodium  - 0g trans fat  - Cholesterol freeLove Crunch tastes delicious.  Its fat per serving breaks down as:  Saturated=1g, Trans=0, Polyunsaturated=3g, and Monounsaturated=1.5g, which rounds out to 6g per 30g serving.For someone like me, who is particular and reads labels, finding this organic product was like finding a treasure.  Love Crunch will be in my diet.  The little pieces of dark chocolate are delectable.

column9: To quote Lucky the leprechaun: They're magically delicious!
column10: Granola's always a good snack, and when you add dark chocolate and 'red berries' to the mix, it's even better. At first I was a little disappointed with the size of the bag for Nature's Path Love Crunch, but after just two handfuls of the goods, it won me over and I couldn't stop munching away. I'm not much for organic foods since I eat healthy on a regular basis, only going with fast food and snacks on the weekends, if that, but this is definitely something I'll consider buying in the future.The clusters of granola are big, and there are small pieces of dried strawberries mixed in, with some decent-sized chunks of dark chocolate. While my bag didn't have many strawberries, the flavor detonated in my mouth when all three of the main ingredients were mixed together. What's funny is that I started out disappointed (bag size) and when my bag was empty, I was disappointed that I was all out. Why couldn't I have been sent an entire box of these things like the Eat. Think. Smile bars and chips I got last month?!Not bad for you, filling, and something you could easily make a cereal out of, I highly recommend this granola mix, and I can't wait to try out the others.

In general I advocate against consuming grains or cereals.  However "Love Crunch" is made with reasonably good ingredients (the primary ingredient is rolled oats) and blended to an enjoyable chocolate flavor.  Spelt is one of the healthier forms of wheat, it's far more desirable (nutritionally) than modern wheat.The sugar to fiber ratio is three to one (six grams of sugars to two grams of fiber per serving) which isn't the best of all cereals but it's reasonable.You've got to love all the healthy ingredients: chocolate, flax seeds, coconut and fruit.For a "processed food" this one isn't too bad.

column9: Nice Snack With Some Healthful Ingredients
column10: This granola is quite tasty for a snack right out of the bag. It has a nice oaty flavor with just a hint of coconut. Every once in awhile you find a chunk of chocolate or a freeze-dried berry. If you're eating it as a cereal with milk, you can slice fresh strawberries into it to boost the fruitiness, but as is the dominant flavor is mostly oats. The chunks of dark chocolate are delicious.I wanted to try this granola just because it sounded yummy, but it can be healthful too, if you control your portions. It's fairly low in sugar. The bag says only 6 grams of sugar in 1/4 cup, which is hard to believe, but it really is a lot less sweet than other granolas I've bought. There are 140 calories and 6 grams of fat in 1/4 cup, which is not low fat, but neither is it excessive. In that serving you also get 2 grams of fiber and 2 grams of protein, thanks to the whole grains and the addition of flax seeds, which also provide some omega-3s. All ingredients are certified organic and non-GMO.Overall a good, wholesome-tasting granola, if you don't mind the infrequency of berries and chocolate.

So, I opened the bag just to have a quick taste to see if I would put a little sprinkling of this granola on my homemade yogurt in the morning..... Yea, hubby and I couldn't keep our hands out of the bag.  Well, what is not to love, dark chocolate and little freeze dried berries and nice big pieces of granola.  Delicious!  Nutritionally, you are getting 140 calories, 55 from fat, 6g of total fat, 1 g of saturated fat, no transfat, no cholesterol, 55 mg sodium, 2g fiber, 6g sugar and 2 g of protein, 2% vitamin c and 4% iron.  Serving size is 1/4 cup and the bag serves 10.Likes-organic, 33% of your daily omega 3's, delicious chocolate, sweet berries, tasty granola in nice big chunks. Oh, did I mention a nice little serving of whole grains? This food is Non GMO-I believe this is non-genetically modified.  A portion of the proceeds of the sale go to food banks which is also way cool in my humble opinion.  I also like reading the ingredients and not seeing a bunch of words I can't pronounce and wouldn't want to put in my body.  Just good old normal ingredients that you know.Dislikes-um, the bag seems small now?  Really, can't seem to come up with a con on this one.  I have never purchased from Nature's Path before, but if I happen to see this I would definitely buy.  It is delicious and I normally make my own granola, so I'm a bit picky and used to a really natural granola.All said, great product that I would definitely buy and would recommend to others.

To answer the question above, only one thing: the soy oil. When there are so many other oils out there that are better for you, the only reason to go with soy is the price (it's cheap). But that is my only quibble with this granola. It is delicious.Chocolatey, with a slight berry tang, this stuff makes for a fantastic dessert.

column9: The granola Barry White would have eaten
column10: This is not a breakfast granola. This is an after dinner desert granola. It's a late night romantic granola. With all its chocolaty berry-ness this granola has to be pronounced like Barry White would pronounce it. LUUUUUvvvvvvv Crunchhhhhh. C'mon, say it yourself. Uh huh. That's it, baby.For chocolate flavored granola this is pretty tasty stuff. We have tried Nature's Path vanilla granola as well, and it is also very good. However "Love Crunch" takes the sweetness up a few notches. Maybe you would want to eat it for breakfast, but to us Love Crunch makes a better late night snack due to its desert-like flavors. It's organic, like other Nature's Path granola, and tastes great overall. Surely it's the granola Barry White himself would eat.

I've always liked granola but this is the first granola that I've loved. Love Crunch Carrot Cake Granola is my new favorite breakfast and/or snack. It tastes exactly how it it is described on the package. This is some seriously delicious stuff. I mix it with vanilla yogurt and it tastes like dessert.

I thought this was the tastiest granola I had ever eaten when I got a bite of the dark chocolate, dried berries, and granola together.  What a great combination!  Unfortunately, there were too few berries and chocolate in the bag, so most bites were just granola.  The granola on its own was good, but not extraordinary.  Although brown and chocolate-y looking, the chocolate flavor was not as prominent as I would've liked.  But it was tasty enough to keep me munching, hoping for those perfect bites of smooth dark chocolate, tangy berries, and crunchy granola.  Few and far between, but delicious!

column9: More than granola - call it a luxury treat
column10: This is called a granola but it is not something I would eat for breakfast.  It does have chunks of chocolate in it, and I just don't think "chocolate" when I think "breakfast".  Never will.However as a snack or treat to enjoy between meals, it is really quite delicious.  I didn't even put milk on it - just grabbed chunks straight out of the bag as dessert after my main meal of the day.It is kind of pricey, at almost $4 for an 11.5oz bag so would definitely be a treat - not something to eat every day.

This is a novelty granola, chocolate flavored with chunks of real chocolate, originally created as a confection for the wedding of an Indian couple who work for the producer. It's delicious stuff and part of the profits are donated to food banks. However, this is a very high sugar, high fat granola (the second ingredient after oats is cane sugar and the third is soy oil) and undercuts the health reasons for eating granola in the first place. Unless you run eight miles every morning before breakfast, you would not want to consume this every day. And please don't give it to your kids to "entice" them into switching from chocolate Co Co Pops. This is to granola as chocolate milk is to milk; strictly a novelty item or occasional treat. Also makes a nice gift or door prize.

Most granola cereal to me is very tasty and that is because they are sweet and have savory bits of chocolate or freeze-dried fruit (and sometimes nuts). This cereal is no different.You are supposed to get 10 servings in this 11.5 ounce bag and at 140 calories per serving (55 calories from fat and 6 grams of sugar), you would have to  eat only 2 tablespoons (or 1/4 cup or less than 1.2 ounces) of this cereal to get the allotted amount (and that's without milk).  I was unable to eat just one serving so I ate 2 servings with milk for breakfast.  The cereal is delicious with the chocolate and freeze-dried strawberries and raspberries but it does pack a calorie punch.The ingredients are organic with rolled oats, evaporated cane juice, and soy oil being the first three ingredients. The dark chocolate chunks are the 5th ingredient and the freeze-dried berry blend the 9th ingredient.This granola certainly has 5-star taste and is as good as most of the other flavored granolas (such as Bare Naked) that I've tried before.  However, the others I've tried have only 7 servings for the same amount of calories; they increased the amount of servings in this bag to reduce the appearance of calories and for that I take off one star.

This Nature's Path "Love Crunch Premium Organic Granola, Dark Chocolate and Red Berries" is the best tasting granola snack I have tried. This is a near perfect blend of granola, good chocolate overtones, and slightly tart berry flavor. This is good both as dry granola snack or with a little milk as a cereal. That being said, at 140 calories and 18 net carbs per 1/4 cup it really isn't something I can justify eating whenever a snack mood hits but it is a very nice treat on occasion.Our sample bag was gone within the hour of arriving at our house and my family has demanded I order more.Highly Recommended!CFH

The red "berries" are very small dried pieces. They melt as powder in your mouth and then you get a "bang" of flavor. The chocolate pieces are also smaller than 1/4" square but have a good flavor. Both of these are offset by the crunch and flavor of the granola. As a taste different from the standard granola, these are a welcome treat. If you want to make it more cost effect, add fresh sliced bananas or a breakfast cereal like Apple Cheerios.

I know I've purchased Nature's Path Products before.This Love Crunch Premium Organic Granola With Dark Chocolate & Red Berries. I think the name is perfect for this granola.There are a few things I like about this granola.  First of all it's organic. Who needs pesticides in their cereal, or in anything else?The picture on the ziploc like seal on the top of the bag which helps to keep the product fresh, it shows a heart shape with 2 delicious looking strawberries, and two small pieces of chocolate which kind of blends into the color of the bag. The bag itself is 11.5 ounces, which is supposed to be about 10 servings.It may look like a small bag, but when you look at the back of the bag the portion size is 1/4th a cup.  As the granola is sweet, which part of that I think is the granola itself, then added to it is the chocolate, which you can see and taste that in the granola, but the strawberries, you can see very small red pieces mixed in.  I do wish the strawberry pieces were larger, and that the flavor of them were more pronounced. To me, the flavor of chocolate and strawberries is a match made in heaven.  I have never tasted a cereal much less a granola like this before.So, that makes for a very sweet, at least to me granola, so you may only need to eat 1/4th a cup, which is what they recommend per serving, which should satisfy you.  It did me.The scent of this granola is nice.  There are different sizes of the granola itself, from larger to smaller.  The chocolate and strawberry pieces are more uniform in size.As to the nutritional aspects of this granola, it's 140 calories per each 1/4 cup, total fat-6 grams, of which 1 gram is saturated fat, total carbohydrates is 20 grams, 2 grams of dietary fiber,6 grams of sugar, 14 grams of whole grains, very small amounts of iron and Vitamin C.On the back of the bag what does impress me is that they say for every bag purchased, they will donate an equal amount to food banks in food or cash, up to $1 million dollars.I love companies who give back.I liked this granola.  While I wouldn't necessarily eat this everyday, it is a nice treat when you do eat it.
This product is amazingly tasty.  I am not fond of coconut, and I love, love, love this stuff.  It's especially good with vanilla yogurt and fresh blueberries.  My children like to snack on it, too.

I have been buying Love Crunch granola at Whole Foods for over a year, so I was very excited to find out that Amazon is now selling it online.  This is the best granola I have ever had.
