Several years ago, I went on a tour of the Celestial Seasonings tea factory in Boulder, Colorado.  The guide showed us the bales of tea as they arrived, machines that ground and mixed the tea, and a machine that put the tea in tea bags.  The tour included a visit to the room where the peppermint tea was stored.  Our guide told us that peppermint was stored separately so that it would not contaminate the other teas.  He did not tell us what was to come.The doorway into the peppermint room was surrounded by bright red stripes. This should have served as a warning to us.  We all innocently strolled into the peppermint room.  The smell of peppermint was overpowering.  It entered my nose, my head, my lungs, and then my whole being was infused with peppermint.  What a rush!  The crowd stampeded out of the room in a hurry.  For the rest of the day and into the next, all I could smell and taste was the mint.I am now addicted to Celestial Seasonings Peppermint Tea.  Every time I have some, I am reminded of that fateful day in Boulder.  The events of that day have changed my life forever.  Amazingly, the tea is still legal, openly sold in stores and on the Internet.  I think that the tea is great, but then again I am not an unbiased observer.  On your next visit to Boulder, take the tour.  Or go a safer route; buy the tea from Amazon.

column9: Delicious taste, but you pay a premium to substitute fructose for sucrose
column10: I eat this jam occasionally with peanut butter on crackers, and it is quite tasty. While it is less unhealthy than other sugary jams, I don't deceive myself that it won't raise blood sugar, because it is essentially 100% fructose, which is just as capable of raising blood sugar as sucrose (white/table sugar)--more on this below.Most people buy this product as a presumed health food due to it being lower in sugar than other jams. It's ingredients are: "Juice concentrate (pear, grape), strawberries, maltodextrin (dietary fiber), fruit pectin, citric acid, natural flavor." This product contains no artificial sweeteners, which are associated with various health hazards.This product's primary claim to fame is that it is, as the label states, "sweetened only with fruit juice." Any jam will have its sweetener listed first, meaning that is its primary ingredient. If you are on a low-carb diet or diabetic, you might want to know that this jam basically substitutes fructose for sucrose. Since fructose is twice as sweet as sucrose, the producers only need to use half as much as they would have of sucrose, so it has about half the calories of regular jam. (On the other hand, many cheap jams contain high-fructose corn syrup--but that's another health issue entirely.) The problem for many people is that they are used to the taste of sucrose, and 100% fructose tastes very different from a combination of fructose and sucrose which is the case with regular jam made with white sugar. To my own taste, since I'm eating a fruit spread, it tastes quite sweet enough to me.The fruit pectin in this product is a standard thickener in jellies and jams and its own natural form of fiber, so I am not sure why the company decided to add in maltodextrin and call that "fiber" too. Anyone with a gluten intolerance should be wary of this product because of the maltodextrin since some people with gluten intolerance are getting sick from the maltodextrin in this jam. The producers claim on the label it is "gluten-free," but maltodextrin can be made from either wheat or corn, and apparently this company is not being careful enough about contamination with gluten.Another ingredient that is problematic as to how healthy this product can be is the "natural flavor." It is possible that the producers add a strawberry extract so they can get away with using less real strawberries, which are more expensive than a flavoring. The definition of natural flavor under the Code of Federal Regulations is: "The essential oil, oleoresin, essence or extractive, protein hydrolysate, distillate, or any product of roasting, heating or enzymolysis, which contains the flavoring constituents derived from a spice, fruit or fruit juice, vegetable or vegetable juice, edible yeast, herb, bark, bud, root, leaf or similar plant material, meat, seafood, poultry, eggs, dairy products, or fermentation products thereof, whose significant function in food is flavoring rather than nutritional" (21CFR101.22). That essentially means that natural flavor is derived from a real food, but the process by which it is derived is unexplained and there is no way to know how safe or healthy a natural flavoring is.

column9: Decent tea at an unbelievable price
column10: First off, I noticed a fair amount of sediment that was trapped in the leaves; it doesn't seem to affect the flavor, but is definitely off-putting as it found its way thorough my teapot's mesh filter. This is my only real complain; however, due to the extremely low price I'm willing to forgive this aesthetic issue. The flavor is great, and you can get two to three good infusions from a set of leaves; use warm (~165 F) water for the first infusion, and allow the temperature to rise by a few degrees each additional steeping. I'd recommend using an airtight container for storage though; the bag the tea ships in is good, but two pounds of tea will last most several months.

In case you have never brewed gunpowder or wonder why the name: This tea is very dry and the leaves are small and rolled tight. When the hot water hits the leaves, they "explode" - they swell to many times their original size. Thus, the name gunpowder refers more to the dry preparation technique of the leaves and the way they expand than it does to thy type of leaves or their taste. Warning, if you brew this tea (or any other gunpowder) use about 1/2 or 1/4 the amount that you would use with another tea. The tea is pretty bitter, a taste I like but it isn't for everyone. Since I like the taste and the explosion means less tea is used (less expensive per pot), I rated it 5 stars.

I am used to bag tea, but this tea is miles above anything I've had before, so I can't imagine what some tea snobs are drinking when saying this is only half-decent; for being almost a quarter of the price of most quality loose teas, this is fantastic.This gunpowder green tea is great; I didn't like plain green tea bags very much, but this has definitely turned me on to the world of loose leaf green tea. It has a wonderful and unique smoky, but sweet, flavor that lasts for several infusions. Because the rolled kernels are so dense, two pounds of gunpowder tea came in a bag about 1/4 the size of two pounds of peony white tea, so enjoy it and make it last!

After reading other reviews, I decided to give this tea ([...]) a try.  For the price, it is a good tea, as long as you take care and brew it properly.  Let it steep too long and it gets very bitter, but that is true with all teas.  I would recommend this product.

Our family drinks a lot of iced tea, and I wanted to get something to alternate with our Taylors of Harrogate, Yorkshire Tea Gold Tea. This tea works very well for iced tea, provided one is very careful NOT to use too much tea. If one uses too many tea leaves, it makes a very bitter brew - which would probably be very fine with a lot of sugar. But for iced, use only a little. I make two quarts of tea with only about the equivalent of two tea bags. The resulting brew is refreshing and satisfying, not at all bitter, and a nice change from normal black tea.I recommend this for those who like their tea iced and want a little change, or if you are creating one of those super-strong "gunpowder" hot tea drinks.

We have found that Coffee Bean Direct has a great product quality and selection. We use several types of their teas and use it enough to make the larger bags very worth while. The bags are high quality as well and reseal effectively using either the attached strip or our food saver machine.

So say you eat one cup: not counting milk, you'll have taken in more than 18 grams of sugar.  I like the taste well enough, but agree with the previous reviewer: it doesn't need to be this sweet. Instead of my tasty flakey chocolately bar, I got a flat, pale looking crumbling mess (except for the places where it had melted and fused together).  In all Flake is an excellent product.  I'd give it 4.5 stars.  But you have to be careful of the seller.  It might be better to buy them from an import gourmet food store or have someone in the UK (if you know someone) mail them to you.  I've learned my lesson.

Flake - a rippled layer of chocolate. In the adverts, you need to eat it in the bath in order to avoid dropping chocolate crumbs. Buy them and put them in the fridge. Eat your flake while balanced over a plate to catch the crumbs. Divine. So much better than typical US chocolate. Yum!
Received the candy 3 days after it's expiration date. Disappointed as I expected to received candy that would last a long time.

i was so excited to order this candy as i havent had any for 23 yrs...when i was last in germany....and to my horror..this candy tasted like it had been saved for that period of time.....it was so stale....i was very disappointed. i love cadbury candy....but for the cost, this was not worth it.....guess i'll have to wait till i go overseas again.

I am british and every year I try to get special items for Christmas.  I just ate one of these flakes and it was stale and dry.  I could not tell what the use by date was as it was in arabic.  This is the first time I have used this company, will not use them again.

Please don't order these, I received mine close to the expiration date. The candy was so stale and it has some arabic writing on it? When I ordered, it said shipped from U.K. so I don't know why they have foreign language printed on it. It doesn't matter to me where it's shipped from but they shouldn't ship products that are expired or about to expire. Disgusting!

I love Flake. I get it whenever I go to Ann Arbor, as the World Market down there is the closest place that sells it (an hour and a half drive for me). So I know what this is supposed to taste like, and...this is not it.The candy is stale. I would think this is a seller problem, not Cadbury's...but according to Amazon I'm wrong about that (as I tried to leave seller feedback about the state of the candy).The thing is, not all of the bars were stale. Also, I've purchased a six pack of these before at World Market, and the six bars came in a packaging clearly made for them. It had the nutritional information on the back, the design on the front, etc. These bars came in a clear plastic wrap container with a big white sticker that said 'Flake 6 Count.' Clearly not the original packaging.I wont purchase again. I'll hold out for a trip to Ann Arbor. So much for saving myself the hassle.EDIT: Just wanted to add...there's some arabic writing on the packaging. Maybe I never noticed before, but I've never seen this on Flake purchases I made in an actual store. Just a big disappointment all around.

column9: Best melt in your mouth chocolate out there!
column10: God I love Flakes!  One of the best smooth milky melt in your mouth chocolate bars out there!  Gotta have em!  If you've never tried them, trust me on this, you will not be sorry ordering these.

Imagine ordering chocolate that is supposed to be from England and receiving chocolate wrapped in paper with Pakistani language(Urdu)all over it. Yes, it contained English translation but I didn't order candy from Pakistan. I ordered candy from England thru Trade Concepts. The candy is not "flaky" but rather stale and old and tasted like cheap milk chocolate. If this indeed comes from England, why do the wrappers indicate they are from Pakistan?I also ordered the "Crunchie" (which is nothing even close to the Violet Crumble from Australia). These too are from Pakistan. The center is not flaky or crunchy or crumbly but rather stale and old.If you advertise that something is "from England" that is the only packaging it should be in. Because of the Urdo all over the wrappers, I can only assume that perhaps Trade Concepts imports from England, removes the wrapper and then rewraps them in their own wrappers? I'm sure the FDA would be interested in this practice.I see by some of the other reviews that I was not the only customer deceived.

Assuming you get these from a good seller(which most people on here didn't seem to get, so be careful about where you get them!), these are far too sweet! They are a decent chocolate, similar to Cadbury milk chocolate bars you can get in the US, but they have an interesting flaky texture. I think they are a bit sweeter than regular Cadbury milk chocolate bars(but those are already pretty sweet too, so am not sure), and even though I like the texture, it's not worth it to pay so much for them. I suggest if you're craving Cadbury chocolate just stick with the kinds you can get in the US, it saves you money and hassle.

I loved Flake bars when I lived in England, and I've missed them. In spite of the bad reviews and warnings, I took a chance and ordered them here. Complete waste of money. :( They're obviously made for export as they're covered in Arabic writing. It's hard to even determine where they were made. They say (in English) that they're made *for* Cadbury, but not where they're made. I don't really care so much about that or the inability to read the wrappers, but the quality is AWFUL. They're all dried up, chalky looking, and off-tasting. I tried to finish one, but couldn't get past 2 bites. Now I'm stuck with 5 more that I'd only give to someone I didn't like. I'd give them to some unlucky Trick-or-Treaters, but I don't want them to TP my house. :(

My wife is from Europe (Russia mainly, but she's also lived in England) and she claims that European candies are better than American candies. She says that European candies are less sweet and more flavorful. From the ones I've tried, I'd have to agree. Funny, I'd never thought about it before. In any case, we live not to far from a Fresh and Easy market. It's a British company and they have a lot of British things, including candies. I've had several varieties of Cadbury chocolate things that were just extraordinary. As such, this evening I picked up a Cadbury Flake Bar. Mmmmmm, Gooood! That''s just delicious! It's not too sweet and has a nice rich cocoa/chocolate taste. My goodness! These are excellent!Gary Peterson

I have a good friend who lives in Britain, so THAT is how I found out about Cadbury Flakes, she sent me a bunch of them and I got seriously hooked! However, packages kept costing over $50 to send! So I saw these and decided to try it. The packaging is NOT from Britain, it's in a whole 'nuther language, so I opened it and tried it anyways and I PROMISE you, I compared the TRUE cadbury flake to this one and there really wasn't too much difference in taste, you'll find that most chocolate will taste like it may have melted a bit somewhere along the way, UNLESS you pay about $30 extra to send it overnight in a cold package (trust me, I do that often with chocolates from CT to TX)I would (and am again) purchase this, it's still better than (one of my faves) Hershey chocolates and beats the cadbury products we have here. Maybe it's the texture, but it's pretty good PLUS I save an extra $50 just by ordering it from here.

column9: bad tasting candy, other reviews were right.
column10: 1) these candy bars were apparently made for overseas distribution but never got distributed.  Now the vendor needs to offload them.  I ordered from a company in Mass. figuring that all the reviews talking about candy with asian/indian language on the wrapper might be avoided but it was not.  Seems you will get these "overseas" bars wherever you get them from.  Even if only one state over.2) more to the point, these bars were horrible tasting.  I took two bites of the first one, and then tossed the entire group in the trash.There it is then.  Hail Flavius!
Flake Bars are the best.  Nothing else like it.Eat slowly and you'll feel like your in heaven!
I first had this item in South Africa on a visit and fell in love with them, now my kids can try them as well.
This is the most deliciuos chocolate! It can be a bit messy, but it's well worth it! If you love chocolate, you'll love Flakes!
Loved the flake bars!  They are always good. Would have given this product 5 stars, but the bars came in a bunch of little pieces. :(

Cadbury's chocolate flake is the perfect topping for ice cream. It's rich milky chocolate is the perfect answer to a delicious dessert. No need to wait to try this, ordering from Amazon it's there in a wink.

column9: melt-in-your mouth light, airy, not too sweet milk chocolate
column10: The first time i bought this chocolate was in a small upscale shop with a lot of imported foods.  It was kind of stale but what can you expect when it's made in the UK and not the US??  But in any case, it wasn't too sweet and it was very light and easy to bite into, like biting into feathery light chocolate flakes, compared to the usual US mainstream cheap chocolate bars which are overly sweet with tons of sugar and too dense to bite into.  It's not something that I would go out of my way to buy since I would buy premium chocolates like TCHO chocolates TCHO-A-DAY 30 or McElrath chocolates  or even Lindt or Ritter chocolates or Ghiradelli, but I'd certainly select them over our usual cheap chocolate candy bars in the US.
If you love Cadbury's chocolate, you'll love these flaky morsels.  Creamy chocolate that melts nicely in your mouth and I confess to loving them with a hot cup of tea.  Delish!
My naughty little indulgence!!!! Gotta have a Flake bar once in a while - reminds me of home. If you haven't tried one yet.....you are missing out!!

column9: Past expiration. Not intended for U.S.
column10: Product arrived 3/12/2012. Item is marked 3/10/2012 with what I can only assume is the expiration date. Product not intended for U.S. as it has Arabic, Greek and Chinese lettering. There is some English but its a bit hidden. Not that the text needs to be English but combining this with the expiration leads me to believe the candy isn't intended for U.S. market. Is there a law against that, selling expired goods imported from another country? This product was packaged by Amazon LLC.I don't want to hurt the product itself with a low rating. Its probably good stuff, but I'll never know because Amazon sold me expired goods.

I'm wondering the same thing as the other buyers. If these are supposed to come from England, why is all the writing in Arabic? I did receive them a couple weeks before the printed expiration date, and they tasted fine, but isn't this false advertising?
Seriously, you can NOT go wrong with Cadbury products! This flaky goodness is rich in flavour and it melts in your mouth. Puts Hersheys to shame!
This stuff is incredible!Melt in you mouth pure chocolate, hand made by lepricons in Cadbury, Ireland, using only the finest ingrediants.Thoes firey little green men put Nestly and Hershy to SHAME!!!
I reviewed this item earlier.As I said,the six pack is the best way to buy this product.It is cheaper than the local retailers near my home in the Richmond,Va. area.

Made my dog very I'll with diarrhea. This brand is top on the list of treats to not buy. Apparently they're causing kidney failure in dogs, hopefully it does not happen to my dogs. Do not trust made in China treats!

column9: FINEST BLEND OF sTROGANOFF IN DELICIOUS SAUCE
column10: Outstanding gourmet taste: the blend of mushrooms, steak and sauce is tantalyzing.  The orders could be divided, so that the entire order doen't have to be defrosted at once.  Possibly divide the large portion into three or four smaller ones. As it stands the order is easily microwavable.

January 3, 2012I purchased the Beef Stroganoff from Omaha Steakhouse last week. It arrived in a small tray covered with plastic. I didn't really read the instructions for preparation ... just got out my trusty skillet and lid. I popped it out the container and addded just a couple teaspoons of water and let it simmer. It simmered about 15 minutes before I tasted it.. The sauce was delicious and the beef was tender. There was only one thing lacking [noodles]. There was only a tiny beef of egg noodles and alot of meat. Nonetheless, it was tasty. I give it 3 stars.
Disappointing in the amount of meat and vegetables. Guess I was hoping for a more natural sauce. The tomatoe base was not to my liking.

column9: Ho Hum, Ho Hum, Slightly better than None (or Folgers)
column10: Perhaps it was the dry, dull, look of the beans that should have warned me of the average flavor forthcoming from my Espresso machine.  Should Amazon or whomever sent me this, state the roasting date on its advertisements?
I bought these because of the amount in bag - they were tougher then the ones i get locally - they get better after spending the night in the refrigerator - but would not recommended if eating fresh.

I do not like instant coffee, but my wife wants something that is quick and easy some morning.  This without a doubt the best instant coffee I have tasted. It is not fresh brewed but it is pretty close

Single serve packets of Taster's Choice. Easy to open, carry, and use. Tastes like, well, instant coffee, but if you're buying instant coffee, you probably don't care. This is the ideal portable caffeine delivery system. The package can even be used to stir the coffee...no mess, no cleaning.

column9: Easy, tastes good, does the job
column10: I decided to try this brand of instant coffee for our office and plant breakroom.  It is convenient and tastes very good for an instant coffee.This works well for people in a hurry. I'll give it 5 stars because it is the best that an instant coffee can be.

So, I no longer have to ask anyone to go through the hassle of having them go to the "Quicky Mart" to procure my coffee! If you don't want to do the "Quicky Mart" route just do what I am doing and buy from this vendor! Why not?

column9: Best tasting instant coffee and sugar free too!
column10: This is the Taster's Choice that I bought 2 years ago, and now buying more because the brewed stuff takes way too long, and in fact, the Taster's Choice tastes better than the brewed stuff.After I ran out of these packets when I bought then in 2010, I decided to go back to the brewed coffee for about a month  (I ground the beans right before I made the coffee) to see if there was any difference in taste.  I could not believe it - I preferred the taste of the Tasters Choice instant stick packets over the expensive organic decaf and regular whole ground beans that I had been buying! So after a month of trying the ground beans and brewed coffee (Hawaii's excellent Lion Coffee with Coconut, Hawaii's Macadamia nut coffee, Blue Mountain coffee, organic colombian decaff from whole foods), I am back to the Taster's Choice packets!It just doesn't beat it for taste and convenience.I am specifically looking for a clean, delicious coffee taste, without any sugar or carbs added. It tastes delicious without anything else added to it.  For fun and health reasons, sometimes, I simply add a dollop of organic coconut oil to make sure I get my daily dose of good fat, add lots of cinnamon to lower the body's insulin response (to caffeine) and it is rich and delicious! Yumm. Please don't ever take this off Amazon - the store prices are waaaay more and it is much cheaper at Amazon!The local Korean grocery store also carry the Korean Brand of Taster's Choice in 100 packet bags but they have it heavily mixed with sugar and milk (very delicious - by the way - if you like sugar and cream in your coffee) but they do not sell it without the sugar and cream so I am buying it at Amazon.

column9: Passable when added to regular joe
column10: true on its own, this stuff barley resembles a fresh brewed at home cup of coffee but when added to a fresh brewed at home cup of coffee it makes a great add-in when making iced coffee.

I must confess before I review that I have never had an instant coffee that tasted as good as fresh ground brewed coffee.  However, I bought this for a camping trip due to weight constraints, and lack of equipment.  At home, this coffee is barely drinkable.  In the middle of a swamp, this coffee tastes great.The packaging is small.  Easy to carry and store.  Just heat water and add the number of packages you require.  Great for emergency coffee supply or camping.  Terrible for everyday home use.I give this 4 stars because it met my needs in the woods.  I'd give it or other instant coffees 5 stars if it tasted like fresh ground brewed coffee.
Horrible coffee.  It's like drinking water.  I'm going back to Starbucks VIA even if it is 3 times more expensive.

column9: No Wheat + No Corn = Big Hit with the Doggies
column10: Newman's Own Organic Chicken Treats for Dogs are a big hit with my three dogs; a miniature poodle, a black lab and a standard doxie. Made in Canada these have the following analysis:Crude Protien: 11.5% minCrude Fat: 8.5% minCrude Fiber: 6.0% maxMoisture: 10.0% maxINGREDIENTS: Barley flour*, ground chicken*, carrots*, apples*, canola oil, rolled oats, natural flavor.  Note: (*) indicates certified organic.SIZE: Medium sized in this case means 'heart-shaped', about 1.5" x 1.5".  You could actually break them in half for small dogs.While this is not supposed to replace your dog's food, they'd like it if it did! The reason I give it 4 stars is because of the 'premium price'. I picked them up at a local grocery closeout store for $2 a bag with 18 months left until the the 'best before' date. My doggies haven't said anything about them being stale, so I guess Newman's Own has done it again.CONCLUSION: Organic, high quality dog treats. Nice product.
Terrific quality product, my dog loves them and it is for a good cause. What more could a responsible animal lover want?

I can only judge by my dogs preferences...she definetely honors these treats.  I ordered by accident the large size instead of the small hearts, not thinking that they come in various sizes.  She is a 17 pound pooch and she loved them. They are so soft that they could easily be handled by any size dog. Thank you!

We bought a single jar at the Mustard Museum in Middleton, WI.  Unfortunately we only purchased one jar since we had a variety of items.  Big mistake on our part.  We've been looking to get another without too much success.Now as to the product itself, we enjoy orange marmalade -- not the bulk produce variety that sits on the shelves of most grocery stores, but the gourmet section.  We like the Tangerine flavor the best, and this is one of the best.

column9: Good but not as good as the tea bag version
column10: I bought this product because it appears that the teabag version of the Pixie mate chai (all of Pixie's teas actually) are no longer being made or sold and it was my favorite drink.  I do not particularly like things that are extremely sweetened so it has been difficult to find the right balance with this concentrate.  It is not bad, it is not great either.  It is extremely sweet as it has the sugar already in it.  The directions recommend mixing half concentrate with half milk and heating.  I found this to be overwhelmingly sweet and thick so I use 1/3 concentrate 2/3 almond milk (which is less sweet even than milk) and sometimes dilute with water a bit as well.  Note this does NOT taste good diluted with just water.If you like things that are very sweet you will love this.  If you find where they are still selling the teabag version please post!
We love the Yerba mate concentrate. It's better than chai tea and goes so well with soy milk...hot or cold. This seller offers the best price on the Internet, with fast delivery. Highly recommended.

I've had the privileges of traveling the world, living in Europe for three years, and being able to sample most any food I've had the desire to taste.  Chocolate has always been one of my favorite foods.That being said, this is simply the best chocolate I've ever had the privilege to sample.  Dozens of subtle flavors dance across the tongue as each type of taste bud brings slight variations in this creamy smooth bittersweet confection.  Best experienced by sharing with a friend, although I'm sure other pairings would work well too.  Easily 5 stars for the chocolate, and the packaging is quite attractive.However, there is more to the experience than simply the product.  In this case, the single 50 gram bar of chocolate costs $12, but the price must include shipping (obviously) which bumps the price to a whopping $22.  No significant options are given for shipping, and "expedited" means that it will take two weeks for the item to arrive.  On the plus side, the chocolate did arrive with a small ice pack, but given that the current ambient temperatures were all well below freezing this seemed rather unnecessary.  The item would have been received much faster, cheaper, and probably as in good of condition if it had been mailed via standard US postage.  So, I deducted one star for service.  I might have thought otherwise had I ordered the item in July; however in that case the single ice pack would not have been enough to survive a two week shipping time.So, overall I highly recommend this chocolate.  Given the cost of shipping, I recommend ordering a quantity sufficient to cover the costs. It only makes sense to order many, as once your friends and family discover you have this wonderful chocolate you'll need enough to share!

column9: Best I've had, though only for connoisseurs.
column10: I live in Venezuela, where the worlds finest cacao beans are grown in a remote village that is only accesible through the sea. The cacao beans grown there are dried in front of the village church in a process the whole town participates in. Ironically, if Venezuelans want to taste their cacao beans turned into chocalate, they must buy it from the extremely high-end Italian chocolatier Amedei, as Amedei has the exclusive rights to all the production of the beans from Chuao, to the last bean. Therefore, when in Europe, I searched for the bars. Amazingly, you can find them easily in classy shops at 10 euros a bar at least. I finally found the gold medal winning Chuao one. I took it back to my hotel. Drank some Perier to wash out all flavor from my mouth. Sat comfortably, and mentally went over the ritual of tasting fine chocolates. I took the first piece, placed it whole on my tongue (you're not supposed to bite), pressed it against the palate and let it do it's magic. The richness, strength, and intense flavor impressed me from the start. As it melted evenly on my tongue, I felt the gnarl of chocalate's natural bitterness, but more woody, remiscent of Royal Salute scotch, but with a sweet smoothness that relaxed my mind. The impressive effect was the aftertaste. The taste of nutty bittersweet wood stayed on my tongue as if the chocolate was still there. Not until I drank more Perrier did it go away. A unique experience in chocolate tasting.I do not recommend a Bud guzzlin' guy to spend money on high-end chocolate such as this one. You can, but you might end up saying that a good 'ol American Hershey bar is better. It's like fine art. If you know nothing about it, you won't fully appreciate it. I recommend it for people that like chocolate and have tried and enjoyed AT LEAST mid-range chocolates such as Lindt and Godiva, and especially if you've tried high-end type such as Cluizel, Scharffen Berger and Valrhona.

column9: One of the best single-origin chocolates
column10: If you think that Hershey's Special Dark is amazing chocolate, please navigate away from this page now and don't look back. Your tongue is not prepared or worthy (as yet) for this chocolate. Save yourself the money and confusion that would be yours should you purchase this chocolate; this territory is off limits to the uninitiated and uneducated. You need to know enough to know *why* this is some of the best chocolate in the world. Suffice it to say that those that are ready for it know that they are ready for it. Are you?So, Valrhona used to have a Chuao, and it was pretty good - Amedei now makes the superior Chuao bar (Valrhona no longer produces one; 2003 was the last year they did so, I believe - Bonnat makes a Chuao, but it isn't worth your time).I haven't tasted this one in a while, so particulars are somewhat hazy - one thing that I do remember quite well is that the beautiful mouthfeel of this chocolate was intense while there was a sufficient quantity present in my mouth, but after I had swallowed the last of it, it quickly left my mouth feeling clean and fresh, as it would feel shortly after brushing my teeth; many chocolates seem to leave my mouth feeling sullied for a long period of time, but not this stuff. Of course, sometimes you *want* your palate to ring with the taste of a chocolate (especially ones that have a really long, complex finish) for a long time - this one simply excites your mouth and quickly moves on, like a flirtation with someone you will never see again; exciting while it lasted, but all it leaves you with is a good memory.

Simply put, Amadei produces the best chocolate in the world.  It's not an opinion, as much as it's a restatement of the results of the past three World Chocolate Awards.  Chuao is a lot different than the Porcelana variety.  Both are amazing, with Porcelana being the pure chocolate flavor and Chuao having more hints of fruit in the flavor.  Either way, each bar comes in ten squares.  I couldn't imagine having more than one square at a sitting.  I'd highly recommend either one of them.

Amedei by far makes the best chocolate in the world. I've had a few of their products and the quality is unsurpassed. I know some may think that the cost seems very high, but if you don't know chocolate, this is Not something you sit down and eat all at one time. You simply take one or 2 pieces at a time and savor it in your mouth. No, you don't just chomp down on good chocolate, Do wine experts gulp good wine, certainly not, they savor it. Their is no difference . If you are looking to try something Way above par, then look no further. The texture is smooth, and the taste is something you never forget. You will never go back to your basic bar after Amedei. I hope you take the chance and try it. If buying off the internet is a problem, try going to a local specialty chocolate shop in your area and see if they have it,or just let them order it for you. That way, if it ships incorrectly, they are liable, not you. Hope this helps with your decision.

I ordered Chocolate from Italy.  Maybe this was the first mistake since it is Texas in the Summer.  Anyway I took a chance because this is suppose to be the best chocolate in the world; according to another website.  Anyway the chocolate arrived at my door when I was not there.So fedex in all its wisdom drove around with it all day and tried again when I was not there.  I had to go to the fed ex office and pick it up.When I opened the box of course the chocolate was soup and the remains of a soggy single ice pack. So I am out $75 and nothing to show for it.Please send a message to this company that their chocolate is not all it is cracked up to be.

Although their chocolate mint water is my favorite, I enjoy this one as well for variety. I really hate a strong mint taste (like spearmint or peppermint) so I love that this one has a mild mint flavor that just makes it more refreshing than regular water. I also like the orange flavor. It's really nice to have flavored water without extra calories or sodium (as in sparkling water).If the strength of the mint is also important to you, check out their coolness meter on the side of each bottle.I only give four stars because I think the water itself could taste more "pure" like Fiji.

Of all the MetroMint waters, I believe this is my favorite. It's not a strong mint --- just a lovely mild tang that makes drinking water a wonderful pleasure.The orange and mint are ever so mild --- just a hint. The only word I can think of is "refreshing".I love the bottles. They are sturdy and handsome and a nice size for any hand. I've read a few reviews of other flavors of MetroMint that claim they taste like toothpaste. I've not had the stronger waters so I can't judge them. But this one certainly does not taste like toothpaste. It's a real treat and I wish it was available in more stores.Highly recommended.- Susanna K. Hutcheson
Omg! Orange mint rocks my world! Can't get enough of this flavor. So cool and refreshing especially when consumed ice cold!

I really like this product but can't understand how it can be so expensive on Amazon.  I just bought the four-pack at WHole Foods (Whole Paycheck) and it was only $5.79. You have to have a lot of nerve to charge more than Wholefoods!

I had a coupon for this water and Kroger had it on sale. So I bought some of it. It is the absolute worst!! It taste like you just drank the water you rinse your mouth out with after your brush your teeth. I took it to softball practice with me. Took a big gulp and gagged!! Then I let 4 of my teammates try it and they did the same. I am glad I only paid 24 cents a bottle for it. Otherwise I would have been taking it back to the store!

C. Rust is correct, the bags do contain a little less tea as they are designed for those who make tea by the cup instead of the pot, something (shock horror :^) the British have begun to do more often.  We also discovered this when we first brought back several of these bags from Costco in Manchester England.  I too wondered if it was worth it as it does take 3 to make a pot whereas the 240 count box size only takes 2 so I did the math and found that it was still worth it to get the 1150 bags.  I just did the math again using the US price on Amazon (yes, we are running out and no trip to the UK in the near future) and it is still cheaper to buy the bag of 1150 bags versus the box of 240 bags.The box of 240 is $0.77/oz based on the weight of the tea in the box.  The bag of 1150 is $0.55/oz.  But even if you just do the math with the number of tea bags used it is still cheaper.  The box of 240 at $19.95 a box is $0.08/bag or $0.16 a pot if you use two bags a pot.  The bag of 1150 at $48.95 is $0.043/bag or $0.13/pot when you use 3 bags a pot.BTW, a box of 240 at Sainsburys in the UK costs $9.48 today but if you factor in the airfare to go and  get it I guess we're still getting a bargain here :^)

I bought this 1150-count bag and have no complaints. The price was right, because 1150 / $50 comes out to less than five cents per bag, which compares favorably against almost any other brand of tea, let alone PG Tips, which I find superior to most other brands. I do not perceive any difference in the amount of tea per teabag in this container as compared to smaller sizes that I purchased from Fresh Market. The container is just a normal thin papery bag, not resealable without a clothespin or other device, and I intend to relocate the teabags to an airtight container so they will stay fresh. I drink at least a pot of tea everyday, consuming 3 to 6 bags per day, so this bag will be used up in a year's time. But even so, it is a good idea to protect the teabags from oxygen. Any type of plant matter will decompose in the presence of heat, oxygen or light--doesn't matter whether it is tea, coffee or cannabis.

However, I find it takes 3 bags to make a six cup pot of golden tea instead of the 2 bags I've used previously that come in the boxes.  I'm guessing that they packaged this large bag for restaurant use, and decided to put less tea in each bag.  The tea is still delicious, but it's probably more economical to buy it in the 160 or 240 count boxes.
This is the best tea ever.  It is a smaller pyramid bag than the original boxed PG Tips, but I like it better.  It is perfect for one cup of tea.

WOW WHAT A BARGAIN.  THIS IS THE ONLY TEA WE DRINK AND IT IS ADDICTING.  MY HUSBAND MAKES A 5 BAG POT IN THE MORNING, AND IF WE FINISH IT, I MAKE ANOTHER POT IN THE LATE AFTERNOON (TEA TIME).  What is so good about TIPS, is that you can heat it in the microwave, even after sitting in the pot, with the bags.....and it is never bitter.  I told one of my daughters what a good deal I had found on Amazon with this huge bag of tea......and she said, "Mom, is it fresh?"  Made me look at the sell-by date and yes it is good until 2013.......It won't last that long;  I will be ordering another one in a few months!  By the way, we started buying the PG Tips Special Blend at a local retail store as Amazon didn't have it....and it is even better...but does cost more.

column9: PG Tips Teabags in large quantities
column10: I love this tea and when I found I could order lots of it at once, I did.  It arrived in sealed envelopes and that was great for storing.  Came by post very quickly and in perfect condition.  Thank you!
I love this great tasting tea.  Happiness is having a lot to enjoy and to share with family and friends.
Received product on time and in expected condition.  Will do business again.  This is the second time I have ordered the 1150 count bag of teabags and have been happy each time.

I purchased these teabags thinking they were regular size teabags, as in 2 servings per bag, which at some point in time was how they were made. After I open the large bag 1150 size I notice the actual teabag is much smaller than what I was use to and read on the bag "one cup pyramid teabags" written underneath the 1150. I was use to making a pot of tea using 2 regular teabags so thinking this was the same size, I made a pot of tea using 2 bags and the taste was lacking, also the color paler, so it was then I discovered the bag had less tea in it and was a totally smaller bag. So now I am having to use 3 bags to get the same strength tea, thus not making this such a GREAT bargain by buying a larger quanity, as I am having to use more bags per pot of tea ! I am thoroughly disgusted and won't buy this size again, I am annoyed that the size of the actual teabag was not noted on the discription of this large bag,its not readable on the bag "on line" for the eye to see. I might buy the 250 size if someone can tell me its the regular size teabag, otherwise I shall not purchase from them again, Mrs Laraine SantagatoP.S. My sister in England informs me that these teabags posted on Amazon in England DO STATE that they are 1 cup bags, they need to do the same on this on this side of the pond..thanks !

I drink a lot of tea.  Usually at least 5 or 6 cups a day, sometimes more, perhaps a bit less at the weekend.  I bring tea to the States from UK - usually Tea Direct fairtrade tea, which you can buy at Oxfam.  It's similar to Brooke Bond Choicest Blend, strong, astringent, refreshing.However, I don't drink it at work, as I don't want to use it all up too rapidly, and they don't ship it to the U.S.  So, my working tea is PG Tips.  I've been buying it on Amazon for years now, and the big boxes are fantastic.But, like other reviewers have mentioned, this big bag is a bit cheaper per bag, and I thought I'd give it a try.Someone else mentioned that the weight per bag was a bit smaller, but I thought that letting it steep for the recommended time would counter that.  Unfortunately, it doesn't.  If I leave it in for around 10 minutes, I get an approximation of the flavor from the regular pyramid bag, but after 5 minutes brewing, when I add milk, the tea is a nasty, weakish grey color.  The taste is, well, OK.  It's better than Liptons.  But it is not as good as the ones you can get in the boxes.I won't make this mistake again.  That said, I *will* drink the remainder of the bags (with the help of my missus), but I consider this a failed experiment.
My dog just loves these treats. They are good for her and apparently, taste pretty good. They are a product of Ecuador.
These are my puppy's favorite treats by far, and I like that it is something completely different than kibble/dog food.

column9: Great alternative to the Aspartame drink mixes out there.
column10: Don't get me wrong, I do enjoy drinking just plain ol' water, but sometimes I desire a little flavor in my beverage, without added sugar.Having said that, I'm surprised that the powdered drink mixes I see at the grocery store are primarily sweetened with aspartame.  After all, Splenda/Sucralose has been out long enough to have made its way to these products.  I found this mix on Amazon and I'm quite pleased with it.  It's sweetened with Splenda, and it has none of the aftertaste often associated with aspartame.  It does indeed taste like fruit punch, with more of a cherry note to it, but very pleasant.One thing to keep in mind is that while each little tub makes 2 quarts of beverage per the instructions, I find that using two full quarts of water for one tub makes for a somewhat watered down taste, so I just adjust the amount of water down a bit (though not worth deducting stars).  That is a matter of taste, so of course experiment for yourself.This is a great product and I highly recommend it.
My husband loves mixing this with Lemonade.  In the summer it makes a wonderful cooling drink.  I can't find it in our local stores was so happy to find it at Amazon.com.

Have been using the 4C products for many years. Hard to find some of the flavors in the stores and ordering from them on line is much more expensive. Amazon carries a better assortment of flavors and it's easier to order and received what I want.

column9: Great product but priced too high on amazon.com
column10: This is one of the few products that manages to LEAVE OUT the extra maltodextrin calories, aspartame, and sodium benzoate. But I can buy this for $4.00 per canister at Walmart.amazon.com needs to offer more competitive prices if I'm going to buy in bulk and wait for shipping.
When Crystal Light became relatively impossible to find, I bought my husband a pack of 4C fruit punch.  He loves it and I'm a hero!

column9: More nutrition than you would think
column10: Cherry Pop Tarts have 10% of the recommended daily allowance of iron, folic acid and niacin. So while not being quite as nutritionally dense as a sugary sweet cereal with sprayed on vitamins, they actually do have some value for vitamins and minerals.Other than that, they are super convenient. If you don't mind burned sugar in your toaster from bits flaking off while you're toasting them, you can just pop them in a toaster to heat them up and add a nice golden toasty flavor to them. You can also eat them straight out of the packet. Each packet holds two pastries, which is very convenient since most toasters have 2 slots. Some have 4. If your toaster has 4, share! You could do a Pop-Tarts, Frosted Chocolate Fudge, 16-Count Tarts (Pack of 8) and cherry combination if you are wild for chocolate covered cherries.Kids love these for breakfast. Wives, well, mine at least, not as much. She makes a face at me eating them and mutters something about candy-coated cardboard.Great guilty pleasure.

column9: Gooey fruity sweetness in a box
column10: Cherry flavored Pop Tarts are my favorite. These taste the closest to real fruit and I love them warm from the toaster. I buy them on sale and in bulk and our whole family loves them. This is one of the basic flavors that has staying power over all the new kid friendly flavors they have been developing the past few years.
The product arrived on time and in good condition. At least I haven't found any broken boxes yet. But the tarts just are not quite fresh.

column9: Love not having to go to the store
column10: I love that I can just order this off the internet at a great price and not have to go to the store.  It ships within a few days of my order.

Misunderstood the count on this item. Thought I had purchased 2 boxes of 16 ct. poptarts. When it arrived I received a HUGE shipment of 8 boxes of 16 ct. poptarts. 128 poptarts!!! Had fun passing them out to friends and family.
Pop-Tarts are a great source for breakfast, because you can eat them on the run. Living on a ranch you just grab and go. They have super taste and you can eat them without milk or coffee.KC

I sent this item to my friends in South Carolina. It was supposed to be for Christmas, but they got it at Thanksgiving and they have enjoyed every morsel. It was so good I'm sure there is nothing left for the holidays.

Did not get what I ordered and emails to customer service didn't get them so send the correct item. I ordered individual slices not a whole cake.  Finally cut into cake sent.  Dry as sand, we didn't like it and tossed the rest.  Won't deal with company again.

My 7-month old son loves Yummy Spoonfuls! Besides rice cereal, this is the only baby food he's ever eaten. I bought a jar of organic baby food at the grocery store, tried it myself, and it tasted nothing like real food, so I didn't want to feed it to him. I researched other options and found Yummy Spoonfuls (via Cookie Magazine). What a great variety of food for all stages, and it tastes like real food! My son has loved ALL of the veggies ... eats the whole amount every time! Mama and baby couldn't be happier with this product. And I love the fact that it's homemade organic food ... I really wanted to make my own food, but can't find the time or energy, and why should I when Yummy Spoonfuls does it all for me!?

column9: Next best option to homemade baby food... if you don't have time to make your own at home!
column10: Brand/Products - Came across it while searching through net for a good organic option to baby food. In my little research, learned the brand had some recognition in its field - like Cookie magazine, some interviews on CNN and other news channel and also has a fan page on Facebook!!Packaging/Shipping - I was skeptical as it's frozen, but came well frozen in a Styrofoam container with dry ice. Yes, wish there was another way of packaging it, but I suppose it has to come frozen so at this point Styrofoam may be the only option... but then I am no logistic/shipping expert so don't know what other options are out there for frozen product shipping that are a bit more environmental friendly and/or recyclable.I signed up for a 4-month plan they offer for the Mommy Club members listed on their website. The owners are great about taking suggestions and trying to improve product line and shipping methods - I was called about recycling the Styrofoam container... that they will send a return label with my next shipment so I should return it to them and they can keep using the same container for each of my monthly order or until the container lasts so that's little better than having a new container each month.Products - I have tried all variety from Creamy Yummy and now starting to try to Mushy Yummy! My baby loves pretty much all creamy variety. I even did my own mixing at home - like mix creamy carrots with creamy peas, creamy butternut squash with broccoli or green beans and all such combination as my baby didn't really warm up to peas by itself! :) I add the Happy Baby rice, multi-grain, or Oatmeal cereals to the veggies and to fruits to make it little more flavorful for my baby. In morning, I give the entire fruit portion mixed with 3 tbl spoons of cereal (used to also add formula or breast milk when first introduced Yummy solids, but now mix only the fruit and cereal) and rest of day I give a veggie combo with like 1 tbl spoon of cereal. Unless my baby is tired or sick, she eats the whole portion.Cost - Yes, it's expansive at $2 for each 4 Oz container compared to Earth's Best or Full Circle or even Gerber Organic baby food, which by the way, are jar baby food and not frozen like Yummy's. It's your pick what you do want to give your baby and I know we all want the best for our babies so one choice over another may not be bad - just what you are comfortable with and what works with your own lifestyle and budget!Savings/Discount Option - I called the owners asking about discount since I ordered a lot in one order and was told that they offer something called Mommy Club. So if I join the Mommy Club, which means sign up for a 4 month commitment to order at least 84 containers (7 cases) each month in any verity of baby food from Creamy or Mushy line then I'd get each 4 Oz container at a discounted rate of $1.60 per container or something like that plus any shipping cost. So I thought that was much better than $2 per container and I was going to order from them anyway for next 2-3 months so thought signing up with the Mommy Club was a good option for me!! Yes, shipping is still very costly and that's the only reason I gave this a 4 start rating rather than 5 - wish shipping could be a little less costly at this price of product!So those wanting to order longterm, don't forget to call or sign up with the Mommy Club to take advantage of the savings in cost per product.They are also flexible on monthly order volume if you just cannot get to 84 containers each month or take a little more than a month to make the next order... so just call and ask for the details.In my first monthly order, I got a free Yummy Baby bib, too... that was cool.I made a suggestion on adding certain grains and cereals to Yummy product line to the owners and they said they are looking into it and probably will have it available around June 2010 timeframe so I am looking forward to that. Until then I keep using Happy Baby cereals and admit that my baby loves it and so do I. I hope Yummy also adds probiotic and other nutrition to their cereals like Happy Baby does!Overall, I can't be happier with the product given that I am a working mother and do not have the time to consistently make my own at home, at least not the variety of fruits and veggies that Yummy offers!

column9: So fresh with NO PRESERVATIVES perfect for my baby
column10: I am a proud moma to a not so healthy baby and finding clean food that his little body can tolerate has been a huge challenge, We have tried every organic baby food brand but to our total disappointment they all have citric and ascorbic acids added to help maintain their freshness which our son is sensitive too. We never knew about fresh frozen food, we are delighted to find Yummy Spoonfuls, I actually never thought I could find baby food without ascorbic acid (vitamin C) and citric acid added nor that it can actually be made fresh like you would at home, OMG, this is how food should taste, the peas, sweet potato, apple and squash all taste nothing like baby food. You all are amazing for making fresh food for our babies.. Thank you. hol cow, this is good, this is the standard to set for baby food..I am a happy mommy

column9: Fresh taste so much better. We love this product
column10: Yummy spoonfuls has been a Godsend!!  The fact that this food is FRESH, PURE, ORGANIC, and EASY is completely unheard of in today's marketplace. As a busy working mother, to prepare meals like this would require a lot of time that I would rather be spending with my family.  Yummyspoonfuls affords me the opportunity to provide extraordinary foods for my baby and not spend an inordinate amount of time preparing and storing it.  The simplicity of the product allows for a great degree of creativity in food combinations.  I am very pleased with this product and I wish it where in my local store. Thank you so much for a great product.

I have nothing but great things to say about Yummy Spoonfuls.  I have purchased the creamy variety pack several times and am now purchasing the Mushy stage foods.  In our area, it is very hard to find fresh/frozen organic baby food.  I really wish I had the time and knowledge to make my own food, but I don't and I truly feel Yummy Spoonfuls is the next best option to making your own food.  My baby has done very well with their food and I feel like I am offering healthier choices for my baby.  I have tasted everything that I have given my baby and everything tastes great.  At first, I was discouraged because I was going to order directly through Yummy Spoonfuls site and the cost to ship to California was extremely expensive.  Then I saw on Amazon and although the cost for the food is significantly higher, you can get free shipping which brings the cost to about $3.75 a container.  I have no problem paying $3.75 a container for frozen, healthy, organic baby food versus $99/$1.25 for jarred food.  Once you compare, you will never want to feed your baby jarred food again.  Also, Yummy Spoonfuls is flexible and willing to work with their customers.  When I place an order for a variety pack, I send them an email with the flavors that I want...so you don't have to go with the flavors that typically come in the variety pack (you have to choose at least 3 of the same flavor).  Bottomline, I highly recommend this product.

column9: Best Organic baby food in the market.. So vibrant in color and yummy
column10: I did another review with the peas, yes we are buying every and any flavors they offered in the stage one since this is the only brand my baby would eat.. Now that I have taken the time to read up on this amazing company, I am no longer surprised that their meals taste this good, just found out that they where actually voted as best organic baby food, also been given an award as most nutritious baby food, named most healthy on the go meals and lots more, look them up and try some, you and your baby will be very happy.. I could not believe how thick the purees are, I had to add a bit of water in the sweet potato before feeding my daughter Adrianne.. I made all the food for my oldest son and I can honestly say this taste by far better than anything I ever made.. I only wish they are in a store around me...I recommend this brand to every mom

column9: Yummy spoonfuls is the best thing I could have done for my son and our family
column10: Yummy spoonfuls made all the difference in my and my son's experiences in getting him to eat healthy, organic solid foods as well as a variety of foods.  There is no other product on the market that compares.  These products are the freshest, most natural in color, "non-slimy" baby food to be found -  I really hesitate to categorize them as baby food.  They are so far above they are truly just food that can be consumed and used by any age group.  My son took to all of them from the start.  He is now a bit over 2 years and I still use them in combinations or as a base for my food bowls, "sloppy joe's" and bread spreads where I can add other chunky ingredients - vegetables, meats, fish, etc.  It makes all the difference for any mother - working or stay at home - to be able to provide straight from the container meals without guilt or add to them when time permits.  Yummy spoonfuls is the best thing I could have done for my son and our family.Thank you Yummy Spoonfuls for an amazing product..

column9: BEST TASTING BABY FOOD FOR AN ADULT !!!!!!!!!!
column10: Due to some health complications my system is getting re-wired, doctors have me on baby food. Like a baby I am too start with single ingredient purees to easily identify any reactions. The past two weeks has been hell. Had forgotten just how horrible baby food was.. Just couldn't get myself go past the offensive stale odor that burst out upon opening the pouch.. A nurse at the hospital told me to try the frozen baby food option.. I picked Yummy Spoonfuls because it was one of the few that had a good variety of the single meals and boy am I glad I did! Here is what I have tried so far..The apple sauce: Never tasted apple sauce like this before.. it taste so light, clean and refreshing.. it taste like I took a bite directly from an apple only I didn't have to chew.The Peas: The color of the peas is so vibrantly green you can tell it wasn't over cooked...it gave me the courage to dig in and I love it.. taste just like steamed peas.Sweet potato: so cream, thick and sweet.Butternut squash.. Taste amazingly light....has never been my favorite food but I am loving it...Thank you for making such an amazing product... I am on baby food for the next 6 months.. I still cannot believe it is baby food.... You guys have completely changed my perception about baby food.. it is not all baby food that taste bad.. Thanks again for helping me during this difficult time in my life.. Please send flyers with my next order....I will pass them out at the hospital...From an adult taste bud point of view, this is impeccable. It is no surprise that babies across the country love this food.

My baby loves this product. I bought yummy spoonfuls to give it a try and was not disappointed. I would highly recommend if you are looking for a great organic baby food that is taste great and whose service is hands down first class.

After reading some of the reviews, I was leary to purchase this cocoa for our fabulous Keurig coffee maker, but had to try it out for ourselves.  At first the cocoa did stick in the cup somewhat but a simple solution is to shake the cocoa cup before placing it in the machine and voila....none left in the little cup.  We love it !!!  On amazon at present buying more.

column9: Yummy and easy cocoa on the go!
column10: I got a box of this cocoa along with my keurig i bought at a local warehouse store. If youve got curious kids, like mine-they were wanting to try out the machine as well. I am so glad they included this box of cocoa. Very nicely made-even with water is certainly drinkable. We went through the box in no time, and are planning a re-order.I would recommend you run the keurig through empty once before having a cocoa. My first one tasted coffee-ish.

I thought it was great that there was hot cocoa for the keurig machine.  this is so watery when you make it.  green mountain needs to improve it.  it tastes like chocolate flavored water.  if you make a product that is intended for the machine it should work well in the machine.  i love all of the k-cup coffees but this cocoa sucks.

column9: Weak unless you excavate the rest of the cocoa out
column10: The output of Green Mountain Cocoa K-cups is highly variable - sometimes it's a well-flavored cup of cocoa, sometimes it's just brown water.This is because sometimes, a significant amount of the cocoa powder stays behind in the cup after the brew cycle. To really get a consistent product, you have to pierce the foil top to see if there is stuff left behind; scoop it out and stir it in, and you get the well-flavored cocoa some reviewers are raving about.This, however, is ludicrous - it defeats the fire-and-forget interaction that makes the Keurig worth it.The only thing that saves the product from a 1-star review is that its quick sugar hit has prevented many an afternoon nap at work. :D
Yes, it is easy, but not good at all. Hot water with little chocolate flavor---Swiss Miss is way better!

column9: I won't be purchasing this again
column10: The chocolate flavor is weak.  What you need to do is use the smallest cup size, then after it is done take out the cup, open the lid of the K cup and scoop out the rest of the powder.  It's drinkable, but barely.Worse then the extra fuss of mixing the powder yourself, is the flavor.  There is a VERY DISTINCT plastic aftertaste.  I thought maybe the water was just so hot it melted the cup, but the plastic cups are made of seem to be the same as the coffee ones which do not have this aftertaste. I think the chocolate is just not a good flavor.  Next time I'm going to try ordering a different brand.

Now first let me start off by saying I am not a big chocolate fan. That being, the taste I percieve as being "great" may be different from yours. If your looking for that rich chocolate flavor then this beverage may not be what your looking for. This is by no means "chocolate flavored water." Its got flavor (as long as you stay with the first two size settings) and is so easy to make why bother with anything else. The bottom line: If your looking for a cup of hot chocolate with a powerful chocolate flavor, these k cups are not for you. If you are looking for a cup of hot chocolate with a moderate amount of flavor then give these a try.When trying these k-cups I did not add anything else before serving (ex: marshmellows) I hope you enjoy and dont let the low review scores point you away from enjoying the easiest cup of hot chocolate you have ever had.
All I can say is this is the weakest brew I've ever had out of a coffee machine. The flavoring is also blatantly artificial. It's convenient but it's not good.

We got a new K-Cup machine and were very excited to try the hot chocolate.  It was not good at all; it was like drinking hot water with a very, VERY slight taste of some sort...possibly chocolate.  I would not purchase this item again.

I purchased this package of hot chocolate for my  parents to go with their new coffee maker. This way, grandchildren could enjoy the machine too. But the chocolate (about $.65 a cup) tastes funny and  will not be appealing to the kids.

I have to laugh at those who give this hot cocoa a poor review. If they would only read the directions it is stated clearly that you have to shake up the k-cup before brewing. Just for kicks I tried the cocoa both ways--first shaking it and getting the best cup of hot cocoa ever, and the 2nd time not shaking it up and getting brown water as some have described here. So the moral of this story is READ THE DIRECTIONS and shake up the k-cup before you brew your hot cocoa! Seems simple enough.... :D

I was keeping an open mind when trying the hot chocolate as I had read many of the reviews. The ones that expressed dissatisfaction were right on. Felt it was extremely watery and tasteless and that was using the smallest cup setting. I would suggest using the machine just to heat the water and use a packet of hot chocolate (Swiss Miss, etc.)
Received this product with the Keurig. Made it with the  small cup setting.Tasted like chocolate flavored water. I'll go back to  Swiss Miss and add the water

The first two or three K-cup cocoa cups I brewed were pretty wretched, even when I shook the cup heavily before using and used the smallest brew size. Then I decided to put a little mik in a mug (an ounce or so), open the K-cup and empty its contents into the mug, then brew hot water only, using the intermediate brew size, directly into the mug.  The resulting cocoa was very good and the extra step of emptying the K-cup was no work at all.I'm not sure I really needed the extra milk, but I like milky cocoa so I added it.I'll be curious to see if this hint helps anyone else.PS  I still prefer the taste of  the powdered cocoa packets (Ghirardelli) that came as a sample with my brewer (or similar ones from Bellagio), but the K-cups are convenient, too
Don't waste your money on this. It's awful.  Stick with making a cup of hot water from the Keurig and adding a good quality package of hot chocolate.

I too got the sample pack included with my new machine.  At first I was disappointed by how watered down the cocoa was but then realized much of it was left in the K cup.  As someone previously suggested, this is taken care of by just simply shaking the K cup before putting it in the machine.  That's it.  (thanks for sharing!) The best part is Green Mtn is the only one I've found that doesn't have "Hydrogenated Oil" as the lead ingredient.  Just for that alone they earn an extra star!

column9: Not what I was hoping for
column10: I had high hopes for this product. I don't drink coffee a lot, so I was excited to find a K cup that I could enjoy on a regular basis. Unfortunately, this product comes out too diluted even when I use the small cup setting on my machine. It tastes very watery, and is not thick and rich as I had hoped. I will finish the box, but I will not be purchasing this product again.

column9: Good Cocoa, but not really meant for a K-Cup
column10: This is good cocoa, but you'd almost have better luck just opening the K-cup and stirring it in. I have found that if I make it as per the box directions, I'll have about 1/4 of the cocoa still inside the cup.Also, you do not want to do this on the large cup size - it will be so diluted that will not want to drink it. I make it using the middle sized cup and use 2 k-cups.I got this on sale for $7, so it wasn't too bad of a price, but I think in the future I will just stick to buying a container of hot cocoa.

column9: 10x the cost of Swiss Miss packets for an inferior product and no real convenience factor!
column10: Let me start this review by saying that I ***LOVE*** my Keurig machine! I can get a great cup of coffee, any strength, any brew, any boldness, any flavor, without brewing up a whole pot. It is a brilliant concept for coffee, which has always lent itself to either mass-brewing or pathetic "instant-coffee".Tea and cocoa, however, typically cost anywhere from $1-$4 per box of 20-30 bags/packets. Tea and cocoa are inherantly single-shot items to begin with, so the idea of paying $10-14 for a box of 24 tea or cocoa K-cups is ludicrous. It offers no real extra convenience and costs about ten times the price. It would be like buying a Kia Rio for $8,000 or a Daewoo Leganza for $80,000... they are both basically the same car, so why pay ten times more for one? It just makes no sense.On a side note, I also have found that this cocoa is a bit watery at times and doesn't even hold up to a packet of Swiss Miss and some hot water.

I love my Keurig and I was ecstatic about the hot cocoa option. My Keurig came with this flavor as part of the variety pack, and I have to say, it was probably the worst hot cocoa I have ever had. Hardly any taste. Pretty much tasted like very watered-down hot chocolate.The only question I have now is whether there are other brands that make a good Keurig hot cocoa, or if the concept of hot cocoa in a k-cup is one that just doesn't work.
In my opinion this cocoa is pretty blah.  Weak, with a really awful after taste.
We've used this product for several months but recently discovered a superior product- it's Tully's Bellaccino Hot Cocoa, which has a much richer cocoa flavor.
Terrific cocoa.  Really satisfied my sweet tooth and makes a great cup of hot chocolate
Like using a teaspoon of chocolate in a Big Gulp...even on the small cup setting.

The Green Mountain Hot Cocoa K-Cups I received with my new Keurig machine have a dreadful off-flavor.  I'm wondering if there is something wrong with this batch, as I see some others rated this product highly.  Regardless, I certainly won't be buying this product again!
I love the convenience of the k-cups, but this cocoa is so weak, even on the 5 oz setting, don't waste your $ on this one.

We have the k-machine at work and the hot cocoa cups were greatly anticipated. The flavor is definitely lacking though. In fact it has a rather plastic aftertaste that is unpleasant. I have started bringing my own hot cocoa mix to work because of it.Meh.

Enjoyed it very much.  One thing is you have to have the Keurig set for the tea cup size to get the full flavor. The middle setting, 7.25oz, is not as strong tasting.  Some here didn't seem to mind and preferred to have the bigger cup. I would put some marshmallows in the bottom of of the cup and push brew, and you have a nice cup of hot chocolate with a creamy marshmallow layer on top.

column9: Tastes fine but the shipping kills the deal
column10: The shipping cost on this product doubles the price which makes it more expensive than elsewhere.

I have been a Keurig owner for 5 years, but just recently became interested in Hot Cocoa after giving up coffee.  My order arrived yesterday, and last night my son and I tried it.....MOST EXCELLENT!  What I got was a rich, and delicious Hot Cocoa that really relaxed me before bed, and I slept like a baby.  I have not yet tried any of the others, but am ordering a LOT more of this one!

column9: Bitter Taste in Mouth Isn't Just Flavor
column10: Similar to my review of the B30 from which I tasted this garbage. Once the hot chocolate is brewed it is bland, bland, bland. Why? Because if you look in the used k-cup, there's the rest of it sitting in the bottom of the cup! Brainless. Better that it's NOT in your cup because of the ARTIFICIAL SWEETENER that is NOT LISTED on the package gives it the tell-tale metallic taste. That's inexcusable, they need to label their products has having an artificial sweetener and artificial flavor, ugh. In addition, it's a trash creating machine, all those k-cups in landfills. Shame.Stay away.
You have to use two of these cocoa's.  One you have to open and put in the cup while using another in the machine.  This cocoa is very weak in taste and texture.
Most water-based hot chocolates are a bit anemic on flavor.  This isn't true with these K-cups.  The chocolate is rich and not watery and it's perfect after coming in from the cold outdoors.

Even though convenient, the "Hot Cocoa" really isn't exactly what is says.  It is more like drinking colored water.  It really was so bad, that my partner tore open the cups and placed the powder in milk.  It took 2 k-cups to make one 10 ounce cup of cocoa.  It was okay then, but it's much easier to get some good ole` fashioned Hershey's chocolate and make a cup that I would just crave.  Besides, living close to Hershey, where the air constantly smells like milk chocolate, supports my local economy!

Prior to trying this we had been using the ghirardelli hot chocolate packets for the Keurig machine.  My kids hated this product.  It tasted like water on the 7.25oz setting on the B70 machine.  I also tried it using the 5oz setting and adding it to coffee.  It was pretty much tasteless. The K-cups may be more convenient but there is no comparison in taste.  My kids prefer the packets and so do I.

column9: Green Mountain Hot Cocoa K-Cups -- Woof!
column10: Firstly, as a rule I don't write bad reviews (nobody needs that kind of karma). But after trying this "cocoa" on 5/19/12 (and I see that a lot of reviews are much older) I thought I'd just warn those of us who might like real cocoa. The main issue is that it is physically impossible to contain sufficient mass of ingredients in a K-Cup to make hot chocolate. A decent cup of cocoa needs at least 3 tablespoons of a quality cocoa powder (such as Droste) to have any flavor at all in 240 ml of liquid (not to mention the other ingredients). While a relatively small mass of ground coffee can make an outstanding cup of brew (think Pike Place Roast), this product can't even stand up to a Swiss Miss (and, sorry, she's terrible--those of us who require a robust cup of cocoa need a real woman!). (That's a joke on the play on words--approved by my wife--a REAL woman so don't accuse me of un-PCness please...)And oh yeah, this stuff tastes salty as well. Otherwise it CAN be made into a HOT DRINK of some sort; just not a passable cup of cocoa....hey Sandra, are you busy? could you please come and take look at this? I'm not being too snide am I? Thanks honey!

column9: Tastes Weak with a plastic after taste
column10: I love hot chocolate so when my wife got a Keurig I had to try the hot chocolate. Boy was it awful. The chocolate taste was so weak I had to add a good scoop of Swiss Miss to make it drinkable. There was also a taste of plastic, I think the K-Cup gets so hot it actually melts the cup a little.

Is this hot chocolate....yesIs this good hot chocolate....um, sortaIs this gourmet hot chocolate....not a chance.In my opinion, the only advantage you get but using the Green Mountain K-cups of hot chocolate is the simplicity of using your Keurig machine to heat the water instead of using the microwave or stove-top. Other than that the finished product is comparable to any Swiss Miss or other brand of powdered instant cocoa. It actually may be worse if you use the largest setting on your machine. The largest setting makes it much too watery.Green Mountain needs to go back to the drawing board on this.3 stars because it does make hot chocolate in your Keurig without having to dirty dishes and tear open pouches, but if you're looking for good hot chocolate, keep shopping.

We just received our Green Mountain Hot Chocolate and at first it did taste a bit thin (I did shake the cup before using it), but I added some caramel & whipped cream and it was perfect. I am not a huge hot chocolate drinker but like an cup when it is cold out. I ended up liking it very much and would buy it again.

This is BY FAR the worst hot cocoa I have ever had.  I can't believe I paid this much money for this.  A .99 cent box of Swiss Miss is SOOO much better.  It doesn't even come close to working correctly on the machine.  DONT BUY THIS GREEN MOUNTAIN PRODUCT.

My daughter and I love this.I bought a Keurig personal machine for our house,and I also have  one at work I use. The trick to having this taste great is a few things:1-Its needs 1 teaspoon of sugar or sweetener added to it2-You cant use it with the larger oz setting,6 oz makes the best flavored drink (that isnt watery)3-shake the cup before you use it4-if you use the Keurig for coffee,run water through it without a KCup,to get rid of the coffee flavor if you dont like coffee.

While I love the taste of Green Mountain Hot Cocoa, the prices for these k-cups on Amazon are outrageous. I have seen this product advertised on other sites for almost half the price. I would shop around for a better price. It seems like the vendors on Amazon are ripping consumers off. I rated this product 2 stars because of the price. If I was rating for flavor alone, it would be 4 stars.

Really, better tasting than I expected! I prefer it stronger so I use the "tea" setting on my wonderful Keurig brewer. I noted that some people had reported problems with clogging when using this product; but I always remember to shake the K-cup (as recommemded) befor brewing, and have experience no such difficulties. I also try to run a cup of plain water after brewing my cocoa to prevent the possibility of cloggin when I brew my next beverage  - probably Tully's French Roast. Delicious, quick, and easy . . .who could ask for anything more? Enjoy!
While it costs much more than I would like, I keep buying as it is excellent!
I received the complete order in perfect condition in just a few days.  I've ordered them before with the same results, and will gladly order again.

column9: This Hot Cocoa is great! Shake well before brewing!
column10: I got myself a keurig Brewer this year and love it! I found the Green Mountain Hot Cocoa and tried it. It was a little watery...after the first experience, I started shaking the K-Cup before brewing my hot cocoa and I have not had one problem since! The flavor is great and it is not watery anymore. Remember vigerously shake the k-cup then put it in the Keurig brewer. I also make sure and don't have it set to the largest cup size.Try this and it will be great each time!

I was worried when I first tried the hot chocolate k-cup for my mini keurig, thought it would be watery.  I was pleased to find this was not so, but still felt it was lacking something.  I love chocolate, and if you do to try this, how about a mounds bar in a cup?  Simply add a dash of coffemate cocoanut creme, for an almond joy, add equal parts of coffemate amaretto and coconut cream, its heaven, fellow chocolate lovers!

Despite the generally weak reviews, I gave this a try because I love hot chocolate and the convenience of the Keurig. Unfortunately, I have to agree with most reviewers who gave this low marks. It is weak and watery and has more coconut oil than actual cocoa.
