I'd like both a coupon AND on sale, but for these, I might only require one; the dogs love them that much.
This candy is so delicious, with a strong apple flavor. Though be warned, it really is "high chew."But I think it's worth it!

column9: This is the best candy I have had in my life.
column10: I've tried almost every flavor by now. The three best are green apple, strawberry, and grape. This pack of 20 will last you a long time so share some with friends; or don't because they will come back asking you for more.
THESE CANDYS ARE DELICIOUS!!! 20 Packs with 10 candies in them each = 200 Hi-Chews! I already ate half of them and it's been like a week. I'm going to have to order more of these soon.
This candy is like Starbursts on steroids.  The flavor is amazing so if you like Starbursts you will love Hi-Chews.

column9: Worth the Price for High Quality

Best for special occasions like going to the movies or would make a great small gift with a gift card in my opinion.In the end it is about quality. I am probably going to try melon next.

column9: Fantastic flavor, great texture; very addictive candy!
column10: The first thing you'll notice when you start chewing a piece of Hi-Chew is the interesting texture; sort of a combination of a gum, a taffy, and chewable wax, but definitely not like anything you've ever chewed before. Next you'll begin to appreciate the tangy green apple flavor that actually gets stronger as you chew.If you're like me, you will NOT be able to stop after one or two pieces, that's why it's so cool that you can buy 20 packs at a time for such a great price here on Amazon. my little dog loves these and I don't mind giving them to her as they don't havea bunch of junk in them.

column9: Dog loves them, but I hate the smell
column10: I have a 70 pound lab mix, and he goes nuts for these treats. He'll devour one in less than 5 minutes, but it's awesome to see him so happy. column9: Good, but try the Extra Fresh flavor
column10: My two maltese really like these treats. I like the Extra Fresh flavor much better. Both of my dogs have really bad dental issues- I brush them every day but I also give them a dental bone every day. The Nutri Dents have gone in their regular rotation. My dogs are pretty small- Romeo is about 11 pounds and Juliet is roughly 9 pounds. They used to be given these mini ones, but because they are pretty aggressive chewers- I now give them the medium version after some trial and error, as these mini ones were devoured too quickly. These treats aren't super soft- but they are relatively soft when compared to other, harder dental treats we have tried. These have a really similar texture to the Greenies brand, but we like these ones much better than the Greenies. These treats smell pretty gross to me, but my pups love them. I like the smell of the Extra Fresh ones- they really smell like parsley and eucalyptus oil, which both can be found on the ingredient list of that flavor. I like that these are gluten free. I like that they have added vitamins and omegas. These ones are okay nutritionally for a treat, and the chewing action is always a good thing, but I like that the other flavor has actual ingredients that are good for dental health. Most importantly, my dogs love the taste of both of the treats. I buy these ones rarely, as I much prefer the other flavor, but these are still good treats. The only negatives I have are that these are really pricey, and they are devoured quite quickly, even by my dogs who are 12 years old and missing nearly half of their teeth. They are still much better than many other treat brands out there and I do recommend them.
My maltipoo goes craaaazyyyy whith these treats! she doenst eat a lot, but she'll beg for these! Her teeth are very clean too! Ive purchased these treat 3 times now and I will keep purchasing them!
My Yorkie had very bad breath and since I have been giving him one of these every morning, his breath has improved so much that I don't mind his kisses on my face anymore.

Luckily, my 4 month old shephard got one before her sister ate the batch!)  I save about $5 ordering the bones on Amazon.

It doesn't matter if I even try to mold it back to it's normal "bottle" form with my hands. Useless! So you have to drink it all in one sitting so that you may recycle the bottle right away. Otherwise, your left with a deformed bottle you have to lay down flat in the fridge. Which ends up taking more space and it looks ridiculous.

I bought this at a local Wal-Mart, and I'm not sure if it's just the batch I've gotten, but it tastes completely disgusting. It tastes like chemicals from the plastic bottle leaked into the water! I usually get the generic Great Value bottled water, and they taste 100x better! I have to hold my nose to drink this water because I almost threw up from the aftertaste. You know what? I'd rather drink tap water since this water isn't any better than it, and tastes a lot worse! I will never buy Aquafina water again unless my life depends on it.

Aquafina is not just any bottled water. When tried it, I wondered why it tasted better.I found out when I learned more about Aquafina.It goes through a seven-step purification process, which includes ozonation and reverse osmosis, which "uses semi-permeable membranes with smaller pore sizes than microfiltration, ultrafiltration and nanofiltration to remove unwanted substances in the water, like sodium and chloride."The other steps remove most TDS (total dissolved solids) from the water. Aquafina's average TDS is 4, which is 2.5 times lower than the FDA standard.The result is a more delicious tasting water.I find that with this water, I drink more water, because it tastes better to me. Because I drink more of it, I'm getting more health benefits.Other bottled waters do some steps, but Aquafina does seven purification steps. The result is a better tasting water.I haven't found a better tasting one yet. If I do, I'll switch, but for now, I am satisfied.

No matter how I have tried to squash the bottle flat on a table, it will fall over. It's frustrating and annoying. I will never buy Aquafina again. I use lots and lots of mushrooms and not only are these very tasty, they are much more economical than buying them in a local supermarket.

I was along on a camping trip with my sons scout troop when someone brought along a half dozen or so of this vegetable blend.  It was very convenient since it required no refrigeration, plus it was surprisingly flavorful for a dry blend when made into a soup or stew.  Unfortunately I have to go along with the other reviewer here when he calls it a major rip off.  Even for an average size soup that is about 2 quarts, two bags of this 4 oz size would be needed.  That makes it far more expensive than it is worth when you can add canned vegetables at 10 oz. (minus the water) for about a dollar a shot. At the same time I cannot honestly put down all of the Barry Farm products, thus the extra star I added.  I have bought and used several other dry products from Barry Farms including their bouillon and powdered eggs and have been very satisfied with them, both price and product wise. Unfortunately as for this particular veggie blend, I cannot recommend it despite its fairly decent taste.  Way too expensive. Even if bought at a case at a time...
Having bought dried veggies at my food co-op, this is the same price! Dried veggies are expensive everywhere and not easy to find.
If you're the type of person that likes to be mugged or have your purse stolen, then go ahead and buy from these people. OUTRAGEOUSLY Expensive for what you get.

There are some days that I just need a pic me up. That's usually when I turn to something chocolatey, usually in the form of a cookie or cupcake. I signed up for the Cookie Athlete "Cookie of the Month club".I have loved getting gourmet cookies shipped right to my front door. I live in a small town, and I don't like store bought cookies. I know cookies, and when they are gross, they aren't worth the calories, but all in all I have been impressed with the cookies I have received (I'm on month 3 now!). I did count my cookies....I got between 1 dozen up to 15 cookies per box so far, but they have been worth every penny!To be honest, I've been thinking that this might be a fun gift to give all my girlfriends for Christmas! They are so hard to buy for....who doesn't love cookies?

column4: ChibiNeko "Sooo many books, so little time!"
column10: As a former soda junkie, I've been looking for different beverages to replace my beloved Pepsis & Mountain Dews. A friend of mine practically lives on Crystal Light & recommended that I check it out. I'm officially a big fan & convert!The Skin Essentials brand of CL boasts that it will help improve your skin as well as taste good. It is still 5 calories (which is the usual amount for CL mixes) & contains some new plant extracts which are supposedly good for your skin. While it still has a bit of vitamins in it, it doesn't have as many as some of their other lines do. (Presumably so they can fit those skin improving elements in!) This shouldn't bother anyone unless they are specifically drinking CL in order to get their daily vitamins. (If you're only getting your vitamins from CL then there's something wrong with that picture!) This drink has no caffeine, so if you are abstaining this is a good one to have. If you need caffeine, well... there's still several other CL drinks to have.Now onto what you really want to know: does it taste good & does it work? Taste wise, it's fantastic. I'm a big fan of tea but not caffeine, so this works out really well for me. The peach element is very good but not overpowering. It's a bit sweet, so people who don't like overly sweet things may want to stick to the pomegranate lemonade skin essentials. I'd still give it a try. I was a bit skeptical about whether I'd like it or not, but ended up adoring it. As for whether or not it works skin-wise, I can't honestly give a real answer yet. I've only been drinking it for about a week or so, off & on. I can say that I've noticed my skin getting silkier & a bit softer, which is enough for me to keep drinking it! (Well, I'd keep drinking it for the taste as well!)Now for price. Getting it from amazon... maybe not such a good idea if you are looking for value. You could honestly find it cheaper at your local grocer's. HOWEVER, if you are in an area where there's not a good selection of CL or far from a proper grocer's, it may be more convenient to order online & have it shipped to you. Then again, it could end up that even if you do live next to a well stocked grocers, ordering from amazon could still be more convenient to your work & life schedule.
I don't usually like things flavored with Peach but this was really good! The peach gives a nice sweetness to the tea so neither is over powering. I have no idea if it does anything for skin though.

This is so good. I don't ever want to be without.  I carry a metal water bottle, often empty.  Where ever I go I can find water. For pennies a drink, I can have the best iced tea.  Great for the environment and makes me really happy.

I'VE BEEN DRINKING THIS MIX SINCE IT FIRST CAME OUT. PREVENTION MAGAZINE RATED IT THE BEST ON THE MARKET FOR ANTIOXIDENTS! I ALWAYS LIKED THAT IT WAS SO GOOD FOR ME AND TASTED GREAT. I CAN'T FIND IT IN STORES NOW SO THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE I CAN GET IT.

I drink alot of Crystal Light and this is one of my favorite flavors!  It is a nice change from regular iced tea taste.  It is slightly sweet but it is very quenching.  I hope they do not stop making this flavor.

column9: Why can't I buy this locally?
column10: We found this flavor of tea in our local store, bought it and loved it.  Then we could never find it again.  Researching it on the 'net, we found that "it is not available in your area".  Why not?  We bought a whole lot of it from Amazon and hope that when it runs out, we can get more.  Yes, it's that good.

column9: Love crystal light, HATE this flavor
column10: I normally love white tea, and peach, and LOVE crystal light packets, so I though, "wow, that's a great deal, I will give these a try!" Wrong! These were so gross, it may just be me, but the flavor was horrid! Stick with pom. cherry!

I drink only green tea with the white peach tea mixed in.  I have lost 165 lbs and this was a welcomed part of my routine.  I am happy to say the Crystal Light Skin Essentials, White Peach Tea is and absolute AWESOME product.

I love the Crystal Light Skin Essentials white peach flavor.  It's much lighter tasting than the regular peach flavored crystal light or other similar drink mixes.  I find it refreshing and satisfying.  Even better, I can carry a few packets with me wherever I go and always have access to a drink I'll really enjoy.  Even better, since it's so hard to find in stores, I can just order from Amazon and have it on stock in 2 fast and easy days.
I CAN'T GET ENOUGH OF THIS DRINK AND IT DOES REALLY GOOD THINGS FOR YOUR SKIN..

column9: As GREAT and the other 5 star ones!!!!
column10: It doesn't lose to "Zico" or the other one that I also gave 5 stars! Great taste!!!! And cheaper than Zico!

My wife loves Perrier and the lemon/lime especially.  Unfortunately, the only place that carries it near us is a local convenience store and singles at that.  This costs a little more per bottle but it is totally worth it to pay more for being able to get 24 at one time.  The product arrived protected by cardboard and completely intact. okay my husband loves this stuff but I'm not a sparkling water kinDa gal however just wanted to say that we received 24 16.9 oz bottles of lemon lime sparkling soda which wasnt what i was expecting but my hubby loves them nonetheless. column9: Taste is excellent and the price was right
column10: Sunflower oil. During a recent trip to Europe I had the opportunity to be blown away and not by the amazing architecture! When I ordered French fries (or chips, maybe), I was met with a light, unique flavor. And it wasn't just the fries that I was enjoying. After inquiring to my fiance, a European, as to the taste, she told me they cook nearly everything in sunflower oil. How have I gone so long without ever having the opportunity to enjoy sunflower oil? It seems it is the corn industry of Europe, so sunflower oil is "cheap" in Europe like corn oil is cheap here in the US.The other issue is that sunflower oil in the US, when and if you can find it, is super expensive. Sure, the Zvijezda oil isn't cheap even after shipping, it was still cheaper than the $5 for 16 oz I can find in stores, so I jumped on this.I assume the marketplace seller didn't have anymore of the 3L bottles and instead shipped 3- 1 liter bottles instead, which was just fine with me as it takes up just about the same amount of space in the cupboard.Sunflower oil has a lighter taste than corn oil but still definable. Sunflower oil also has a similar smoke point as corn oil, which means you can use it at a higher temperatures (especially for deep frying). Over all, I am quite pleased with this oil. It isn't the highest grade, but if you are using it for cooking over cosmetic use (go for higher grade for something like that!), this is a heck of a deal and a great replacement or compliment next to your corn and olive oil (if you want oil to flavor something, best to use olive).

I had read on Dr Oz website that Sunflower oil helps fight belly fat. So I got this as an alternative to other cooking oils that we have been using. I have even used this to replace the olive oil normally used in pizza dough. It makes the texture of the dough fantastic and so easy to handle. I love this product and will buy again and would certainly recommend to friends and family and other users of Amazon. Side Note: There is not a real difference in flavor between this and other oils that I have seen or tasted and this one is better for you. The only time I use any other oils is when I am low on this one and/or I need the strong flavor from olive oil for Italian dishes.
This is a wonderful oil.  I am not able to get Sunflower oil anywhere locally unless I want to pay a huge price for a small quantity.  Even with the cost of shipping, I would purchase this again.

This soup is good stuff - that is, if you don't have a soy allergy.  Unfortunately, the ingredients list here on Amazon is incomplete - it neglects to list the soybean oil that's in there.  I bought a whole case of these and now I can't even eat the stuff.  :(

column9: YOU CAN ALWAYS COUNT ON LIPTON!
column10: This product is wonderful and there were no problems. This was so nice to have on hand for those "unexpected" parties and gatherings. I was able to whip up a quick dip & just grab a bag of chips and bring to the party. There are so many uses for this product. I used in dips, soups, stews, gravy/sauce, rice pilaf, etc.  Sure comes in handy for that extra flavor!  Just perfect!

I like salt and use a lot of it, but it's a condiment we can easily add ourselves to taste; and should not be in a flavor mix. I have used this mix in soups and rubbed a beef roast with it before slow cooking and it's great except for too much salt.

Then I thought I would try good old Amazon!!! I like mixing this with half sour cream and half cottage cheese...makes a good dip for pretzels...

A cooking-challenged bachelor's best friend for tasty, healthy meals and snacks.

Fantastic.

I was SO glad to find this on Amazon. I had been looking for it in the store for a long time. It absolutely makes the best cheeseball. The alternatives were better than nothing but this makes it delish!
I love the spinach dip recipe featured on the box. I make a lot of it during the holidays, it goes fast. I stock up when I find it on sale locally, it is cheaper than on here.

These crackers are delicious & the flavors are subtle, not overpowering.

column9: excellent cracker, but doesn't survive shipping
column10: I first ran into this cracker at AJ's Fine Foods (a local grocery).  These crackers taste great and have a generous amount of Rosemary on each cracker (when it hasn't fallen off the cracker).I recently ordered a pack of 6 boxes from Amazon and found the same problem that most of the boxes in the local grocery had.Each box *should* have several large crackers the size of the box.  But the large crackers don't seem to survive shipping/handling either from Amazon or to the local grocery and so what is in the boxes are lots of cracker pieces ranging from 1/2 cracker size to pieces the size of a quarter. column9: Really close to the real thing
column10: I really enjoy this bread. The three children under the age of 10 also enjoy it. I change the recipie a little by adding in finely milled flax seed into it. the only issue i have with it is that it tends to overflow in some Bread maker machines. Other than that I LOVE IT.

column9: Best mix for white GF bread
column10: When my son was first diagnosed, I tried making GF bread from scratch. I spend copious amounts of time and money on a variety of flours. When I found this mix, it was like a gift from God. I've since tried several other mixes, but none turned out as consistent a product as this mix. I do make some tweaks, however. I add a packet of unflavored gelatin (increases the protein content and helps with texture) and a teaspoon of xanthan gum. Often I will use my own yeast, just to make sure it's fresh. With these tweaks, I can easily make very good bread--without a bread maker (I have one, but I get much better results without it). I do find that I have to double the cooking time, but that could be from our area's temp and humidity and our oven.I've occasionally tried some variations, such as raisin and cinnamon, poppyseed, etc., with varying results. Overall, however, this is so much better than the awful pre-made, mass-produced shelf-stable breads, better than other mixes, and as good as many of the local freshly-baked GF breads that sell for eight dollars a loaf in our area. My son still likes his frozen bread for some sandwiches, but otherwise we often make this.Amazon's subscription-price is competitive, so we'll move to that!Updated to add that I no longer add xanthan gum to the mix, and the results are just as good.  With better proofing, my cooking time is only a little longer than what is listed on the box. Try cooling the loaf in the oven, with the temp turned off and the door opened a little bit.

Gluten-Free Pantry Favorite Sandwich Bread.The title says it all. It is my hubby's favorite - GF, MSG & related products free, aspartate free, easy to make, stays together, and tastes great - much like potato bread only a little heavier. Yes, I know Amazon just raised to about $3.91/box + free shipping on the subscription plan. It makes a large 2 lb. loaf which I cut into two 1-lb. loaves before slicing which makes it $1.96/1-lb. loaf. If you look at the price of a decent white bread in the stores, the actual price is not too bad, considering it is a GF product. I look for not only GF and great taste, but affordablility.The only difficulty I have had is that it doesn't keep more than a week at best at room remp or in the frig, so I put 2 slices in sandwhich bags, then put the sandwhich bags in a freezer bag and pull out just what I need to use at the time.

I'm wheat intolerant and this is the best bread we've tried.my wife likes it so much she often bakes it for herself as well. we like to add potato flakes, parsley and olive oil to make it even better.eating it warm with butter on it is oh so good!

This is by far the best GF sandwich bread I've tried yet, Whole Foods makes a good one as well but for the price GF Pantry is much better.  It actually tasted like white bread.  It was moist and fluffy.  Cut it thin because it is really filling.PS Pamelas GF bread mix was strange, very dense and tasted like bisquits, and Bobs Red Mill stinks of Garbanzo bean flour

I am recently gluten-free, and first tried Bob's Red Mill Mix (it was o.k.) This was MUCH better!  It doesn't have a really strong "GF" flavor, so I don't have to load it with toppings to cover it up. It is drier on the inside than Bob's--not the gummy texture. The edges toast up really nicely! column9: Best gluten free bread mix ever!
column10: The Gluten-Free Pantry Favorite Sandwich Bread Mix, 22-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)I have found this to be the best gluten-free bread mix there is available.  You do not need a bread machine.  Works great and is quite easy to use your oven.  My husband even loves to eat it when it is hot right out of the oven!
This mix is great, I never had a bad loaf of bread using it and it taste good. Compared to the frozen bread you buy at health food stores this beats it hands down. very quick and easy.

We use this mix when I'm strapped for time. It's quick and easy and is our favorite alternative to my own recipe. I add 1/4 cup of sweet dairy whey which adds to the taste and texture! My entire family likes this bread, even my picky hubby! It makes a great sandwich, perfect french toast and UNBELIEVABLE grilled cheese!

This bread has a good taste and texture. It is simple to make in the bread machine. I have found, however, that in my particular bread machine it does not do well on the gluten free setting. I have had much better luck using the traditional settings that take longer. On the GF setting it ends up too doughy. It is good for a couple of days after baking. I always have some of this on hand for when I am feeling too lazy to make homemade bread.

column9: Not MY Favorite Sandwich Bread, but it is good
column10: I can understand why so many people love this sandwich bread. Especially when compared to pre-made frozen loafs of gluten free bread, this is especially good. It compares very favorably to "real" sandwich bread.So why the 4-star review? No single reason was worthy of removing a whole star from my rating, but taken all together, there were several things that left me less than excited about the bread. The main issue is that although the bread has a wonderful texture, is soft, moist, and chewy, it was too moist to make decent grilled cheese. The grilled cheese lacked the necessary structural integrity to hold together while flipping over and we had some difficulty with that. In my household, this is a big deal. Grilled cheese is my husband's favorite dinner, and he's pleased as punch that we can have grilled cheese again, but was very clear that this was not the best gluten free grilled cheese he's had. He's not gluten free himself so his standards are pretty high, I'll grant you that.Additionally, the PBJ test wasn't ideal. The bread had all the qualities I would have expected would make a delightful PBJ, but the peanut butter and the jelly seemed to get lost in the bread. The bread is a little "wiggly" too, which made the slices hard to keep from tearing apart when handling. cutting the sandwich in half helps.I also tested different storage methods for this bread. It kept well on the counter, wrapped in plastic. It also did well frozen, and defrosts on the counter quite well. Storing in the refrigerator is not recommended, however. The moisture content of the bread is high enough that storing in the fridge leads to condensation inside the plastic, making for slimy, soggy bread. Not good. But who says you have to store it in the fridge?Making the bread was easy with a stand mixer. It took all of ten minutes to make the dough and get it into the pan. The dough isn't nearly as sticky as the dough from the French Bread mix, but the process is basically the same. It's got a relatively short bake time, as well, at 30 minutes. This makes it less time-consuming to make than many other mixes and recipes. I'm continuously pleased with the mixes that Gluten Free Pantry produces.So yes, overall this was a great loaf of bread. Not my favorite, and not the best for grilled cheese or PBJs, but I can definitely see why it's so popular, and if you're looking for a loaf of bread that's close to the "real deal," this will probably make you very happy.

Just made my very first gluten-free bread with my new breadmaker (BREADMAN PRO AUTOMATIC BREAD MAKER TR875 with gluten-free setting) and it's just so impressive! Moist, tasty, you can't even tell it's gluten free! I can only compare it to the store bought GF breads, and it's just in a league of it's own!

This is the best GF bread mix we have tried so far. The price here at amazon is the best I've ever seen.  I hope they keep the price low....as you know if you are shopping for GF products it can sure burn a hole in your wallet.
Love this bread mix and I've been using it for several years. In my option, it's the best gluten free bread mix on the market!

This Gluten-Free Pantry Sandwich Bread is very good.  I have made many loaves of their French Bread, but after trying the Sandwich Bread I actually think this one is more to my liking.  It's a little softer than the French Bread and more like "regular bread".  After baking, cooling, slicing and freezing the loaf (in 3 bags), I find it tastes better and holds together better if I toast it a little first before eating it.

This bread is fantastic.  The only gluten free bread my wife has found that she likes.  It is easy to prepare, although my method is to mix the dough in a bread machine and then bake it in a regular bread pan in the oven.

column9: Best gluten free bread mix ever!
column10: Do you miss having a good sandwich since you became gluten free? No more worries! Buy this, bake it, slice it to your heart's desire! It won't crumble like other GF bread. Make French toast, etc. too!  I sometimes make cinnamon raisin bread by adding spices, fruit and nuts. Heavenly!  I usually make it in my bread machine on a 3-hour basic bread cycle. It needs to be lightly stirred at first until it mixed. It's also very good when baked in the oven.  The mix is not lactose free but is tolerable for me. I have it on regular shipment!

I've never used a bread mix for a bread maker before, much less a gluten-free one. Since the bread maker wasn't the latest model (Toast Master 2 lb. 'Bread Box'), it had NO directions for gluten-free bread. I was worried about outcome. There are several "directions" for different types of bread. I started with and used the directions for 'white sandwich bread'. No problem. Everything worked great and I ended with a good tasting, nice textured loaf of bread. Very pleased with mix and outcome. It tasted better than the gluten-free loaf we bought!

This is the best GF bread mix I've used, although I didn't think so after the first time I baked it. It was under baked, very dense and heavy. After a few more tries I have a great recipe for a success: first I use more liquid (2 cups), add 4 tbsp ground flax seed and extend baking time to 40-42 minutes. I baked it in an electric oven and in gas and both do great job.

Fluffy, it isn't, but the loaf rises and keeps well, tastes 'fair-to-middling'. It makes quite a decent sandwich compared to any recipe I have tried in the past 11 years - and believe me, I have tried a LOT of recipes...  I just think it is  pretty pricey, not cheap, but cheaper than buying all those different GF flours, only to turn out a pathetic, crumbly & peculiar-tasting loaf.  So far, this is the best alternative I have found.
this really is great bread.  My husband the bread baker even liked it a lot.  Will be using this bread often.

This is one of the best gluten-free breads I have ever tasted.  It is far better than the ready-made breads in the store.  The one caveat is that you have to be careful if you are using a bread machine to bake this bread...each bread machine operates a little differently, even if you are baking to the instructions for gluten-free bread.  You might have to adjust the amount of yeast and/or water to get the bread to rise properly and to not over-flow the bread machine.  I don't think you will be disappointed.

I initially purchased this mix because the eggs were not included and it doesn't contain peanuts/tree nuts and is not processed in a facility that does. My 3 year old has nut and egg allergies and is gluten intolerant. I have made 3 loaves now and finally my 3rd attempt came out perfect. I used ENER G egg replacer for the 2 eggs required in the recipe. The first batch I made in a machine that did not have a gluten-free cycle. I used the quick cycle and the loaf came out ok, not great. The crust was very thick and hard an I had to cut it off to make it edible. The second batch I made in a machine with a gluten free cycle and the loaf was slightly underdone in the middle, so a little dense. I just made the third loaf with the gluten free cycle, I just extended the cycle by choosing a darker crust option. The results were a beautiful, fluffy, tender loaf that my 3 year ate with gusto. My search for sandwich bread is over! Now on to burger buns... =)
Get it at Drugstore.com for $7.00 The product is very good though. Tasty and keeps you gluten free. I would look around for better prices. Our local Sprouts carries it s well.
I love the product, and being able to get it at such a great price (30% discount) made the purchase even better!  I'll definitely be back.  And the delivery was convenient and quick!

column9: great product for a gluten free bread
column10: Both my son and i have celiac  disease and finding bread that was good was challenging.  we tried so many and this is the best one we found.

This is by far the best GF bread I've found.  SO EASY to bake, and relatively inexpensive, as GF breads go.  All you need is milk (or water), butter or oil, and eggs (or egg whites), and VOILA!  Delicious GF bread.

I'm not gluten free, but I have recently become wheat free and doing without bread has been a challenge. The premade stuff in the store is horrendous, so I thought I'd try making my own. After a couple of failed projects, I decided to try this mix. My bread machine is old and doesn't have a gluten free cycle, so I just used the regular large/light cycle and it seemed to work fine. It rose well and had a more pleasant aroma than other GF breads I've tried. The texture and taste are also much closer to the real thing than others, albeit a bit dense in comparison to wheat bread, but that's just a fact of life. And surprisingly, it is easier to slice than regular bread I've made. All in all, a more than acceptable substitute.

This is the closest thing I've found to regular bread. I find it simple to mix up and bake as well, which is even better! I warm the oven and pop it in there to rise, especially when it's cold out. It rises really nicely and then cooks up great. I have to cover mine partway through with foil to keep it from getting too dark on top. I have had trouble with it sticking to the pan when I go to get it out. My mother-in-law uses a double-walled pan (like the air bake cookie sheets, only in bread pan form I guess) and doesn't have any trouble with sticking, so I guess I'm going to have to try that! This gluten free bread mix is worth the time and money.

column9: Great Bread for our Celiac Family
column10: Our entire family of 5 really loves this bread and guests have as well.  It is holds up well for GF overnight french toast!  Add a little vanilla, pumpkin pie spice, and extra sugar to the recipe for a yummy treat.  For some reason the mix overflows my bread machine pan so I have to watch it and scoop some out while it's rising.  This never happened when I used to make gluten bread in the machine.

column9: nearly foolproof mix, low on flavor
column10: I've had great success with this mix in my zojirushi bread machine. Ithe mix comes with a premeasured packet of yeast to which you simply add milk or water, eggs, and oil or butter. I have made bread with milk and butter and also with water and oil. I don't notice much difference between types.the loaf produced rises well, bakes quickly and has a fantastic crust. I find the plain white recipe lacking slightly in flavor, but have done well adding Italian spices/garlic/onion powder twosome loaves, and cinnamon and sugar to others.All in all this is a perfect loaf of bread for my gluten free kids' lunches. I bake a loaf on Sunday night and we slice off of it all week. the texture is excellent and the bread hold up well, no toasting required.

Wow... I'm not gluten insensitive but my girlfriend has celiacs.  We recently got a bread maker and have tried a few packaged bread mixes.  I can honestly say that this is easily the best gf bread mix and is better than most whole wheat gluten breads or regular breads you purchase from the supermarket.  It has caused me to give up normal breads and join my girlfriend in her gluten-free diet.  Bob's is good too but (very spongey) but Gluten Free Pantry's sandwich bread has amazing flavor and that homemade bread texture.  The store bought gf breads aren't even close to being on the same level as this product. Simply great!

column9: Delicious!! Best bread mix out there.
column10: I've tried a few different bread mixes and recipes using gluten-free flour, and I think this mix is by far the best. No gluten-free bread tastes the same as bread made with wheat flour, but this bread is just as good. My bread machine doesn't have a gluten-free setting, so I used the Quick Bread setting and it came out perfect. The only thing I had to do was to scrape down the sides of the bread pan a couple of times during the process. Great texture and flavor. After eating this, I don't miss "real" bread at all!!

column9: The Best Gluten free bread - hands down!
column10: I have been making gluten free breads in my breadmaker for a couple of years now. Not much to it - very simple to follow and great results every time (get a breadmachine with gluten free setting if you want to use this mix). I love the flavor of this bread - not a strong taste at all, which is what you want if you want to make sandwiches. People who expect gluten free breads to taste like regular breads will always be disappointed - there is nothing that will be exactly the same as regular bread, but this one comes the closest, in my opinion. Almost all freshly made gluten free bread mixes will end up in a slightly spongy, damp bread. I always toast mine if I'm making sandwiches and it turns out fine. I don't toast it, however, if I'm eating it as a side with my meal (such as soup), and even my whole family who is not GF loves this bread! I used to be a devout Pamela's bread mix fan (which is also good), but after trying this one I have to say this is the winner hands down. Pamela's tastes fine, but doesn't slice as easily and has a flatter shaped bread -- not the most ideal if you're looking for sandwich bread.This bread also makes nice thicker slices if you're looking for dinner bread. I also use leftover bread for excellent french toast even if it's stale. Makes great stuffing cubes, too. I slice and freeze leftovers, take them out of the freezer and either toast them or leave them on the counter for 30-45 mins before serving and they are perfect. Smaller amounts of leftovers can be used for bread crumbs in recipes if you toast them first (can also be frozen).By the way, I happened to add sliced olives, grated parm cheese, and italian herbs to the liquid before adding the flour, and the bread had a wonderful flavor! Great for dipping in olive oil.

column9: Living gluten free for 4+ years - I love this bread.
column10: I had pretty much given up all hope of finding a good "normal" gluten free bread.  The only gluten free bread I had liked up to this point was some cinnamon raisin bread from Whole Food's frozen section.  But cinnamon raisin bread isn't too good for a turkey sandwich :)  That is where this bread comes in.  This is the first gluten free bread that I have tried that makes a sandwich something I look forward too again.

I have never had "gluten free" food.  I baked the sandwich bread for my brother, and oh my, it was good!!!  Hope he enjoys it!  I also bought gluten free flour....next thing to bake is a birthday cake!

column9: Tastes like real bread and very fluffy!
column10: Great bread mix, easy to use without the bread machine.  I prefer the "french" bread version, but this one is great too!

column9: My main stay for bead love it
column10: I tried a lot of breads but none measure up to this one.I am Gluten free amd I use this bread and even bake it in muffen rings and make H.B. buns that raise up and look and taste like regular H.B.Buns. Also Amazon with (sub.and save) and free siping is beter price than Wal-Mart.Try it and Enjoy.

If you don't have time to make your own bread mix... or haven't perfected the flour mix yet (and it is an art) then this it the next best thing! It tastes like "real" bread! I've fooled many a gluten eater with this bread. I love to throw it in the bread machine and come home to freshly made bread (or wake up to it)!I can't rave enough. Locally I pay 6-7 dollars a box, so this is great deal!

perfect for the bread maker and sooo quick! I have tried a dozen differnt recipies and thismakes up the best! dont even bother with making your own mix. I have a small bread maker so i use only half the mix each time and its wonderful, everytime. also i use egg white to make it more fluffy!

column9: I can have a sandwich and toast again.
column10: I love this bread.  I've missed the ease of just grabbing a sandwich or toast.  This bread tastes so good and turns out full and fluffy, like bread should be.  I recommend this mix.

column9: Wonderful gluten free bread mix from Amazon.com
column10: This bread mix makes a great loaf of gluten free bread. I have been on a gluten free diet for the past 7 years, and have tried most of the bread mixes, and found this product to be the tastiest.  The subscription order, which saves 15% on the cost, and arrives automatically on a regular basis, is just great. Thank you Gluten Free Pantry and Amazon.

column9: Finally--bread that comes out great in a machine!
column10: I found out I had a sensitivity to wheat so tried to find alternatives. After getting tired of soft corn tortillas for lunch every day, I decided to try this mix. I put it in my plain old Regal bread machine on the rapid cycle. (Mind you, it's very basic and doesn't have a gluten-free setting.) Wow! I couldn't believe how well it came out. I have made many breads in that machine but none have been better than this one. In fact, I rarely use the machine because the breads don't have the texture I want. This one was different. It was super moist and cut into beautiful even slices. Very good tasting, too, though I'll probably add a dash of stevia to the mix next time (since I like a tinge of sweetness). Even though I'm the one watching my wheat intake, my husband ate up half the loaf he liked it so much. The only drawback is the price, but I guess you can't complain when you get a pack of yeast along with it.
YES!! A bread I can eat!! It tastes great, awesome texture, stays together, it's real bread!! I love it. I am so excited to have found this!

Gluten Free Pantry's bread mix is the best I've tried (and I've tried many mixes, including some homemade ones myself).  It tastes great (maybe slightly too sweet), has perfect consistency for GF bread, and is fairly durable and not too crumbly.  All this combined makes it my "go-to" mix when I want bread.  And no, you don't have to microwave/toast it like you do with other GF breads--it's perfectly fine as-is, even after being taken out of the fridge.However, one thing that bothers me is: whenever I make it and take it out of the oven, it always seems to rise much higher on one side than the other, and winds up almost splitting in half sometimes on the side that's risen too much (in fact, that's exactly what happened to me the first time I tried it).  I'm using the correct size pan for it...it REALLY poofs up when you bake it.  Has anyone else experienced this issue?

I have been gluten free for a little over a year now and bread is the one thing I miss. I love this bread, tastes just like "real bread" should. I made this bread in the crock pot and I also made it in the oven. Both ways it turned out perfect!

As I type this, I am eating my first sandwich since going GF in Sept '10. I have tried every GF loaf on the market and tossed every one of them at first bite. My dad bought me a bread maker for Christmas and there is no specific "GF setting". There is a quick bread/cake setting which I used according to the package directions. I was so skeptical and just bought a box from the store to try before I paid for a case from Amazon. BUY IT HERE! Do Super Saver and buy it. That makes it about $3.50 a loaf, which isn't unheard of for better breads, and certainly cheaper than store-bought GF breads. Don't expect a light and fluffy texture. I hesitated to put it on the "regular" setting since the directions say use the quick setting. It's moist, denser, but holds together SO well! Don't crumble at all. I'm going to get a case and have it on hand!!
I've tried several other brands of Gluten Free Bread mixes, and I've always returned to Favorite Sandwich Bread mix.  It freezes well and toasts great.

column9: The BEST - tweaked for my GFCF daughter
column10: I have tried several other ready mixes for my bread machine, and this is hands down the best.  My 2 1/2 yo daughter was diagnosed PDD-NOS and we thought we'd give GFCF a try.  It's like a light bulb came "on" with the diet.Anyway, I made a few substitutions to meet our needs:  I use Almond Milk (instead of cow's milk or water) and a popular, vegan, organic buttery spread that is dairy free in place of butter.  Added a dollop of honey, and it is so yummy.  Even my husband thinks this is the most "real bread" tasting option we've had thus far.Now, if I could find an acceptable hazelnut spread substitute, I'd be golden!!!
Highly recommend this product.  Bread is one of the better gluten-free breads on the market, alongside making your own from scratch.

column9: The best all purpose gluten-free sandwich bread
column10: This always comes out tasting great. What I really wanted it for was to make french toast and it's great for that but it's just great out of the fridge.

column9: Gluten Free Pantry Bread Mix...Best By Far!!!
column10: I have tried several prepackaged Gluten Free Bread Mixes and this is by far the easiest and best tasting of them. I have a daughter with a Gluten allergy and we had hunted for a bread that wasn't like a brick or just awful and crumble apart. This is the one. It is still "gluten free" so its not like Wonder Bread, but it is edible for certain.
My husband has Celiac Disease and finding a good sandwich bread has always been a struggle.  This is a wonderful mix and I would highly recommend it.

column9: Simply THE best GF bread anywhere
column10: I have been cooking and baking as well as buying products that are gluten free for 15 years. This is absolutely the best Gluten free bread I have ever seen , including those available from bakeries or in stores.  I mixed all the ingredients together, not even taking care to beat the eggs separately, etc.  Baked it for an hour. Presto. The best looking best tasting GF loaf we have ever seen. As a bonus, the loaf was a normal size, and much better for slicing for sandwiches. Although we often use storebought (eg Ener-G tapioca), the size of the slices on ready-made GF bread is ridiculously small.More importantly the texture of this bread was perfect. and the bread was totally flexible, no crumbling whatsoever. Sliced up like 'normal' bread, no falling apart.

I was diagnosed with Celiac disease last spring and finding gluten free bread that tastes good has been nothing short of a nightmare. I love this mix. It is so easy and versatile. I use it in my bread machine on the gluten free setting and add some extra time on the bake cycle to make sure it's done. I also add about 1TBsp of honey to the wet ingredients to moisten it up a bit.This bread makes delicious deli style sandwiches. No more frozen bread for me!

column9: Please leave this mix in the original box.
column10: I agree with most of the reviews on this bread.  I have been gluten free for 10 years and at first I made my own bread from a recipe from Gluten free gourmet, but when I found Gluten Free Pantry I have made only the sandwich or french bread by GFP with the exception that someone else bought some other brand, one was so bad I used for cold bread pudding.  I just noticed that the new owners have changed the box.  Please leave keep it in the original box.
I have been using this product almost a year, and it is excellent. I use a bread machine, but it is easily prepared in a conventional oven.

This product is far ahead of prepared loaves of bread. It is as easy to prepare as a cake mix, providing you are using a bread machine with a Gluten-Free setting. The bread holds together for sandwiches and is not crumbly or dry at all. It is delicious!
Since I have been diagnosed with celiac Disease, I have tried numerous Gluten Free Bread mixes, and this by far the best.  What you purchase already made is very dry and crumbles when you touch it.

This is the best gluten free bread I have found in 6 years of looking and trying.  It is great to enjoy bread again that does not have a strong taste and smell and has a normal bread-like texture.  I hardly notice that it is gluten free!
We've tried a lot of the other brands and flavors, and this is really the best we've found so far.  My gluten-eating husband loves it too.
I have used other gluten free bread mixes and found this one to be excellent.  It holds together without crumbling and has a good flavor.  Bakes up very well.

The first loaf was a little confusing, but then I caught on! This can be made by oven method or bread machine - both instructions are on the box.  After I mixed it and let it rest I was concerned that it only was as high as the bread pan.  I now know that it will continue to rise in the oven as it bakes.  It cuts well and the taste is the best we have tried.

column9: the next best thing to wheat bread
column10: I was completely surprised by how this turned out!  While it was rising, I was doubtful, but once it cooled and I sliced the bread, I was eager to taste it.  The texture was very much like white wheat bread, and the taste was very delightful!  My 16 month old is allergic to wheat and she loved being able to eat bread again (she has terrible eczema from wheat, tomatoes, dairy, and eggs), but even my 9 year old loved it.  Definitely recommended!  My only complaint is the price! over $6 a loaf including shipping.

This is the best bread I have made so far hands down!!! I have tried making some from scratch from cookbooks and I have also tried Pamelas... but for some reason it never came out right.This bread is the closest to homemade regular bread that you can make and it is soooo easy.I will be making this our familys favorite!

column9: Excellant product let me down recently
column10: I have been using Gluten Free Pantry Sandwich Bread mix with excellant results ever since my wife was diagnosed with Celiacdisease. I have used this product in bulk as well as in the 22 oz. box. In my last order the second box I opened did not have the yeast packet which should come with it. I can understand how this can happen, but it does mean I can not use that box. Having said that, I like the product and my wife dearly loves it.
This is a great tasting gluten free bread. Good texture and taste. Easy to slice.I use a bread machine and have never had a disappointing loaf.

This is my favorite bread so far.  My kids and husband love it, and I am excited to use my bread maker again (had stopped because normal bread made me feel sick- was before celiac diagnosis).  I've also done the dough cycle in the bread maker and then made rolls, which everyone loves.  I've suggested this to my brother, who I suspect is also celiac.  Enjoy!
Easy mix.  Great taste.  Works well with my bread machine and makes large loaves.

I absolutely LOVE this bread!  I am the only one in my household with celiac disease and the only one who is gluten-free, but my whole family likes this bread better than store-bought gluten-full bread.  It is not dense, dry, or crumbly at all, and when I have served it to people outside my family, they couldn't even tell it was gluten-free! This is by far the best gluten-free bread I have found.One tip - it does seem to rise much better for me when I make it in the oven as opposed to my bread maker.  A pastry chef had suggested to me that it may be because of the upright loaf pan (rather than a horizontal one) in my bread maker not allowing it to rise well, since gluten-free breads often have difficulty rising anyway.The only reason I did not give this bread 5 stars is because I am so disappointed that Amazon has removed it from their "Subscribe & Save" program.  It is still much cheaper here than buying it in the stores, though.
This is a good neutral tasting bread and holds together for sandwiches better than others.  Best taste in "sandwich" bread category I've found in gluten free. Easy to make. Would recommend.
This is our favorite gluten free white bread mix.  We use it in our breadmaker, and it always comes out perfectly.  We use it for sandwiches, and toast.  I order this by the case

My wife has Celiac and she makes her own bread using Gluten-Free Pantry Favorite Sandwich Bread Mix. She has found it to be the best for making her bread The Gluten-Free Pantry Favorite Sandwich Bread Mix, 22-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)
Good texture and easy to prepare.  My kids will actually eat a sandwich on this bread.  Great Product

It is the best tasting bread I have found in my search for bread.  And the convenience of ordering from Amazon. com keeps me from having to drive all over Oklahoma City looking for the best price of bread mix.

My kids were never thrilled at the idea of a sandwich until we started using this bread mix.  I use it in the bread machine and it's fluffy and tasty every time.  Nothing like the frozen rice bread options out there.
My husband likes this GF mix. He uses the "white bread" setting on the bread machine, instead of the GF setting. The GF setting did not produce good results.

My husband has been diagnosed with Celiac Disease.  It has been very hard for him because he loves his bread.  We have tried several kinds and have found this to be the closest in texture and taste to wheat based breads.  Cook it in a bread machine using the light bread setting (if cooked too long the crust can become chewy).  Also used dough cycle to make rolls so my husband could have a hamburger bun.  Used the bread also to make stuffing.  Highly recommend this.

My husband and 3 of our 4 kids were recently diagnosed with Celiac Disease. It's been a struggle to feed the crew but discovering this product has been a big help. We actually did a bake off with 3 different brands and no question Gluten-Free Pantry Favorite Sandwich bread was the winner. Once in a while we use their French bread mix for variety. If you're new to this gluten free thing my advice is to buy a bread machine with a delay timer, load it up before you go to bed and when you wake up you'll have a nice, fresh loaf of bread. When it's just made it's great. Later you'll need to toast it. We also make French toast and grilled cheese sandwiches from this and the kids feel like their back to being regular members of the eating world!

my 6 year old daughter was told that she has celiac disease about 6 months ago. She loves this bread. We tried every kind out there until we found this one. Thanks for making my life just a little easier, I didn't know what we were going to do for lunches at school. She asks for a sandwich everyday now.

This bread mix is the best GF bread I have found. Although it is expensive ($4.60 per loaf), it's worth it. Note: Super Walmarts carry this product and it's $4.95 per box. Most other stores charge $5.50 or more.

My husband loves this bread.  I have bought so many ready-made breads, and other mixes that have just been thrown away, but this bread is wonderful, easy to make, and tastes good.  Just ask my husband!  I make him a loaf about twice a week.

column9: FANTASTIC GLUTEN FREE EGG FREE DAIRY FREE BREAD
column10: This is the BEST gluten free bread we have found.  Since we have to be nut free and egg free as well we use the gluten free pantry sites recipe for an egg free version it is GREAT!

column9: easy to make, best GF bread yet!
column10: I really recommend this bread mix. It's the best Gf bread mix I've found yet. I usually make it, half regular, half with Cinnamon raisin. It's fabulous!!

We've been gluten free since March '07, and we've tried plenty of bread mixes and recipes, and this is the one the kids like the best.  They take sandwiches to school, use if for grilled cheese and toast, and we throw the heels in the food processor to use in meatballs and meatloaves. Not a crumb gets wasted! :-)
My son will eat sandwiches just like BEFORE the celiac diagnosis.  It's the best bread product we've found yet!

The Gluten-Free Pantry Favorite Sandwich Bread Mix, 22-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)My husband is a bread freak and not being able to have regular bread this is a God send. This bread is execellant , I made it in bread machine and not as good or fast as making it in oven.  Love it.

Hands-down, my favorite bread. Soft, nice flavor, easily sliced, doesn't crumble and adaptable for other flavors (the cinnamon raisin version on the box is great, too.) A must buy for everyone who needs to eat gluten-free. You won't miss regular gluten bread again after having this freshly made sandwich bread on your plate.

We've used this Gluten-Free bread mix since 2005.  I use this for basic sandwich bread.  I've learned to add one more egg white and decrease the water amount for our bread machine - comes out consistent every time.

column9: Favorite Sandwich Bread from the Gluten-Free Pantry
column10: Best Product Out There!  Can't Eat a Gluten-Free Sandwich Without It!  Amazon Sells This at the BEST Price, Too!

This is the only gluten free sandwich bread mix my kids like.  It always turns out great!  I do cover the bread with foil the last 10 minutes of baking so it won't be overly brown.  We always have a good stash of this on hand.  Good price on Amazon, too.

After going gluten free, we have tried so many different breads and most are just heavy and not good at all.  We decided to give this a try and are happy about it.  My sons gobbled down the first loaf in record time.  They love it.  We also used it to make mini hamburger buns for the kids, baking the bread in cup cake pans.  Definitely worth it.  And, it is not overly time consuming like so many other bread recipes.This bread does have a bit of a yeasty flavor and is not all light and fluffy, but is not heavy as a brick like most GF breads that we have come across.  It also makes a great grilled cheese!

What a relief when I discovered the G-F Pantry bread!!  I was diagnosed with Celiac several years ago at the age of 59.  What a life change.  Tried the rice breads but they just didn't come close to a bread product.  I add fiber and honey to the bread and it does not change the consistency at all.  I did find that using a large bread pan works best.  Thank you G-F Pantry for a very user-friendly product.

column9: Best Ever Gluten Free Bread Mix
column10: A gluten allergy creates a number of rather difficult problems.  This bread mix solves the most difficult one, as do a number of other mixes.  The difference is, that the Glutgen-Free Pantry Favorite Sandwich Mix yields a loaf of bread that is actually good to eat.  It's good in taste and texture; a rare treat.

column9: Now THIS is an excellent bread
column10: I was really excited when I discovered this foolproof bread mix- it has great texture and flavor- and actually tastes GOOD. Try it with margarine (or butter) and honey on top- I think you won't be disappointed. Also works really well in a bread machine, even if it doesn't have a gluten free cycle. This is a great bread for newly diagnosed celiacs (just remember, it won't be QUITE like you remember gluten being, but it's a new, good different) as it is so easy and only requires a few common ingredients. Then after you have your legs under you, you can try the world of gluten free baking from scratch, which in my experience yields the absolute best results. BUT this bread is great for times when there's no time for serious baking, and is WAY better than most of those nasty premade breads (though Whole Foods sundried tomato bread may give it a run for its money). I almost feel like I should give it 4 stars, because I stopped buying it after a while, but it really is good for what it is, so in memory of my old relationship with this bread mix, I gave it a 5. :) (I  am currently in a Bette Hagman phase- search for her cookbooks)
I have tried many recipes and mixes over the last year.  Nothing compares to this bread!

This bread maker-mix makes a large loaf - 2lb - and because the dough is very thin, you have to pay attention to it while it rises so it won't overflow.  Made right, this bread is not as dense as many wheat/gluten free breads and it is tasty - almost like bread with wheat and gluten. It tastes best fresh out of the oven or as toast.

I bought this bread mix due the high rated reviews.  The mix made a beautiful loaf, but the flavor wasn't the greatest.  The only way I was able to eat it, was to pile it with peanut butter and jelly.  As stated by one of the reviews it also contains milk, I'm lactose intolerant. I will give Pamela's a try.

column9: Who Knew Bread Could Make Me Cry.....
column10: Who knew bread could make me cry!! With a new diagnosis and a grumpy picky 15 year old son.... I was at my wits end to find something, anything he would like.  I literally held my breath when I put this mix together in my bread maker (2lb wellbuilt - and it actually overflowed my bread pan!!) anyways... signs on the doors to be quiet for fear the bread might fall.... sniffing the air every 10 minutes thinking "Yup smells like bread... could it be??".  It had just cooled when my son walked in the door starving.... (being in high school, football, and lunch time have been rough!!) I ask him to sit down I've got something for him.... holding my breath some more - watching his first bite and him jumping up and down, "Mom is this for real? This is AWESOME!"  Let me say that again, "This is AWESOME" now when have any of us heard those words from our teenagers mouth in relation to anything.  I got huge hugs, kisses and high fives, I think he even was dancing!!! My other 4 kids in the house tried it and couldn't believe it wasn't "regular" bread!! That is saying something cause let's me honest there are some out there that you just can't  fake liking, even a little bit!!  The other kids are so happy that he is happy cause these last couple of weeks have been rough on all of us, mostly on him.  Thank You Thank You Thank YOu - you won't be sorry with this mix!!

column9: A very good bread, with some tips
column10: I have been gluten free for several years, and I generally don't even attempt to eat bread anymore, even the gluten free kinds.When we discovered that gluten seemed to really affect my autistic son, we had to come up with something for lunches for school.This mix had good reviews so I decided to try it. I have a dedicated gluten free breadmaker that was a gift.With a little toying, I was able to program my machine correctly for the bread. The first loaf I made was underdone in the middle, so I increased the baking time by five minutes for the second one. It wasn't a total loss, because I put the underdone pieces in a buttered skillet and fried them until they were done in the middle.You will need to choose the lightest crust setting you have and change it so there is only one rise time for the bread. Also, while the bread is mixing (it mixes for about five minutes or so), push the mix down on the sides with a rubber spatula about halfway through mixing. This only takes a minute. Now that my machine is programmed, all I have to do is hit the button, come back in about three or four minutes to push down the sides, and then in an hour I have a loaf of bread.As all gluten free bread, it will fall apart a bit if you cut it while still warm. The best way to do it is to make the bread, unmold it onto a paper plate, wrap it in plastic, and put it in the refrigerator. When it is cold it is much easier to cut with the bread knife. Also do NOT cut the whole loaf ahead of time or it will dry out within a couple of days.The bread tastes fabulous. There is milk contained within the mix, so it's not good for gluten free casein free people. I gave a fresh slice of it to a friend who is NOT gluten free and he thought it tasted great. I'll never buy store bought loaves of gluten free bread again, though. This tastes a hundred times better!

When I was diagnosd with Celiac Disease, I started on a search for good BREAD!!! And this is it!!!!! Easy to work with and actually tastes great. I was not successful using my bread making machine - this dough worked much better with a regular electric mixer. This mix also makes wonderful cinnamon bread!

The price was considerably better a while back at $19.44. How can they figure the original price was $6.30 per bag, when the company who manufacture's this product sells it for $3.99 per bag plus shipping. For the price they are charging now, I can get it at my local healthfood store for much less. The product is excellent and have used it for many years, but Amazon's price is not a deal anymore!

column9: Best Bread ever when extra water and honey is added
column10: This bread mix is the best ever but you have to play with it a bit. Depending on which bread machine you use, extra water may need to be added. Also play with bake time till you get it right. Both of these take a bit of time but worth the effort. Also to make the bread a little more moist add about 2 tablespoons of honey to the mix, it realy helps.

column9: Better bread if you use your own yeast
column10: We'd been making this bread for a long time with results that were all right but nothing to rave about.  Then we opened a mix with a packet of yeast that felt as though it had solidified.  Rather than use it and risk losing a loaf of bread, we substituted a packet of our own active dry yeast that was fresh.  What a difference it made!  The bread was lighter, fluffier and not sunken in the middle like it always is when we use the yeast that's included in the package.  Now we are using our own yeast to make this bread, which increases the cost.  Glutino's "Perfect Rise Yeast" is not only far from perfect, it's apparently stale and/or out of date.  The Glutino company needs to do better!

I waited until I made this bread mix a few times before I would review it. This has by far been my favorite bread mix. I have completely given up on trying to make my own and will now ONLY buy this.A couple things to note is 1.) I let the dough rise accidently for 2.5 hours and I must say this was the best accident. The bread rose above the pan and rolled over some but it was almost like it completely changed the texture of the bread. It was way more fluffy like real bread. I will from here on out be letting this dough rise for at least 2 hours. 2.) I like to place foil on it half way through so that the crust doesn't become too dark, and 3.) when I pull it out of the oven I  like to baste it with milk and it softens the texture of the crust.

column9: Best Gluten-free bread I have found.
column10: I have tried several gluten-free breads over the past 7 years of living a gluten-free diet.  Most of them have either been really dry and/or taste like cardboard, or be too moist and good for toast but not sandwiches.  This is by far the best bread I have found for sandwiches and hamburgers.  I don't even miss wheat bread anymore.  This bread is worth the money.

This is perhaps the easiest, most neutral tasting GF bread mix I have tried yet. It was the first I bought, and it made my GF transition much simpler.You CAN mix this by hand. I tried a single box first to be sure, then came here and ordered a case. It makes a large, 'normal' looking loaf of bread. The texture is wonderful for the first 2-3 days, then I slice what's left and store in my freezer until I need another slice. Try the Cinnamon Raisin bread recipe and make french toast for a real treat! Play around with the recipe. Try it with milk, then water. Try it with butter, then oil. Eggs, or egg-less. My personal combo is oil, eggs, and 3/4 water to 1/4 milk.The cons? A bit crumbly, and not enough 'chew' to the bread to pretend you are eating a rustic bread. All and all though...you can't go wrong starting your gluten free journey here.

column9: The best GF bread we've had; it's our regular.
column10: This is the only GF bread my son will eat. You can actually have sandwiches again!

We found this sandwich bread to be very satisfactory.  We also were very pleased the way you expedited this order,It was packed verey well and came in good time.Thank you for sending me this information toorder from you.Sincerely,Kathleen Maynard

column9: The best gluten free bread I have ever eaten
column10: To date, this is the beat gluten free bread I have ever eaten and it can be easily made in your bread machine. In the refrigerator, the bread will keep for weeks without molding.

column9: So sad it has milk in it
column10: I'm allergic to all gluten, eggs, all dairy, corn and soy beans.  Finding a bread I can use seems impossible.  Looks so good but it has milk in it.  One bite and my throat would swell shut and I can't breathe.  Oh well guess I continue to live without bread.

My husband and I just made a batch of this bread, and while it smells and tastes amazing, the fact that is contains "skim milk" and "whey" means that my neither of my kids can have it!!! I suppose this is a lesson in reading every label before purchasing--I've been spoiled by Bob's Red Mill Gluten-Free, Dairy-Free Bread.

I make at least two loaves a week,in a Breadman bread maker.  It is the best bread for people who must be gluten-free. It is much like the bread Mother use to make.  I think everyone could enjoy the flavor and texture.  It has my vote.

column9: Pretty good for a rice based bread....
column10: I have no problem with this bread and am sure it could meet a lot of people's tastes and needs. Rice based breads have their problems though -- dry, crumbly, GF taste and texture. Definitely give this a try but my recommendation is Bob's Red Mill Gluten-Free Homemade Wonderful Bread Mix. Read my review there. Power to the garbanzo bean!!!

column9: The bread that fools them all!
column10: Our 9 year old was recently diagnosed as celiac and we suspect she may not be the only one in our family with the 'wheat issue'.  My 9 year old loves to eat bread and milk and, of course, now she can't have either.  I knew there were gluten-free flours and breads out there, but they're not easy to find in my local grocery store.  I went online to Amazon Grocery to see if they offered anything and to see what customers' reviews were.  I wanted to try something that others had enjoyed, not just buy whatever (few) items they happened to carry in town. This bread mix was very highly rated, so I bought a whole case to give it a try.I received a bread machine from my mother that wasn't a special 'gluten-free' type bread machine, so I gave this bread mix a try using the standard method.  It took some adjusting to get the best ingredient combination to yield the right taste and texture, but this formula is a winner!  The instructions on the box call for either milk or water, butter or oil, and several types of egg combinations.  The best tasting (and texture) combination was milk, olive oil and 2 large (whole) eggs.  The smell of the freshly baked bread brings the whole family out of hiding and into the kitchen, salivating as I slice into the warm loaf.Celiacs need not despair!!!  This gluten-free bread mix makes the most delicious bread that's so good it's hard to believe it's not traditional wheat bread.  It also takes the hassle out of trying to purchase and concoct a wheat-flour substitute that can be used to THEN make bread that anyone accustomed to wheat bread might actually want to eat.  Our whole family LOVES this bread.  THANK YOU, THANK YOU, THANK YOU!!!

We have tried many GF breads ... both prepared and mixes.  None of them were acceptable substitutes for "real" bread.  This bread is a keeper. Rises well. Slices easily.  Tastes great.  My son loves it so much that we put it on auto order.  My husband got into it and didn't realize that it was GF.Hint 1:  This makes a 2 pound loaf.  It WILL rise enough to overflow a 1.5 loaf bread machine.  I use the bread machine just to mix the batter and then let it rise on the counter and cook it in the oven.Hint 2:  No preservatives.  The bread stores best if you let it cool, slice the entire loaf, and store in the freezer.Hint 3:  This bread mix is NOT casein-free.  Milk is ingredient #4.  Whey is #5.

column9: Gluten-Free Pantry Favorite Sandwich Bread Mix
column10: We have tried other mixes and have found this to be the best on the market. We make it in a bread machine and it turns out great ever time. It is best toasted. It makes great garlic bread by toasting in the oven with garlic powder and butter. Toasted in the toaster with peanut butter or jam. My husband didn't like it as a sandwich bread until I started toasting it first.Great for grill cheese and etc.

I made a gluten free meal for my Bunco group.  My menu was early Thanksgiving.  The main item was hot turkey sandwiches.  I mixed the Gluten Free Pantry Sandwich Bread Mix according to manual directions.  I divided it into 12 greased  8 oz.Corelle bowls, covered them with plastic wrap sprayed with Pam.  I put them on two cookie sheets in the oven preheated to 250 with a pan of boiling water and shut the oven off  to rise until I liked how they looked.  I removed the plastic wrap and heated the oven to the temp. on the box of mix and baked until golden brown and sounded hollow when I tapped the top.  I cooled them on a rack and then froze them in zip lock bags.  The day of my party I took them out of the freezer and cut them in half.  I placed them on a serving tray and put them in a paper grocery bag to warm them in the oven just before serving.  My gluten free friends were elated to have real food that everyone was eating as well and they didn't have to worry what they could or couldn't eat.  By the way, the rest of the menu was Sweet Potato Oven Fries, Cranberry Applesauce, Relish Tray of Carrots, Celery, Ripe Olives and Pimento Olives and Pumpkin Mousse for dessert.

I have used this product before, and it makes a wonderful loaf of bread. But Amazon (or wherever it comes from) should really check expiration dates. While it's still in date now, I ordered 6 boxes and they all expire in 3 months! I don't bake bread THAT often, so I'm VERY disappointed, which is why I'm only giving it three stars.

I have used this bread mix for quite some time now.  I recently ordered Pamela's gluten free bread mix, which came in a close second place, but I kept wishing I had the mix from the Gluten Free Pantry instead.  It bakes a loaf that is not too different from gluten containing bread.  Some GF bread mixes make a doughy loaf, but this mix bakes all the way through with a consistent texture.  Although most GF breads need to be toasted to make them more palatable, you really can make a very good sandwich with this bread untoasted. Like most GF products, you need to refrigerate this bread to prevent mold.  If you are looking for a GF bread mix I definitely recommend this mix from The Gluten Free Pantry!

I have used this bread and I like it very much.  The taste and texture are great and the bread is a little easier to make than Bob's Red Mill.When you add the shipping cost to the price of the bread, the result is an astonishing $6.61 per loaf!  I will continue to buy this mix from my local stores.

I'm not sure what the problem with this bread mix is.  There appears to be too much batter for the specified 9x5 pan.  It mushrooms up over the top and then while cooling the sides suck in.  It seems to turn out better when baked in (2) 4x8 pans, but the sides and bottom still shrink in.  All in all it's not a pretty loaf, but it is yummy fresh from the oven with peanut butter on it.

column9: This is supposed to be bread?
column10: Sure, this bread is good if you like having your ham & cheese between two slices of pound cake. I was not happy with this product at all. It was very cake like, but besides that the taste was awful. I will be making croutons out of it, hopefully I can mask the taste with loads of garlic.

This is a wonderful mix that makes a hearty bread and works excellently in my breadmaker on the regular setting.  I have been using it for over a year now, since I was diagnosed with Celiac disease, and I've never missed wheat bread since I began using it.It's very easy to make in the breadmaker.  The mix does take two eggs, which might be more than some people would like to use, and butter or oil as well as milk or water.  I usually use dry, non-fat milk and real butter.  It made primarily of corn flour and rice flour, has a full flavor, and is dense but not heavy.  My husband, who is not gluten free, enjoys it as well, especially toasted.  It has been commented to me that it has a slightly sweet taste, but I don't particularly notice that.I use it for cold sandwiches such as peanut butter or chicken salad, for hot sandwiches such as grilled cheese, and it makes the most excellent toast I have ever eaten.I have tried other gluten free breads, but this remains my favorite.

Positives:The mix is easy and quick to make, requiring only about an hour total time for a loaf of bread. Appearance is very close to a wheat-based 'white' bread. Cost is comparable to most other mixes that I've tried. It keeps well and holds together well with toasting and constructing a sandwich. It made good croutons, too.Negatives: I did not really care for the texture that much. It is fine at the first bite, but with chewing falls apart into a granular mouth-feel that is off-putting. Also, the bread has something of an after-taste that I did not like very much. I found myself really loading up my sandwich with spicy mustard, pickles, tomatoes, et cetera to cover up the taste.Overall, this bread is "okay" but not great. It is certainly better than most of the loaves you will pick-up from the freezer at the grocer's. I would recommend trying it if you are looking a child-friendly gluten-free bread, as it does look very much like white bread.*The texture improved when I made the bread using a bread machine vs. by hand. I would recommend that method for making this particular brand.

column9: What happen to the old MIX
column10: My girlfriend has been using the product for some time now. She has been on auto ship with Amazon. She just got a new shipment and the box has changed and it doesn't cook the same way the old mix did. She has tried a few times but it never comes out the same from the bread machine. I was wondering if anyone else has notice this change.John

New to the gf diet.  After trying the dry packaged stuff at the store, using a recipe from the internet and Bob's Red Mill--this stuff is unbelievable.  We are a bread lover family and this bread passed the test with flying colors.My husband's mom is always baking goodies and this tasted just like her homemade bread.  Perfect to take to Holiday meals and the gluten crowd wouldn't even know--it's that good.Even if a miracle occurred and we could buy white bread, I'm not sure we would want to--it's that good.:)

column9: Best bread ever- ridiculously easy to make.
column10: I've tried about a thousand different packaged gluten-free bread mixes, making bread for my girlfriend.I've tried gluten free flour that replaces regular flour 1-to-1.They have all turned out mediocre at best, inedible at worstKobe beef burgers with absolutely inedible buns),with all the loaves being small, dense, and not much rise or loft.This was the happy opposite.I don't have a bread machine, but I followed the simple instructions- water, butter, eggs, mix for three minutes. Seriously, three minutes, and then turn out into the pan, smooth with wet hands or spatula, cover and let rise.It cooks in only 30 minutes(!!!), and is done when it sounds hollow when thumped. Every other recipe I've ever tried cooks for 45-60 minutes until it reaches an internal temp. of 190-210.I let this rise on the stove top for 45 minutes as the oven pre-heated, and then put it in to bake. I about had a stroke when I checked on it, and it had risen over the top of the pan to make a regular sized and shaped loaf. Mine finished in about twenty five minutes. I unpanned it immediately and let it cool on a rack for about thirty minutes. I sliced several pieces, and they were moist and tender, and tasted like regular bread.If I could give this six stars I would.Two quick notes,Gluten free breads are fragile- you must let them cool before you slice or handle them.When you cover the bread to let it rise, I used a sheet of plastic wrap I smeared with Crisco. It really worked well to stop the risen bread from sticking to the plastic, and allowed the plastic to be removed without peeling the skin from the loaf.
