column9: One of the best hot sauces I've tried
column10: As a self-proclaimed connoisseur of hot sauces, I would have to say that Melinda's Naga Jolokia is my absolute favorite.  While not as hot as some of the other sauces made form the Bhut Jolokia (Ghost Pepper), it definitely has the best flavor of the ones I've tried.  That said, it is still very hot and there have been times my digestive system has hated me for using too much.  As far as Melinda's sauces go, I would consider this one of the best ones, and as a fan of Melinda's, that's pretty good.  As for heat, I would consider Dave's Jolokia sauce a little hotter, but I'd choose this everytime, just because the flavor is better.  But then again, that's just my opinion. Get both and try for yourself...and get that whole milk ready.

This is no run of the mill hot sauce.  It has instantly become my favorite.  The flavor is complex and satisfying, while the heat seems to gradually build to an intense burn that lingers for a few minutes.  This is not for those who can't handle heat, nor is it for the heat junkies that love the "must sign a waiver to consume" sauces made with capsaicin extract.  If you are someone who appreciates flavor and heat, Melinda's Naga Jolokia is definitely worth trying.

I have to agree with the other reviews. This sauce is very flavorful and by far the hottest Melinda's will ever be able to make. I love Melinda's because they don't try to destroy you with heat, although this one has some SERIOUS kick to it. They really know how to make a flavorful hot sauce, and this one ties with the 4x Reserve as being my two favorites.

THis sauce lives up to its name and the reputation of the Ghost Pepper.  It's more than merely hot, though, because it has flavor  andwhen it's used judiciously, will not overpower the taste of the food.  It provides more than augmentation like, say, Tabasco, because the Ghost Pepper isundeniably hot, and if you use it too liberally no doubt it will render your sauce, your sandwich, your potatoes more molten than you may like.But a few drops, strategically placed and swirled around, will give you a short burst of intense heat and a lingering taste that, while hot, makes good foodeven better.  Highly recommended for pepper devotees.
I think it has a better flavor than the Mad Dog ghost pepper sauce, but it isn't as hot.  So, it all depends on what your looking for.

column9: Very hot but still has flavor
column10: I've reordered this a few times now and love this hot sauce. It is very hot (ghost chilis and all). But unlike a lot of them out there that are just hot and harsh, this actually has a good flavor to it. Assuming your taste buds survive the heat :)

column9: Now I know why they call it the Ghost Chili
column10: Like most Melinda's hot sauces, they aren't the hottest around. You CAN find hotter sauces made from the same pepper... but whether you taste the pepper is a different story. What I've noticed with this brand of sauce is that you can actually taste the pepper. Now to this particular sauce... I tried dabs of this sauce on omlets or pizza with no particular note or notice. It seemed no hotter than any other habanero based sauce I've had in the past. All hype.. right?One day I decided to use it for a dipping sauce for french fries... not such a good idea. This sauce is fine in small amounts, you get a good dose of the taste of the pepper. But try to use it like a habanero sauce is a mistake... it's painful. Slow, constant burn really sneaks up on you, just when you think it is not that bad... it's too late. Have respect for the Naga Jolokia!

I really like this hot sauce.  It has excellent flavor and the heat seems to spread through your whole body and stay with you well after you are done eating.  This pepper sauce not only has a unique flavor, it has a unique feel to it.  I'm a fan for life.

I love hot food.LOVE IT! I have finished a bottle of the regular Melinda's and two bottles of the xxxxReserve Habanero Sauce. The Naga Jolokia sauce is hot and delicious.I was suprised that it wasn't hotter. At first I just tried a dash or two but quickly realized that I could handle quite a bit of it.Don't be scared by the name, If you like hot food, you'll like this sauce.

I should of bought two bottles of Melinda's and saved on shipping because I have been putting this delicious sauce on everything.  Not as spicy as I thought it would be, but it taste great with a good burn.  It burns much more than any store bought sauce I have tasted.

This hot sauce is GOOD!I am a chili head with over 30-40 different "active" hot sauces and much more used and in storage. This sauce is one of my favorites. The sauce really works off of the heat and flavor of the ghost pepper and does not try to mask it like many other naga jolokia sauces. It is very spicy though and would only recommend to serious chili heads who like a great heat and great flavor.

Don't let the Naga Jolokia title scare you. This hot sauce actually has a decent heat and decent taste.Good:# I enjoyed the taste of it. It doesn't taste like battery acid, unlike some hot sauces.# Medium-to-hot. Won't be unbearable, even if used in a large amount.# Perfect to cook with.# Isn't runny - is actually a paste similar to ketchup.# I like the design of the bottleCan't think of anything neutral or bad to say about this product. I would recommend this to anyone.

column9: You have to try this sauce!!!
column10: I love it - plain and simple.  Melinda's has created the best hot sauce EVER!  Painfully hot and flavorful too - how is this possible?  Ballistic all natural heat and delicious, I'm hooked!

I sought this one out because I like Melinda's and I like that it contains peppers, not extracts.It's good - first jolokia sauce I've tried. I've had a few of Melinda's habanero sauces and like them very much - definitely my favorite brand. But I think Melinda's carrot, etc. blend matches much better with habanero than jolokia - they seemed to clash a little bit. Seems the jolokia overpowered the other flavors rather than blending.Definitely hot. Worth a try. Melinda's fans may be a bit disappointed.

column9: Nice and Hot - with great flavor and not just heat.
column10: A very good and very hot sauce...a few drops will do.  Not overly hot like the Dave's Insanity where all they use are extracts.  You actually get some flavor with this one.  It does take some getting used to if you are moving up from Habanero sauces...take it a drop at a time until you develop your toloerance. Once you do, you'll not go back!  I started with a couple drops, and now use this as my go-to sauce of choice on eggs, in chili, on my breakfast sandwich....it's just so good.

Ok...my husband had me purchase this sauce as he is a big pepper fanatic and could not wait to try the Naga Jolokia pepper. He was sorely disappointed in this sauce. We live in the Caribbean and are accustomed to really hot peppers, although I personally am not a pepper person.After the first tentative taste of this sauce my husband sighed in disappointment and proceeded to literally drench his food in it to get that "eye burning, choking" sensation that apparently all pepper fanatics can't wait to experience.I have not tried the sauce, but he says that in addition to the heat being just mild to moderate, there is not much flavour there. Anyway, heat level is a subjective and relative thing, so as far as my review goes...thumbs down on expected heat and flavour.I think his next step is to try the raw naga jolokia peppers. Good luck to him!I would just like to add to the above review and state that it is now 5 months later and I have since tried the naga jholokia sauce, as my spouse did not seem that impressed. I found it hot and spicy, but nothing that made my eyes water. The heat from the ghost peppers has been tempered with carrots, papaya and passion fruit. Still maintain the 3 star rating.

column9: Hills Bros. Sugar Free Coffee, French Vanilla Cappuccino, 12.0-Ounce
column10: We really like it. It tastes more like hot cocoa than coffee though. We were looking for cappuccino flavored coffee.

Love the whiskey , hate the sauce. I like my BBQ sauce sweet and this is not. Has a strange flavor that I can't describe. I hope they would make a different recipe with a sweet taste to it. Wasted my money , no one like this stuff so I guess it goes in the garbage.

Sadly, this has very little flavor, and is definitely creamy to the point of almost being watery.It does not really taste like almonds at all.I don't like leaving this review, but other Amazon reviews have helped me, so, here it is....
This item is labeled as "NS" (or No Stir) which means it should not separate. The item which arrives is not a "No Stir" almond butter.Other than the separation, this Almond butter is quite tasty.
My son loves his PB&J's...but is not allowed to bring the P to school, so I make his sandwiches with this and he loves it. I'm just bummed that Amazon doesn't have it on subscribe&save anymore.

I loved the single serve packaging for the honey maids.  I love these with peanut butter as a quick snack when there is no time to go to hospital cafeteria or when working on the computer. Great taste and the individual packaging helps to keep each snack fresh!

HoneyMaid's Fresh Stack Honey Grahams are the classic HoneyMaid graham cracker in new packaging. In the old box, the grahams came in sheets of nine crackers to a package. Each cracker a sheet consisting of two cracker squares. In the new box each package contains eight single squares. The squares are close to being the same size. However, when I placed one on top of the other, the new crackers were just a smidge smaller than the old.Nutrition wise, it is important to note that the new Honey Made Fresh Stack Honey Grahams contain two servings to a pack. One serving of four squares contains 130 calories, 3 grams of fat, 1 gram of fiber, 8 grams of sugar and a whopping 24 grams of carbs. The crackers contain 4% iron, 0% Vitamin A, 0% Vitamin C and 0% Calcium. Overall, the crackers lack in nutrition and should be viewed as more of a treat than a staple. If you eat the whole package you will need to double the calories, fat etc.The new packaging is certainly nice at keeping the crackers fresher. And one could argue it is better packaging, because though more material is used, fewer crackers are most likely being thrown out because they are stale.Overall the crackers are not all that nutritious so eating them along with a variety of other nutritious foods is important. For a more nutritious cracker, regular whole wheat Triscuits are satisfying and delicious. But for s'mores and homemade ice cream sandwiches, it is HoneyMaid Graham Crackers for sure.

column4: Marshall Carter "Ornery Gamer, Fiend Club Member"
column9: Why didn't they think of this sooner?
column10: There's not much reason to review the actual graham crackers here. If you like graham crackers, then there's absolutely nothing to dislike here. This is the same classic, sweet, wholesome snack you've been enjoying from Honey Maid for years, just packaged in a way that's better for you (and the crackers). Every time that I've ever bought graham crackers in the past, the larger packs will end up being halfway eaten while the remaining crackers always (and I mean ALWAYS) end up stale. By changing the packaging and giving you six bundles instead of two, your crackers will stay fresh, crisp and tasty until you're ready for them. Throw in the added convenience of the smaller packs (much easier to throw in a bag, purse or lunch box) and this is truly one of those ideas that leaves you wondering why it hadn't been done years before. Honey Maid Fresh Stacks are now the only way to buy graham crackers.

Honey Maid Fresh Stacks are so good and very convenient to carry in your purse or car. When you need a snack to hold you over for lunch or dinner, these are great. They stay fresh in the pack and have the same delicious taste. These are a great size for on-the-go snacks.

I like graham crackers, so how can you not rate them 5 stars? And they ARE Honey Maid.The only difference is this box has six packets, with 8 crackers to a packet. The only advantage I can see to this is taking them in your lunch or a picnic or something. I actually think 8 is a bit much for lunch. 4 or 6 and you could easily send them in your kid's lunch. So that is my one question to Honey Maid. What were they trying to accomplish?

I absolutely love graham crackers and these are just so cute. they come in packages of small squares.  i put them in my purse for work, and i went overnight on a little trip and kept a package with me just in case i coudn't get a meal, my sugar woudln't drop.  the flavor is perfect, they were crisp, fresh and just wonderful.i liked them so much i tried to find them in my store and they didn't have them.i think i will just order them from Amazon.they are absolutely wonderfulthe packaging is what makes them.  instead of you breaking the normal graham crackers, they come like they are already broken in half.  the perfect size

These are the graham crackers you remember dunking in milk when you were a kid.  Yum.  What they've done here is to change the sleeve size inside the box so now instead of two large sleeves, the crackers are wrapped into several smaller ones so that you can worry less about the product becoming stale.  As long as the price is the same either way, I would vote for this product over the traditional.

The 6 smaller packages of graham crackers in this box is definitely more convenient than the larger wax paper packs that comes in the usual box of graham crackers.  Ideal for lunch boxes.  These indvidual packs help the crackers stay fresh until they are ready for use.  Ideal for making smores with one marshmallow per cracker.

column9: Great for kids and diaper bags
column10: I often have products that go stale on me or have to put in baggies to stay fresh.  These packs are the regular graham crackers but are in small packs that are perfect for on the go traveling.  They fit nicely in a diaper bag to take with you out the door.  I would highly recommend these crackers if you have a snack monkey like I do.

This is one of those "What took them so long?" products.  The large/normal package of graham crackers is always too much - too often, crackers go stale because we can't finish them all.  So this new "half" packaging is much better.That said, they could STILL stand to shrink down the amount of crackers in each package.  It's too many for lunches.  Kids only eat about 2 crackers (which is one whole one) at a time.It's great for picnics and campfires (S'mores), though!

These are regular Honey Maid graham crackers.  The ones we know and love.  However, as other reviewers have pointed out, 1 package is TWO servings.  Those of us watching our calorie intake need to be aware of that.  The packages are convenient but the crackers arrived broken so whether it was the shipping or a problem with the packaging, I don't know.  Overall, I did enjoy it and it was convenient for lunch at work, but would prefer individual portions to keep the second serving fresh.

These are a great snack to carry along for kids!  They are already broken in half, which also makes them great for s'mores.  My 2 year old son was hooked, he always gets frustrated trying to break his graham crackers.

column9: Great Idea.  Great for Lunches and Snacks
column10: I was glad to see our long time favorite graham crackers in a snack size.  They are great for lunches and snacks.  Best of all, they stay fresher, longer.
Very very yummy graham crackers in an easier to manage size! Plus the stay fresh packaging ensures that these crackers always stay fresh and crisp!
The portions for this product was on point and great for an anytime snack. I would recommend it to parents for school lunches.

The Graham Crackers here are the same ones I've enjoyed as a treat for the better part of my life.  The difference here is that they're already "separated" into single squares.  They're also packaged into smaller groups.  You're getting the same number of crackers over all, but there are fewer of them grouped together in the wax paper bundles.  So if you just want one or two crackers, you don't get as many sitting in an open pack getting stale between snacks.
Though the idea of graham crackers is not new, the individual packaging is. The packaging makes taking the crackers along very convenient. Plus, they do stay fresh longer. I highly recommend.

column9: Great for travel and snack, not anything special for regular eating.
column10: This is the perfect size and amount for packing a small snack while traveling or for school.I did for some reason think they had a different taste, maybe it was just my opinion, but they did not seem as "fresh or crisp".My kids still enjoyed them without complaint.

These are delicious graham crackers that are divided into convenient portions. If you love graham crackers then you'll love these. The portion size is great for travelling or packing in a lunch box. That said, some care is needed as the crackers are pretty fragile. If they're places in a brown paper bag then they could end up being a conveniently portion a graham crumbs. Packing these in a hard lunch box or being careful with your packed lunch is the way to go.

column9: Improvement on an old friend:  Fresher and more convenient
column10: How do you improve on something like graham crackers?How about if you make them taste fresher and put them into smaller inside packages.I've been used to buying a box with 3 inside wrappers.  This new packaging has 6, so the contents of the box stay fresh longer.It's also nice if you're concerned about total calories.  I often end up eating the entire section of crackers, so in this packaging it's only 250 calories if you eat the whole package.Yes, the interior packaging is a bit hard to tear open, but that's probably what helps keep them so fresh.  Try scissors to open the package.Improvement on an old friend--Graham Crackers!

column9: Good Graham Crackers in Better Packaging.
column10: I have found better Graham Crackers but these are quite good and we buy them frequently. I like the new packaging since each individual package contains just enough for one time. With the old packaging, there would almost always be a few crackers left over and no way to seal them so they would start to go stale.If you have never tried Honey Maid Graham Crackers, they are worth trying and be sure to dunk them in milk, coffee or tea as they are great that way.

Honey Maid has gone to the trouble of packaging their crackers in single serving portions.  Each box has 6 packages and each package contains 6 single squares of cracker, half the size of the original Honey Maid cracker. If you can see some benefit in handling a smaller cracker or having the crackers packaged in single portion sizes, or your market is out of the regular size crackers, then this product is a good choice for you.

We've tried the generic brands but keep coming back to Honey Maid. The kids say that they taste better, and I have to agree. The honey flavor is more apparent, the others taste a bit cardboard-like in comparison. I do use the generic brands for when I make a graham cracker crust, as it's not as noticeable when used in recipes. But for snacks, we stick with Honey Maid.

column9: Great idea - Smaller package stays fresh longer
column10: This little change makes all the difference in ensuring that your graham crackers stay fresh longer.  There are 8-squares in each sealed package.  I often found that after opening a traditional package, all the crackers would not be eaten in one sitting and when the kids would go back for more a few days later, they would already begin to taste a bit stale.  Since each package can easily be a snack for 2-kids, I no longer have this problem.  The smaller package also seems to travel better with less crumbs getting scattered when I'm serving them.  Although I prefer the fresh stacks when traveling due to the smaller size, the packaging certainly isn't "crush proof."  Frankly, it's the same type of waxy wrapper that contains the rectangular graham crackers so you need to handle the package with care or many of your crackers will be crushed.  In other words, this package isn't something you'd throw in your kid's book bag for snack unless they like a lot of crumbs because they'd be pulverized to dust before they got to school.  Overall however, I really like the packaging idea and I'd definitely always buy the square stacks over the rectangular packaging providing there is no price difference.

column9: A Taste of Nostalgia And A Good Treat
column10: It's been years since I've eaten Honey Maid graham crackers, and tasting these brought back all the nostalgia of my childhood! What kid doesn't love these?? And in convenient, on-the-go, pack 'em in your lunch sizes? It can ONLY be win-win, right? Well...maybe.This box consists of 6 individually wrapped packages of 8 crackers. By having them individually packaged, it does make for a much more convenient way to pack them into a lunch, or an on the go snack. And having them individually packaged also means the crackers stay fresh and crunchy. No more stale, soft crackers - although, I do remember that I enjoyed those as well as a kid. Go figure.For some reason, I had always assumed graham crackers were healthy. I guess that's because moms were always feeding us kids these crackers when I was a kid. When I read the ingredients now, as an adult, I'm not sure I would feed my kids these crackers on a regular basis - especially covered in butter, as we used to do when I was kid! However, as an occasional treat or snack, I really don't see any more harm with these than I do with the occasional cookie.What disappointed me the most (and the reason I subtracted one star), is the deceiving packaging, in my opinion. Most people will assume that one "fresh stack" is equal to one serving of graham crackers, and perhaps feel okay with putting one stack in a child's lunch. NOT SO!! Each "fresh stack" consists of TWO servings. So, the combined calories alone, equal 250. That's not including the fat, carbs, etc. I really do wish Nabisco had packaged these as single servings. For me, eating 4 crackers was enough (a single serving). Attempting to eat all 8 crackers would have been too much, but there is no way to re-seal the "fresh stack" packaging once it has been opened. It was really disappointing in a product I otherwise found totally satisfying.

column9: Great taste and texture from an old standard, but....
column10: These are pretty much the same honey graham crackers from long ago, with that great grainy flavor with a hint of honey. They are in a smaller size. Fine, I never had much of a problem with the original size, but whatever makes us happy. I guess this size will help keep portions wrapped and fresh. I just wish Nabisco would dispense with one old custom: using partially hydrogenated oil(PHVO). Yes, if they do use it, it is a small enough quantity to meet the requirement of being listed as zero grams of trans fats, but it adds up. In this case, this product may or may not contain PHVO. So, it is obvious that PHVO is not absolutely necessary to produce this product, nor is it an economic necessity. So, we should ask ourselves, since we know it isn't good for us(that is why the amount present is listed on the nutritional panel)and is totally artificial, why does Nabisco have to deal with it? Don't they CARE?Let's keep in mind that the CEO of Nabisco make lots and lots of dough(sorry for the pun), so maybe they should be replaced with someone who can manage to pay attention to producing the best possible product for the best possible price. I would be happy to take the job.

I've always liked Honey Maid graham crackers--they' just delicious. These snack stacks make them easily portable in snack sized portions. This is especially valuable if you have kids, or if you don't eat graham crackers in large quantities. These are a win/win in my book.

column9: Perfection in a single size pack.
column10: Love, love, love Honey Maid Grahams and this is the perfect thing for my household since I'm the only one who eats them.  The small packages are great and perfect for the one sitting without having the rest of the package get stale.  It will work lovely this summer when it's humid out.  Nothing worse than soft soggy grahams cause of the humidity.These are also perfect size for lunch boxes.  Great healthy snack for the kids and adults alike in perfect size pack that doesn't need to be stuck in a baggie getting all mushed up.  I don't know what else I can say to being lucky enough to live in an age where things are making life so much easier.  You gotta try these.
The little portion packs were great for smores at a campout and for putting into lunches without the need to open up the box and reseal it to keep the crackers fresh. I would definitly buy this again

OK, these are graham crackers.  Same ones you've always had, they're fine.The good thing about these is that they are packaged as squares, not the larger two-square rectangle. What's the big deal?  They are easier to take a few to snack on.  No more breaking the big cracker in two and letting the rest of the package get stale.I just wonder why it took so long to package these correctly.If you're using a recipe -- use the old box.  If you are munching them straight, buy this package.

column9: Not Bad for a mass Produced Product
column10: Honey Maid Fresh Stacks, 12.2-Ounce (Pack of 6)Honey Maid Fresh Stacks: Honey GrahamsI have not had a Graham Cracker in years, maybe not even in decades. As a kid I liked to eat them in several ways; dunked in milk, or broken up and placed in a bowl with milk poured over them like a cereal, with fruit; strawberries, raspberries or grapes, but especially eaten right out of the box and spread with butter. My other graham delight was chocolate covered Graham Crackers.Given all of that nostalgia, I decided that of the various products offered me to review on the Vine Program, I would try the graham crackers. I had stopped eating packaged cookies years ago, except, now and then an all natural cookie product from one of the all natural bakeries or grocers. I made that decision because everything else seemed to have a multitude of questionable, unsavory or toxic sounding ingredients, and because one of my standards with baked goods is, I usually eat nothing that contains more than four or five ingredients.I was not happy about the Cotton Seed oil, let alone this partially Hydrogenated Cotton seed oil. However, 15 or 16 ingredients for a prepackaged, mass produced, eatable product and with only three questionable ingredients, is not bad at all. Usually, the ingredients on bakery goods number as many as 30-50 many of which sound more like solvents or gasoline derivatives than healthy food products. Normally, I avoid eating any product which has more than four to five ingredients.The Grahams also had fairly decent Nutrition support for a high volume manufactured product. There was no Cholesterol, minimum fats of all kinds, and 25-30 grams of dietary fiber, along with 300-375 grams of carbohydrates.The ingredients in the making of the Grahams were: Unbleached enriched Flour,  (Far better than bleached flour), a variety of vitamins, Graham Flour-Whole Grain wheat, sugar, (Far better than High Fructose Corn Syrup) Soybean or, and here is an ingredient I was unhappy about - Partially Hydrogenated Cotton seed oil). There was also honey, leavening (Baking soda and/or calcium Phosphate), salt, "artificial flavors"- (Another of my least favorite things to eat). Thus, there were only a few ingredients, which did not meet my standardsI opened the box of Honey Maid Fresh Stacks: Honey Grahams and tried one right out of the box, and three with spread with butter, washed down with a glass of water (I no longer drink milk). The one without the butter tasted well but was a bit dry, hence the butter. In both cases, the crackers were as crunchy as I remembered them to be. I am a sucker for crunchiness in almost every product made with any sort of flour or potato product; pizza crusts, toast, French Fries, etc.The taste of the Grahams, was surprisingly good. They were crunchy, flavorful, and when spread with a thin layer of butter, you wanted to keep eating them.So, if the few ingredients I mentioned as downers does not alarm you and you like Grahams, I suppose you could give them a try, or you could buy an all natural graham cracker at an all natural bakery and compare taste and ingredientsFor a widely distributed, mass produced product, I give it a 3.5 out of 5, on the overall cookie Rating scale, and a 3.75 on the natural ingredients scale. As far as taste goes, I would give it 3.75 - 4 stars. Not bad for such a product.

What nice about these is that the crackers are in six nicely portioned packs so that the rest do not go stale so quickly. They of course tasted great as well but then I am not a graham cracker afficionado so my opinion in this case may not be the valuable here.

Well, the crackers are the same as you get in any package, but this is suppose to be a more convenient, "fresh"er way of using them. They are wrapped in brown plastic wrap and all the corners are broken, some of the crackers are in pieces. I think there are too many in a pack anyway, 8 crackers is too many to put in a lunch box for a 4 year old. I'd like to see a little sturdier wrapping so the crackers don't break up so easily in the box; and in the lunch box they become a total mess. I'd prefer to buy the regular box of crackers and put the amount I think is right into the divided plastic lunch container I use for his lunches.I even think it's too many for us grownups to enjoy at one time and sort of forces you to eat all 8 crackers in the pack, by suggestion, or risk putting a couple back to get even more broken up.As for the product itself, I love them.

Tasty, not too bad on health, and great for a snack to throw in your bag. I particularly liked how the crackers came in little packs with small strips of 8. They were a great snack to munch on while I was at work and I didn't feel guilty about it. I would definitely recommend to others to try. Filling, lightly sweet without being overly-sugared (I hate when foods are loaded with sugar since I'm into healthy eating), portable, and scrumptious.

"Mmm, mmm, good" may be the copyrighted slogan for Campbell's soups, but it could also apply to Honey Maid's delicious crackers. They are a perfect snack with coffee or milk, and these Fresh Stacks are very convenient if, like me, you usually skip breakfast because the time you might spend eating is devoted to getting a few extra winks of sleep instead. These crackers are just the right size for those whose stomachs just can't tolerate a big breakfast, anyway. Of course, like almost any good food, Honey Maid Fresh Snacks are good at any time of the day or night.

One of my pet peeves about buying graham crackers is how fast they spoil in those big wrapped packages. These "fresh stacks" packs take care of that. Still a little much to pack for a snack or in a lunchbox, they still are smaller amount. No need to break these in two, creating piles of crumbs.These packs contain smaller sized pieces, smaller stacks and a fresher product. Its totally worth the change.

I wasn't sure about this product. I figured it was a way to reduce the portions / increase the price. Well, actually, we like the smaller packets. No more open packets stuffed in ziplock baggies, stacking up in the cupboard. My husband actually went out and bought his own supply for his office.Same great taste; updated, convenient, on the go packets.As my 3-year-old grandson says: Good job!

column9: New Packaging for an old favorite
column10: These are the same graham crackers that have been around forever - if you made smores, they were probably on these graham crackers.  If you bought graham crackers and told your kids they were cookies, they were probably these graham crackers.I mean really, graham crackers are an awesome snack for little ones, and aren't so bad for us grownups to snack on either (at least in comparison to some of the other stuff we jam our faces with)So what's so new?  Um... well now the crackers are stacked up and wrapped into different stacks so you only have to open one stack at a time... this keeps the rest of them fresh I guess.  I don't know that it's worthy of a huge marketing campaign or a higher price, but it IS nice to have fresh graham crackers.

column9: A new update for an old favorite....
column10: What's the nicest thing you can say about a cookie?  It's crisp? It's not too sweet?  It's made with graham flour?  It's a Honey Maid graham cracker?Just when I thought they couldn't be improved on, someone thought of small packets to retain freshness.I confess:  I too often eat grahams and milk at night and this is ideal.  Of course others may have better eating habits, but for those on the go or lunch boxes, or midnight sneaking, er, snacks, this new packaging of an old favorite works for me.The bottom line:  Five stars.  It's a great packaging idea for an old favorite; it should please those who love graham crackers.

Our family has always enjoyed the Honey Maid Graham Crackers, but would never eat a whole stack at one time. This usually meant that many of them would go stale and ended up in the trash. This new packaging is just the right size. No waste. Even if the pricing for this is a little higher, it means much less waste so is still more economical.

Ok. These are good - really good. Even better, the small packages keep the remaining ones fresh after you gobble down an entire package. The smaller packages have less calories than the bigger packages in the standard product. What a clever diet idea. This way we secret snackers have the satisfaction of destroying a whole pack, and the smug feeling that comes from fooling yourself into eating less.  They make excellent lunch snacks for the kiddies - just the right size.

When I open up a new bag of Honey Maid Graham Crackers, before I know it, the bag is completely empty.  These Fresh Stacks gives you the same Honey Maid taste in smaller packages, basically a original size split in half, which makes it easier to curtail the amount you eat in one sitting.  There are six sheets in six packages in every box.  One complaint is the original flavor is a little bland and I wish Honey Maid would release the smaller size for their cinnamon cracker product, which I prefer, too.

column9: new smaller packs make it easier for us to take them on the go
column10: My 7 year old son loves Honey Maid Fresh Snacks.  The new smaller packs make it easier for us to take them on the go.  Now we don't have to always repack his snacks into a zip bag.  He is always hungry, and Honey Maid Snacks are a better alternative than convenience store candy.

If you're a fan of graham crackers and also have kids or a need to take snacks with you, this is a good way to go.  The crackers themselves are half the size of the normal (2 pieces vs 4) and then are packaged in smaller packs as well.  The smaller packs are a good size for easy on the go snacking.  That's the only difference between these and the originals.  So basically, you're getting more packaging inside the box.  I won't speak to whether or not that's good for the environment but it's definitely convenient.

The taste remains unchanged over the years. The packaging has been changed for the better, but you will find the same taste that made you love these crackers over the years. Dip 'em in milk for the extra yum.

You don't have to twist my arm to eat graham crackers. Some are better than others; Honey Maid are pretty near the top of the pile. This edition, which separates single servings into neat packets, is convenient and handy. I took one packet a night to work and was pleased that they were quick to hand. Sure, you can package your own; but as a time-saver, I appreciated these. I'll be looking for them to be produced in Cinnamon next.

column9: Same great graham cracker taste packaged for freshness
column10: The Fresh Stacks are half-sized graham crackers packaged eight half-sized crackers to a stack. This new way of packaging them will presumably keep them fresher because you have fewer crackers in each package so they will sit in the opened package for less time before they're eaten. The taste is the same yummy Honey Maid graham cracker taste as the traditionally sized longer rectangle graham crackers. Interestingly, I checked a package of the traditional long Honey Maid graham crackers and high fructose corn syrup is listed as one of the ingredients but it is not one of the ingredients for the Fresh Stack graham crackers. If you are concerned about limiting HFCS in your diet, the Fresh Stacks are the way to go.

Some people may not realize that carrying around large bulky packages of your favorite snack is so last century!Honey Maid Fresh Stacks is modern, convenient and less wasteful ( as in, most throw out stale or unused product -- except my neighbor, but that's another review. ).  Honey Maid Fresh Stacks still have that crispy Honey Graham goodness and the scent wafting from the newly opened product can still invoke fond  memories of a very happy childhood -- it's just been down sized, a bit, to fit a modern lifestyle.Honey Maid Fresh Stacks are just a really smart choice. 'nuf said.  Highly Recommended! --Katharena Eiermann, 2011

I have to say I really like what they did with these graham crackers. It's such a simple thing that works very well for me. I'm use to graham crackers being very long and a lot of times I don't want to eat the whole graham cracker, but once I take it out I have to eat it, because I don't want to put a partial graham cracker back into the box. Well, with these graham crackers, they are sized to the perfect size when I just want a small portion. But I do have to say that it seems to taste slightly different and my friend noticed, too, but it's still good.

column4: Penny Pinching Polly "Check out my website fo...
column10: I love the Honey Maid Fresh Stacks!  Being a big fan of Ritz Crackers, 12-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6), I couldn't wait to try the Honey Maid version!  I was not disappointed.  We like to take graham crackers with us on trips to the zoo, the park, and other places where healthy treats are hard to come by.  I can keep a Fresh Stack in my tote bag, and not have to worry!  There's just enough in there for a snack for myself, my daughter, and a friend so I'm not wasting half a sleeve of crackers by them going stale before we need another snack on the go.Each cracker tastes as fresh as the first one, even if you're like us and it takes 6 weeks for you to finish an entire box.

column9: My favorite crackers in a perfect size!
column10: I've always loved Honey Maid but just not the size. Now they come in the most perfect size of little squares. The taste is great as always with some whole heat and honey in them. The best part was that the stacks were also individually wrapped so you don't have to open the whole box at the same time. Love the crackers and the concept!

column9: Yummy crackers, perfect size, for two people!
column10: These crackers are a perfect size-the larger ones crack, and you sometimes end up with uneven pieces. They are great for snacks (we had some with Cinnamon Swirl Peanut butter,and the cracker complimented it perfectly!). Since they are in smaller packages,they are not likely to become stale as quickly as the larger packages. For crusts, these smaller packages are probably not suited, as it may take a while to unwrap them, as opposed to larger packages. The small packages also allow for convenient snacking on the go. The flavor and texture are perfect!

column9: Fresh Stacks - Where Have You Been My Entire Graham-Cracker-Eating Life?
column10: I grew up eating Honey Maid Graham Crackers as an after dinner dessert snack.  My parents convinced me that it was even better than cake and to this day, I still crave a tall glass of milk and some Honey Maid Graham Crackers (never found another brand that was quite as yummy.)  They're still delicious, and as far as I can tell, the taste is exactly the same, but this packaging solves most of my biggest peeves with the crackers before.I no longer have to figure out how to break the thing in half perfectly along the lines to get it to fit into my glass of milk so that I don't lose half of the soggy goodness in the bottom of my cup.  These are the perfect size for dipping in milk and even better for Smores!  No more fumbling to break a cracker into the perfect Smore sized square while holding a flaming marshmallow!  Lastly, the stacks are individually sealed, so you can eat an entire stack without having the rest of the box go stale before you can finish the rest.  If there was one improvement I would suggest it would be to have the "serving size" be the same as a single "fresh stack" but since this isn't marketed as a calorie counting type of product, it doesn't really matter.  I'm hooked on these and since the Honey Maid graham crackers are still a treat for me, I'll be buying these instead of the normal rectangular crackers from now on. Yum!

column4: J. Thompson "Janet's Treasures, a little of e...
column10: I loved how these were packaged! I put them in my daughter's and husband's lunches one day. They both loved the taste and the way they were packaged. I like the flavor of them. They even tasted better than the regularly packaged ones. I would recommend these to people I know just for the fact that the packaging makes them easy to pack and go!

I absolutely love graham crackers. However, I hate them when they lose their fresh taste. This packaging is a pretty good idea to keep them fresh at home, but also makes them more convenient for taking to work or school. The crackers have the same excellent quality -- so, what's not to like?

column9: Convenient size, but not convenient packaging
column10: 3-stars for the packaging. The crackers are, of course, excellent. Someone was on to something by putting these in snack size packages. However, usually when you eat something on the go you will eat a little now and a little later. What you need is resealable packaging. These "fresh stack" packs come in the regular old brown glued plastic wrap. You still have to provide the zip-lock bag yourself. At least these fit in a zip-lock bag easier than the full size stacks.

I liked the taste of these cookies and they reminded me of my childhood.However, these are packaged different.  They are sealed in a plastic wrapper, not the wax type paper from a long time ago.  I am guessing that this keeps the graham crackers fresh tasting for a long time.They were crispy and had a decent taste.  My only complaint was that several of the packages were damaged and the crackers were crumbs.

Honey Maid Fresh Stacks are the same tasty graham crackers you've always gotten, but now they're in 6 packs of squares, instead of 3 packs of the longer, rectangular crackers.There's not change to the crackers themselves, they just broke the rectangles of 4 crackers into squares of 2 and wrapped them up in little square stacks, but the 6 smaller stacks actually make it pretty convenient as a grab-n-go kinda thing.I like using them for lunches. They're a great size for that kind of thing.

I have always enjoyed this type of cracker so I was happy to have a chance to review this one.  I was very impressed with the packaging. I can't tell you how many times different crackers or cookies have gone stale on me because they were not closed properly. This will not happen with this product.  They have several packs inside  with just the right amount of crackers to enjoy at one sitting, or they are perfect to pop in your purse and take along with you. The flavor and texture were great. They were very fresh and none of them were stale. That is such a major factor in my opinion. I will definitely look for these in my local store. A very good product in all ways that I gladly recommend.

column9: Great concept but a terrible waste of packaging
column10: First off the crackers are very, very fresh. So that being the intent, they were wonderful. There's six little packs in a box and each of the individual packages is about enough for an 8 year old or a 6 year old to enjoy during snack time. The 6 year old had a bit of a problem with opening the packaging, but the 8 year old was fine.Also helpful to note, it's the perfect size for a midnight snack for the 37-year-old.The crackers are tightly packed and we didn't have a single broken cracker in the bunch, and did I mention how fresh they were?I had to dock one star because of waste though. While I like the idea of throwing these in the kid's lunches as a snack pack, they are a bit big for their lunch kits, and frankly there's a lot of excess garbage that is created from a box of these.That coupled with the price, it's just a better deal to buy regular graham crackers and put those in lunches. So my environment-guilt precludes me from stocking up on these for kids lunches.But I see where they're going with it and I like the idea of it - it just feels wasteful.

I have long been a fan of Honey Maid graham crackers.  They are just about my favorite snack food for me and the kids.  In the past, I would break them into halves so that they could fit conveniently in whatever bag I was using for lunches or outings.  On top of that, I would have to remove them from their sealed bags into a Ziploc bag, which always seemed redundant.  Now, I can just move them from the box into whatever bag I am using and it is super fast and convenient--the perfect snack to grab quickly when heading out the door.

Everything about these Honey Maid graham crackers are identical to the ones you're used to.  There's nothing different aside from the fact that they're just divided in half.  They have yet to come up with a way for the crackers to not crumble inside the packaging.  In fact, the brown plastic packaging is still the same.  I thought the crackers were going to come in clear cellophane packs how they're represented on the box, but they're not.Don't get me wrong: I love these graham crackers and have since I was a kid.  Nothing will change the fact that I love the taste and the childhood memories that go along with them.  The reason for the three stars is due to the lack of innovation.  You can still buy the old school packs and break them in half and you have virtually the same product.

The same great Honey Maid graham crackers that I grew up with have gotten even better.  While the same great graham cracker taste is there, it is no longer a brick of a package.The new Honey Maid graham cracker "Fresh Stacks" packaging makes these way easier to enjoy and leads to less waste.In the olden days of the graham cracker brick, you'd open the package, have a couple of their rectangles, maybe even snap them in half to make them squares, and then put the brick back...only to have the rest go stale.Or maybe you'd get a Ziploc baggie to hold the opened package of remaining crackers.  (More packaging needed!)With the new "Fresh Stacks," you're getting 6 graham squares in their own wrap.  6 squares...now that is a perfect snack.  Add a sealed cup of strawberries and this new dynamic duo can be thrown into your lunchbag for an afternoon snack.Going camping and want to make s'mores?  Throw a couple of individual packs, marshmallows, and chocolate into your camping bucket, and you are set.The same thing goes for if you need to break a couple of packs down to make a graham cracker crust.Simple, easy, and perfect to stash in my cupboard.  I am in love with the new "Fresh Stacks!"

column9: Why did it take so long?
column10: Every box of graham crackers that has ever entered my house has ended up with many or most of the crackers broken.  The long crackers are just too hard to handle without breaking them.  Are we just too klutzy in my house?  Maybe, I dunno.  And what's the point?  Doesn't everybody break them from rectangles into squares to use them, anyway?What I do know is that these "Fresh Stacks" are the solution to our breakage problem.  They taste just as good, very equal to every other graham crackers - nothing special, better or worse, there.  But they stay squares, without being broken!  It's a minor miracle!The squares are much more convenient to use.  Much easier for s'mores (we have a lot of bonfires in the backyard).  Much less breakage, much fewer crumbs or waste.These "Fresh Stacks" are a nice thing that make life just a touch easier and better at our house.

column9: everything a graham cracker should be
column10: My kids munched through this box rather quickly, as they have discovered the joy of making marshmallow smores in the microwave. The crackers are packed in small waxed paper stacks, so if you don't eat the whole box in a week, as we did, the crackers in unopened packs will stay fresh longer.  The crackers do contain hydrogenated cottonseed oil, which we generally try to avoid, but otherwise we rate them very highly.  They are crunchy,sweet, and everything a graham cracker should be.  I like the handy small sized packages, which are a good size for 2-3 kids to share.

If you like the regular size Honey Maid graham crackers, then you will love these handy little snack packs.  They are the same great tasting grahams as the regular size, but wrapped in smaller, easy to grab and go, sealed packs.  You get six individually wrapped packs per box.  Each pack has a stack of eight grahams measuring 2.5" x 2.5", each graham scored in the middle for easy breaking/dunking, although I prefer to dunk them whole by the corners.  Now all I need to do is figure out is how to take my glass of milk with me on the go!  Yummy!

Great idea.  Individual packets of graham crackers just perfect for snacking.  Highly recommend.  If you've got kids these are a must.  If you snack in bed like me then this is far less messy.  Good idea who's time has come.

column9: Same delicious graham crackers, with less mess and breakage
column10: They're Honey Maid Graham Crackers. You've probably eaten them before. Slightly grahamy, delicious, and a huge mess since they're typically about 2x the size that any rational human wants to hold and eat.Thankfully, those marketing geniuses over at Nabisco heard your cries, and released Fresh Stacks. They're graham crackers pre broken in half. That's it. They come in smaller packs with enough crackers for a really hungry person, or two slightly less hungry people. I appreciate that, since they're not getting stale or gummy like the normal ones do when I can't eat 15 oz in one sitting.For normal people, you'll love them. If you're Andre the Giant sized, stick with the original.

column9: Crispy, Tastey Crackers on the Go!
column10: I've always been a fan of graham crackers.  They're a light, tasty snack that I can stash in my desk drawer at work.  But keeping an entire box on-hand can be too much of a good thing.  As addicting as they are, it would be easy to eat one right after another until half the box is gone!.  These individually wrapped packages are the answer to that temptation.  Toss one (or two!) packages into your bag and head out the door. Carrying one package with you, you'll never eat more than 6 crackers, reducing the temptation to over-indulge! The crackers themselves are nice and crispy.  The individual packaging keeps the crackers fresh.  The only thing that would make these better would be if the package was resealable.  Altho most people will eat all 6 crackers in one sitting, I like to nibble on them throughout the evening (I actually didn't my package the first night and had to paper clip the package closed!)  These are also an excellent snack choice for moms on the go. Toss a package or two into your diaper bag or purse and you'll always have a snack on hand for your toddlers or children.  No more begging for a cookie or candy bar with Graham Crackers on hand!

column9: Too Subtle - Not Great for Spreads
column10: I like to snack on crackers but the taste was altogether too subtle - more sweet than salty, which makes it less likely to pair well with cheese or some other kind of salty spread. The crackers were also fragile and crumbly - not that most crackers are hard as rocks,  but there is too much air in it. I guess they're meant to dunk in coffee or tea, rather than dipped in a spread. I was not that impressed and will go back to my Ritz crackers.

column9: Really Convenient For Those With Young Kids
column10: I love these little snack pack sized graham crackers.  As a mom of two toddlers (2 years and 3 years respectively), graham crackers are a staple in all situations - particularly during car rides.  However in most cases, I don't need 8 full sheets of graham crackers to give to my kids - I'd probably only need about half of that.  This is where the brilliance of the Honey Maid Fresh Stacks come in: each pack contains 8 half sheets of graham crackers.  I don't have to spend any time opening a pack and putting half the crackers into a ziploc bag which will probably be forgotten in the back of the cupboard.  I don't have to worry about graham crackers going stale because my husband tossed some crackers in a ziploc for the kids, but didn't bother sealing the remaining crackers up before tossing them back into the cracker box.  I can put a pack of these crackers into my kid's travel backpack or in the car one day, and open it up weeks later when I actually need the crackers because the kids are starving.  Brilliant, I tell you.While I'll still buy the conventional 3 stacks per box type graham crackers (we can eat a lot of graham crackers), I think I'll be picking up the Fresh Stacks for our day trips - it's so convenient!  Highly recommended!

Graham crackers are always popular with our kids.  However the normal size packages often go stale before we finish them.  These smaller packages are great for our little kids.  The half-size crackers are a better size for them, and the smaller packages ensure that all the crackers are gone before they go stale.

column9: On old favorite, in new packaging
column10: Truthfully these Honey Maid Fresh Stacks couldn't have arrived at a better time.  Our two-year old Grandson was visiting recently and these became his favorite snack. Each and every time the pantry was opened we heard "Cracker, please?".  What I appreciated most besides it being the same graham cracker I remembered, was the new packaging. Many times I have opened a larger pack only to not finish them and end up finding stale crackers the next time. With these smaller packs we are more likely to finish a pack, but if we don't they easily fit into a ziploc sandwich bag. The are also PERFECT for smores; just grab a pack of crackers, some chocolate and a bag of marshmallows! You can even make them easy (and fun!) at home with this: Microwavable S'Mores Maker.  The only negative about these would be the cost.  Being a new product here on Amazon, they are a bit higher priced than most would want to pay.  If they were to be included in Subscribe & Save, then it would be a bit more reasonable.  My suggestion for now would be to look locally, I found them in my local grocery store for about $1.15 less per box.

It's about time that we get an easier way to enjoy our Graham Crackers!These smaller packages with squares rather than rectangular crackers make both serving and storing easier.  One pack was enough for one day's snack for my kids and I didn't worry about the remaining ones becoming stale.  Yeah!  I also liked the smaller size which fits in a bowl when the bigger side did not.  Same great taste with more convenience which comes in handy when you're a mom of 3 kids and on the go.

column9: Great for moms on the go
column10: My son LOVES graham crackers. In fact, they are a staple at my house. These fresh stacks are a great size for throwing in a purse or diaper bag. The smaller packages keep the crackers fresh and are great for busy moms on the go. We've really enjoyed them at my house. My son gives them two thumbs up! I keep a pack on me at all times. :-)

column9: The Way It Should Have Always Been!!
column10: These graham crackers have an extreme advantage! They are packaged better than any other. These little blocks of 8 square grahams (which equals 2 servings according to the Nutrition Facts label), stay fresh and unbroken, and are very easy to use. The packs are small enough for a lunch box, desk drawer, or purse, and have perfect portions for eating in one sitting without having to worry about what you will do with leftovers. For those of you who love peanut butter on grahams, you could take along one of the little Jif To-Go peanut butter cups and you have a perfect little meal/snack! This Honey Maid Grahams Fresh Stacks packaging is so long overdue for graham crackers. It's perfect all around, and it goes without saying that these grahams themselves are a tried & true classic that are always delicious!

I grew up eating Honey Maid graham crackers. I've tried the other brands but, for me, none compare to Honey Maid. The idea behind the Honey Maid Fresh Stacks is clever! They are the perfect size for my lunch sack. Also, for mom's with small children they're fun sized!The only issue I found with these crackers is that they aren't the same consistency as the Honey Maid graham crackers I've eaten in the past. Maybe the batch I got was not so fresh? These were crumbly and dry. I'll use these with peanut butter to see if it can overcome the dryness of the product.Great idea and possibly better if bought via the grocery.
The familiar buttery graham cracker taste is there. I appreciate the packaging. The small individual packets prevent breaking and help keep the crackers fresh.

Graham crackers are a staple on every camping trip, but for some reason I don't think of eating them in between trips.  The problem with graham crackers is that they are messy (lots of crumbs) and once I open a package, I can never eat them all before they go stale so it feels like a waste of money.This product at least solves the second half of my problem.  Each little package has two servings of crackers that are half the size of the "normal" crackers.  I don't mind that it's two servings in each bag.  I share, or save the second half for tomorrow, or eat the whole dang thing myself.That all being said, often the price of smaller serving bags is much higher than the normal product, which would not make it worthwhile for me.  If the price was somewhat comparable, especially considering I would probably throw half of a regular box away, I would absolutely buy these crackers on a regular basis.

Some products shouldn't need reviews because they just make so much sense.  Who doesn't love Graham Crackers?  Have you ever met a toddler whose eyes didn't light up when you handed him or her a honey graham?  My 3 year old loves them, and it's always been difficult to pack them: with the usual large packages, you have to put some in a ziplock baggie or something like that to prevent them from going stale. This new "fresh stacks" packaging has just about the perfect amount in one wrapper - throw one of these packages in your backpack, give a few to your kids, have one yourself, and nothing goes stale. It's the perfect packaging for a perfect snack. There's honestly not a single thing wrong with this product.

column9: Graham Crackers Cut in Half and Packaged in Smaller Packs
column10: These are exactly the same Graham Crackers Nabisco sells in the traditional rectangular form, but cut in half. The smaller pack size is nice if you use them slowly as there is less chance for the unused crackers to get stall and soft. Other than that, they are just like the originals. I wouldn't pay more per ounce for these than for the traditional ones unless you frequently end up with stale, soggy graham crackers due to slow use rates.

while these tasted very good, i found them a little crispier than other graham cracker i've had - and i liked it. really like the packaging too, half size individual serving type. conveninet and easy to use or carry.i recommend these and will buy them.

Brilliant packaging! Rarely do we go through an entire package of the regular sized cracker, which means I have to find a ziplock baggie, and make sure they get eaten before they turn from crispy to soft.With these fresh stacks I get just the right amount, no worrying about them going stale, and they are so much easier to toss into the bag for on the go snacking. Plus, of course, the delicious honey maid taste. Yum!

Nabisco has always been one of my favorite brands, and these Honey Grahams are one of my favorite cookie/crackers. These still have the same fresh, crispy, and wonderful flavor, but the size and packaging is different.I like that these are packaged in 2"x4" individual packs. They are great for lunchboxes, office desk, or just a quick snack. I like them at work with a cup of hot tea, and sometimes when I don't have time for a real lunch, they are great with peanut butter or Nutella - just excellent!There are 6 "fresh stacks" per box, and each one is considered 2 servings, so that is the only thing one needs to be careful of. It is too easy to open and eat one entire snack pack, which is 250 calories, so be careful to watch how any you eat at once or just share a pack!

There's nothing worse than a soggy, stale graham cracker.And there's nothing better than a fresh, crunchy graham cracker.That said, as one of the few "non-mom" reviewers, I think that the new Honey Maid Fresh Stacks are a brilliant idea for those of us who really don't feel the need to measure our every bite and count our calories but who enjoy a great treat and not have to dread the next time we dig into the box, only to be sorely disappointed by the lackluster of an aged, flaccid graham cracker that even peanut butter can't rescue.The new fresh stacks are exactly that: FRESH. Delicious and crunchy and Honey Maid is still the best graham cracker out there - accept no substitutions!I will buy this product just based on the fact that I have an option other than the longer "sheet" crackers which, unless you down an entire pack (this is where I WOULD count the calories), continue to disappoint.Indulge your Inner Kindergarten-er.Now, where's my peanut butter?

column9: The Convenience of Honey Maid Fresh Stacks
column10: The Honey Maid Fresh Stacks package of 6 package of 12 crackers is a handy idea for moms on the go with toddlers, working folk who want a nutritious snack, and just about anyone who needs to keep small amounts of snack items handy.  A distinct advantage of this form of packaging would be redction of waste.  Have you ever eaten a stale graham cracker?  Once was enough for me!  My only concern was in regard to pricing for this new form of packaging; does the difference in price per unit justify itself?  It does for me.

column9: Leaving opened crackers in the box is a thing of the past!
column10: I love graham crackers and I think this new packaging is a great idea. High five, Honey Maid! And while this packaging remains a great idea, there are both advantages and disadvantages.The advantages. Smaller portion-sized stacks for one. If you know of the "regular" Honey Maid boxes, in one of the stacks you get a bunch of crackers that you can't finish in one sitting, and often they're stale when you go back to them another day. Here, the crackers are halved and a hungry eater can easily finish a stack off in one sitting, so leaving opened crackers in the box is a thing of the past! Sometimes I'll even have two stacks. And they taste great fresh. These are also good to take on the go, so stuff 'em in your coat pocket or purse and a snack is just inches away at all times.The disadvantages. Graham crackers are brittle as we all know, so if they're shipped there's a good chance they might break or fall apart before arriving in your hungry arms. I'm going to look for them in stores instead of ordering online.
These are fairly typical graham crackers, which I enjoyed well enough.  Conveniently, they are wrapped in small packs, which is nice for packing lunches, etc.

column9: Nice improvement to use smaller packages!
column10: Always a great product but the Fresh Stacks are handy for those of that need them to stay fresh for a longer consumption period.

This was an excellent idea.  I am now a grandma and I have bought MANY packages of Honey Maid graham crackers over the years - and it has always been a frustration that they often go soft before they can be used up (unless we had a playdate with lots of little ones eating graham crackers!). This way of packaging makes so much sense.  The packages were easy to open and everything was completely fresh.

I always have graham crackers in the house because they make a great snack alone or spread with some peanut butter but inevitably I end up with some stale crackers before I can eat all the ones in the larger packs.  Problem solved with these fresh stacks!  Even if you don't eat the whole stack at once (which I don't recommend because although it's a small stack it's still pretty loaded with calories) The small size of the crackers make them easy to store in a zip lock bag.  They're the perfect size for tossing in my bag if I'm going to be out all day and want to have a snack with me.

I've always liked graham crackers, but these really pump it up a notch!  The honey flavor makes them fairly sweet, and absolutely delicious.  They're great for satisfying a sweet tooth craving.  And as the only person in my house who eats graham crackers, I appreciate the "fresh stacks"-- little square packages of 8 squares of graham crackers (think half the size of a regular graham cracker).  This means less time for them to sit in an unsealed package before being eaten, so they stay fresher longer.  Because nutrition is also important to me, I took a quick glance at the ingredient list which revealed that they have used unbleached flour as well as whole grain wheat flour-- no bleach in sight, hooray!  I'm not thrilled that they did use partially hydrogenated oil, but I guess you can't have everything especially in something that tastes this good.  Overall this is an excellent product with great taste and mostly wholesome ingredients, in packaging that will keep it fresh.  Highly recommended!

My toddler and I love graham crackers, but I stopped buying them because they would usually get stale before we could eat them all. I love these smaller packages. The box comes with 6 packs. Each pack only has 8 crackers (one serving size is 4 crackers). No more ripped wrapping and crumbs everywhere. The graham crackers taste great too! (:

I love graham crackers but it seemed like the packaging hadn't changed in the last 50 years!You open the box, you remove one of the 3 sealed packs, take out 2-3 crackers and then you have to find a way to seal up the rest and remember to eat them before they get stale.Not with Honey Maid Fresh Stacks!^ smaller sealed packs in each box gives you the option to throw a whole pack in your purse, diaper bag or lunch sack for some good snacking all day. Plenty for 1 person and some to share, none going stale on the pantry shelf while you're wishing you had them in your drawer at work!Great idea for updating a favorite snack!

These tasty graham crackers are crispy, not too sweet, and a serving of 4 squares has 130 calories.  They come packaged in 6 stack packs, and the calorie count for the whole pack (8 squares) is 250.The flavor brought back childhood memories of a glass of milk and a couple graham crackers after school, and then out to play. In other words, the flavor hasn't changed much in the MANY years since I was a kid :>)The new packaging makes them convenient to take along with you, either to work, or school, or wherever.  The only drawback I see to the packaging is that you might eat the entire stack, since the package isn't easily resealed.Some reviews have mentioned their fat (from cottonseed oil) and sugar content, and I will add here that they also contain a good amount of sodium (170mg for 4 squares, 340mg for 8 squares). But I think that, as with all snack foods, you have to read labels, not overdo, and make choices based on your individual dietary needs/restrictions.For me, these were a healthy enough choice for a delicious snack.

column4: Lonnie E. Holder "The Review's the Thing"
column10: Honey Maid graham crackers have been a family treat for decades.  However, one of the problems with graham crackers is what to do after eating several grahams, but the package is not completely empty.  In years past, the answer is that the grahams seem to absorb moisture and lose their crisp texture.Nabisco's answer to this problem is to reduce the amount and size of grahams in one package.  Now the grahams fit better into a lunch box or bag.  In addition, if you use half a package for one lunch, which is a single serving, the other half is ready for the next lunch or a snack.  If you forget to use the other four grahams in a package, then only four lose their crispness.Though I applaud Nabisco's attempt to increase packaging effectiveness, there are other options, admittedly involving a small amount of labor.  After opening a standard package of Honey Maid grahams at our house, the leftovers go into a sealable storage bag.  The sealable storage bag keeps the grahams from absorbing moisture for a lengthy period.  Though I have yet to do a price comparison, I suspect there is an additional cost for the convenience of the smaller graham squares.  We will probably keep using sandwich sized storage bags to keep leftover standard sized grahams fresh.Good luck!

column9: Same graham crackers; but lunch packable
column10: I'm a big fan of Honey Maid graham crackers, so ordered this product for review.  They are the same graham crackers we know and love, which traditionally have come in large wrapped stacks of cookies.  While I am entirely capable of eating one wrapped stack of cookies at a go, in principle one shouldn't, and they weren't convenient for packing for lunch.  These are wrapped in smaller, more lunch sized packets.  Each packet eight cookies, for a total of 250 calories; a box has six packets.

column9: Classic Honey Maid taste - convenient packaging
column10: We love Honey Maid grahams in our house.  This new packaging is nice.  My kids especially liked that the grahams were in the squares, smaller serving, easier for smores or peanut butter graham sandwich.  I liked that it was a smaller stack, keeping the grahams from getting stale also easier to put in tupperware/rubbermaid container to pack as a snack.  Convenient, delicious product.

column9: The crackers are great, the package doesn't travel well
column10: I was pretty excited to get a full box of these in the mail.  I rarely eat graham crackers anymore, but when I was a kid, I loved them.  These crackers are very good, easy to break apart, good crunchiness and texture, not too sugary, don't have that weird cinnamon stuff that comes off on your hands the old school grahams had and only have 250 calories in the whole fresh stack. I guess they also give calories for 1/2 a stack, maybe I should be doing that than eating a whole stack greedily.My only problem with the crackers is the packaging. It might be that they travelled in the mail, but they don't travel well.  Even in the separate stacks in the box, they crumble and leave a good amount of bits in the bottom of the pack.  Which isn't good if you need to open them, without scissors, on the run or out on the town.  I wouldn't be able to tactfully get these open without getting crumbs all over myself.  The bags have that sort of potato chip bag seal that if you open it the wrong way, all the contents spill out.  I open mine with scissors, but at that point, I might as well just buy a regular box of crackers instead of these.I don't have any kids to feed these to, so I can't tell you about that.  They make a fine snack for me...but then I eat pretty well and hardly ever snack.  I don't think eight crackers is too much, especially if you eat sensible meals during the day.  But I could see the problem in only wanting half the stack.  I haven't opened one of these with my hands yet, maybe I should in my scientific lab (my patio) to make sure if it breaks apart and crumbs fall out all over, some birds will pick them up and I won't have to clean up my kitchen.  I couldn't see being able to seal these well if I opened them by hand and can't because I use scissors to open them.  There would be no way to fold the flap down.

column9: Why didn't someone think of this before!
column10: Graham crackers have always been packaged in larger stacks, which meant that you never used up the whole stack and had to tightly repackage the remaining crackers to prevent spoilage. This new, much more compact packaging avoids waste and has an even better quality: it makes them more portable--a very good thing for graham crackers, which are so soothing to the stomach and digestion.I remember that, when I was pregnant, I always had graham crackers in a drawer at work to settle my stomach. I always take them on trips, since I tend to get every type of travel sickness imaginable (air, sea, car--you name it!)and its something to have in the hotel room between meals or at night that is neither too sweet nor salty. I also use them to accompany medications that have to be taken with food--and this new smaller packaging is just what the doctor ordered.

Way back in the 1800s, Reverend Sylvester Graham was on a crusade.  Disgusted by the "venereal excess" of the youngsters of his day, Graham created a special vegetarian diet with his very own modestly-named Graham bread at its core.  Graham bread, the progenitor of Graham crackers, was made from whole wheat flour...unlike that other, sinful bread.  Graham promised that following his diet would solve a wide variety of disorders, including indigestion, headache, spinal diseases, epilepsy, and insanity. The diet wasn't for everybody - virginity until age 30 was also a requirement.  Still, good old Graham wasn't too far off the mark. He advocated brushing teeth daily, drinking clean water, regular bathing, exercise, and (GASP!) a good night's rest.I feel healthy (and more virtuous!) every time I bite into one of these delightfully pure snacks. Especially when I sprinkle them over a scoop of vanilla ice cream and chocolate sauce with a dollop of whipped cream on top. It's sinfully good!

I have ALWAYS loved Honey Maid's Graham Crackers, so the taste would never be in question, hands down my favorite.I like the fresh stacks! Perfect!  I like being able to take a small package with me to work (with Trader Joe's Peanut Butter Cream Cheese- yum!) to snack on and know that I don't have to open up an entire package and worry about the rest going stale.  I have a 7 year old and these are perfect to throw in my purse and have ready for a snack at any time!

column9: Same great taste in a slightly smaller package
column10: This is the same great product I've enjoyed for years.  The upside is that the stay fresh stacks are a good snack size, and I can just grab one and go.  The downside is that the whole box is somewhat smaller than the normal size grahm cracker box.

I would have to say, for the most part, Honey Maid graham crackers are the epitome of graham crackers.  Are they the best tasting graham crackers out there? Probably not.  Are they the most easily accessible? I would say yes.  In my mind, Honey Maid graham crackers are the ones I use as a frame of reference in my psyche.The graham crackers in this package don't taste any different than the standard honey grahams Honey Maid/Nabisco puts out.  The draw here is the packaging.  The packaging is called "fresh stacks", which translates to smaller size.  The goal here is to induce a longer level of "freshness".  Normally these graham crackers are long, well these crackers are half the size and are enclosed in tiny parcels.I will admit the idea is almost flawless, almost.  The major issue I have is this. A serving size, according to the box is 4 squares/crackers. However, each "fresh stack" package has about 8 squares/crackers in them.  So if you only eat half or a few crackers you are now flirting with your food going stale.  Since it is next to possible to close this "smaller package".  With all the focus and recognition going towards portion control in this country, one would imagine that food companies would adjust their packaging/marketing.  Oh well, the crackers are still very tasty and the concept of the packaging isn't bad.

These graham crackers are packaged in individual servings which makes them very convenient to carry with us to sporting events for an on the go snack without getting crumbs all over the place.  The serving size allows us to open up a pack, eat it all and throw it away without having left overs that end up in crumbs at the bottom of the purse.  Very convenient.  The crackers themselves are delicious and stay fresh until opened.

"Honey Maid", make a great snack product. I have brought them for many years. You can eat them as a snack or them in various recipes. At holiday season I keep them on my shelf for back up incase of running out. I use them on ice cream as a topping or in drinks like smoothies. Just use your imagination, you;ll love them.

The new packaging of the graham crackers into smaller stacks is a great idea.  I always just broke the cracker into two for my son anyway and this saves me that step. Also, there are fewer crackers per package so they stay fresher longer which I also love.The graham cracker is...well...a graham cracker. You've had `em, they're tasty.So, these crackers are primarily about packaging and convenience. The change in packaging is nice (as explained above), but is the convenience fully worth it? Depends on the circumstances I suppose. But they are tasty.

column9: Crackers are still great... 2 stars for packaging
column10: The crackers are the same here as the typical/old boxes except halved.  Still delicious.  But the packaging is not an improvement.The "fresh stacks" are still wrapped in that brown plastic that is really hard to open without ripping it to bits.  Sure there are fewer crackers per package, but you still need to just happen to want exactly how many are in a package to avoid having to pull out a zipper bag for the leftovers.  Now if they had designed the old packages to be reclosable, that would have actually been helpful.

These are pretty standard graham crackers.  They taste good and are moister than some brands that I've tried.  While I enjoyed the taste, I wasn't as fond of the size and packaging.  Rather than being the traditional sized rectangles like most graham crackers, these "fresh stacks" have been cut in half so that they form small squares.  There are eight crackers packaged together in plastic, and each box contains 6 little packs of the crackers.  To me, this doesn't really serve any purpose and accomplishes nothing other than increasing the packaging.  I didn't find the size any more convenient or easy to eat, and I'm really not happy with the extra packaging.  I'll be sticking with the old-fashioned graham crackers.
How do you improve graham crackers?  Put them in more convenient packaging.  What with 8 squares per stack and 6 stacks in a box, this is a great format for traveling, picnics, children's snacks.
