Most of us have liked Graham crackers since we were kids. When you buy a regular box however, unless you finish them quickly, they can go stale. We've tried cookie tins, Tupperware containers, but eventually, the crackers absorb humidity and flavor, so the number one selling point of these crackers is the fact that 8 are wrapped in one stack, enough Nabisco says, for two servings. Well, maybe not, especially if you are making Smores. 4 squares equals about 1 of the old fashioned sized crackers.And I will admit there is a taste difference between these and store brand crackers. I'd recommend this for those with younger kids to pack a lunch, a relatively healthy snack; it's easy enough to toss one of these stacks into a backpack or glove compartment to curb your appetite.

If you're thinking about buying this product, you most likely already love honey maid graham crackers.  (And who doesn't?  They're the best!)  These "fresh packs" are awesome, much better than the traditional packages.  They stay fresher longer, and are great for camping or to stick in your bag for a handy snack for the kids later.Will definitely be buying more!

The latest twist on Honey Graham Crackers by Nabisco is a nifty snack pack version. The 12.2oz box contains six packages of 8 graham crackers. The suggested serving size of 4 squares contains a mere 130 calories. The crackers are flavorful and tasty. For moms-on-the-go, these individually wrapped packages are ideal. For adults, the number of crackers in each package can be troublesome. Four crackers as a snack are plenty. What do you do with the other four if you are at the gym or work? Eat more than you really want, or try to wrap them up for later? Graham Crackers are crumbly. Also, for all those on Gluten-free diets, this snack isn't for you. Overall, I liked this product very much and would recommend buying it.

As a kid (long before many readers were born) these crackers were a staple with our household.  There was only one desert and that was Nabisco Graham Crackers with cold milk and that was the best combination.  Sure there were other brands but this was one we could afford along with the Nabisco Premium Saltines.  At 29 cents a package it was reasonable.  Fast forward to the present and low and behold the almost same formula for Nabisco Graham Crackers exists and in a similar package with a few exceptions.  Today's package is a pack of six with "about" 8 crackers in each package compared to the old package that had about the same number of crackers but each stack had a cracker that was twice the size of today's but the same or similar weight.  All told, little has changed in those 60 years or so except for the packaging.  It is the same wax type paper that is difficult to reseal and keep the crackers fresh.  The box is of similar cardboard quality that does little to protect the contents.  In spite of several requests to Nabisco to present the consumers with quality packaging that compares to its costs I have seen no attempts to correct this condition.  There is an annoying factor to me that causes me to reconsider brands when the contents are made up of many broken, cracked and crumbly pieces of product regardless of what king it might be.  Nabisco blames the condition on the stock clerks in the grocery stores even though the stock is placed on the shelves by Nabisco salesmen.  Then they blame anyone but the production or packaging at the source location.  That tirade is the reason these crackers did not get a 5 star.The packaging aside and we have a tasty cracker that has withstood the sands of time.  Gee, sands of time...  Sorry, but grocery stores have few products today that were around so long ago and fundamentally presenting a similar formula of product.  I guess it might be safe to say that Nabisco followed the rule of "if it ain't broke, don't fix it (including the packaging)" routine.  The one thing I like most of all about this package of Fresh Stacks is that they are not overly packed with sugar.  So when that graham cracker crust gets cut into the end result is one of near profection and largely due to Nabisco's crackers.  I hear the background musicians saying in one breath we have to hear about all the cracked crackers and now we have to hear that the crackers have to be cracked to make crust.  Weird reviewer.  All kidding aside.  Great crackers and will continue buying even when they are cracked.  Something that tastes this good is worth a few problems.

The Things I Like About These Honey Maid Fresh Stack Crackers--  They are portable, perfect for a lunch box or a brief case or backpack.  The packing makes it easier.  It's compact, and the way the crackers are packed you don't really need to break the crackers apart, which results in alot of the times making a mess, and for different sized crackers.What I Didn't Like About These Honey Maid Fresh Stack Crackers--  I didn't really care for the taste.  The taste is very bland, but then I guess they are also suitable for a topping, which would definitely make them more palatable.  I've definitely tasted other graham crackers that I've enjoyed alot more than these.  I really don't taste much of a honey taste, more of a fake taste to me.Good in a pinch, but that is the best thing I can say about these.  Wouldn't purchase them myself.

column9: Same great grahams, not much improvement on packaging
column10: First off, let me say that the grahams are the same great honey grahams that they've always been. Nothing has changed flavor-wise. What is different here is the packaging.I don't dislike the new packaging, but I don't think it's much of an improvement either, at least not for my family. We still don't finish one wrapped "package" of grahams in one sitting, so we still need to put the open package into a sandwich size ziploc bag and back in the box to keep it fresh. (I tried putting it into a smaller snack size bag, but it doesn't fit.)Whereas the old packaging gave you 3 wrapped "packages" of double grahams per box, the new packaging gives you 6 wrapped "packages" of half-grahams. There are 8 half-grahams per package (so you are getting the equivalent of 4 of the old longer graham crackers in each wrapped package).  According to the serving size on the box, this is 2 servings. For some people this is a definite benefit. If you are feeding 2-4 people at a time, you could easily finish off one of these newly sized packages, thus saving some from going stale or from having to use a ziploc to keep the remainder fresh. However, personally, in my family we don't usually eat that many grahams at one time, so we still can't finish of one of the new size packages in one sitting. No increased benefit for us, personally (but I can see how it could be for some people).One plus to these new graham packages might also be for those serving small children. The crackers are already in half, so you don't need to break them yourself. (The longer grahams were always too big for little ones, I think.) I don't know about other people, but half the time when I'd try to break them, they would not break right down the middle, so this alleviates that issue.What would have made this new packaging perfect, would be if each individual package had a ziploc built into it so you could reseal it.  Or, they could have changed the packaging completely, getting rid of the box and packaging it more like Chips Ahoy where the cookies are not wrapped in individual packages but lined up in one large package that seals closed after you open it.Overall, I don't have a problem with the new package but I can't rave about it either.  It's more or less as functional as before.  Still great grahams though!

column9: I prefer this to the one made by "Back to Nature"; packaging can still be improved
column10: This cracker is made of simple ingredients and tastes very simple, too, but with a mild fragrance which seems to pair well with milk. As has been expressed by another reviewer, its texture crumbles easily (a characteristic of graham crackers, I assume), but it doesn't really break easily in the middle despite what the line on each cracker seems to suggest. The fact that these crackers come in 6 little bags of 8 crackers is a good idea (as other reviewers have pointed out), though it seems to me that they could have made the bag even easier to open. As it is, when you try tearing open the bag from the side, the crackers can crumble a little bit.
Really enjoyed the crackers.  Great flavor, crunchy and healthy.  Would buy when looking for next healthy snack.

It's been a long time since I had Honey Maid Grahams and they're better than I remember.  I really like the packaging.  I can put these in the car for a road trip and not have to fuss with the box or a plastic bag.  Even though other people may not be able to eat all eight crackers at one sitting, I have no problem with that, so this packaging and serving size are just right for me.

column9: Great on the go stay fresh pouches
column10: Each pouch comes with 6 graham crackers in it.  Just enought to grab as you run out the door with kids.  They are fresh and tastey, nothing less from Honey Maid.  Very convenient!!

column9: It is a graham cracker after all
column10: Honey Maid must have a challenge. How do you improve on a graham cracker ? You don't. You simply provide the best tasting graham cracker on the market , and promote it as such ! With a dab of butter , these were the best on the market

This is a simple review.  Excellent Honey Maid Fresh stacks in packaging that works for those of us who keep them in vacation homes strictly for making s'mores.  I can't tell you how many boxes of graham crackers I've fed to the squirrels and birds over the years because we only needed a few crackers out of a box, and then the humidity at the lake house ruins the rest--even after double bagging in ziplock bags.What a great idea.  yes, it is more expensive per cracker this way, and yes, it is not the best choice for simple packaging, but throwing out 3/4 of a box of regular packaged grahams isn't exactly good stewardship either!

column9: Old favourite in a S'mores-ready size
column10: These are a winner.  As soon as I received these I called some friends and arranged a S'mores making party around their firepit.Being the same classic graham cracker that the kids knew and loved, there were no complaints on the flavour, no complaints on oats being on the cracker or on the cracker being "different".  Additionally, since the crackers are perfectly S'mores sized right out of the packet, there was less fuss about one kid having a more perfectly broken cracker than another, and fewer frazzled parents trying to juggle sticky burnt marshmallows while aiming for the perfect break along the serrated line for fussy kids.Another plus is that these are packaged in stacks of 8, which is both a perfect size for snacking and for toting around.This is frazzled parent and fussy kid approved. I will definitely be buying more for the summer camping trips.

You probably already know exactly what the Honey Maid Graham cracker tastes like. Although, you might cover your grahams with chocolate and marshmallow. This is the same cracker, but half the size. Instead of 4 perforated sections, there are two.Each box comes with 6 "stacks" as they call them. Each stack is individually wrapped with 8 crackers. This would be the equivalent of 4 regular size grahams. I find that these stacks are reasonable sizes for single servings, so you don't end up with an opened wrapper with stale grahams. Like the originals, these stack wrappers are not resealable.I definetly prefer this packaging comapred to the standard packaging.

These are normal Honey Maid graham crackers.  Who doesn't love them?  I found them as tasty as ever.The main difference in this product is a packaging difference.  While normal graham crackers come in two long packs with many crackers, this one comes with the crackers already broken down to squares.  Each small square pack of eight crackers comes in its own wrapper.This is a great, simple idea.  If you're a busy, on-the-go person, I think you'll find this product very convenient.  It would be great for packing a lunch for school or work in a hurry.  It would also be great for moms to throw in a purse or diaper bag to have a fast, easy snack for toddlers.  Also, in our family we find that we might only want to eat a couple of crackers, but once you open a pack you feel like you either have to eat them all or let them go to waste.  This product solves that problem.I would say that it depends on the price of the product if it really makes sense to buy these.  Ziplock bags are pretty cheap, and it doesn't take too terribly long to throw a few crackers in there.  Also if you have a large family that would consume an entire pack of graham crackers before these go stale, then this product adds no benefit, is harder to get into, and is worse for the environment.  All in all, though, I think this product has a place in the market.  If you're like me and find yourself trying to grab something quickly while you're always running late, this is a great choice.

Nabisco has taken a great product and made it more economical.  We love graham crackers in our house for snacking but no one eats a whole pack at one sitting.  Now, they've made smaller stacks that are convenient to throw in a lunch sack, diaper bag or glove compartment.  Anywhere really! You won't have to worry about them getting stale since you can eat them in one sitting.  Each pack has about eight crackers. Cheers to Nabisco for making my life easier (no more ziploc handy snack bags for our lunch sacks!)
I loved these crackers. They are not too sweet with perfect crunch. My niece and nephew (6 years old and almost three years old) loved them too. Yum!

column9: Wish it were the full 14.4 oz.
column10: I actually love the idea of smaller packages because, it never fails, the big ones get left open and get stale or smashed.  I also prefer the smaller size crackers.  They are just easier to use and save me from having to break the bigger ones in half, often resulting in a busted up cracker.  The taste is the same as ever and my family and I have always loved Honey Maid graham crackers.  So, why the four stars?  I feel that this new packaging is just a way to hide that they have reduced the amount of product in the box.  Standard graham crackers are 14.4 oz.  This one is 12.2 oz.  If they had made them the same size, I would have happily given five stars.

The Packaging: I really like the packaging. There are 6 small packs in 1 box; so its ready to take with you where ever. Each small pack has ~8 crackers in it. None were cracked in the one i received. I dont think it would be an issue anyways as they are nicely packed.The Texture: Lives up to its name of 'Fresh Stacks'. They are dry but not so dry that your mouth becomes parched and it becomes a chore to chew and swallow. After a little chewing it melts quite nicely in your mouth. Each cracker; you can think of as a slightly bigger square credit card in terms of the size.The Taste: It strikes a nice balance in terms sweetness. You definitely get a graham/cinnamon type taste; with the sweetness of honey. Works well with peanut butter as well as my personal favorite nutella.In case your interested here are some nutritional facts(note that this is for 1 pack,i.e, 8 crackers):Calories: 250Fat: 6 gTotal Carbs: 46gSugars: 16g

Well, if you do, then you'll love these Honey Maid Fresh Stacks. They are the usual, delicious Honey Maid graham crackers, only they are halved into squares which are packed into 6 separate servings of 6 squares. The point? To keep them fresh, which is much appreciated, and also to make them ready to pack for lunch or travel! Great idea! I've had graham crackers that have been in the fridge too long, and they're not so good. These are crisper than I'm even used to ever having. The individual packages are sometimes tough to open, but that is my only complaint here. Well, that and one other. Aren't you going to make Fresh Stacks of the chocolate grahams? Love those. And I know my mom loves the cinnamon ones. As yet though, I have only seen the Honey version in Fresh Stacks form.

This is exactly what you would expect from Homey Maid. The same crackers you know & love but in nice little packages. Each square is about half the size of the normal full, long graham crackers. Each package contains 8 squares. I don't know about everyone else but I always seem to make a mess with the crumbs with the regular packages so these are much better. Less crumbs everywhere. They are also perfect to take as a snack into work or school. Would definitely choose these over the normal package!

The box I received had no viable damage yet a lot of the crackers were broken and crumbled.I prefer the old rectangular style as opposed to these crumbly squares.  They are Gram crackers, they are still good, but I'm not impressed by a marketing gimmick.

column9: Convenient packaging for your favorite graham crackers
column10: These taste identical to the regular packages of Honey Maid honey grahams.  The difference is in the packaging.  Each plastic package holds 8 half-crackers.  This means each individual package is half the width and about 2/3 the height of the regular product.I try to avoid buying products with excessive packaging, and these actually don't have a whole lot more waste than the regular box. We are always putting our grahams in ziplocks to keep them fresh, but this new product makes it easier to grab a pack to go.Overall love the new format, especially for camping and traveling.  This is our kids #1 snack.

I suspect that anyone in this country that is over three years old has tried graham crackers; they have been a snack item around our house for years. We go through phases of eating them frequently to eating them occasionally but we rarely go for too long a time without having them at snack time.The problem we have occasionally encountered is the problem of staying crisp; when they aren't consumed fairly quickly, especially in a humid climate, they can get soft and lose a lot of their charm. This is countered by packaging them in individual groups of crackers which can be opened sequentially.What Nabisco has done with these is to use that principle to package only eight crackers in an individually sealed package. The package can be partially resealed if one is not in the mood for all eight at once.According to the package a serving size is four squares which would apparently mean there are two servings per individual packet. The section on Nutrition Facts distinguishes between four squares and one fresh stack with all numbers rounded. As one would expect the values for the stack, which would be eight crackers is about twice the number for four which would be considered one serving. One serving is 130 calories, Total Fat 3g, Sodium 170mg, Potassium 50 mg, Dietary Fiber 1g, Sugars 8g, and Protein 2g.A fairly nutritious combination in a convenient carry-along package; a nice solution if you're on the go or looking for really crisp crackers at home. Personally I find them much tastier with peanut butter spread on them!

column9: Same Great Honey Maid Taste in a Smaller Pack
column10: I tried it and really enjoyed it.  My daughter tried it and "loved it! Hence, the 5 stars.  The smaller package size makes it more convenient, but not that much more.

column9: Same great product, more convenient packaging
column10: These are the same Nabisco graham crackers that have been around for decades, so I don't need to describe the product to you.  However, this new multi-insert packaging allows you to use fewer crackers at a time without exposing the rest of the crackers in the box to the air.  There are six smaller packages within each large box instead of the traditional two.  That means the unused packages retain their freshness seal rather than allowing the crackers to become stale like an open package would.  The crackers haven't changed, but the packaging has improved, so the next time you buy Nabisco grahams, make sure you get the "Fresh Stacks" packaging - a definite advantage over the other packages.

We love Honey Maid's graham crackers in our family, especially having a toddler around they're practically a staple in our household. The Honey Maid Fresh Stacks are conveniently packaged, but still the same graham crackers we've loved. When I first saw the Fresh Stacks version the first thing I thought of was that these are perfect for s'mores! We will definitely be packing these for our next camping trip. (Or even our next trip to the mall, for that matter, my daughter will enjoy these anytime.) We're also a fan of making ice cream sandwiches with them, spreading Nutella on them, and adding them to desserts we make (s'mores brownies, anyone?)As a mom, I appreciate the simply ingredient list - it's not full of scary looking words that I can't pronounce. Honey grahams can be the perfect snack and now Honey Maid offers them in portable, perfectly portioned little packs. Great for the lunchbox, the diaper bag, the carry on bag, you get the idea...

column9: Fantastic for families on the go!
column10: Honey Maid Fresh Stacks are great. Not only do they taste delicious but they come in 6 small packages inside the box, it makes it easy to keep them fresh. The small packages also make it convenient to take a snack along on the road. I just toss a pack in the diaper bag and when the kids are hungry I break it out. These were a big hit in my house and make a great treat.

column9: I get it - same great crackers, better packaging
column10: I have been eating Graham Crackers since I was a kid. 50 years ago, my mother spread peanut butter on a few and wrapped them in wax paper with my lunch. But she always broke up the double length crackers and I got used to eating them that way. We usually have a box or two (or three) around the house and I still break them up to relive the good old days. With today's new packaging, the crackers come pre-split and wrapped nicely to keep them fresh. Clever idea, I must say.I just have to figure a way to package some peanut butter so I can have them the old fashioned way during recess.

These crackers remind me a lot of graham crackers. They have a similar taste, texture, and crunchiness. They do however seem a little denser and more filling. Much like graham crackers, they're delicious with peanut butter.They also come nicely packed in 6 individual plastic packages of crackers. The extra packages keep them fresh longer because you don't have to open them all at once. It also makes them more portable as each package is a square instead of a long rectangle which makes them a lot better for packing in lunches or anything else portable.

Honey Maid graham crackers are naturally good and rank high on my list when it comes to buying graham crackers.  So this reveiw is for the packaging and not the product.  The crackers come in 12.2 ounce box with six half stacks.  These make for ease in adding to lunches, picnics or any on-the-go activity.  That basically means that two of these stacks make up one standard size stack.  Price makes these more expensive, around $4.50, than the regular package but much more convenient for travel.  If you are buying graham crakers for cheese cake or pie crusts buy the regular package, but for carrying convenience this is the way to go.  Well worth having on hand.

I LOVE graham crackers, and Honey Maid is my favorite brand.  Always has been, and probably always will.I expected the main benefit of these Fresh Stacks crackers to be that they would stay fresher longer -- the reason being each "stack" only contains two servings (4 squares per serving).  They did succeed in this way.  However, I noticed, upon opening a Fresh Stack, that they also started out tasting fresher than the standard Honey Maid grahams.  They also had a fresh "snap" to them upon biting a piece off a cracker.  I'm not sure why, and it's certainly something I didn't expect.The only thing I didn't like about these crackers is that they don't easily break in half the way the standard Honey Maid does.  They do have the typical "score" mark that graham crackers usually have, but the score is not as deep, so they don't break cleanly  in half.  This probably won't be a big deal for children or adults, but I really do prefer breaking them in half for older babies and toddlers.

column4: Mrs. K "From the wilds of the Mojave"
column9: New packaging fits better with modern life
column10: Chocolate bar-check! Ginormous marshmallows-check! Big box o' graham crackers-check! Make one, two, three s'mores. Wow, that's really way too sweet to deal with more than once a year.So, the rest of the chocolate bar is gone before the evening is out. A couple of the marshmallows get thrown into cocoa before they become puffy rocks and they get tossed or the dog snags the bag.But the crackers? They get put back into the box and go back up on the shelf by the high fiber stick cereal you really should eat instead of swiping the kid's sugar pellets. On a quest for snacks 3 months later  you find the sad, super stale remains falling out of the inadequate wax paper wrap and opt for a bowl of crispy twigs instead.Not any longer! Honey Maid has changed up the way they package graham crackers to better mesh with life today. The smaller packs fit easily in purses, diaper bags, or the outside pocket of the gym bag.It's a great size for sharing. The opaque plastic wrap you've known and loved from Premium Saltines now protects the slightly sweet wholesomeness of eight 2 3/8-inch  square Honey Maid crackers.When opened, you get to experience the aroma of super fresh crackers. And two weeks later when you open another package -- they're still super fresh and crispy. Great idea Nabisco!Nom, nom, nom!

Graham crackers are a great snack, but the problem is when the package is opened, they usually get stale before you eat them all out of the packets in the box.  This new smaller packaging will prevent that problem. The crackers are the same as usual, but the packaging is much more convenient. The box comes with individual packets with 1/2 the usual amount per packet, so you can probably eat them all up before they go stale. There are 8 crackers per packet, but they are half crackers, so it is really like 4 of the usual size ones. The packs are perfect for toting around for kids, or in the desk drawer at work, I even keep a packet in the car incase of emergency hunger pangs. I will never buy the big packs again, this smaller size makes so much more sense. Try them, you will probalby like the smaller size packaging too.

Okay, so I love graham crackers; ever since I was a kid. I suppose everyone does. But I want to address the new packaging, which is what is really at stake here. It is funny that I "just happened" (serendipitously) to get tired of the music on the radio and pop it over to AM today in time to hear some right-wing guy foaming at the mouth over this exact product! It was amazing. My timing could not have been better. First off, whoever it was, was hilarious. he really was going off about how you pay the same amount for less graham cracker (goodness <--my word).Well, I don't quite see it that way. Look, I am certain graham crackers will still come in the industrial size, but the idea of the new packaging is to keep them fresher longer. The BIG problem with graham crackers (other than the fact that they don't all come topped with double-cinnamon and sugar of course) is that you eat a few and say "yum!" and then you put the box away. When you come back for more, usually a week or two later, they are a bit mushy. They never quite taste as good as they do when you first open that brown wax papery wrapper. Actually I am crunching the wrapper now. is that cellophane? well you can use a ziploc baggie (if you have one handy) but it is a bit of a hassle and not 100%. But with the new packaging each "stack" (each little package is about -- wait,let me count the one's I haven't eaten yet and do some math here . . .) looks like about 8 "half crackers" (remember traditional graham crackers are doubles and you have to break them in half).That is a large "single serving" for me. It is about enough for you and your girlfriend to share (give her the larger half (she gets 5 and you get 3 if you want to a happy marriage in the future) with a romantic glass of milk(?) or hot chocolate by a fire. If you have kids you could toss them each a pre-wrapped "stack" and nobody argues about sharing or getting less.There is a downside to this though. It seems most of my graham crackers are broken. This really annoys me. Perhaps it was just this box I am reviewing, but I like my graham crackers unbroken and pristine (and if at all possible coated with cinnamon and sugar--but they never quite give you enough c&s). These are still crunchy and tasty; I am having some now with some hot chocolate, just to ensure accuracy, but this broken thing really gets me.Now as a disclaimer: I did get these through the Vine program, so they have been mailed, but it seems to me that ALL graham crackers are mailed, or trucked, or planed . . . It may be the packaging on this. So, the result is that they are super convenient. You know how many graham crackers you are eating and you can EASILY stop at one stack and know you haven't binged on "most of the box." That part is nice. The smaller wrapper serves as a nice "holder" while you are eating your graham crackers, so you don't need a plate, and if you don;t tear it open all the way it catches the crumbs from broken crackers. You simply toss it away when you are done. I am not sure what the recycle factor there is on this brown plasticy-paper stuff.I can strongly recommend this for convenience. You should check the prices locally to make sure you are not paying a lot more per ounce of course. But it really does make sure that every time you want some graham crackers they are fresh and tasty, and just the right amount. This was a great idea.Anyway, thanks for reading.

First, the Honey Maid snacks (honey graham) are excellent. The better part? The packaging which allows you to have 8 smaller graham crackers in a pack which is perfect for lunches. Excellent taste. Excellent packaging. I'll give it "two thumbs up" or, in the case of Amazon Vine? Five stars.

column9: I wish I would have thought of it...
column10: They've taken a familiar product and changed the packaging and I love it!  I remember the days when my graham crackers used to get dried out because the box and the wrapper had been opened and there was no easy way to save the rest of the package in an airtight fashion.  This new packaging takes the smaller squares and puts fewer of them in the familiar waxy-like wrapping paper.  This makes it very easy to take a small package with you and put it in your purse or add it to a lunch box.  You don't have to worry about the rest of the package drying out.  I simply love this idea and will be buying this product more often in the future as a result.

The Honey Maid Fresh Stacks product is the perfect way to transport the treat into school lunches, picnics or whatever need you may have to enjoy a delicious snack of graham crackers.  Also, the packaging keeps the product fresher than the original way of packaging graham crackers.

I've always loved graham crackers, they are one of my childhood comfort foods that I used to spread with peanut butter or made into S'mores.  I don't buy graham crackers often (not sure why), so I was excited for the oppportunity to try this product, Honey Maid Fresh Stacks Honey Grahams.  The crackers themselves were as I remembered, super crispy and tasty.  What I do like that's different(and is the point of this specific product) are the smaller, 2" by 2" wax paper cubes ("stacks") that hold eight square crackers.  Graham crackers typically have been packaged in much larger wax paper bricks, and once opened the uneaten crackers needed to be eaten at that time or put into airtight containers soon thereafter.  Graham crackers seem to practically act like desiccants in absorbing moisture from the air, so if they're not eaten soon, they will get soft.  These smaller wax packages are a nice solution to this issue of having too many crackers unwrapped at a time.Each 12.2 ounce box has six cubes (or "stacks"), and each stack has eight crackers which, according to the box, is two servings of four crackers each.  I think in all honesty one stack is, for most of us, one serving.  <g>  These grahams are low fat, relatively low sugar, and each stack (8 square crackers) provides 12% daily recommendation of fiber and 10% of iron.  Certainly better than a lot of other snack options.  I will be getting this product again.

So, I'm usually a Keebler guy, and even then it's the Cinnamon Grahams.  That said, I don't eat a lot of any sort of graham on a regular basis regardless ... my household would (most days) test graham-negative across the board (for you microbiologists out there ;), so this is sort of a minor detour from the norm for me.  Still, nothing wrong with a little Honey Maid from time to time.Anyway, the packaging is about right for two people to share a packet (2 -not 4- individual, regular rectangular crackers each, stacked 8 high).  This is a departure from the old 4 per sheet packaging, and it's a huge deal, and here's why.  To finish off one of the old (standard/larger) packets of graham crackers (4X the amount per packet, roughly), you have to be both voracious and consistent in your crumbly graham consumption.  If not, your crackers are likely to go stale before the open packet is gone, necessitating waste and the opening of another big packet.  These "Fresh Stacks" packets are a day or two's worth of breakfast snack, then you open a new/fresh pack w/o wasting the old one.  Yes, it's more packaging and smaller, but seriously, haven't you ever had the size/spoilage issue?  Savings via bulk aren't savings until you consume everything you bought.  Barring that, you need a new calculation factoring in only price per quantity used...just sayin.More importantly, who's ever made S'mores and had to 1) hold a piece of chocolate 2) hold a fire-stick with a flaming marshmallow on the end while 3) trying to break a graham-cracker slab into roughly equal halves ... all the while holding off inquisitive, insistent and "helpful" little fingers and a frenzied dog (who also seems to think chocolate is the cure for cancer, adding to the furor) amid a chorus of verbal coaching on how to "do it right" ... ?  Am I the only one?  So, I hate it when the slab breaks unevenly, thus these Honey Maid Fresh Stacks eliminate the challenging operation of bisecting a graham cracker slab while both of my hands are partially otherwise engaged.  Not that it's a giant, groundbreaking innovation, but I usually judge inventions and updates to products based on how many times I've said, "Dang!" in reference to the situation said innovation addresses.  I've said "Dang!" to stale, half-gone packs of grahams, and I've said, "Dang!" to botched S'mores, so these cut the mustard in my book.  Like with the spaghetti pot on TV that has holes in the lid for easily draining your noodles, I found myself wondering why nobody came up with this sooner...

column9: The REAL REASON They Changed the Packaging
column10: I ate these crackers as a child, and from time to time as an adult.  It has been several years since I had them; they are still really tasty.  As I a kid, I liked to dunk them in milk: an afternoon snack that brings back a happy feeling from my childhood.They taste slightly different to me, probably because they reduced the amount or type of fat used to make them, or reduced the salt, to make them healthier by today's standards.  Anyway, I still like them.But the PACKAGING is different: these are "Fresh Stacks"; smaller packets, and more of them.  This is an "improvement": the crackers will stay fresher that way, or that's what they want you think.  But what they don't tell you is that you also get fewer crackers per box.I think the old package will disappear: this is the replacement.  Soon you won't have a choice between the older packaging and the new.  Why? I read about this in the New York Times, the same day I wrote this review.  (You can find the article at nytimes dot com slash 2011 slash 03 slash 29 slash business slash 29shrink.html.)"Kraft is introducing 'Fresh Stacks' packages for its Nabisco Premium saltines and Honey Maid graham crackers. Each has about 15 percent fewer crackers than the standard boxes, but the price has not changed. Kraft says that because the Fresh Stacks include more sleeves of crackers, they are more portable and "the packaging format offers the benefit of added freshness," said Basil T. Maglaris, a Kraft spokesman, in an e-mail."Since the article says it has 15% less, they must have reduced the package size before, because I remember the box as one pound, this package is 12.2 ounces.They reduced the quantity to keep the product at the same price point:"Consumers are generally more sensitive to changes in prices than to changes in quantity," John T. Gourville, a marketing professor at Harvard Business School, said. "And companies try to do it in such a way that you don't notice, maybe keeping the height and width the same, but changing the depth so the silhouette of the package on the shelf looks the same. Or sometimes they add more air to the chips bag or a scoop in the bottom of the peanut butter jar so it looks the same size."There's nothing wrong with this approach, though it seems a little sneaky.  It happens all the time, probably always has; still, it is useful to know about it.  It does not take away from my opinion of the product.  After all, the alternative is that the product would cost more, because prices go up with time.
Besides being great graham crackers, the packaging is perfect.  Just the right size to put in a lunch bag, or for a snack.  Very pleased.

Many companies are downsizing their packaging and upsizing their prices. I read an interesting article in the New York Times today about companies sneakily repackaging their products to charge consumers more for less product without them knowing:"Kraft is introducing "Fresh Stacks" packages for its Nabisco Premium saltines and Honey Maid graham crackers. Each has about 15 percent fewer crackers than the standard boxes, but the price has not changed. Kraft says that because the Fresh Stacks include more sleeves of crackers, they are more portable and "the packaging format offers the benefit of added freshness," said Basil T. Maglaris, a Kraft spokesman, in an e-mail."So yes, you're getting more little packages of crackers in here, with fewer crackers than you used to get. If you don't use them up quickly, maybe that's a good idea for you, but if you're going to be using the whole package to make a graham cracker crust, for example, this is simply wasteful.

I love graham crackers.  They're one of my all time favorite snacks but I don't like them after they lose their just opened crunch.  I immediately loved the idea of individual serving packs of grahams.  They're great for taking as a snack to work or putting in your lunch, and whenever you eat them, they're fresh, crunchy and perfect. I actually wish that the "fresh stacks" would have been made a little smaller because 8 square crackers is more than I can eat at one time so I still end up having to have sandwich bag or container to seal them up.  I think four graham squares would be the perfect size or the "fresh stacks" could be made resealable.

column9: same graham cracker in different packaging
column10: This is a curious item.  The product itself is actually the same as Nabisco's graham crackers that come in larger sheets and larger packages.  I guess someone at Nabisco thought it made sense to repackage these graham crackers into smaller portions, but with all of the "100 calorie snack packs" that abound today I think Nabisco missed the mark here.  Each "stack" of these crackers is actually nearly two servings, which contain about 250 calories total.  The box itself gives the nutritional information for a full stack (7 squares) as well as for 4 squares, so it seems like Nabisco is acknowledging that the full stack is more than one should eat at one sitting.  I'm not sure why they packaged these crackers in this manner, then, since the crackers would stay more fresh if each individually wrapped packet contained only one serving.As for the product itself, I quite like graham crackers and enjoy these, but I prefer the kind with a cinnamon and sugar coating versus these more plain, honey graham crackers.Good with cold milk!

If you like to pack graham crackers for snacks in lunches and backpacks, these small stacks are a great way to keep portions under control. Instead of having to open a big stack of cracker sheets, and have them stale and limp a few days later, these small packs of squares stay crisp and crunchy.The box has six stacks of eight squares each. Nutritional information is provided for both a serving (four squares) or an entire stack (eight squares).These stacks make sense financially, you're not throwing away unused cracker sheets that went stale or paying for baggies to seal up leftovers.They make sense from a dietary perspective too, it is painless portion control.

These are the same great tasting Honey Maid crackers but with the added convenience of individual `stacks'.  Each box contains a total of 6 stacks and each stack has 8 cracker graham cracker squares. The total calories for an individual stack are 250 calories.These snacks are ideal if you are in a hurry and want to grab something and are great for throwing in lunch boxes. Another plus, is the smaller packaging does not compromise the freshness of the product.

Most people would wonder what is so great or different about New Honey Maid Fresh Stacks Honey Grahams crackers. Well, it's not just the fresh taste of the crackers themselves that has me excited. It's the New packaging. You see, Honey Maid has taken their crispy, tasty crackers and put them in 6 individual packages that hold about 8 crackers each. and The crackers are not the larger ones that can be broken up into smaller pieces. These are big squares. (about 2 inches square)This individual packaging is great for school lunches, portion control or when you just want a few crackers and dont want to leave a whole package open. The crackers remain fresher and crispy I think this is a wonderful idea and it makes the crackers taste that much better. I know I will be popping a package in my bag for a mid-day snack at work. Honey Maid took something I already love and made it better. Now THAT'S "Keeping it Fresh"

column9: My favorite graham crackers without the waste
column10: My one beef with graham crackers is that they always seem to go stale within a day of opening the package (even when we transfer them to a ziplok bag).  Since my 3 year old and I are the only ones who eat graham crackers, we always end up throwing half of a usual packet away.  With these fresh stacks, we don't have the waste, which is wonderful.  Each little package has just the six squares, perfect for snacking for the two of us (pair with peanut butter or nutella for a real delight!).When you think of graham crackers, Honey Maid grahams are the traditional ones that come to mind.  The Keebler grahams are a little too sweet/cookie-ish and the store brand grahams are simply inedible.  I always get the Honey Maid for that nice graham taste, and love using them for s'mores.Great new packaging!

Honey Maid Graham crackers have been around for years and they taste the same.  It's a dependable snack that isn't too high in sugar.  In fact, the nursing facility I work at allows graham crackers and milk as an approved snack for their diabetics.The packaging is ideal, and will probably result in less waste of crackers that aren't eaten immediately, as these crackers become stale overnight once opened.  You get 8 crackers in each individually wrapped snack, which, in my opinion is more than twice what one person should eat in one sitting.  Institutions are sold graham crackers packaged in two's, and that would be better, I think.As another reviewer mentioned: these crackers drop a lot of crumbs when broken apart.  Therefore, these snacks are better eaten outside, or directly over a plate.If I had to choose between purchasing graham crackers packaged in bigger portions, and these smaller packages, I'd pick the smaller.  While I am still wasting some crackers due to staleness, it's not nearly as many as before.

I never understood why graham crackers in such large sheets...like little sheets of plywood. :) These are the same graham crackers that you know but are packaged in a more travel friendly size.Whether making smores, packing for a lunch, or just grabbing a quick snack this size of cracker makes more sense then the large sheet of plywood that you would have to break into a more manageable size only to have them break in an uneven manner.Taste is great - they could win a grahammy!

column9: Same product, different box. On-the-go convenience!
column10: It has been awhile since I had Honey Maid graham crackers, and my taste buds welcomed that classic graham cracker taste back when I opened these up for the first time!  They were a bit more dry and crunchy than I had remembered them, though.  Not the greatest by themselves in that state but crying out to be dipped in milk!A few things to point out:1- the picture of the packaging here at amazon makes it look like maybe there's a cellophane see-through top on the box, but it's actually just the usual cardboard box, but with a photograph on top of what the contents are.  Nice to see a fair representation OUTside the box of what is INside, though, unlike many ('not actual size') products!2- the standard rectangular graham cracker size has been halved into two separate squares.3- the paper packages that contain stacks of graham crackers contain fewer squares than the 'regular' packaging.  I think there were 8 squares in each mini-package.  They are, however, just as awkward to tear open.  I remember the 'regular' packaging being wrapped much tighter around the crackers, too.  Seems like you're less likely to get stale crackers in this new package design.Why buy these instead of the 'regular' packaging?  Mostly because it's more convenient to take on the go.  I would argue that one mini-pack is almost too much of a snack for one grown-up, and definitely too much for one toddler!  But my 4-year-old and I together enjoyed one at the park the other day, so all is well!

Moisture is their kryptonite so this works. Once you open a pack of graham crackers there's a clock on 'em... there seems to be no climate dry enough. These are full size crispy squares, a pack holds six crackers. (I'll take the side of cookie in the cookie-vs-cracker debate if you're in the mood to argue.) I'm unexpectedly grateful that I'll never ever have to eat another soft graham cracker. Sort of takes a load off.

Honey Maid graham crackers smaller portion packaging is  big win in our house. As a parent of five- three eight and under-- snacks and lunches are a daily struggle. When I open the traditional size package of graham crackers no matter how hard I plan there are always some leftover and I can't count how many half packs I've tossed because the crackers have become soft. Currently I purchase the bulk box warehouse option of Honey Maid Graham Crackers and while I will still continue to get this size I will also buy a few boxes of the fresh stacks to stick in lunches, to take to the park, stick in a backpack/diaper bag etc. This size will be for the kids (big and small) in our home who open the large packages, take out two crackers and never ever put the leftovers in airtight containers!!!

Over the past few weeks, I have had the opportunity to try these Nabisco Honey Maid Graham Crackers, and also Back To Nature Apple Cinnamon Oat and Back To Nature Golden Honey Oat Graham Crackers.These are good, not too crumbly, break easily, and make nice snacks.  However, in direct comparison, they come in second to the Back to Nature Honey Oat Crackers.  Back to Nature has a more pronounced honey flavor.  They also have only natural ingredients.  Nabisco can earn an extra star from me by eliminating the artificial flavor and replacing it with more natural honey.

Graham crackers were our staple snack as we were growing up. We ate them with milk or peanut butter. In the hot and muggy days of summer the crackers would get soggy even though we wrapped them in wax paper. The Honey Maid Fresh Snacks people have come up with something practical and appealing in the wrapped packs of 6. They won't go stale. Ideal for packing the the kids' lunches or enjoying an after school treat. They could be a lunch time lift for busy parents or a pick me up at coffee break time. Enjoy FRESH Honey-Maid packs anytime.

column9: Familiar taste, new packaging, worth the price?
column10: These crackers are exactly what you expect from Honey Maid - familiar graham taste, serrated lines for breaking the crackers, etc.  The big development (if you will) here, are the "fresh stacks" - that is, slightly different packaging from the originals. Instead of four-panel crackers sealed in two packets within the box, you get six stacks of eight, two-panel (half of the original) crackers.The packets are not reseal-able and each contains what the nutrition facts consider to be two servings (one serving is four squares and each packet contains 8 squares).As with many grocery items that are packaged for convenience (baby carrots, pre-sliced apples, etc.) you pay more.  If you're looking for an easy, pre-packed snack for an outing...I suppose this helps but it is up to you to decide whether your time is worth the extra cost here.

column9: Great Idea for Freshness, But Execution Suffers
column10: Sometimes, there's just nothing else that'll satisfy a snack-tooth.  Graham crackers and milk have been calming me since probably 1959, my first year in Sunday school.  I'm a single woman, and a traditional box of graham crackers gets, maybe, 1/4th consumed in a year.  The rest go stale and get thrown away.  This idea of "snack sized" packs of graham crackers is super!The box has six small packs of graham crackers in it, and the graham crackers are not the traditional "four square" size, but "two square" size.  Doesn't matter the size to me, but the flavor of the graham cracker does.  And these Honey Maids are, in my humble snacky opinion, the best graham cracker on the market.  In each snack pack, there eight "two square" crackers in a fresh stack package.  I'd call that a serving.  Honey Maid calls that two servings, so watch the nutritional numbers.I found the crackers to be, largely, crumbled and broken.  Granted, I have never consumed crackers that have been mailed to me, so this could be a problem of shipping, rather than Honey Maid's problem.  The corner of the Honey Maid box (not the shipping box from Amazon) was bent and crushed, so I will assume that the crackers don't normally run into this problem when you purchase them in the grocery store.  The broken-ness of the crackers dented my enjoyment of the grahams, as I tend to like to dip them in milk for just a second.  There wasn't much to dip at times!Flavor=great.  Idea of individual size servings = ideal!  Nutritional breakdown on package = a bit misleading.  Physical quality of mailed crackers = not so much.That said, I'll look for them in stores, where I can monitor their transport from shelf to home.  Thanks, Honey Maid!

column9: Small Packets Stay Fresher With No Waste
column10: Nabisco Honey Grahams have always been a favorite in our house and now they found a new way to package them in convenient smaller packets. With 8 squares to a packet, this means you'll always get a fresh and crispy graham cracker every time. These squares can be conveniently snapped in half on the dotted line down the center. The square shapes are perfect for S'mores. The honey grahams have so much more taste than plain graham crackers, that they even taste good just by themselves. Half a pack which is 4 squares are only 130 calories, so if you like to add a little butter, jelly, fruit or anything else for taste, adding a thin spread will still be in line with anyone counting calories.The best thing about this packaging is you'll never have waste. In our house, we don't eat crackers on a daily basis, and I always end up tossing the unfinished box away months later when the crackers are stale because they are no longer crisp. Nabisco has combined their great tasting honey grahams with a great packaging which will end up being a great money saver in the end.

column9: Classic Graham Crackers with Updated Packaging
column10: These graham crackers have been around forever and taste great as usual. This particular packaging is an improvement because instead of 1 or 2 packages in a box for all the crackers, this has six packages in a box. So you have less crackers per package which is better since the other crackers won't get stale. Unless you eat a lot of crackers at once this is an improvement over the normal type of packaging.

column9: Great snack size and S'more size!
column10: These grahams are packaged in squares instead of rectangles which makes them perfect for grabbing to throw in a diaper bag or in your purse for quick snacks!  There are 8 squares per package and my husband pointed out the fact that this was perfect for S'mores making for our family since we don't have to try to break the graham into perfect squares now and 1 fresh stack is enough for 4 s'mores.The grahams are fresh and as great tasting as always, Honey Maid is a staple in my pantry, and I have to say that these "Fresh Stacks" are going to be the new packaging I buy from now on!  What a great idea for them to move away from the rectangles into a more ready to snack shape.

These are the same Honey Maid Graham Crackers we all grew up with. Generally accepted as a healthier alternative to store bought cookies, they still offer enough sweetness to satisfy that craving for sugar that most of us have from time to time. The only real difference here is that instead of the old rectangular crackers in 4 sections, they are half-size squares of 2 sections (I remember breaking the full size crackers into 4 smaller sections before eating them). I guess the thought is that the smaller size packages will be less likely to get stale before eating this way.I am ambivalent to the change in cracker size personally, and certainly wouldn't pay extra for it (fortunately, it appears that Nabisco isn't charging extra for the value add). Five stars because I love the graham crackers. P-)

column9: same old honey maid crackers, nice smaller size
column10: I have always loved honey-maid crackers dipped in tea 'chai'. These ones of course have the same great taste, but come in smaller size and packs. So when you open one, two people can finish one pack easily - that's the only advantage of this sized pack.

I've always enjoyed graham crackers, well at least I did before I started eating healthy.The individual packages are convenient.  But beware of handing a small child an entire package which amounts to 250 calories.Kudos to Nabisco/Kraft for providing the "nutritional facts" both in the absurd "serving size" and also for an entire "fresh stack".I found these to be rather dry and what I might term "stale" tasting even though I'm sure they are fresh.  They don't always break cleanly on the "dividing line".  I'd like to see a softer, more moist product.

I had forgotten how good plain graham crackers are (you know, when they're not the bookends of s'mores...).  These are the same tasty Honey Maid graham crackers, essentially broken in half (two of the small rectangles, instead of the large "brick" of four rectangles) and stacked up.  There are 8 of these "halves" in a sealed pack, which turned out to be two servings.  (I didn't notice that at first, but it is worth acknowledging, if you have concerns about portion size and/or calories.)This box didn't last a week at our house (hey, it's 6 packs per box, which is officially 12 "servings") but I see the definite advantage of having the crackers sealed into smaller packages, as they would be less likely to get stale.  I also stashed a pack in my purse on my way to work (very convenient).  They would be equally convenient for tossing into the diaper bag.No qualms about buying these in the future, though I have not yet seen them at the grocery store.  But the grahams I received from Amazon were fresh, so I would not hesitate to purchase them from here in the future.  Yum.

I loved Honey Grahm Crackers when I was growing up and these have the same flavor. I can see someone saying the perfect size to make Smoores or ice cream sandwich. Instead of the long 4 piece packaging with many crackers this has a small package of 2 servings of crackers. The package could even fit in you shirt pocket of a t-shirt. Another convenience is when you open this package you will most likely eats them before they get stale which may not always be the case in the large packaging depending on your families size.The down size is if you are looking for something for your child's lunchbox each package is two serving sizes. The package is 250 calories of which 50 calories is fat. So you would not be want to pack a full package. As for myself I found them just as tasty as I remember and a satisfying snack. This is old time favorite in a smaller wax paper package. 4.5 stars.

column9: CHILDHOOD TREAT IS STILL FUN TO EAT
column10: Nabisco has repackaged its popular Honey Maid Graham Crackers in what might be called a "snack pack." It's just a smaller box to make it easier to snack at home-- or take with you if you want to snack on the go. The product comes in six fresh stacks; same value, same classic taste. I easily finished off two stacks in two days. I prefer my graham crackers to have cinamon (which these don't); just to give it a little extra flavor. But these are still the perfect afternoon snacks. I recommend washing these down with a big glass of milk; which also makes for fun dunking.

column9: Same delicious taste in smaller packages
column10: The traditional large-size graham crackers are broken into two squares and packed in separate, waxed-paper packets. These are probably a better choice for kids' lunchboxes and adults' lunch bags, too. And in humid climates, will keep leftovers - which get soggy - to a minimum. So, a good idea, and the waxed paper is low-impact enough that it shouldn't matter much that the packaging is increased.

column9: The little stacks are a step in the right direction
column10: These graham crackers are the ones we are used to, except they are packed in half-sized packs of eight double-crackers--about a 3x3 inch square.  Like the ad says, nice as a portion at home or on the go.  They are crisp, delicious, and break evenly on the perforation, which seems to be rare among similar products.

column9: Fresh, well packaged, just like I remember them!
column10: These are almost just like I remember them when these were a treat growing up.  The difference is, rather than having a large rectangular 4 section cracker to deal with - that never broke in half right, these boxes have 6 square packages in the box, each package has 8 square crackers.  Each package is wrapped in a wax-paper-colored plastic bag, sealed well for freshness, but not sealed so hard that you get mad opening the bag.  There is a slight scoring in each square cracker and if you are careful, you can break each in half, but in my case, that's not needed - a square at a time makes for a great treat.  Goes perfect with milk!Enjoy

They are exactly the same thing as the regular crackers, but half the size, along where you would normally brake it in half. They are perfect for little hands and making smores. You would normally brake it in half to make smores, these ones are already the right size.As for the taste of them, they taste exactly like their larger counterparts. They are ideal if you are looking for things that are more of a snack size.

In this day and age of portion-controlled snacks (like 100 calorie packs), this is a great idea, but one fresh pack is basically two servings, so I still ended up putting the open pack in a zipper bag. So next time I'll just buy a regular package and portion it out myself. The crackers were excellent though, light and crispy, perfectly tasty!

I've always liked graham crackers for a snack. These are really good. Crispy texture, great taste and brings back a lot of great memories. I am now switching to this brand after tasting these.... they're really really good!

column9: A small premium for crispy grahams
column10: Same Honey Maid graham crackers, but instead of 3 large wax-paper-wrapped stacks, there are now 6. Note, this is 2.2oz less crackers (the traditional box is 14.2 oz, and this is 12.2 oz), but it solves a common problem of stale crackers, or spreading crumbs.

column9: Great snack item in a more convenient serving size
column10: Great idea, providing SMALLER graham crackers in SMALLER packages. Ideal for packing lunches. More than a grade-schooler could polish off in one lunch, however, so you may find yourself breaking down even these smaller packages into zip-top bags when you're packing lunches in the morning. I like Honeymaid graham crackers better than the generic graham crackers in the market. This is a good idea, but I'd have made this box with TWELVE little packs of graham crackers instead of six.---My teenagers have DEVOURED these packets. They do not appear to feel that the number of crackers in each one is any kind of issue. Our last box of graham crackers lasted months. These were gone in a week.

column9: Delicious and a more managable size
column10: These taste just like the regular honey made graham crackers, but they are squares and not long rectangles. They are also wrapped in smaller sections making them a nice snack pack size for an adult.

I have always loved these graham crackers, but a major aggravation was always that they would get stale before I could finish a pack. Well, Honey Maid has solved that problem by making these new 2-ounce packs! The same great taste you love, but now in a smaller size!

Packaging: The packaging for this product was hassle-free, easy to open, and reasonable given the amount of product supplied.Product quality: The crackers were very fresh and tasted just fine. It was consistent the the quality that I have come to expect from the brand name Nabisco. These were the perfect size for dunking into a small cup of milk as an after-dinner snack.Overall opinion: I would highly recommend this product to someone looking for a mildly sweet, yet low-fat snacking option.

column9: Nice on-the-go packaging and tasty product
column10: This package comes with 6 eight graham cracker pouches.  The pouches are made of the same type of material (wax paperish) that normal honey grahams come in, so it's difficult, if not impossible, to re-seal them in their own packaging if you don't eat the entire 8 cracker sleeve in one sitting.  The advantage of this packaging is that it's smaller portions than a normal pack of honey grahams, so they're good for a snack or with a meal.They are a little hefty on the nutritional side of things.  One of the 6 packs has 250 calories, 6 grams of fat (1.5 saturated) and 46g of carbs.  Probably not something you'd want to eat every day, but there are worse things out there for you!Honey grams are a great tasting cracker, my favorite of any graham cracker brands.  The box I received had freshly packed crackers that were not stale.  If they price is right (sometimes products charge way too much for 'convenient' packaging) then this is a great buy.

I've always been a graham cracker fan and these are very good! I usually get very aggravated when the pack goes stale in a day.. but this is packaged very differently. There are 6 smaller size stacks of crackers. Perfect for a few people to snack on and not ruin the whole box.  The crackers themselves are very light and crunchy. A wonderful snack for the whole family.

column9: Convenient Packaging for a Great Product
column10: I am a big fan of graham crackers. I enjoy them plain, with a tall glass of cold milk. Honey Maid Fresh Stacks (12.2 ounce box) presents the graham cracker in a new and convenient way, packaged eight squares to a pack, six packs to a box.Easy to bring along when you are on the go (such as an airplane trip, when you don't want to pay for the expensive unhealthy snacks the airlines are providing). And, if you like to be creative with your graham crackers, Fresh Stacks are great for making Graham Cracker smores, or Graham Cracker peanut butter sandwiches. They taste great, are low in fat, and now offer more convenient packaging. Highly recommended!

These are your standard Honey Maid Honey Grahams, just packaged with slightly smaller servings. Instead of the huge crackers, you get half-sized squares that are bundled in smaller wrappers. They're still not individual servings, so if you don't eat them right away, they will go stale. But at least you'll have a lot less waste than with the original giant packages.I'm giving it four stars because I love Honey Grahams, but it loses a star because it's not actually snack-size servings. Other than that, these are great!

column4: Jason P. Pumphrey "the movie & music man"
column9: tasty little treats in nice little packs!
column10: Honey Maid Graham Crackers seem to heve been around forever (I can always remember them in my 37 years on this rock). I remember my grandmother (who sadly passed in 2009 at age 87) giving me these when I would come to visit her each weekend in the late 70's/early 80's. I still like Honey Maid Grahams to this day.  The nice size packs are perfect for taking to work as a snack.

Honey Maid Fresh Stacks are the same Honey Maid Graham crackers you know and love, just packaged differently.  8 fresh little graham squares to a packet, just right for school lunches or tossing in your pocket or bike bag.  Each packet would provide 260 calories, so even at this size it might be a bit big when compared to all the 100 calorie snack packs out there.I don't know anyone that doesn't love graham crackers.  But the staleness issue is universal.  Once the little tan package has been opened, the crackers have a limited life span.  This will definitely allow those of us without lots of graham cracker eaters in the house to have fresh ones on hand.The perfect size for smores, these are packed as squares, or half the large rectangles we are used to.  But even the square size is hard to eat without getting crumbs everywhere.  The only improvement I would suggest is a more rectangular, snack friendly shape.  Of course, that would make smores difficult.In any case, the breakthrough with this product is in the packaging.  I abhor over-packaging of any kind (even the above mentioned 100 calorie snack packs of various snacks).  Its not cost-conscious, and its not friendly to the environment.  But I'll give Honey Maid a pass in this situation.  It doesn't add up to be much more packaging than before, but will result in far less waste.Great idea!

I had to get on here quick to write a review before these were all gone.  They are very tasty!  I like that they are high fructose corn syrup free, although they do have "soybean and/or partially hydrogenated cottonseed oil."The small packages are perfect for on the go.  They're also great for at home.  I used to put the open large packages into a ziploc bag to try to keep them fresh, but these little packages are just the right size, each containing 250 calories and 8 square crackers.  The crackers themselves are a nice size, at half the size of the traditional graham cracker.  No more breaking them in half and getting crumbs everywhere.  These are tasty and convenient.

These are the perfect size for a lunch box or to stick in your glove box for a snack on the road. I like how they have portioned in seperate packages because in the past I have found my graham crackers do become stale. I will buy this in the future for lunches or a quick sweet snack.

column9: Convenient & Tasty!  Great On a Long Run or Bike Ride
column10: These graham crackers are simply delicious.  I love them. This new packaging, with smaller portions, makes it convenient to take to work, school, or on a long run or bike ride.  You still get the same yummy honey graham cracker taste, but in a more convenient package to take on the road.  This new size is also easier for kids to handle.  The traditional crackers are a bit too large for small hands. Overall, a great product.NOTE: Each individual stack brings two servings (8 crackers. 130 calories per serving).

column9: One instance where packaging CAN make a difference.
column10: Nothing remarkable here- just good ol' Honey Grahams that taste the way they always have - simply delicious! The difference is that they are being packaged differently in more efficient snack sizes. Having put this to the test I can honestly say that this is one instance where packaging does make a difference. Grahams tend to go soft if left open for too long. In this case by wrapping them in portion sizes it allows you to maintain freshness for longer. Good idea Nabisco!

column9: The Same Crackers Found in Campfire S'Mores
column10: Lingering evenings by campfires, sitting on old stumps, fumbling through the delicious art of s'more making always involves Honey Maid honey grahams. These are those crackers.Unlike their classic brethren, these are batched in six packs of eight crackers. Otherwise, they are the same. Future campfires can include passing out a pack to each person (I dare not say child, knowing adults love them as well).The recipe is simple:* Two crackers make a sandwich around a piece of milk chocolate and a marshmallow.* Hold tightly together (but not too tight) over a fire with tongs.* When the chocolate and marshmallow melt just enough to be squishy, eat.* Wash down with hot chocolate.Eight crackers are also just enough for a snack, as I am having now, accompanied by orange juice.--Brockeim

I have not eaten a graham cracker in a very long time.  These are nice with a crunchy crisp taste and honey flavor.  They are conveniently packed in smaller packages that hold 8 crackers each.  Easy to pack for a lunch or take on a day trip.I really enjoyed the flavor of these graham crackers and would recommend them.

What I expect a graham cracker to be like. These could easily qualify as comfort food for most people.They seem to have the right amount of honey which is just a touch. Also they have a nice healthy cruch when you bite into them.Earlier in the day that I received these cookies I had been repairing fences. As I was a bit hungry I was happy to find that these had been delivered. These honey grahams sure hit the spot.

These crackers come packed in small 3x3 inch squares that are easy to toss into a lunch bag or to pack for a trip or snack while on the road in a car, airplane, etc. Each pack contains 8 crackers with a total of 250 calories and these crackers are quite tasty and filling as well. There is about 16g of sugar per pack, which is about 1/2 of one can of soda. Each pack also contains 14% of your daily sodium and 9% of your daily fat content, but no trans fats.The crackers would also be perfect for smores by a campfire and are just the right size, about 1/2 the size of the large sized graham crackers I remember as a child.It is a very filling snack and I enjoy these crackers and would recommend them to anyone who wants to have a few good snacks to toss into a lunch bag or for after school.

column9: Same Honey Maid product in a much easier size
column10: These are the tried and true graham crackers that we all know but the small square size is a big improvement.  I suppose if you're making s'mores the original size might be better, then again s'mores built on this smaller platform would work out nicely too I bet.  These square graham crackers, as best I can tell, do not have the perforated lines that the original size has.  The lines that suggest you could cleanly break them into four neat pieces but rarely do.  However, this size is very easy to break in half with fairly even results.  I withhold one star for the partially hydrogenated oil, the artificial flavoring, and the fact that there is more white flour than whole-grain graham flour.

Honey Maid graham crackers are a staple in my home. We've tried other brands, but none can match the grahamy flavor Honey Maid. While I was initially a bit disappointed the crackers do not come doubled up like the standard graham crackers, it soon becomes clear why. Keeping the crackers smaller and more tightly packaged, preserves the crisp quality of the crackers making them exceedingly fresh.Graham crackers have been around a long time. They first were produced as a brand in 1829 by a Presbyterian minister as a way of curbing... Unwanted `carnal' desire.  I didn't realize that, but while researching for this review I found that amusing- While I can't say that graham crackers work that way for me, they certainly do make a great snack.To further the taste-test on these crackers I offered some to my sister and mother and they were both quite pleased with the fresh crisp quality of these cookies.

The appeal of this specific product is suposed to be the packaging. The individual stacks of crackers are smaller than typical.Well, it falls a little short. The packages aren't anywhere near single-serving. There are 8 2-3/8" squares in each hard to open pouch. That's about twice -- close to three times -- what I would consider a single serving.The pouches are so thick, you either need a sicsors or knife to open them, and there is no way to roll them closed again. You either need to plan on finishing them before they go stale, or find another container to store them in. Hardly what I'd choose to call "fresh stacks".The crackers themselves were fine. Nothing spectacular one way or the other about them. But then again, we're talking about a pretty utilitarian cracker here, so one person's spectacularly good would be someone else's spectacularly bad. So not much to say there.All in all, unless the size of the pouches are just the size you usually want, it's not worth paying extra for these. I'm just going to get regularly packaged crackers, and store them in a larger plastic bag to keep them fresh. If I'm going to need a plastic bag anyway, why pay extra for these harder to get open pouches that need to be opened more often, too?

These graham crackers are a lot better tasting than the organic graham crackers that I have tried. And compared to other brands (generic) I much prefer the crunchy sweetness of Honey Maid. The graham crackers taste so fresh and are the best for dunking in milk or tea. I love these as an alternative to cookies. Fortunately, the packaging ensures that the last graham cracker is as good and crispy as the first one. The portable and palatable treats are great for kids or anyone on the go (and for making perfectly shaped s'mores).

column9: Best way to get fresher graham crackers.
column10: These little packs of 6 graham crackers are a great way to keep the crackers cripsy and fresh.Usually, you open the pack and then need to transfer the unused ones to a ziplock back to keep them from getting  stale.These little containers make it so you can put the little packs in your kids lunchbox or take em with you for snacks and they are always crispy and fresh.The wax paper wrapping is also easy for little hands to tear open.This should have been done a long time ago.

These aren't bad graham crackers, but they're not great, either (I prefer Keebler).  Cheaper store-brand crackers might be just as good, depending on your preferences (and store), and the "convenience" of smaller pouches seems be designed purely as a cost-saving (less product per box) function for Nabisco.I was initially intrigued by the new packaging concept.  I like having the crackers split into squares, and the smaller pouches are a good idea.  But if they're going to do it this way, I wish they had made the pouches single serving (rather than two servings).  Otherwise, there's just not a lot of point to having smaller pouches.  And the pouches are impossible to open without using scissors or breaking the crackers in the process.And speaking of broken crackers, probably two-thirds of my crackers were broken on arrival.  This is probably from shipping, so if having whole crackers is important for your purposes, you might think twice about ordering these online.Overall, this isn't a bad product, but just be aware of what you're getting (just 12.2 ounces divided into six pouches).

column9: Same treat... a little better package
column10: I'm not going to get too terribly excited about this, but it probably makes sense for some folks.  Basically what Nabisco has done is to package those addicting Honey Maid Graham Crackers in half groups.  Huh? The standard way of grouping the product is to  put them in stacks of full-size crackers, each of which breaks into four smaller pieces.  So the innovation here is to split the crackers in half.  And to add insult to injury, two of these half crackers are smaller than one of the "old" ones.So the benefit here is that there is less likelihood that the crackers will get stale in the box, due to the fact that you'll have fewer of them in an open wrapping than before.What I'd like to know however, is why did they stop there?  Why couldn't they have come up with a better form of wrapping the stacks that wasn't so damnably irritating to open?  That might have received four stars from me.  This only gets three, and only because the crackers are still so tasty!

column9: Fresh and yummy, but was delivered as mostly crumbs
column10: This was one of the freshest, crunchiest graham crackers I have ever tried, the individual packages are too big for a single serving, so it is a good idea to have someone to take it away from you before you eat almost 3 servings of graham crackers.I think packing the crackers in single serving sizes would have been more useful.The overall product package is not protective enough to make this a good item for ordering over the internet, I was sent a single box and in each individual package you were lucky to find a single unbroken cracker.The only bright side of ordering this from Amazon would be if you really like making desserts with graham cracker crusts and would like your crackers to come pre-crushed.Final thoughtsTasty item, individual packages too big to be a single serving, overall package is not protective enough to survive Amazon's rather inconsistent packing process.

These individually packed graham crackers by Honey Maid are such a  great idea. The crackers stay fresh and crispy and you don't have to stress over eating the entire pack because you fear they will become stale. These are a great idea for children or individuals who want a nice,quick, and easy snack that has a great package that's very effiecent.I will defiently buy this newly packaged graham crackers so that I can have a simple snack and not have to worry about binging on an entire pack of crackers.
