The packaging does not travel well but if you place it on the top of the lunch bag or purse then you have a nice fresh snack perfect for work or school.In today's society with many children overeating and becoming more overweight I think that small steps like these can help parent's maintain control with some of the overindulgence that has been going on with our children. Great idea Honey Maid and good job.

column4: Keith E. Webb "Creator of The Coach Model"
column10: I love Honey Maid graham crackers! These "Fresh Stacks" are the same recipe as their longer cousin. It's like the long ones only snapped in half and packaged in stacks of 8. There are 6 packages of 8 in each box.It's a good idea. Smaller packages allow you to open and not have to save the remainder of the package for many days, thus crackers are fresher. If you make smores (with roasted marshmellows and chocolate) these are already the optimal size. And because they are smaller than the regular size, they'll fit in a bag or lunch much easier.One thing to watch out for is that the individual packages are not single serving, there are two servings inside - a total of 260 calories.So, this has all the flavor, in the size I usually break them into anyway. A winning combination.

Received this as a stand-alone item, so ordering them with something else might be different, but my box came completely crushed.  If you order this to be flavoring on top of ice cream, great, but as actual snacks, you'll only get about 2 out of each individual package that's not broken.

These graham crackers are delicious and perfect for taking on camping trips or picnics where s'mores are an option, since they're already just the right size-- no breaking larger crackers into uneven halves!  The little packets really cut down on the tendency of grahams to go stale before you've used them.  However, it would actually have been even better if the folks at Honey Maid had put these in packets about half this size, so that my family and I could have a single serving per pack in our lunches.  As it is, they're very calorie-laden and one little pack should be about two servings of crackers, which leaves you needing to store the other two or three until you're ready for them, meaning you'll need another bag to hold them in the mean time or some other method of keeping them from leaking graham crumbs and sugar all over your bag.All in all though, these are a great idea.  They're certainly perfect for group snacking, and with just a tiny adjustment they'd also be ideal for single serve.

column9: Perfect for snacking while in the office.
column10: COSTAs of date of this review, a pack of 6 cost $27.32.Each box contains 6 stacks with 8 crackers in each stack.If you do the match, each box cost $4.55, and each stack of 8 crackers will cost you exactly 75 cents.At 75 cents for 8 crackers, the price is reasonable for that mid-day office snack when you are hungry but have already finish lunch, and dinner is hours ahead.the packaging is good enough that it can withstand being thrown around in a purse, though the corners of the crackers will be cracked.NUTRITIONeach stack is 250 calories (a no-no for those on diets)saturated fat is 8% (1.5g), no trans fat, polyunsaturated fat is 2.5g (reasonable), monounsaturated fat is 1g (reasonable)NO CHOLESTEROL! (yay)Sodium is 340 mg (14%) <--- careful for those who need to watch sodium)Iron is 10% (good)TASTEAdults will prefer the taste better as younger kids will feel it needs just a bit more of sugar. Teenagers and older kids will like. Some crackers are a bit dry so it can get stuck in your throat. But the taste is good! beats the hunger pang.ALLERGIES: contains WHEATThe box can be recycled.RATINGFor Office: Afor teenagers' lunch: Afor little children: B

column9: Same Honey Grahams - more convenient packaging
column10: These are the same Honey Graham Crackers we grew up on, in a new package to keep them fresh.If you are one of those who finds yourself throwing away the rest of your graham crackers because they get stale, you'll find these Fresh Stacks a more convenient way of keeping them fresh. They come 8 squares to a package, and can be more handily used in this smaller size package.However, if you are looking for something to carry with you (lunch, snack, etc.) you need to note that these packages are each TWO servings. What is nice is that the package clearly notes the nutritional value for both the single serving AND the package size. The package size has 250 calories and 6 grams of fat, as well as 46 grams of carbs - a "hefty" snack for anyone trying to moderate either item. In fact, if you add peanut butter to these (I keep the individual packs of peanut butter on hand, which could be easily used with these), you hit 500 calories.While I appreciate the convenience, I would most likely compare the price with the "regular" packaging before I purchased these, and carry the individual servings in a sandwich bag. Good idea ... just don't assume one serving per package. ;-)

Honey Maids are the only brand of graham crackers I buy, and my kids and I go through at least a box a week. We love their relative healthfulness - 5 grams of whole grains to 8 grams of sugar per serving is much better than cookies, fruit snacks, and even many brands of granola bars - and we love their incomparable great taste. The boxes we usually buy at the store contain big packs of rectangular-shaped grahams that really don't transport that well, but these little packages contain two serving sizes worth of crackers in easy-to-handle squares and are just perfect for snacking on the go. I love them!In my experience, Amazon Grocery prices vary greatly from item to item... I've found wonderful savings on some things and head-shakingly high prices on others. The current price on these crackers is nearly twice what I pay for the slightly larger, traditional boxes at the local grocery, so I certainly won't be stocking up here and now, regardless of the convenience. But I'll be sure to keep my eye out for a better deal in days to come!

I love the idea of packing graham crackers up in smaller portions.  The size is perfect for grabbing and taking with me when I go somewhere to read or throwing in my purse for a snack.  These come 8 crackers to a stack - a serving is listed as 4 though, which is 130 calories - and stay nice and crispy for quite a while.It's awful for you, but these are great smeared with peanut butter, a little vanilla frosting and chocolate chips.  Pretend it's non-fat or eat them while you run on the treadmill.

These graham crackers taste delicious!  Unfortunately, I just polished off one whole square package in a matter of minutes. :)  These are GREAT for snacks for the kids or to use to make a pie crust.  I do like that the individual plastic packages and crackers are the smaller SQUARE size (which is half the size of the original RECTANGLE size).  I always felt the HUGE rectangles were a bit too big.

column9: These are your grandfather's graham crackers.
column10: Here is one product that seems to have been left unmodified for generations.  This is a review of HOENY MAID FRESH STACKS HONEY GRAHAMS.  The product consists of a total 345 grams of graham cracker.  This is about one third of a kilogram.  To provide some perspective, the typical adult in America weighs about 65 kilograms.The crackers come in a box, and in the box are six envelopes, each envelope containing 8 square-shaped graham crackers.  The American consumer, and perhaps people in Europe, might be more used to graham crackers that are rectangular shape.  Apparently, the goal of using only 1/2 crackers that are square, instead of full-crackers that are rectangular, are to extend freshness, for those who only eat graham crackers once in a while.  Yet another reason for this new packaging is likely to prevent breakage, that might occur with the traditional rectangular crackers, during transportation.But a more likely reason is to allow people to take individual servings with them, perhaps on trips, to school, or to work, with the confidence that the crackers will be kept safe, secure, and intact.  In my opinion, and perhaps those of others, one serving amounts to 8 crackers.  Thus, the great benefit of the HONEY MAIN FRESH STACKS product is not really "freshness," but ease in packing an individual serving for school or trips.Now for the good part.  The crackers taste just the same as they have for generations, at least to this palette.  When I opened one package, I got the whiff of vanilla.  Or anyway, it was a pleasant aroma.  The color is light brown, perhaps the color of your favorite puppy, or perhaps the color of a stone formation at one of the National Parks in Utah.  The flavor is graham flavor.  The texture of this product is on the soft side.  Compared to another type of cracker, for example, SALTINES, the HONEY MAID graham crackers are softer and less cracky.  To conclude, I would not characterize this food as "an adventure," but I might be tempted to call the HONEY MAIN graham cracker, addictive.According to a well known source (Wikipedia), Graham flour is a type of whole wheat flour named after the American Presbyterian minister Rev. Sylvester Graham (1794-1851), an early advocate for dietary reform.  Graham despised processed white flour and believed that bran was the cure-all for the bad eating habits of his compatriots.Rather than simply grinding the whole grain wheat kernel (bran, germ, and endosperm), in graham flour the components are ground separately. The endosperm is ground finely, initially creating white flour. The bran and germ are ground coarsely. The two parts are then mixed back together, creating a coarse-textured flour that bakes and keeps well. Graham flour is used to make graham crackers and pie crusts, among other things.  It should be noted that the nutritional label on the HONEY MAID box clearly reads, "graham flour."

This Fresh Stacks approach is ideal! I love to make peanut butter and graham cracker snacks, and each of these individually wrapped packs contains eight squares each (the packaging indicates "About 8 Crackers") which turns out to be just the right amount [typically] to avoid leaving open leftovers in the box to lose crispness.The crackers are already in a square shape for many baking and snacking needs. Although the crackers have the signature dashed score on the cracker, I have yet to be able to break it straight across as I could with the full sized rectangular crackers.These are the same delicious Honey Maid graham crackers they've always been, only now they're available in this fresh-pack option that's even more convenient for a brown bag lunch than the original form. I think they're great!
I ate it with peanut butter spread on top as finger food with my girlfriend. It's delicious precut sizes are helpful when eating it as dinner or snack. It was dinner for us. We're poor.

column9: My rating is based solely on the packaging, not the graham...
column10: First thing I have to say is that these are the regular honey maid grahams.  I like them.  They are a good product.  I would generally give this product five stars.  My two stars are for the packaging.If I were to buy these, I would just buy them in the standard pack.  They are a lot cheaper than these smaller wrapped stacks.  They have basically taken a couple of graham crackers, broken them in half (literally, they are not produced in smaller pieces, they have been broken in half), and package them in smaller bundles.  These bundles are appropriate for 2 or 3 kids.  There are too many grahams to be individually wrapped.  If it were me, I would break a couple, throw them in a baggie, and save a little money and packaging.All in all, I will continue to buy this brand.  My kids prefer it.  I won't buy them in this packaging.  As a side note, this and ritz type crackers, I don't buy from Amazon.  These came obliterated.  Seriously, I didn't have a single one that wasn't broken.  This is a grocery store item.

column9: Love graham crackers: added 04/04/11: Buy 'em, you'll love 'em!
column10: Update 4JUL11: Well, believe it or not the last package is still crispy and good tasting! These are winners! I'm changing my star rating to 5 since the extra packaging works.Just like I remember 'em (and my wife agrees), though I haven't had one for at least 15-years. Tasty, and with the individual packaging, I assume the vast majority will stay fresh longer than opening one big package... I will update this when the testing is done, though I don't know if I'll have the packages around long enough to do a really strict test ;-)4-stars because extra packaging = bad for environment. The alternative is keeping crackers/cookies in the freezer which keeps 'em fresh, though I assume if you access them frequently you are using a lot more electricity = bad for the environment too.

column9: Super convenient. Perfect for 2 year olds.
column10: As a parent on the go, you always are trying to fill a bag at the last minute with snacks for the kiddo's. This is why string cheese, banana's and these new "fresh stacks" are great. We also like the Ritz version. Just grab a small pack as you are heading out the door and you have a quick PB and Graham Cracker Sandwich or a simple snack on its own.We love them and the kids love them. Winner!

These Honey Maid Fresh Stacks are good portable snacks great for carrying in a bag or purse for those times when a person needs a quick "pick me up" The snack is a smaller version of the popular Nabisco Honey Maid Graham Crackers.  Each pack has eight  graham crackers that are about 25 percent the size of the original cracker.  They provide a tasty treat, advertized at 24 grams if carbohydrate and 130 calories.There are several problems: The serving size is four (4) crackers, but each "pack" has eight (8).  So when I am on the go, I either eat half of the "pack" for my 130 calories, or eat twice what I thought.  If I eat half, then a leave four crackers which will spread crumbs throughout my carry bag.  It would have been better to make each pack four coachers (Or 6 crackers at 195 calories), but 260 calories is too large a snack for me.Second, these crackers are not gluten free.  Gluten free snacks are becoming increasing popular.  Third, because of the "partially hydrogenated" oil, these are not recommended for anyone with heart disease, high blood pressure, or weight problems.It seems a shame that Nabisco did not market a more healthy snack.  This "snack pack" is the same cracker as the regular honey graham.  If Nabisco would re-market this without gluten and substitute a different oil, this product could be superior.  As it currently exists it is an average snack.

Honey Maid has always been one of my favorite brand of graham crackers.  The new packaging of six crackers in a compact form is handy.  Mothers of toddlers will love the convenience of these fitting easily in a purse or small pocket.  However, I found these crackers dry and hard to break apart.  They crumbled easily and wouldn't break at the serrated lines.  I am not sure if this is a storage problem or if this batch is over baked.I would try these again if I bought them fresh.  As is, I would want to buy another brand in that I don't enjoy stale crackers.

column9: An Iconic Snack Made Even Better
column10: As a big fan of graham crackers (and who makes a better one than Honey Maid?) I am often disappointed in getting back to an unfinished portion and finding them stale. After being stuck with practically bendable crackers later, I started emptying the whole container into a ziplock back and hoping they remained crisp.Well, now they've introduced a new "Fresh Stacks" packaging, which cuts the number of crackers in each individual package in half. Just about the right amount of crackers for two to enjoy.The rest is easy, just get a glass of your favorite beverage and enjoy these iconic crackers, knowing that the next "stack" is going to be crisp and fresh! My serving suggestion is to layer vanilla ice cream between two of these bad boys and you have about the best ice cream sandwich possible.But exactly does the world "graham" mean? In 1829, a minister named Sylvester Graham invented a new way to process flour. Instead of grinding whole grain wheat kernels , graham flour's parts get ground up separately. The inside of the kernel gets ground at a fine setting, which makes standard white flour. Then the outside germ and bran are ground using a coarse setting. Once they are all mixed together, it creates a more textured product which bakes easier and tastes sweeter. It's also much better for you and has a higher fiber content.Well, as alternately boring and interesting as that all is, we owe it to Sylvester for today's resulting graham crackers, which are pretty much a staple food at my house. And Nabisco's Honey Maid is - after much testing of other manufacturers' competing product - easily the best graham cracker out there. And this new packaging idea has made them even better!

These beverage coasters are made out of some strange material that simply does not hold up.  I would think that the first, if not the only requirement for a coaster would be that it has to be waterproof.  Cold beverages "sweat," and the main reason to even use a coaster in the first place is to protect the surface beneath them.  These become waterlogged almost immediately, and quickly start to crumble and disintegrate into a sticky goo.  Even when new and perfectly dry, they are extremely brittle, with small pieces breaking off almost immediately, and unless great care is taken, tend to crack and shatter in normal use.I did notice that when I failed to clean one of these up fast enough, the dog ate it, which was worrisome, but he did not suffer any ill effects.  So at least these coasters are non-toxic, and certainly biodegradeable.  However, they utterly fail to perform their intended purpose.  I would give this product zero stars if I could.

The packaging is the focus here, and the individual packs make it easier to grab and go, which is what I did. It seemed that the crackers stayed fresh longer, although I have no scientific data for that. I liked having it in the right size to throw in the lunch bag with some peanut butter and get going. The crackers themselves tasted great, I have to admit; better than other brands for sure. After I ran out of this box, I went out and bought another one next time I went shopping, which I guess is the ultimate proof; I got one for free, and I liked it enough to pay for the next one! Overall it's a good product and a great packaging idea.

Taste is great -- but by the time I got the package open it was largely in crumbs.  The packaging is too tough -- unless you have a scissors or knife handy.  Can you put an opening slit into the package?

column9: This is what I expect from a Gaham cracker
column10: I love Graham crackers.  I love crispness, and the way they crumble in your mouth.  I love the subtle sweetness and the hint of spice.  And, these graham crackers deliver on all of those things.  They are exactly what I expect from a graham cracker.  Nothing more, nothing less.  The smaller sized "stacks" are much more convenient for snacking, or using for something like s'mores.  It doesn't take a lot of effort to break a traditional graham cracker in half, but this avoids the annoying problem of them not breaking evenly, or crumbling in the process.  I would be happy to order these again.
Who doesn't like graham crackers??These are light and full of flavor.  Individually wrapped packages make them easy to take with you.For you GC loves.... this one's for you!Thank you.MEF

The taste is what you expect from graham crackers. Very authentic taste. The size of the cracker is perfect. Already set up to make smores if you so desire. Each individual package inside contains 8 squares and only has 250 calories a package so its a much more filling/healthy substitute for a bag of chips from your vending machine at work. Really good. Would defiantly recommend to anyone looking for a much healthier snack.

of course if you package snack in smaller packaging vs big bags it'll stay fresh longer.not sure if the extra packing drives up the cost more or not;daycare providers might be better off with the full wrapped stacks, but these are good for lunch bags and dieters.

The kids loved these and they didn't last long at all... that's the real test of a snack to me.  If the kids like them and they are pretty healthy, you have it made.  The individual-serving size containers help you keep them fresh... if the kids would let them last long enough to go stale in the first place, which they won't.  Still, this packaging method is good for taking them with you, as the wife (or you, if you are a woman) can throw some in her purse and have them ready at a moment's notice.

column9: Can't go wrong with Graham Crackers
column10: This is a great snack, and at a good value. I am glad they are not super-sugary or loaded up with junk. Simple and tasty.

column9: VERY handy, great crackers, not sure if it's worth the price though
column10: I am VERY particular about my graham crackers. In a nutshell, anything other than Honey Maid is second class by a long shot (with the exception of some expensive organic types!).  So as far as the crackers themselves, I give them a glowing 5 stars.My one thing I don't care for is the extra price you pay for the smaller packs of crackers.  I know I am a bit odd in the fact that we have a larger family (and thus I can easily open up a large pack and it will be gone in an instant!), but I just couldn't justify the price of the crackers for the small packs.  That being said, they ARE handy for when it's just me and the toddler, especially when we are on the road and going to appointments, grocery shopping, etc...  so I totally get the convenience thing.  So if you like the convenience of having a smaller package and don't mind paying a little bit more for that, then I would HIGHLY recommend!That being said, you may also want to look at Back to Nature's graham crackers when they are available from Amazon (the other sellers are way too expensive)... they are even tastier (which is rare, like I said I love the Honey Maids!), and they also have small packages with the added benefit of some extra whole grains in them like oats.[...]

column4: Diane B. Wilkes "Diane Wilkes, Voracious Reader"
column10: I have great memories of S'Mores, so I decided I needed to make some of my own, hence the Graham Crackers. It turns out that my memories remain sweet, but my tastebuds have matured and I find the combination of graham crackers, marshmallows and chocolate way too sweet.However, the Honey Maid Graham Crackers by themselves make a most delicious snack. Just the right amount of sweetness, nice and crispy (but not too hard), these snack crackers are a wonderful treat. In this form with the fresh stacks, they remain fresher than ever, and are the perfect traveling size for a kid's lunch (or mine, for that matter!).

Love these! Like someone else said, taste isn't an issue. HoneyMaid always has the best graham crackers, no contest. However, these individual, smaller packages are MUCH easier for toting around as a snack.Would definitely buy these again!

My wife loves graham crackers and milk as a afternoon snack.  She taste-tested Honey Maid Fresh Stacks and said that they were good, very good.  "Why", I asked.  Because they add a little something to spice up the crackers.  What else can I say.

I love the idea of these.  Each pack you can grab and go with and they stay fresh.  Great for campfire time and the perfect size for S'mores.  Stick a pack in a ziploc with a Hershey bar and marshmallows and you are ready to roast.  The others packs stay fresh until you are ready to eat them.
These crackers had a nice "graham cracker" flavor, not flat or stale like some brands.  The packaging would work well for picnics, lunches or grab-and-go snacks.

column9: Still got stale easily, but a nice thought
column10: If you can eat an entire one of these little packages in a half a day, you won't have to worry about staleness. However, I would just recommend getting the regular size with less individual packaging and using a reusable zip bag or other container to keep the rest from getting stale. The graham crackers themselves were the usual good but not outstanding Honey Maid fare.

These are graham crackers packaged in smaller quantity.  It was great for grabbing quickly when running out the door and short on time, for a snack for my preschooler in the car or wherever we were going.  I also kept a package in my diaper bag for emergency back-up snack.

column4: Prosecute Wall St. Criminals "End Corporate Rule"
column10: This was a great idea to package these in smaller quantities to take along. We also like that they're not overly sweet.

Not real easy to mess up graham crackers, I suppose. But these are great for smores because we'd generally break regular graham crackers in 1/2, and these are all ready done. (Not that it was a real cumbersome task.) Very tasty treat.

column9: Nice, slightly healthier alternative to snack-pack chips
column10: With an elementary-school child and a middle-school child, a busy parent often resorts to buying the pre-packaged snacks.  Call it a sign of the times, but I will admit to buying snack-packs of chips (bad), seaweed (good), and cookies (not so good), for the days when we're too lazy to pack fruit or repack bigger packages of cookies/crackers.  While graham crackers aren't the healthiest snacks available, it's still better than frosted cookies or chips.Overall, nice.  I'd personally prefer a bigger multi-pack, though, 6 is on the small side.  I'd rather pay more for a 12-pack.

I really liked these graham crackers. There isn't anything different about the taste of coarse but the way they are packaged is ideal for man things.Instead of being big rectangular pieces these are halved. This makes them ideal for parents with smaller kids who just want to give their kid a quick snack.Another great use for these is definitely smores! Thanks to these already being broken down into squares you don't have to worry about accidentally breaking them when juggling your chocolate and a flaming marsh mellow.The only thing I could offer in the way of advise to Honey Maid would be to package them in stacks of 3 instead of 6 as the serving size is 3, but that isn't anything to keep me from purchasing these.I'll be keeping an eye out for these at my local grocer!

These are typical graham crackers.  If you like graham crackers, these are as good as any.  The real difference is in the packaging -- rather than those big cellophaned stacks, you get smaller stacks.  This is great for single people or those who just want a few crackers.  In a regular package, once you opened the cellophane on the big stacks, they started getting stale.  These smaller stacks prevent that from happening.

These are great traditional graham crackers in convenient smaller packs.  I like that the crackers are square and not the standard oversized rectangles - the squares are great for smores and snacking.  I like that they are a convenient size to put into a zip baggie for freshness or just eat the entire pack for a snack.  Minuses are that these are a big brand graham cracker and thus are not optimal for nutrition - only 1g fiber per serving with first ingredient unbleached enriched flour (second ingredient graham flour) and contain the not-so-good-for-you sugar, PHOs (soybean and/or partially hydrogenated cottonseed oil) and artificial flavor.  Honey comes after the sugar and oil in the ingredient list.  They do taste very good and I will likely purchase from time to time.

column9: Good graham crackers -- the kids like 'em
column10: There's not a whole lot you can say about graham crackers. They're exactly what you expect, the same old slightly-sweet, crunchy crackers that we remember from when we were kids. As snacks go, they're reasonably healthy, although I generally prefer to buy the low-fat variety. Yes, they have sugar in them, but they also have dietary fiber, so at least you're getting some good stuff along with it. My kids eat these several times a week and always enjoy them.The idea behind the packaging of this particular variety is interesting: the crackers are packaged in smaller quantities, six squares per package. (Each square consists of two rectangular halves.) In theory, this is a nice idea, allowing you to grab a pack and bring them on the road or wherever else you're going. The problem is, six crackers is really too many for this purpose. If they were packaged in quantities of four, for example, I would find them a lot more useful.

I have five children. I put these snack crackers on the table in front of them and said, "Go ahead and try them." They were completely devoured within about a minute. Based on my picky children's eating habits, I'd say that's a pretty ringing endorsement.I tasted maybe one or two and found them to be quite delicious. I would certainly buy them again if I ran across them in the supermarket. Great product.

column9: Same great taste but new packaging
column10: I love that Honey Maid came out with convenient packaging. I am a huge graham cracker fan and now I can just grab them on the go. You get just enough in the package to fill your snacking urge without having too much or too little. I love how they stay fresh longer since you get 6 smaller packs within the box. This is a great snack for you on the go or for your children at school. I highly recommend these convenient fresh stacks if you like graham crackers.

column9: Our fave snack, in the perfect size!
column10: My kids are pretty sure that Graham Crackers are the best thing ever. And they don't want any other brand but this one. They are picky little brats. When I got the opportunity to try these 'fresh stacks' - snack size type things, school was just getting ready to let out and I thought "why not, looks like a quick school snack" and grabbed it.I honestly forgot about them until the last few days of school. And thank goodness for that! My kids are in Elementary and the last week of school is completely insane trying to get everyone up and the projects done and the fun stuff done and... and... and... I had like NO food in the house. I told them to buy lunch and then went rooting around in the pantry.SCORE! I handed them to them and said "graham crackers, let's go". After I finished explaining that no no no no... these really WERE graham crackers, just in a different package, off they went.And they then took them for the next two days. I'm told this was the perfect size with just enough for their school snack and was super yummy to boot.That makes my kids think I'm a rockstar mom. Thanks, Honey Maid.Great product. Great size. Great idea. Sold!We've since bought a few packages of these. They are great to toss in the car when you aren't sure if you're going to be late getting back for dinner, to the soccer game, or just when the kids are whining. I like that it's portioned too. Keeps them from just mindless eating them. (I told you they were graham nuts).

I was already familiar with the Honey Maid crackers and always enjoyed them. The flavor is always consistently good. This option is better because the box contains six individually wrapped packages with about eight or ten crackers in each pack. It's great because you don't have to open the whole box with worry about the remainder of the crackers getting stale. The individually wrapped packs would also be good for snacking on the run. It's easy to just grab a package of these and put them in your purse for later. The only drawback is that sometimes eight crackers is just more than desired for a snack and there is no way to really seal the bag to save them for later. But, overall, this cracker is a delicious snack choice, especially if you are on the go.

column4: Jennifer Spinner "wife, mom, all-around nice gal"
column10: No need for plastic baggies or sloppy tin foil wrappers.  Honey Maid Fresh Stacks are the perfect package for a snack on the go or to keep a few in the car for unexpectedly long rides.We homeschool our children, so there's no need to pack lunches, but - if the price is right - I'll consider buying these again in the future.Recommended.

column9: A Great Snack in a New Size
column10: Honey Maid Graham crackers are as good as ever - a great snack for kids of all ages.  When my children were younger, we would go through the larger packages very quickly and never had a soggy or stale one.  Now that just my husband and I are at home, the large packages get opened, we have a few crackers, and then the rest end up going stale and get thrown out.  This happens even though we put the crackers in zip lock - can't figure out why!With this new size, we are able to share a small package and keep the rest of the crackers fresh for the next time we want a snack.  I can imagine taking a small package on a flight or a car trip (sometimes a little snack helps with motion sickness.)  I like the idea and will certainly purchase more of the Fresh Stacks size. I hate throwing food away so paying a little bit more for convenience may actually mean savings in the long run as we are sure to finish the package.  Buying cheaper doesn't always mean a bargain - it is only a bargain if you like the product and will use it up commpletely.

column9: No more throwing out 1/2 packs of crackers!
column10: With a house full of small children, we eat a lot of graham crackers.  A lot.  These mini packs are a great!  They keep the crackers fresh and I throw out a lot less crackers.  The packs are the perfect size to keep in my purse for after school snacks.  I like to pair them with the mini-size peanut butter packages from Jif to give them a little extra nutrition.All in all, a great idea.  I wish they would have done this a long time ago.

column4: B. McCarthy "Engineer, CERT, Amateur Radio Op...
column10: So the question here is what should I be reviewing.  If I review the graham crackers, I would point out that the reduced fat version is healthier and tastes the same.  If I review the packaging I would point out that you pay more per ounce and could save money by doing this yourself with ziplock bags, but the idea is sound and nothing is defective about it.  And if I reviewed the Honey Maid brand against other brands, I would say that they are similar in taste and texture and that they live up to the quality that one would expect from the brand.I hope that gave you insight into all aspects of the product.  Overall, I am going to go back to buying the reduced fat ones and ziplock bags.

column9: The crackers are great as usual.
column10: The product was offered for review because of the packaging.  They are stacks of square crackers, one half of the large ones that we are used to.  They come in two serving packs. I liked having the crackers already broken in half, because that's the size I give to a child.  I think I'd prefer to have re-sealable packaging, but this wasn't bad.  We never did have to eat soggy or stale crackers.Just be aware, this is a package that is a right size for having several toddlers hanging on to your skirts, not a size pre-packaged to put in lunch boxes.

These are the same Honey Made graham crackers I grew up eating so if you liked those or you like them today, what is there not to like here?In 2+oz packs they are easy to use if you want to control portion size and also to transport though they will still break apart just as if you put then in your own baggie. That's the only potential negative here because they do cost more than if you portioned out your own crackers.  But if you are busy or just don't want the hassle, this is a good way to help yourself and your loved ones take just a bit of sweetness with you.

These are tasty asusual, not too sweet just a kiss of honey-loved that they are in mini packs helps to keep them fresh and makes is easy to grab some on the go. They were so good we ate them before we could make smores, or have them in any other recipes for that matter. The whole family loves them I highly recommend you give them a try!

The size of the packages is very compatable with a lunch bag or sack.  The crackers and a few pieces of cheese or some peanut butter traveled well and did the trick for a workshop held away from the job.The crackers maintained their shape and taste through two days of travel.

column9: A classic snack in smaller packets
column10: These are your classic Honey Maid graham crackers -- a long-time snack favorite -- repackaged into smaller packets. This makes some sense: With fewer crackers per packet, the others stay sealed where they won't get stale. Also, each packet is now a handy size that could fit in a pocket or a purse.You might want to think about how graham crackers are consumed in your household to see if this is a good fit. Do you go through packages fast or slow? If fast, then the staleness concerns may not even be a consideration. Would it be handy for you to take a packet on-the-go as a snack? If you're only going to eat them at home, the smaller packet size will be less important to you.

Who doesn't love graham crakers?!? Now that they are in these neat lil packages, they have become even more transportable. Just pop em in ur lunch bag/box, purse, backpack, glove box.. They are that portable!! The taste texture are the same as we all have been accustomed to, so no surprises there. Pick up a box today.

I really like how they packaged these crackers, which is the big selling point.  Rather than having a package 1/2 full sitting around getting stale, the crackers are packaged in smaller amounts.  The size is nice too.  The square packages would fit nicely in a lunch box.  A great idea!

These are the same Honey Maid Graham Crackers that we all know and love, just different packaging.  They are squares (actually the same size squares as 1/2 of the full-size crackers) packaged in stacks.  These are nice for my household now (just 2 of us) as it keeps the crackers fresher (since there is a smaller amount in each package).  I would have really liked them when I had little ones and wanted to keep some crackers in a bag for hunger crankies.  They are sized perfect for s'mores also!  Just grab a package or two, no need to juggle hot marshmallows and chocolate while you break a cracker in two.

Smaller squares in smaller pouches makes this same great snack/treat even easier to enjoy.  You can pack in lunches, take on trips and still enjoy the freshness of a new pack, without twice the quantity of crackers.

column9: Great taste that both Adults and Kids will enjoy
column10: Believe it or not, this was the first time that I've tasted this brand of graham crackers.  They have a nice sweet taste (hence the "honey" part), but not overly sweet.  My toddlers enjoy getting these as a snack.  We'll also be sure to build some 'Smores snacks with these as well.Generally the crackers break according to the perforated lines.  I mention this because I hate when snacks crumble when you don't expect it and make a big mess for you to clean up ;)I'm pretty happy with these crackers and plan to buy more.

column9: The Crackers You Always Loved, But More Convenient
column10: These crackers are always good - if you like them.  I won't say there is any difference from other Honey Maid Graham crackers.  But I will say normally they are quite large and in long stacked packages that are incovenient for lunches or travel.  These packs are similar to the new 100 calorie packs or single serving packs - much easier for kids lunches or for watching your diet.  Overall this is main convenience, otherwise you can stick to the larger box for savings.

I had always enjoyed graham crackers. These individual servings were great for me to take to work in the morning one at a time. Even though it's not a super healthy breakfast, it help held me through some of the busier mornings when I was in a hurry. I would eat this while I drink honey water.The flavor is great, too. Not too sweet. It's a good snack with warm milk. The grains in the crackers are tasty and adds to an interesting texture if you like whole grain food. Even opened, the crunchiness last a very long time (a couple of days), though I did put it in the fridge.

Anyone who has had the trouble of trying to break apart graham crackers in the middle of maintaining a campfire, divvy up marshmallows and divide chocolate squares knows that it is not very easy. The fact that this often occurs in the dark, after the sun has gone down, makes it even more difficult. The process could turn what is a pleasant family getaway into a fumbling, bumbling fiasco with some if not all of one's tasty treats falling on the ground.This format of graham crackers allows for easy placement, and so allows the user a convenient way to enjoy their post-dinner campfire delight. The Honey Maid taste and quality is still there. Now it's just more convenient.

This packaging for graham crackers is wonderful for families with young kids.  There are six packages of grahams in the box, each containing about 8 half-sized crackers.  We are able to travel with these a little at a time and not worry about the whole box going stale.  They are also great for making smores, as they are already the right size.  Great idea when wanting to make smores for just a couple of people.

In one deft move, Nabisco has solved my one and only problem with graham crackers: that the packaging just doesn't keep them fresh.  These little packs are not only a bit better at keeping the grahams crisp longer, they keep more fresher by reducing the number per sealed pack.  I'm sure someone at Nabisco casually suggested this little gem of a solution, and I hope that chap gets a solid pat on the back.  Well done!

column9: The quality and taste you've come to expect in a more convenient package.
column10: What can I say.  Honey Maid graham crackers are good.  Always have been.  This packaging seems to make way more sense than the traditional rectangles in a larger package that go stale when you don't eat them all right away.  It's probably psychological, but the crackers seem thicker than I remember them being, but I think it's because they are so fresh the crispiness makes it seem like more cracker!  Whatever the reason, the package size is easier to tote and keeps the crackers fresh.  5 stars all the way.

column9: Same tasty graham with keep fresh packets
column10: These are among the best honey graham crackers.What sets this apart from others, is that each box has several small packets (8 crackers in each) inside that you can take with you, so even if you only eat a few at a time (a hard thing to do!) you will still get the benefit of fresh, crunchy crackers when you open the next packet a month or two down the road.

This is a just half-sized and smaller-packaged version of honey graham crackers. They taste the same as you would expect but are packaged "conveniently" for tossing in with your lunch. Personally, I would rather pay less and package what I want to put in my lunch on my own most of the time. What may be considered a plus by many is the individualized packaging; you no longer have to be concerned with them going stale. However, and I may be in the minority here, I actually do not like my graham crackers to be super fresh and crunchy. I usually open a package and let it get some air for a day or so before I start eating them, after they have gotten a little soft and less crumbly. Each to his own! :)

Well , these were a hit!!!From 2yrs. and up , all Graham cracker lovers  went crazy for these !!It was the rich but slight honey flavour that put them above the restThey were also just a bit more crisp as opposed to the usual 'mushy' feel of most Graham CrackersThey had great taste, texture and priceNice value

column9: A half honey graham cracker is still a honey graham cracker
column10: I like Honey Maid graham crackers, but I don't see much reason for this new packaging of a familiar product.  It's the same graham cracker they have always had, just one cracker instead of the usual two (that you can split apart as they have a line in the middle).  I guess it might be slightly more convenient to have the single cracker, but to me it is a kind of waste (if it ain't broke, don't fix it).  When you figure the price in, the regular double cracker is cheaper; to me this is a no brainer (same product, lesser price by buying the original).

So many times we'd open a package of graham crackers just to have half of them go stale. But with this new packaging that didn't happen. They seemed a little more crisp, too, which made for a good texture. All around we're big fans of the new Fresh Stacks.

column9: Great idea but double serving size.
column10: No one likes stale graham crackers but unless you keep them in Tupperware or eat them quickly, they get stale fast.  Welcome Honey Maid fresh stacks.  These have the same great taste as the regular package but in double serving packs.  That is where Honey Maid went wrong.  If you are going to put the grahams in smaller packs, why not single serving packs?  If you want a single serving you still are left storing the remaining half of the opened pack.  Also, the packs are hard to open and I seem to break the crackers getting them opened and also the crumbs fly everywhere.  Last, I'm not sure if this was a shipping problem but two of the packs in my box were opened, which defeats the whole purpose of having a "fresh stack".  So 5 stars for taste but minus 1 for poor implementation.

These Honey Maid "Fresh Stacks" are super cute.  Just the right size to throw in the diaper bag on the go.  There are 8 graham crackers in each 'stack' so 48 total.  My daughter is 18 months old - these are very convenient and keeps the rest of the crackers fresher.

I love honey maid Graham crackers but find invariably we open a pack and don't finish it and the rest go stale pretty quickly.  This box contains packs where each original cracker is half size (think s'more size without having to break them). We typically would open and eat what was in the pack.  The weight on this box is less than the weight on the long cracker box but there is less waste because they are in a more convenient size and you aren't opening way more than can be eaten, so they aren't going stale.  If you have a smaller sized household or just can never seem to break your crackers in half perfectly for s'mores then these are great.

Compared to other graham crackers, this is much better than your generic brand, but also very crumbly.  It's not as moist, but doesn't dry your mouth, and the taste isn't too strong.It may be crumbly because of shipping, so I'm hoping others get theirs intact.
Love these snacks. and the individual packages makes it easier to take on the go for a quick snack. I'm sure it amazing for school kids. But I loe it at work at my desk! :)

column9: Nice and handy for grab and go.
column10: If you like graham crackers but don't like the mess of having to open up an entire packet then this is for you.  These fresh stacks are perfect to grab as an on the go snack or pack in a lunch.  Since the fresh stacks are smaller amounts you don't have to worry about opening up a huge pack to take a few out and having the rest go stale.  These are a no brainer purchase if you are going to be buying graham crackers.

I have always loved and enjoyed Honey Maid Graham Crackers. The fresh statcks are an added plus. The crackers stay fresh a lot longer. Since only a few are wraped together, you don't have to open the entire contents to enjoy a few crackers. They are evenly portioned. Great to put in lunch box for kids and adults. I love the new packaging for easier access for traveling or just for a quick snack on the run.

I have not had a graham cracker in decades. I was very happy to try out a box. I grew up with them. I ate them at my friend's house; my mother bought them, and remember them being available at the child care center my mother managed. I remember they were wrapped in wax at the time and breakable. I had fond memories of them.I will say, as another reviewer wrote, I might have got a slightly `stale' box or overcooked one. I think more overcooked. The `crackers' are really dry and do not have much taste to them. They are just very dry and have not moisture when you put them in your mouth. They taste alright but with the box I got it is hard to judge.I do like the fact that you have 6 individual snack sizes in the box. I live alone and use zip lock baggies for other boxed items but having these individually wrapped helps. I well say the box itself does not stand out much and I think I would walk right past them in the market. They need to make the font bigger and also the actual photo of the item. The majority of the box has what looks like `tiles' on it (meant to be graham crackers).All in all I would give these 4 stars hoping I got an overcooked box. I would also buy them in the future and know when my daughter is old enough I want her to grow up with them like I did. All and all a great snack.

One of the biggest problems with graham crackers was that you had to find a ziplock bag or something to put them in after you opened them because they would get stale very quickly if you didn't. This new form of packaging cuts down the amount of crackers in each package by half so the remaining crackers stay fresh until you open them. A great idea that was a long time coming. If only Oreo (another Nabisco product) could do this also we would really be getting somewhere.

Unless you're making s'mores, chances are you don't finish a whole pack of graham crackers at a sitting; I know I don't.  Honey Maid graham crackers are, in my opinion, a great tasting cracker, and the individual "fresh stacks" packets are a very convenient way to keep them fresh and crispy.  It also makes them a good grab 'n' go option when trying to get out the door in a hurry.  A very practical way to package graham crackers.

column9: Smaller packs for people who hate stale crackers
column10: I like the mini packs in these boxes.  I have always hated opening a new pack of graham crackers because I know I'll have to dig out a plastic bag to seal them up in afterwards or just have to toss the extra in the garbage.  I can't stand smooshy graham crackers!These packs are a little big if you want to eat them as a snack (I like 1-2 full 4-cracker pieces)with 6 2-cracker stacks in each package.  It is enough to make a few s'mores with my girls without going overboard, so I like that idea.  It is also small enough that I could pack one as snacks for the park or with a packed lunch for more than one person.For me, I love the idea but took off a star because it isn't a single pack (for one person)but is enough that I would waste less if I wanted to snack on grahams.  Just don't expect that you can get these and pack one in your child's lunch box unless your child REALLY likes grahams.

column9: No more crumbs all over me
column10: The biggest plus feature of these Honey Maid Fresh Stacks is quite simply - you don't get graham cracker crumbs all over you when you attempt to break apart large sheets of typical graham crackers.  I don't know why they ever made them that way - long rectangles that you have to break apart to eat.  The convenience of being able to pull out of a smaller "square" container 1/2 of a regularly sized cracker is great!  You don't have to break them to eat them!  Except for this one convenience the product is the same as typical grahams.  But that feature is worth it if you are crumb conscious. :)

I got this 6-pack simply to round up an order to get free Amazon shipping.  The Cilantro does not have much taste or smell when sampled from the palm of my hand.  Maybe the flakes work well when seasoning/cooking a turkeyburger but my palate did not tell me so.

I did my research and ask my pharmacist friend regarding this product before I took the plunge to invest in such an expensive sugar - it just seems too good to be true! The only "bad" things I could find are bloated stomach or diarrhea, which didn't occur to us at all.I first bought this from NOW Food. When I finish the 3 pounds, I order it from Prescribed for Life. Maybe it is just me, but I found both the taste and the smell are better than the NOW food one (I can smell watermelon). So now, I just reorder from PFL.I have one little tip to share with potential users: although this product stated that it is heat-stable up to 160C or about 330F, I found that it is best not to bake with it. The best way to use it as a white sugar substitute is to stir in the food you are cooking at the last step to minimize the cooking, or stir in hot tea or warm water to mix with beverages. Using it to sweeten yogurt also tastes great. Bottom line is avoid heating it.

I am well pleased with the granulated erythritol as a sweetener for some of my desserts. Product was delivered in a timely manner and I feel it is a great value for the money.  I am diabetic and this can be used without adverse affect on my blood sugar readings.

column9: you can never go wrong with Galaxy chocolate.
column10: It was received well within the date range expected. The product was just as described. The only reason I gave it 4 stars was because chocolate had melted quite a bit by the time I got it. However, it tasted just as amazing! Thank you and will do business with them again!

When I ordered this new product I wasn't sure what to expect.  To me Newtons are those chewy little bars with the fig filling of which I am such a huge fan.  When my blueberry flavored Newtons Fruit thins arrived I found out that they are thins indeed and quite a departure from the figgy fruit bars. These Newtons are really a round thin cooky (a little over 1/8" thick x 2.5" wide)with lots of crunch.  In spite of the fact that this really doesn't meet with my preconceived idea of what makes a Newton, these are exceptionally good cookies, and appear to be healthful as well.  I love the ingredients--all natural and flavorful. They are sweet, but not overly sweet, which I like.  Blueberries and flax seeds are two of the ingredients I was happy to see as components of Newtons thins. If you are expecting a spin off of the old fruit bars you might be disappointed, but if you're into flavorful, healthy, crunchy cookies to snack on like I am, I think you'll enjoy this new Nabisco product.

I confess that the brown sugar was what grabbed my attention, but the whole family enjoyed the Blueberry Brown Sugar variety of Newtons Fruit Thins.  I loved the brown sugar and blueberry taste and the crisp crunchiness; these thin cookies reminded me of shortbread or shortbread cookies.  One family member dipped hers in yogurt (perfect combination, she said), and we all said that we would be buying more of these!  They are perfect for snacks or dessert, and I think I'll try them with ice cream--the kind of dish where the cookie is stuck into the top of the pudding or ice cream.

column9: An Excellent Snack - Packaging Needs Work.
column10: My husband and I both loved these cookie/crackers, and they didn't last long!  They did seem to be slightly addictive for both of us, but 3 is the serving size, and 3 was enough for my sweet tooth, too.  I didn't think my husband would like them, but I caught him eating them 2 or 3 times.  They didn't taste at all artificial to either of us.  The taste was like a blueberry muffin, but quite crisp.  They ARE thin, but they're also larger than most cookies, which is why 3 was enough.  I'm not saying we couldn't have eaten more, we easily could have, but 3 as a snack really did satisfy my sweet tooth.There was a problem with the packaging on the bag I received - they were nice and easy to open, which I liked.  You just pulled on a plastic strip, and they opened.  I THINK there was supposed to be plastic left to close the bag on, but there wasn't.  Since the inside wasn't enclosed in anything, a closure was badly needed.  This could have been just one bag malfunctioning, but if not, this needs to be worked on.There were plenty of blueberries, and while you couldn't really taste the brown sugar, it was obviously in the mix.  Just a glance at the ingredients, compared to another type of cookies we had showed quite a difference in the amount of some of the ingredients - less of the bad and more of the good.  They're not meant to be a healthy snack, they're still a cookie, but healthier than most of the cookies we buy.  I will DEFINITELY be buying these again!

These are light, fruity cracker-like cookies that are amazingly good. They're stiff, so I imagine they'd be good carriers for cream cheese and fruit for a party yummy. The bag needs to be kept secure to prevent sogginess, so yummies made this way probably couldn't be made too far in advance. FYI, they're about 2 inches across, so they're not bite-sized unless you, like me, have a big mouth. Highly recommended.

column9: I wish my Mom were here...
column10: That woman can wax rhapsodic about a cookie in a way that I can only dream of, but I'll do my best.  Actually, I'm not sure that I'm prepared to wax rhapsodic about this cookie, but I did like it.  The combination of blueberries and brown sugar sounded wildly appealing to me right from the start.As is generally the case with tasting/testing something new, I invited a group of my co-workers down to my office to sample along with me.  The reactions were varied, but none were too negative.  Most of my co-workers were happy to try the Fruit Thins, but weren't planning to purchase them for themselves.  Some commented that they felt the cookies were, "too sweet," but personally, I don't understand that.  These days, so many sugary, chocolaty treats taste overwhelmingly sweet to me.  I found this one to be just about right compared to more childlike cookies.  It's just the sort of nibble to enjoy with a mug of tea.Other co-workers commented on the cookie's texture, due primarily to the inclusion of wheat flour, oats, and flax seeds.  One compared it to a tastier teething biscuit, but having never tried one I'm not prepared to comment, LOL.  Personally, I like the inclusion of fiber and whole grains.  In fact, the entire ingredient list is reasonably healthy.  It's a treat I can feel good about eating.  And I especially enjoyed the subtle crunch of the flax seeds.As for me, I liked the flavor a lot.  You can see the crushed berries in the batter and you really get the blueberry taste.  Oh, and I've had the semi-resealable bag open on my desk for a week now.  The cookies taste as fresh and as crisp as they did on the first day.  That's impressive.  Not only would I buy these cookies again, I'm looking forward to trying other flavors.

column9: Tastes like a graham cracker with bits of blueberry...
column10: These Fruit Thins were just OK in my opinion.  They reminded me of a Graham Cracker with pieces of blueberry throughout.  Although I don't think they were bad, I certainly don't think they were fantastic either.  It's not anything I'll ever be craving or would go out and buy.  If I want a munchie I'll grab something more flavorful.  My 8-year-old son liked these but my 9-year-old daughter didn't care for them much either.  Unless you're a fan of graham crackers and stuff like that I don't think I'd recommend these.

column9: Great new cookie for Newton lovers--all natural, too!
column10: These cookies really do taste a lot like Newtons, but not as sweet. One problem with the regular Newton cookie is it can get a little too sweet. I found these cookies to be a bit more addictive than the Newtons. They have a great natural flavor, with all natural ingredients(Nabisco has taken some time to finally come around with healthier ingredients). The quality and freshness are also excellent, along with attractive and practical packaging.

They don't have the chewiness like the classic Fig Newton does. These are more like a chip consistency, or a very crunchy cookie, but about half the thickness as a cookie. Taste is quite good.However, they do contain Palm Oil, which is very high in saturated fats. This is the current trend, creative packaging to make something look like a healthy snack food, but when you read the ingredient list, you find that it is junk food. They do use unbleached, but enriched flour, and there is some whole grain flour.

I like the flavor of these cookies, and crisp is certainly an appropriate word to describe them. The thing is, people who are looking for a sweet cookie are probably going to be disappointed. People who like things that are not extremely sweet but still flavorful and a bit sweet will. I am not sure what's with the newton label since the only thing it has in common with a fig newton is the name, but they are still enjoyable. On a side note, I like the package the cookies come in too, keeps them fresh and easily closed again.

I am a bit addicted now. I really enjoy the overall flavour.It is not too overpowering in artificial flavour, and it is not too overly fruity. There is not too much crunch, but it isn't like a "normal" Newton fig bar.The blend of the flavours is great and the blend makes it a nice, satisfying taste that isn't too sweet, but gives it enough flavour to be enjoyable satisfying.

These comments are for "Newtons Fruit Thins - Blueberry and Brown Sugar" sold by Nabisco.The package states "crispy cookies" think the firmness and thickness of a graham cracker - yes that firm. These 3-inch round wafers come in a rigid plastic tray that slides into a foil-lined package. Nonetheless several cookies in the two packages I sampled were broken into several large pieces upon opening. Probably not typical but that's what I observed.I found the cookies brittle; they had a tendency to break into several pieces after a bite. As an adult I could compensate be adjusting my method of holding the wafer but children will have a problem.I found the blueberry and brown sugar cookie without much flavor. The package state "made with real fruit" therefore what you have are many small pieces of dried blueberries throughout the cookie. The consistency was adequate but the flavor must have been baked out during the process.I was somewhat taken back by the work "Newtons" in large letters on the package. My understanding of this term is of a soft chewy fruit filled cookie like a fig or apple Newton. I do see the connection then again I am not in Sales or Marketing where these decisions are made.

I really liked the taste of these cookies. They are a cross between a cookie and a cracker. I tried the blueberry and they didn't have an artificial taste. Unfortunately,  I think 130 calories for three thin little crackers is too high for a snack.  They weren't very satisfying and it only made want more.  Not for me but they certainly taste good.

Despite looking a lot like cookies in the image on the packaging, these fruit thins are more akin to crackers.  They are very slightly chewy, but would have been better if they were more chewy, closer to what they look like in the picture, which is why they get only 4 stars and not 5.  The taste is very good, and if you like blueberry muffins, you will like these, as they taste like said muffins condensed into crackers. The blueberries in them are real blueberry pieces, these also provide some of the chewiness, which is pretty good and a great layer of flavor. They are a very good choice if you are in the mood for something sweet but crunchy, and not overly sweet like cookies or candy.

column9: Thin crisps, cross between cracker and cookie
column10: Crisp thin cracker/cookie/wafers about 3 inches across and one eighth inch thick with blueberry speckles throughout. Tasty--everyone in the family enjoys the light, sweet taste. The right consistency that chews crisp with the taste of Fruit Newtons. The only drawback I notice is a few berry things get caught in the corner of your teeth similar to when you eat poppy seed muffins--not a negative, because it's a lingering effect of yummies you get to enjoy after the Fruit thin is gone. They actually paqk a lot of the thins in the package. We enjoyed them lots.

column9: makes a great snack - and healthier than chocolate chip cookies!
column10: I give it 5 stars because these are healthier than the chocolate chip cookie I ate today, and they taste really good.  As other reviewers have commented, the blueberry taste is pretty much spot on - real dried blueberries. they are not too sweet, which is what I thought they may be with "brown sugar" in the name.  They are nicely crunchy and much more like a cookie then a cracker, which is what I had thought looking at the picture on the package.  I ate these with vanilla yogurt which made for a great combination.  I think I will try some of the other flavors as well.Here are the facts from the packaging (why doesn't amazon list this?)ingredients: unbleached enriched flour (wheat flour, niacin, reduced iron, thiamine mononitrate (vitamin b1), riboflavin (vitamin b2), folic acid), whole grain wheat flour, soybean and/or palm oil, sugar, rolled oats, dried blueberries, brown sugar, flax seeds, fructose, salt, baking soda, soy lecithin, natural flavor.(contains: wheat, soy)serving size: 3 cookies - serving per 10.5oz package: about 10amount per serving:calories: 140, calories from fat: 45total fat: 5g (saturated: 1g, trans: 0g, polyunsat: 2.5g, monounsat: 1g)cholesterol: 0mgsodium: 90mgpotassium: 50mgtotal carbohydrate: 21g (dietary fiber: 2g, sugars: 8g)protein: 2gEnjoy!!

I like things with blueberries, and I was hopeful for the Newton Fruit Thins Blueberry Brown Sugar.  I've been taking them in my lunch since I got them, and I'm fairly pleased with them.  A single serving is 3 cookies, and I find this to be enough to be satisfying.  They are crisp but not crumbly, and the taste is pretty good.  The only complaint I have for these is the ingredients.  I find it hard to believe that brown sugar and blueberries are not enough to sweeten them sufficiently.  Down the list of ingredients you will find "Fructose".  If they do need another sweetener, I would rather see evaporated cane juice.  All in all, though, this is picking nits for a non-organic product.  While there are better choices out there, they are many far worse.  It's probably one of the better products that Nabisco makes.

I enjoyed these Newton Fruit Thins very much! They are crunchy, lightly flavored snacks that were perfect for the mid-morning break at the office.  These are not "fig newtons," though; they are not sticky (and are therefore great for work or school snacks), but they can crumble in a lunch bag.  My family has taken to these, and we now buy them regularly.  Recommended.

I'm crunching on one of these biscuit crackers as I'm typing this.  Not quite wafer thin, these Newtons Fruit Thins are pretty yummy.  Not too sweet, yet flavorful.  What I like about them is that you can actually taste and see the actual dried blueberries in each cracker, and three of them only have 5% DV of saturated fat.  That means you can eat up to three without feeling too guilty about it.  The packaging is attractive, with an easy-to-seal opening.  Each bag contains 30 cookies too; a good number.  I can see this being a painless, healthier alternative to actual cookies.  Good job, Nabisco!

column9: blueberry muffin taste, in a thin cookie wafer
column10: Remember when Fig Newtons were boring? there was only one flavor, one shape, and they were the kind of snack my grandmother kept around that the grandkids all hated.These are NOT your grandmother's Newtons.  These "Newtons Fruit Thins" are sort of a cross between a cookie and a cracker. They are thin and crunchy, and not overly sweet. The Blueberry Brown Sugar tastes just like a blueberry muffin. It is very tasty and perfect with a cup of tea or a tall glass of milk.These fruit thins come in other flavors as well, although I've now tried them all and the blueberry are my favorite. I passed these around in a "taste test" to my husband, 6 yo son, and 80 yo mother. All loved them. We buy them every couple of weeks and even put them in my son's lunchbox.Two Thumbs Up!

The taste was okay.  The cookie is thin and light and crispy.  You can really taste the blueberries, which is a good real honest to goodness blueberry taste.  But overall, the sweetness level was okay, the cookie was just meh.  I don't know it's like a cookie that was trying too hard.  We have been crumbling it up and putting it in ice cream, yogurt, mixing it in with granola.  The other problem that we have ended up having with these is that I did not know prior to purchase that the cookies had flax seed in them but not all of the seeds were finely ground, which means that well one the health benefit is lost but also the family members in my house who have diverticulitis got really ill after eating these cookies.I can't put my finger on what I didn't like about them.  Perhaps because the serving size is 3 cookies or thins and that is not at all satisfying as a snack and so it feels like another junk food disguised as a health food.  Taste wise they are okay.  But since they aren't really that healthy, I'd rather pop a real fig newton.

column9: Good, reasonably healthy for a cookie
column10: When I think of Newtons, I think of the incredibly portable snack that I could take along on long bike rides for energy.  They wouldn't really crumble away and were fairly healthy.  Since my biking days, they have expanded their flavor choices, and now they have expanded the product line further.These Fruit Thins *are* thin.  A package contains roughly 28 cookies, in two rows in one of those little plastic trays.  It was a great number for me, as there are seven of us, so they split up evenly.  Of course, I took the two that arrived as total crumbs, and the one that was broken... so this review is based on one whole cookie and a lot of pieces.My husband declared that, "these taste like blueberry muffin crackers!"  I don't happen to agree with the cracker part, exactly.  My kids (ages 5-13) all loved them and commented that it tasted like real blueberries, not that fakey stuff.  Opening the package, it even smells like real blueberries.These aren't as healthy as I would expect from Newtons, but they are decent.  This is something I would consider purchasing for my family.  I love that the ingredient list doesn't include anything I don't recognize.  Next time, I think I want to try the chocolate raspberry though...

column4: Shana "That's my opinion- I could be wrong!"
column9: Nice crunchy and sweet snack without being heavy
column10: These are great when you have a craving for something sweet. These are crispy and just sweet enough to satisify your craving. I love that 2-3 of these Newtons Fruit Thins will give me that sweetness I sometimes crave, yet, they are not heavy at all. These are not soft & chewy like a regular "fig newton". The texture of these is more like a sweet cracker with a softer middle. These are not overly sweet, the sweetness reminded me a bit of the taste of an animal cracker. I loved the flavor combination of the blueberry and brown sugar.My fiance who has a serious sweet tooth wasn't that impressed with them, but, I'd definitely try these again. These are more for those who don't want an overly sweet dessert.

I tried the fig and honey version first, and while they were good, these (the blueberry) are delicious.  The smell is just like a fresh baked blueberry muffin, and the taste is authentic (doesn't seem like processed blueberry).  I was pleasantly surprised.  While these are nothing like fig newtons (which I thought they might be based on packaging), they are a tasty, crunchy treat that isn't too sweet, and is a nice alternative to the typical boxed cookie.

column9: Not quite as good as the Newton fruit crisps
column10: A crispy little cookie snack, good for on the run and to tide the kids over. We have been crumbling them up and putting them in yogurt with berries instead of granola. Not bad at all, even if they can't compare to the original Fig Newton!

These cookies are very tasty! I not only enjoyed the flavor, but the crunch and occasional bit of fruit add an interesting texture. This great cookie reminds me of a fruit-enhanced shortbread. Hard not to eat too many at one time!

column9: perfect with a spot of tea
column10: The Blueberry Brown Sugar "Newtons Fruit Thins" were not what I expected. Thin is the key word to this product. There is no discernible brown sugar flavor, and there is just a hint of blueberry. The cookies are slightly bland, very lightly sweet, and easy to break apart. The plastic tray held many pieces of broken cookie. My first reaction was "so-so", but then they grew on me! I realized that the blueberry flavor, although very mild, had no artifical aftertaste. Three of these cookies equal one serving with 140 calories, 5g of fat, and zero cholesterol. These cookies are absolutely perfect to serve with a cup of freshly brewed hot tea. I would also like to try the other flavors of this product.

These are all right.  Not sweet enough to be called a cookie, but good with tea.  They have a nice crunchy texture and a decent flavor.  I wasn't crazy about the blueberries in them that were more like chewy candy pieces than actual blueberries.  They aren't all that bad for you and are pretty low in sugar, but if I want a cookie I wouldn't reach for these.  They aren't great for you in the first place and I'd rather cheat with something that tastes better.

These are okay tasting.  They have a decent blueberry flavor and are not overly sweet.  The texture is not the greatest though.  They are kind of dry, almost like a blueberry cracker.  These would probably be better if they were chewy.

My kids, especially, just loved these. They're so nice and crispy, such a nice crunch. The blueberry taste could be a bit stronger, but overall a delicious product. We'd definitely buy them at the supermarket.

These fruit thins really hit the spot for a quick snack. I usually begin to starve at around 4pm and I have been saved by these little cookies many times. 3 cookies equal 140 cal. Perfect if you are watching your weight but don't want to totally deprive yourself of the good things in life.

Before requesting these, I read a few reviews because the last time I requested a snack via Amazon Prime, said item supposedly had a laxative effect. Like many other people, I originally thought that these Fruit Thins (despite the name) would have a fruit filling within. I'm actually glad they don't. I'm also glad I chose this flavor over the figs, though that is the next flavor I do want to try.Opening the bag was extremely easy. While some of the cookies were broken, it wasn't too big of a deal for me. What's even better is the twisty tie attached to the plastic wrapper. Convenience, much?The cookies are thin crisps with little pieces of blueberries scattered throughout. They're crunchy, and while the initial bite was weird, I soon adjusted to the taste and fell in love with each bite. It didn't take me long to devour two cookies.The serving size suggests 3 cookies, and I had to force myself to stop eating these. I could easily pig out on these sometime, they were that enjoyable. And, surprisingly enough, my mother enjoyed them too. She even said she would be willing to buy these in the future.I'll have to agree with her. Try them for yourself!

column9: Somewhere between a cookie and a biscuit
column10: The "whole grain" on the package is for real making the texture a little coarser than most folks are expecting in a cookie.  They are thin and dense, not chewy but not brittle and crumby either.  They are tasty (not overly sweet and the blueberry flavor is nice) but not special.  And they tended to get stuck in my teeth.  More of an adjunct to coffee than a dessert or snack on their own.

I don't recall how many years it's been since I've baked a dozen Betty Crocker Blueberry Muffins -- I used to love to, and loved them. Never got a dozen either since I always snitched dough (even though I was supposedly a grown up) so what a nostalgic treat to open this bag and get a whiff of blueberry exactly like the muffins were! The texture and consistency is somewhere between a crispy style cookie or a cracker. The taste is really good, and not at all overly sweet, as I had anticipated from it being called a Blueberry Brown Sugar Thin. I'm very pleased with these, they seem to have worked hard in their kitchen to get a good balance on this. I will plan to try the other flavors as well.

I applaud Nabisco for putting a little more "health" into this cookie. However, I should qualify my review by stating that in no way is Nabisco marketing this product as some sort of healthy treat, but I think this product gets a good nod for being better than most grocery store cookies, without sacrificing taste. On the nutritional side, 3 cookies has 140 calories (not bad, Oreos are nearly 80 for one cookie). Better though, a serving has only 8 grams of sugar, 2 grams of protein and 2 grams of fiber. Even better, they really taste good! You can even taste the blueberries! These cookies don't contain the evil high-fructose corn syrup, but it does list "fructose" in the ingredient list, however it's way down on the list next to baking soda, as opposed to the first or second ingredient as is usually the case with most cookies.These cookies got an enormous thumbs up from everyone in the family (including our super picky eater!). If you love Fig Newtons, but can't tolerate the high sugar content, these are a good fruity cookie alternative. The texture is crunchy, but not hard like your teeth are going to crack, and the fruit flavor is the real deal. It comes in three flavors; fig, cherry and blueberry.

Pleasant -- though not memorable either for brown sugar taste or blueberries!  And since both flavors are personal favorites, I was understandably disappointed at this "wafer" even though I expected more of a soft "cookie'!And at 140 calories per "wafer" -- well this is quite a diet-buster for such a pedestian experience.  Better stick with Fig Newtons.

column9: A diet-friendly snack that's still really delicious
column10: I'm a big fan of Fig Newtons and their fruit-filled cousins, but if there's one thing that the original Newtons cookies aren't, it's low-calorie.  I ordered the fruit thins hoping that the cakey goodness of Fig Newtons had been preserved in a slightly less fatty format.  Upon their arrival, I discovered an entirely different-- but delicious-- cookie.  There's definitely an emphasis on fruit here as the flavor of blueberries comes through strongly, but these are more like a graham cracker in many ways.  The texture is good, but not at all cakey.  It's not terribly brittle, if I had to compare it to another type of cookie I'd say they're similar to the texture of a butter cookie.The calorie count on these is really quite low.  At a serving of three, it only costs about 140 calories and just a few grams of carbs!Serving suggestion from my family is: eat these with a glass of almond milk.  What a delicious desert, no sacrifice of taste for good health whatsoever.

column9: Reminds me of a tea biscuit
column10: These are definitely "grown up" cookies -- not too sweet and a nice, crumbly but not dry texture. These would be delicious with a cup of tea.  Actually, they'd be delicious anytime.
