As others have mentioned, they do have a strangely addictive quality to them.  I would certainly buy these cookies again, although I'd probably watch for them to go on sale.

I opened a bag of these and placed them next to the coffee at our morning meeting. Everyone grabbed at least one.After finding my first cookie sweet and full of blueberry, I deemed Newton's Fruit Thins worthy of hoarding. Too late. By the time I went to refill my coffee, the open bag was pretty much demolished. It less than ten minutes, eleven people had polished off all but one cookie.I am always pleased to find a satisfying snack that won't blow my diet. While these aren't exactly "diet food," they certainly are reasonable in the calorie count area. Three cookies come in at 140 calories.Whether or not you're dieting, these are a great tasting, sweet snack that you'll love if you love fruit.

I loved these.They are really crispy, which is hard to find in cookies - they all seem to be soft cookies anymore.The blueberry flavor comes through, although the blueberry bits have a raisin type of texture.The only downside I could see is there was a large amount of breakage.  Don't know if that was because of shipping or if they would normally have more breakage because of the crispness of the cookie.

column9: Delicious but beware, as one is not enough!
column10: This thin wafer is qite tasty.  The blueberrys taste real and not like an artificial facsimile.  They are sweet, but not too sweet. If you are someone who likes more of a biscuit type cookie, this is the cookie for you.However, one will not do or be satisfying.  These are a bit addictive and it is very easy to reach for another. Because they are thin and not too sweet, it is easy to think they are not too caloric, but they are, so be careful on that front.I bought some of the chocolate raspberry variety today and I like them even better!  But anything with chocolate is better.The only downside is the package, in my opinion, is a bit small to justify the price.

column9: Taste is Great - Good Cookie Alternative
column10: Overall, I like this cookie alternative.  They're crunchy, not soft and cakey like I was originally expecting from a Newton ("A cookie is just a cookie, but a Newton is fruit and cake!", right?) but the crunch is pretty satisfying.What I didn't like, and what brought this down two stars was the blueberry bits.  I can't tell if they're seeds or if they're very hard dried bits of blueberry, but without a doubt, that stuff gets stuck in your teeth so it gets annoying to eat since you'll undoubtedly spend some time picking out the blueberry bits from your molars.The taste is great, and I really like the crispy cookie, so I'd probably buy this in another flavor, but those hard blueberry bits getting stuck in my teeth are enough to stop me from buying this flavor again.

The 36 year old, the 33 year old, the 4 year old and the 18 month old...we all love these. I really hope I can find them on the shelf at my local store. If not, I will be ordering them. They're crunchy, but they don't fall apart when you eat them. The blueberry is a bit chewy if you really focus on it. The flavor is like a flat crunchy blueberry muffin. Seriously, I love these!I received a free package through Amazon Vine in exchange for a review. No additional compensation has been received and I was only required to write an honest review. All opinions are my own.

Newtons Blueberry Brown Sugar Fruit Thins are a tasty little snack.  They have just a hint of sweetness from the blueberries and brown sugar but they aren't overwhelmingly sweet.  I love that they use real dried blueberries instead of some artificial imitation.  With the Newtons name I was expecting a softer cookie but the thins are very crispy/crunchy with more of a cracker texture.My 2 1/2 year old daughter and my husband both enjoyed these as well.  The Newtons Blueberry Brown Sugar Fruit Thins get thumbs up all around at our house.  I love that this is a snack everyone enjoyed and with whole grains, real fruit, and just a little sugar it is a treat I can feel good about giving my family.

Nabisco has a winner here! I'm normally not a cookie eater because there are so many childhood favorites that we now know are just not good for you. This cookie has no trans fats, no corn syrup; but does have 8 grams of whole grain and made with real fruit. The fruit is much more subtle than the traditional Fig Newtons, etc. I will definitely buy this product again.

I've always enjoyed Fig Newtons, but for completely different reasons than these cookies. When it comes to these cookies, I really like the crunch. They are nice and crunchy, and the thin design is good, too. I appreciate the fact that there are natural ingredients here like rolled oats and dried blueberries. The blueberry taste comes through well. Great as morning munchies as I'm getting ready for work, actually!

You can smell and taste the fresh blueberries. No buttery or greasy aftertaste or feeling on your fingers. Crunchy, yet makes no sound if you munch on it where you're not allowed to eat (hey, good to know!!!). Makes a great snack!!!

These certainly seem a bit odd, with the way Newtons hype on the box about the whole grains, real fruit and lack of corn fructose syrup.  You might think they're too much of an attempt at a healthy cookie to be any good, especially when it's a 'crispy cookie'.  But, as people have mentioned, think more along the lines of cookie biscuit and you'll have Newtons Fruit Thins.  These remind me of ginger snaps in a way, minus the ginger flavor.  They're great with tea, a crisp cookie with lots of blueberry flavor that lingers in your mouth (and teeth...) thanks to the bits of dried blueberry throughout.  They don't come across as a 'healthy' attempt at all.  I'm now eager to try the other two flavors.My one complaint is I'd doubt that I'd order these through the mail again, as the package did arrive with about a third of the cookies damaged in some way.  They might be a bit too thin and crisp to be mauled about by the post.

I don't know what I was expecting when I ordered this product, but I was pleasantly surprised when I received them and started munching away.  These cookies are crunchy, lite waffers that are neither too sweet or too tart.  They make a good mid-morning snack or lite desert.  If you want a cookie that won't weigh you down and like fruity flavors then these fruit thins are for you.

I've never been a huge fan of fig newtons, but these cookies are pretty tasty.  They're kind of like Danish butter cookies with a bit of blueberry.  They're probably appropriate for someone trying to diet (but are tasty enough for someone who isn't worried about weight) because they don't seem to have that much sugar (8g per serving of 3 cookies (30 grams)) Also, they have some whole grain which you'd think wouldn't taste good in a dessert, but this is good.As you might imagine this is a dry cookie, not moist (again butter cookie texture) and they are thinner than a typical cookie, but also not that small - about 2 inches across, I think.  3 cookies (which is one serving) is pretty satisfying and a 140 calories isn't extreme.The packaging has the white plastic flaps on the end that let you sort of reseal the bag, but I've never thought that to be the best system for preserving freshness so I'd probably move the cookies to ziplock bags if you're not going to eat them fairly quickly.  Oh, and now that I'm looking at the bag, it says "contains: wheat, soy".  So now you know.I actually really like those Nabisco 100 Calorie Fudge Petites 100 Calorie Packs Fudge Petites, Mint Fudge Chocolate Shortbread, 5-Count Packs (Pack of 6) which obviously are slightly lower calorie and super delicious, but my issue with a lot of these portion control packs is the amount of packaging required seems less than great for the environment. So points for these fruit thins for not having as much packaging although obviously the temptation of eating more is there since the bag that holds all of them is open. (He says, now that he's had a total of six cookies.)Overall, it's not like triple German Chocolate Cake Supreme, but for a fairly "sensible" dessert with some whole grain and real fruit (oh, and the bag just informed me there is no high fructose corn syrup) I think these are pretty good, and I'll probably get them again.

As far as cookies go, this isn't going to ruin your diet (much) and it's pretty tasty too!  Three cookies, and they aren't tiny cookies either, are 140 calories.  There are 2g of both fiber & protein.  They aren't too sweet, which is great for me.  These are called "cookies" but they seem more like crackers.  They are kind of dry, which I don't mind, but the blueberries make them a little chewy.  The ingredients DO NOT list sulfur dioxide (a color preservative for many dried fruits).  Yay!  Sulfur gives me hives anyway.As of right now, these are $18.22 per package for 4 packages of 10 servings each.  I'm hoping these become subscribe & save items.  These are good & I will probably get them again.

I've always liked Nabisco Fig Newtons with the thick filling. These Newton Fruit Thins fit in to the Newton family of products well. The thin cookie was bursting with blueberry flavor & a hint of brown sugar. It had just the right amount of sweetness. I enjoyed it with a cup of cofffee. Something about it reminds me of the Fig Newtons in a good way. I look forward to trying all the flavors.

column9: Very tasty, relatively healthy snack; a little on the expensive side
column10: One of the other reviewers really hit the nail on the head when he described these as tasting like crunchy blueberry muffins, although I would probably go with "crispy" instead. I really like the taste, which is strong on the blueberry and not overly sweet (probably due to the lack of partially hydrogenated corn crapola). That said, I did have them approved by a kindergartner -- it's not that they aren't sweet at all.  While I wouldn't exactly call this a health food, it's not too bad in that department for a snack food without artificial sweeteners. The only downside is that at nearly twenty bucks for 4 bags, they're kind of pricey.

My wife and I are always looking for healthy snacks that don't taste like cardboard. She could probably lose 10 pounds and I should lose 50.  By watching sugars in store bought foods I've been able to lower my sugar from 122 to 102, going from prediabetic to almost normal.  Of course my wife would disagree with anyone referring to anything about me as being 'normal'.  These crisp cookies have a pretty good flavor, are a bit granular and have a slight aftertaste.  Compared to mother's homemade cookies, they don't stack up very well.  But for those like me trying to watch their sugar, fats and sodium, they measure up quite well to similar products.

column9: Tasty wholegrain snack but 47 calories per cookie
column10: This is a promising whole grain snack, with the main caveat being that it is 47 calories per cookie. The taste is actually good. Not overpowering, but you can definitely taste the whole grain and the dried blueberries.Opening the bag for the first time brings up the smell of blueberries. Inside the bag, there is a plastic tray with two rows, with about half of the cookies in each row. The outer bag is the seal, so there are no extra material. One box contains around 30 cookies.The serving size according to the package is three cookies, which gets you 140 calories with 8g of whole grain, 2g of fiber, 8g of sugars, 2g of protein, 21g total carbs, no cholesterol, and a reasonable 90mg of sodium.The main issue is stopping at one or two or three cookies :)

These Blueberry Brown Sugar cookies don't even remind me of Fig Newtons at all. For one thing, they aren't soft. They are crisp, light cookies with a distinctively blueberry flavor. I like that they aren't overly sweet. Great with a cup of coffee or tea! They also contain whole grain, and no high fructose corn syrup, or hydrogenated oils. Not sure they would really fall in the "health food" category, but they would definitely be better for you than a lot of things on the cookie aisle!

column9: Newtons Fruit Thins Blueberry Brown Sugar
column10: I was very excited to try these cookies, the description sounded fabulous.  I opened the package immediately upon delivery and I wasn't disappointed.  The blueberry flavor is predominant but not overwhelming, and I don't know that I could say for sure that I recognize a brown sugar taste, but the cookies are crunchy and light, with a nice balance of the fruit flavor to crunchy cookie.  The blueberries are actual small little bits, not just a flavoring.  Cookies are not too sweet, which is also very nice.Serving size is 3 cookies for 140 calories, 10 servings per bag.  There's little fat or sodium, but also minimal nutritional value.  You'll get 8% of your daily fiber requirements with each serving and a trace of iron, and that's it.  But then, it's a cookie, so what else does one expect from that? On the ingredients plus side, the cookies are made from unbleached flour, whole wheat flour, rolled oats, real sugar and flax seeds.Overall this is a very nice cookie and I would buy again for myself as well as serve to my friends and family.

I have only had a pack of Newtons Fruit Thins for a few days, but unfortunately they are almost all gone.  These cookies are really tasty.When I originally ordered the Newton cookies, I thought that they would taste like Fig Newtons, only in a new cookie format.  I was surprised when I actually bit into one of the cookies and it was a bit harder than a fig newton.  I love the fresh taste of blueberries that permeates throughout each of these cookies.  Furthermore, the cookies are not THAT fattening for you, as it is maybe 150 calories (I cannot remember the exact amount and do not have the bag with me at the moment) for three cookies, which is not too bad for this type of treat.  I will definitely keep these on my shopping list when looking to purchase more cookies, as they are great!

I was expecting a cookie when I ordered these. They are actually more like crackers than cookies (which is not necessarily a bad thing). The blueberry taste is extremely strong. So, if you are craving a slightly sweet, fruity cracker, you will like this new Newton product. If you're expecting an after meal dessert/cookie, be prepared to be somewhat disappointed.

The fruit thins are hard to define.  They are extremely thin, even thin for a cracker.  I was expecting something more like a cookie.  They are very crisp and crunchy.  (No sign of the delicious newton cookie / cake here.)  There is a mild blueberry flavor, and not much sweetness. I think the flavor would have fared well in a thicker, soft cookie.  As is, the fruit thins just don't work for me.

When you first look at a wafer, you may be disappointed, thinking that won't be tasty.  However, they are quite delicious and we're thinking it is the perfect thing to go with tea or coffee.  They are not overly sweet and more filling then their thin wafer may make you think.  I would definitely use these as a stand alone tea cracker, as a sidecar with ice cream, or possibly even with a wine/fruit/cheese plate.  Can't wait to go get some more.

column9: tastes like a crunchy blueberry muffin
column10: Just as the title of my review says, these Newton Fruit Thins in the Blueberry Brown Sugar flavor taste just like crunchy blueberry muffins. The blueberry flavor is distinct but not overpowering. The brown sugar is subtle; the cookie isn't too sweet (I personally would prefer it sweeter, but my husband and younger son thought it was perfect as is!). The cookie is chewy where the blueberry pieces are, so that's either good or weird depending on your personal inclinations.These cookies are lower in sugar and fat than many cookies, so they're a healthful alternative to the typical sugar bombs. Should be pleasing to blueberry lovers of all ages! They make for a nice treat. My son has already asked for them in his lunch tomorrow!Not sure about the price here, though. Seems kinda high and worth doing a local price comparison (just as I did on the Nabisco fudge mint Oreos, which were considerably cheaper locally).

Newtons Fruit Thins are quite delicious.  As soon as you bite into one of these crispy cookies, you can taste the real blueberries, right down to a few seeds, but I did not specifically notice the brown sugar flavor. They are just the right thickness to be crispy, not hard.  The package contains a plastic tray with 2 rows of cookies, 15 cookies in each row. Very enjoyable!

Simply, the cookies are delicious and have a pleasant amount of crispiness to them. Plus, per the package description, they are also a healthy treat. That's really the way I would sum it up, a delicious, healthy treat. As for calories, 140/serving, a serving being 3 cookies. So, the only caution I would offer is because they are delicious, there could be a temptation to have too many of them at a time, especially since they are thin cookies and not very filling by themselves.

I've never reviewed a cookie before this one, but I'm going to do my best to describe the experience of eating it and provide other information that might be of value.These cookies are circle shaped, with their circumfrences probably about half again that of a large cracker.  Despite the name they're fairly thick.  The ingredients they contain are pretty basic and mostly all-natural.  A serving size is three cookies, which will not be terribly filling but will probably be fine for those who want a midafternoon pick-me-up or to walk away from a large meal with a little sweetness on the tongue.  It's 140 calories per serving and is a bit heavy on the fat (5 grams a serving, which comes close to being 2 grams a cookie) but then, it is a cookie after all.Flavor is very much a matter of personal opinion, but I think it tastes great.  The brown sugar and dried blueberries are more or less equally present, and the distinct but complementary interplay of two mildly sweet flavors is more interesting than I would have expected from a cookie like this.  It's not going to satisfy a hard-core sweet tooth, but then that's hardly what this sort of product is meant to do.Texture-wise, it's just a little bit crispier than I'd like, but not to the point that this takes away much from my enjoyment of the product.  And, while not exactly moist, the cookies are not at all dry, either.  And, since the package seals quite efficiently, I don't see them drying out in the cabinet.My only other complaint is that quite a few of them arrived broken.  Not only is this a mess, it makes it much harder for me to keep track of how many cookies I'm eating; and since each one packs a fair amount of fat, I definitely don't want to go over.But, I guess, that's the way the cookie crumbles.

But personally, I'd classify these more like a cracker than a cookie, based on the fact that they're thin.  The blueberry smell & taste is stronger than I expected (good).  I kind of expected them, as a cookie, to be sweeter, but as a cracker, the sweetness is acceptable.  I'm not a huge cookie or cracker fan, but a few of these would suffice as a nice little snack.  I definitely wouldn't devour the entire package in one sitting.  I passed them out at work, and 5 out of 7 thought they were excellent, 1 wasn't thrilled because he thought is was a pathetic excuse for a "cookie", and I thought they were just good, hence the 4 star rating.  Based on current Amazon pricing, I'm thinking they're a bit overpriced, although if cheaper in the supermarkets, I would definitely buy again.  I would definitely be interested in trying other flavors.

The word 'Newtons" makes me think of figs but this tasty treat might change that designation. You can really taste the blueberries in every crispy 'biscuit' I use the 'biscuit' term because this is much more akin to an English biscuit (cookie) than the normal American fare. The package heralds the blueberries and brown sugar and for once it's a valid claim  - you can really taste them both. If you like a cup of hot tea, this tasty treat makes an excellent accompaniment! And if it goes well with my afternoon cuppa then this praise is praise indeed!

column9: Newton's Fruit Thins Blueberry Brown Sugar
column10: OMIGOSH! I loved these little snacks! They use real blueberries, so you have a bit of chew with the crispness of the cookie. I will definitely be buying more of this product.

I have to admit when I first ordered these I was expecting them to be a low fat, low calorie snack.  I was a bit wrong.The "Crispy Cookies" (As they call them) are really quite tasty, a very crispy texture, but not particularly crumbly.  A pleasant brown sugar sweetness and tiny little blueberries throughout the cookie.  Overall the cookie-ness is really quite nice.Crazy thing is that the serving size is 3 cookie crisps and the calorie count is 140 per serving!  That is over 45 calories per little cookie crisp.  And almost a third of those calories are from fat.So, to break it down, they are tasty cookies, thin and crispy, maybe 2.25 inches in diameter, very yummy.  But not for calorie counters or those on a diet.  Only get these if you just want crispy little flavor discs.  But really short of the calorie count there is nothing not to like about this fruit thins.  If you have any questions feel free to leave a comment and I would be happy to respond.

Is what I innocently (Ha!) replied to my husband because these were so yummy I didn't want to share. Wonderful blueberry aroma when you open the package is followed with a cookie chock full of real blueberries, none of that gross fake blueberry stuff. The cookies are very thin and crunchy, a shape I normally associate with crackers, what I think the British would call a biscuit. Tastes a lot like brown sugar shortbread, and there are a buttload in the package. The only bad thing is how many you can eat before you realize you've been gobbling them like a kid :)
Yum.PROS: Blueberry taste & feel. Thin, crispy cookie. Boatloads of 'em in the one package.CONS: A bit too sweet for my tastes, but not enough to make me throw them out ;-}Try 'em, you'll like 'em!

column9: Good taste but be aware  of the packaging unless you want "cookie pieces"
column10: In a departure from my usual music and DVD reviews here on Amazon, today I'm reviewing a cookie (or is it a sweet cracker?). Hey, I love food too!This package of "Newtons Fruit Thins" - in the Blueberry Brown Sugar flavor - came to me through Amazon's Vine Program. They sent one 10.5 oz package to try.When I opened the sturdy box from Amazon I found the box well padded with an air bag. When I opened the product's bag, however, I found that about a third of the packages 30 cookies were broken into small pieces. I don't know whether this happened in transit from Amazon or in transit from Nabisco to Amazon but it did. The cookies are in a plastic tray with no top protection. I point this out because - even though this might be the case in a supermarket, I don't want you to expect to serve whole cookies to guests - or yourself - when you open the package.Because it's a packaging issue I deducted a full star.Now as to the taste.  I liked them. They are not too sweet, though sugar is up there in the ingredient list - before the "real fruit. Actually there is sugar in there twice - refined sugar before the fruit and Brown Sugar after the fruit. So, yes, I liked the taste.I try to read ingredients - especially when they tout "whole grain". Per the package the first ingredient is Enriched Wheat Flour and then Riboflavin and THEN Whole Grain What Flour. So it's there - just not at the top. So I took off another star.There are 42 calories in each cookie - suggested serving is three - but you'll be tempted to eat more. Personally, I wonder what they'd save with eliminating the "Brown Sugar" or the plain sugar.So in summary, I would eat them if served to me but probably wouldn't buy because of the "breakage factor". I'm still eating the "pieces" that came.Steve Ramm

column9: The ENTIRE Family Loves Newtons Fruit Thins!
column10: My luck with cookies bought online has not been great...UNTIL NOW!!My entire family LOVES Newtons Fruit Thins!!We received the Blueberry Brown Sugar and devoured these thin rounds of deliciousness in 2 days.  They are crisp with a bit of chewiness. The blueberry actually tastes like BLUEBERRY (not like the fake blueberry so many breakfast treats taste like...)!! AND they made my taste buds sit up and dance a happy dance!I highly recommend Newtons Fruit Thins and hope you will give them a try. I know you'll love them as much as I do!

column9: A Healthy Snack, not too sweet
column10: It was not love at first bite.  It did not satisfy my sweet tooth; it was crisp rather than gooey/chewy like the Fig Newtons the name reminded me of.  But one serving is 3 thins, and I got to liking it.  I suppose it is a good thing that I won't feel like chowing down the whole package.  Reviewing the ingredients and nutritional info, I decided it's a nice enough snack. Though balanced more on health than taste, it is enjoyable too.  And it should be great for people who think most cookies are too sweet.I served them for dessert after a lunch for five people who have reasonably discerning taste in food and average concern for eating healthy.  We all agreed that they were pleasant, but not compelling, not bad for a reasonably healthy snack.  Some "health foods" are more focused on health and nutrition than taste; these seem to be a good balance between taste and health.TASTE / TEXTUREThe thin cookies are crisp, more dense than most crackers, crunchy, not chewy.  They have some sweetness; you can taste the whole grains and the dried blueberries too, though they did not add any blueberry flavor to the cookie other than the blueberries themselves.  It has brown sugar as a sweetener, but "sugar" (presumably white) is listed well ahead of the brown sugar, perhaps explaining why the brown sugar flavor is subtle.  The dried blueberries tend to get stuck in my teeth for a short time, though if you're having these with tea or coffee, that should help.NUTRITION3 thins is one serving, totaling 140 calories, 45 from fat (32%).  The sweeteners are sugar, brown sugar, and fructose; no High Fructose Corn Syrup, as it says on the package.  The first ingredient is unbleached flour; the whole grains come later.  8% fat by weight; 5% is saturated fat.  No cholesterol, and low salt (4% of daily recommended).  No vitamins; a little iron. 2g of dietary fiber (8% of daily recommended).To put the nutrition in simpler terms, they are not bad for you, but they do not contribute a lot of what you need every day, either.BOTTOM LINEI find them pleasant, but I won't be seeking them out.

My hubby and I tried these tonight after dinner.  I gave them 2 stars and he gave them 4 stars.  So, I averaged a 3 for these.  It tastes more like a sweet cracker than a cookie.  Hubby said the berries were a little too chewy. I didn't think that was a problem. It's not something I plan to go out and buy.  Hubby will probably finish this bag of them. I might like them better if they were in strawberry, apricot or cherry.  There just wasn't enough good flavor to make me want more than one.

column9: Pretty good. A bit strong on the flavor additive. Somewhat diet-friendly
column10: At 47 calories each, these cookies are a very modest indulgence for grown-ups who want a little something sweet. They taste strongly of brown sugar and VERY strongly of blueberry -- probably due to the "natural flavorings" noted on the ingredients list. More "honest" flavored cookies are frankly better tasting, and if you are into all-natural or gourmet foods you're going to find them strange.  But if you want a blueberry "blam," you'll get it here.These pack a lot of taste into a small number of calories. The texture is very good, with just the right amount of snap when you bite them. And you get a lot of these thin cookies in each bag. Overall, pretty satisfying.

column4: Prosecute Wall St. Criminals "End Corporate Rule"
column9: Not too soft, not too sweet...just right
column10: I really love these new & very different cookies.  They are crisp yet chewy, not extremely sweet like most cookies.  The dough reminds me of a cross between a digestive & a graham cracker, but very crisp & thin in comparison to either of these.  Bits of dried fruit throughout make it chewy at the same time, & quite unique.  I'm finding it very difficult to stop eating these.  I got both the fig & blueberry and they're both excellent, although I probably like the latter a wee bit better.
This is an excellent packaged cookie made with fairly healthy ingredients.  The cookie is crisp, with a strong blueberry flavor.  It loses one star for a slightly cloying aftertaste.

I tend to favor fruit desserts and cookies and cakes over chocolate, so be aware of that as you read this review. I like Fig Newtons and all the different fruit Newtons, but I wasn't sure what to expect in these cookies. I was pleasantly surprised.Unlike Newtons, these cookies are very light and crispy. They're a bit delicate, and they broke easily, which is probably why they're packaged in plastic trays in the bag as opposed to simply being free roaming in the bag. I think if I were to put them in a ziplok bag, they'd all break into pieces. Not the sturdiest of cookies, but very delicately crispy.The flavor is fantastic. I love blueberry, and these cookies have a strong blueberry flavor and nice aroma. The brown sugar makes it a bit sweet but not overly so. This was definitely less sweet than a chocolate chip cookie.The texture is nutty and you can definitely taste the whole grains and fiber, which I like, but which other people may not care for. It's also a drier cookie, not as oily as normal chocolate chip cookies bought at the store or on the grocery shelves. I tend to favor this, but other people used to more butter or lard might find the cookie a bit dry.I enjoyed eating these with sweetened tea. I really think this is my new favorite store-bought cookie.

The Newtons Fruit Thins sounded like an excellent product, but I was disappointed.You can taste the blueberries, and the brown sugar is a nice touch. However, the cookies I received seemed to be really dry. I think there are a number of products on the market that have a better taste.

These crispy, flower-shaped thins really taste like blueberries.  They're like a summer picnic... fragrant, nutritious, delicious.  There are no whole blueberries in there, just bits of dried blueberry stirred throughout the cookie.  There is some blueberry flavoring in there aside from the blueberries... I can taste it, and sure enough it says "natural flavors" as a last ingredient.  What I like about these is that they're not too sweet, and they contain no hydrogenated oils.

column9: Pretty tasty, and not your usual *Newton* cookie
column10: These are very different from the old model Fig Newton cookies we grew up with, very crispy and no filling. You can smell the blueberry as soon as you open the package (which is very easy to open and seal back up again). The blueberry flavor is front and center and I also picked up on the brown sugar flavoring as well, but this is not an overly sweet cookie (which is great, as I don't like things heavy on the sweet factor). I picked up on a bit of an aftertaste, but nothing to deter me from trying more of these. The package was delivered to the office and I've shared it around with good comments from all.This is most definitely a *crunchy* cookie and not a soft one. Several of them were broken up a bit, so I suspect the boxes they came in took some rough handling from the men in the brown trucks. I've noticed some other reviewers commenting about putting  the crumbles on ice cream or spreading soft cheese on the cookies. Hopefully mine will be gone before I succumb to that temptation.There is a claim on the packaging that these do not contain high fructose corn syrup, which is all well and good, but I did find "sugar" and "fructose" in the ingredient list. The nutritional facts state there is 8g of sugar in each three cookie serving size.

I have never been a fan of newtons, especially fig newtons; I never could understand how anybody can stand the texture.I don't like blueberries either, in general. However, I love brown sugar; therefore, I had decided to give it a try.I am pleasantly surprised.It's aromatic with the blueberry flavor, but it does not have the gooey texture of the berries. It does have the nice scent of brown sugar. The texture is crunchy, with a slight burnt flavor on the edges (my favorite). It is a filling snack, but it is not overly sweet, and it's great with tea.I shared this with my children and they all enjoyed it, and asked where they could buy it. I told them I got it from amazon; they hope to see it in the stores.

I've been a fan of Fig Newtons for as long as I can remember, so I was thrilled to try these Fruit Thins.The initial burst of blueberry was phenomenal. My mouth was doing spins. The crunch was right on the money. This is one of those cookies that as soon as you eat one, they're the new best thing in your world.My apologies to my family. I didn't share any of these mouth watering delights. I ran in the closet with some ice cold whole milk. An hour later, I was fat and happy.

Nabisco's newest Newton Fruit Thins Cookies are not only totally delicious, but they are loaded with nature's best ingredients that promote a healthy heart, arteries and cells. I'll begin with the taste. These round scalloped edged cookies are super thin and crispy and loaded with blueberries. There is no high fructose corn syrup- only real blueberries. Just opening the bag, you will smell each cookie bursting with the delicious blueberry aroma.As for the ingredients- unbleached flour, whole grain wheat flour, rolled oats, dried blueberries and flax seeds provide your body with nature's healthiest ingredients that will actually strengthen and extend your life. Blueberries are one of nature's strongest antioxidants that prevent free-radical damage. What blueberries do for your arteries is strengthen the artery walls, which very few foods can do. As we age, the artery walls thin out, and berries- in particular the strongest blueberries are the number one food that strengthens them-preventing blood clots. Whole grains are known to give you an abundance of energy and strength, just like a race horse gets from oats. As for flax, it lowers bad cholesterol, lowering your blood pressure, making it easier on your heart muscle. One of my parents line of ancestors lived on a flax farm for centuries and they easily lived into their 100's, the oldest being 107- without a nursing home!  That's what flax does for your heart and arteries- keeps them sparkling clean! If you want to live both healthy and long- eat those berries and flax seeds!These cookies are crispy and delicious, with just a hint of brown sugar added to the blueberries for additional taste. With real fruit, whole grains and flax seeds and only 140 calories from 3 cookies, you'll be satisfying your crunchy snack cravings and your body's need for a healthy heart and arteries. This is the best whole grain blueberry cookie I've ever tasted and it deserves a whopping 10 Stars!
These cookies combine healthy eating with a crispy, crunchy taste. 3 cookies add up to only 130 calories, without sacrificing taste. Very good combination.

These cookies were unexpectedly tasty and crispy given the fact that there was no hydrogenated fat in them. I always look at the list of ingredients for the word, "hydrogenated" even when the label says "no trans fat."They're not too sweet, with a slight taste of blueberry and brown sugar. I agree with other reviewers that they have an addictive quality to them, and with only 140 calories for three cookies (about 47 calories per cookie), one could get into trouble by overindulging. My husband and I really liked these, however.These would be perfect for dunking in milk or crumbling over ice cream. Enjoy!

Newton's Fruit Thins are a good snack, as soon as my 2 year old saw the package he asked for a "cookie" and ate it quickly. I would not call it a cookie but they are quite good. The Blueberry Brown Sugar flavor was great, my whole family enjoyed it. The down side for me was that they are a bit too brittle and sometimes would 'shatter' when you bit into it. The package was also very noisy, there is no way you can get into it without the kids hearing you.All in all it is a yummy snack for the whole family.

I absolutely love the taste of these "British Biscuit-like" cookies. The smell of blueberries burst out of the package. The Newton's Blueberry Thins were crisp, tasty and filling. You can enjoy them without ruining your diet if you stay to the serving size of three. The only concern I have is the packaging....about half of the cookies were broken into tiny crumbles {these would be delicious sprinkled over vanilla ice cream, but I don't think that was the intent of the product designers) and re-sealing the package, once opened, is a bit tricky.

column9: GOOD BUT NOT MY FAVORITE TREAT
column10: At first I thought they were very plain, but once you've had a few, you pick up on the flavors and they are pretty good. I didn't pay close attention to the nutritional facts, but I would assume they are a little healthier for you than alot of cookies out there since they are made with real fruit. These are good for snacking, a light dessert, and maybe even a quick breakfast if you are in a hurry. I had the choice between trying this flavor or fig and honey, so I'm curious what the other flavors taste like and may try them sometime if I run across them at the store and they aren't too expensive.

column9: You Can Really Smell The Blueberry
column10: The minute you open the package, you can really smell the blueberry.  I didn't taste much brown sugar taste.  These Newton's Blueberry Brown Sugar Fruit Thins are not sweet, they seem more like a cookie biscuit to me, something you would have with a nice cup of tea.Or they taste to me for some reason like an unfrosted pop tart.If your a blueberry lover you might enjoy these.  Blueberry is ok, but definitely not my favorite fruit.  On the back of the package they do seem to make two other varieties in this product, which I might enjoy more.They are crispy, and the package says they are made with real fruit, naturally flavored.  If you are a Newton's fan you might enjoy these.

I like Fig Newtons, but I was really surprised that these cookies are more like graham crackers than the Fig Newtons I am used to eating.  These a really good cookies.  For three, the calorie count is 140 and 5 grams of total fat. Three cookies contain 1g of saturated fat, 2.5g of polyunsaturated fat and 1g of monounsaturated fat.  I carefully watch my sodium intake so I was pleased to see that three cookies contain just 90mg.  The blueberry flavor comes through as does the brown sugar taste.I would recommend these cookies as a nice snack.

I have never been a fig newton fan but I figured I would give these a try. I am glad I did!. They were very tasty! The blueberries taste fresh and there is just the right amount of them in each cookie. They are not your typical soft newton cookie, much more crisp (as the packaging states) but I like that! My husband and kids (who are all fig newton fans) loves these cookies as well. I highly recommend these as a good healthy alternative to your typical cookie. If you are a friut and cookie fan these will no dissapoint!

Things to note about these cookies are they are not Fig Newtons, they are more like graham crackers, though not as crumbly.  They are low in carbs and contain High Fructose Corn Syrup.  The blueberry taste is there, but the brown sugar taste is not despite being prominent on the cover.  Good cookie product that is not as bad for you as others.  The price on Amazon or at least the seller that is listing on Amazon is very high and you can get these in stores much cheaper current.  Hopefully Amazon adds these to the subscribe and save program.

I thought these were going to be a "Mommy only" snack. I even informed the kids (and my husband) that they were Fruit Thins, not cookies. They quickly informed me that they were cookies, and delicious ones at that. So, so much for a "Mommy only" snack. The kids (4,3, and 1) love them. And they are perfectly happy with just one, though the serving size is 3 cookies. My husband said they were the perfect dipping cookie. They are thin and crispy, but they don't flake or crumble. Even though the flavor is Blueberry and Brown Sugar, the Thins also contain rolled oats and flax seeds, which give it a nice oaty flavor. They are not overly sweet, but sweet enough to be a cookie. To me, they taste a bit like giant Wheat Thins with chewy blueberries in them. They are definitely a hit at our house. They are something I will most definitely buy again, since they do have some good stuff (fiber, protein, iron) to go with their "cookie" label.

I admit I'm a Cookie Monster.  I think these are my new favorites.  I enjoy thin cookies because I can eat MORE!  These Newtons are crisp, not too sweet and  the chopped up REAL BLUEBERRIES add just the right chewy texture without getting stuck in my teeth.  There are lots of blueberries, oats AND Flax seeds!  Healthy ingredients.I'm tired of granola bars.  They're either too hard or too chewy.  The texture, taste and ingredients of these are, in my cookie opinion, superior.As I said - I have a new favorite cookie and I'm definitely going to try the other flavors.

I love Fig Newtons - have since I was a kid. The soft and chewy bar, the fruity filling...Yum. So I was curious about these when I saw them and decided I wanted to try them. Having said that - they were pretty darn tasty!These are hard and crunchy, like a slightly sweetened cracker. The fruit bits were more chewy, and you can definitely taste the fruit flavor. I think I was expecting something more like a thinner newton - still soft and with a layer of fruit rather than mix-ins, but the flavor is quite tasty. They are not overly sweet, which is nice.They are lower in fat and sugars than many "cookies", though by no means are they truly *healthy*. It was nice to see that there is no HFCS, and the added flax seeds are a nice touch.I would certainly buy these again, though probably not on a regular basis. As a treat though, they are tasty and reasonably healthy, and the kids loved them. Actually, we all did. Well worth buying in the future!

Don't let the name fool you! Newton Fruit thins are really tea biscuits in disguise. Not quite as hard as biscotti, they have a crunch that is easier to chew. My wife and I enjoyed them with our morning tea. For those of you who enjoy blueberries you'll love these tasty treats. While I would have preferred the fig taste, these are delicious. A word of caution about ordering them through the mail, the front biscuits in the package were broken into pieces, a minor fault that I can live with. L.W.

These new Newton Fruit Thins are really a good cookie. First of all I am reviewing the Blueberry Brown Sugar flavor. The taste is quite good without being too sweet or sugary tasting, also no funny tasting white stuff in on it or in it. A good blueberry flavor, with just enough of a brown sugar taste. Nutrition wise they are okay, better for you than most, also good with a cup of tea.

column9: Tastes great, but NOT a healthy snack
column10: I got these thinking they'd be a great healthy snack to take to work for in between meals. While they taste great, they're not healthy. They're kind of a cross between a cookie and a cracker. They taste really good - not too sweet, and the blueberry flavor doesn't taste fake. Taste-wise, these get a 5 all day long.Inside the package is one of those trays like Chips Ahoy come in. It would be easy to eat a whole row of these (maybe 15-20 thins). But if you did that, you'd be eating 933 calories and 33 grams of fat! A serving size is just 3 thins, and even though they are kind of big, they're still...well thin. So 3 thins might work as a dessert if you pre-ration them, but otherwise I think you're always going to want more than 3 to be satisfied.The first ingredient listed is 'uncbleached enriched flour,' and 'whole grain wheat flour' doesn't make an appearance until about halfway down the list. It does have soy in it, and the fruit flavor seems to come only from dried blueberries and no weird stuff. The ingredient list is pretty short, which is nice. Nutriton-wise, it only has 2g of dietary fiber and nothing really notable for vitamins. I'm a bit disappointed. You'd think something called 'newton fruit thins' would have some redeeming nutrional quality, but these don't. It wouldn't be hard to make them a more healthy snack, and I wish Nabisco had done that.Despite how good they taste, the serving size/calories/fat issue makes them not a good buy for me, because they're just not a healthy snack. They're junk food disguised as a healthy snack, which might even be worse than plain old junk food.

What do you get when you combine blueberries and a cookie? You get these tasty morsels!The texture of these cookies is about the same as a Chips-Ahoy cookie, but instead of chocolate chips you get really tasty blueberries that are a bit sweet and tart.The added bit of texture and crunch from the flax seeds is nice to see (I add flax to practically everything I eat).Ingredients wise I was actually quite shocked to see very few and those few are actual ingredients, not junk!My only complaint (besides them being addictively scrumptious) is that they aren't really "good" for you. Three of these cookies have 140 calories, 5 grams of fat (1 saturated), and 8 grams of sugar. So I would probably suggest using these as an alternative to other snack cookies.If you are looking for something a little sweet and want that cookie texture, these will fit the bill perfectly.

column9: Delicious, but one is not enough
column10: Being diabetic, I am always looking for snacks that have low carbohydrates.  Generally for diabetes they recommend 15-30 carbs per snack.  At only 7 carbs per cookie, you can eat 4 of these and still be within the recommended limit.  You probably will need to eat at least 4 to feel satisfied, as they are thin and not that filling.  They do have a nice blueberry taste; not artificial tasting at all.  The cookie texture is nice and crunchy; not too dry and not too moist.  Not exactly a brown sugar taste, but very pleasant.  I can't imagine anyone not liking these.  I liked them very much and recommend them.  They are not overly sweet either, which is really nice.  You could easily eat 1/2 a bag at one sitting if you are not careful, or even the whole bag.  If you have self discipline you can eat just 2 or 3 and satisfy your taste buds, although maybe not your hunger.

New products are often not new, they are just a variant.  This cookie is quite different and worth eating.  Not caring about calories or whether it's good for me, because, quite frankly, I'm eating a cookie:  I want it to taste like a cookie.  This one does just that.  It is crispy, tasty with just enough brown sugar and offset with the dried blueberries that have substance as you eat.Very good offering.

I'll admit, I wasn't expecting much when I received these. I figured they'd be dry with that fake blueberry taste, but I was wrong! These are a great between meals snack. Much better than the chocolate chip cookies or potato chips I normally reach for. Two of these thins along with a big glass of milk were just enough to satisfy my need for a snack. That's strange too...I'm not at ALL a milk drinker. I can't stand the stuff on it's own, but after my first couple bites, I felt the need to pour a glass. They go great together!Overall, I really liked these! The blueberry taste is spot-on, and they're a great size, not too big, not too small. I saw the chocolate raspberry flavor in the grocery store this afternoon...I think I may have to go back for that flavor!

When I first received these they weren't exactly what I was expecting...I guess I had in my mind the soft cookie'egue qualities that make Fig Newton's, Fig Newtons.I ate one plain and wasn't impressed.  I fed one to my husband who described them as "okay".  They were cracker'ish, and kind of boring.Ladies and Gents - I was making a mistake.  These MUST be dunked in something, coffee or hot chocolate - I don't care.  THEN they take on a new world of flavor, delicious and light and hard to stop eating. Light blueberry taste, with a not too sweet dash of brown sugar.Delicious.

column9: Delicious, cant wait to try other varities
column10: Today, I had the opportunity to review a new treat:  Newtons Fruit Thins.Now, I have never been a big fan of Fig Newtons because, well, I do not like figs.  But when I heard about these cookies, I decided to try them, because they were not only healthy, they were also fig free!  The flavor I chose was Blueberry Brown Sugar.The first thing I noticed was the info on the packaging.  One serving was 3 cookies, containing 140 calories, with 5 grams of fat and 2 grams of fiber.  That is not too shabby for cookies, as long as they are good.Next I noticed that these cookies had appeal for those in stricter diets.  They contain real fruit, whole grain, and NO high fructose corn syrup.  So, in other words, Moms can feel good about giving these to their little ones.But, how would they taste?  I decided to dive in.  As I opened the package, I noticed the cookies smelled like real blueberries, which is always a plus.  The smell was sweet, and fresh, like homemade blueberry muffins.  I was getting really excited by this point.I got the recommended serving of three cookies.  I immediately noticed that their thin, crunchy texture reminded me of what the British call biscuits, so I paired them with a cup of chai tea.  Finally, time for my first taste.  I took a nibble, and was pleasantly surprised.  They were delicious!  They are very flavorful, and the serving of 3 cookies is just enough to satisfy a sweet tooth.  They held up well being dipped into my tea as well.I am happy to say, I am a huge fan of these cookies, and so is Hubby. And since he is suspicious of anything healthy, fruity, and with no chocolate components, that is saying a lot! I will definitely be getting these again, and most likely will try the other flavors they have out as well.

column9: Good for peanut butter & jelly sandwiches
column10: I think product has the texture of a cracker however I did not find it crumbly.Like a cracker, there are tiny holes punched in the top - perfect for peanut butter & jelly to ooze out of when 2 are put together with filling.Product does not work standalone for me, I also tried w/feta cheese on top. Others dunk'em.Like the ingredients, except for the decorative flax seeds. Do taste "hint of brown sugar".The product is really thin, which makes you think they will last awhile.

column9: Like a Cold, Dry Pop Tart
column10: Extremely generic "bluberry" taste, extremely crumbly and overall unsatisfying.  The only reason I gave these two stars is because as cookies go, the nutritional value is marginally more favorable than the standard grocery store brands.

I really like Newtons' Fruit Thins Blueberry Brown Sugar thins. They're light and have just enough flavor to go great with coffee.  They're thin and crisp, with more taste than a Graham Cracker. If you have a craving for sweets, this satisfies that craving, or if you want something light then these are great for snacks. I really enjoy them and even like the thins with the cranberry flavor more. Good treat!

I had low expectations for these - perhaps just because they're from a "normal" mega brand and I prefer home-baked? - but they're surprisingly good!  If you cut off a blueberry muffin top, set a few books on top of it to squish it down, then toasted it in a toaster oven for a few minutes, this is what you'd have!  Very crisp, nice brown sugar richness, and not too sweet.Unfortunately they don't seem like something enough people will pick up on to justify Nabisco keeping them around, but they are good!

I am completely amazed that this is truly one of the first times I have even had a blueberry flavored cookie.  I love blueberry muffins, and this cookie captures that taste and puts it into a crispy cookie that I could literally not stop eating.  Even my picky husband was trying them out and reaching for more!  If you haven't tried these you should, and I guarantee you will not be disappointed!

These crackers have dried blueberries in them. I found them to be thin crunchy, and quite tasty. They are closer to crackers than cookies though. Stolen minutes after I left them out at work. A high recommendation indeed.
My supermarket seems to be slow in restocking shelves - run out of these cookies alot.  My guess is they are popular!

I found these to be disappointing.  I thought they might be soft and chewy, based on the fact that Fig Newtons have that kind of crust.  These were instead hard and crunchy, which isn't necessarily a bad thing.  They just didn't taste that good.  Kind of bland and cardboard-y, with barely any fruit flavor.  I won't be buying these at the store.

I agree you can't stop at just one serving (3 cookies), so I would suggest hiding these. They are 7% of your calorie RDI, but the blueberry redeems them (what else would you expect from the Newton cookie subfamily of Nabisco?). At 90 mg of sodium (4% of recommended daily values), these fruit thins won't break your blood pressure (if you are concerned, read  Bringing Down High Blood Pressure), So far I haven't been able to find any of the sodium variants that are usually used in processed baked goods (they are present in Newton's Fruit Crisps, Newtons Fruit Crisp Snacks, Apple Cinnamon, 8-Count Boxes (Pack of 6)). This is a great snack, and as one reviewer commented, contains ingredients you can pronounce.

I like how simple ingredients list is for this product plus the cookies taste good. However I found blueberry flavor to be to artificial. So I am naturally wondering what the heck is that natural flavor they put in there? I tried these and the fig version of these and likes the other ones better.

I have to say I liked these.  The blueberry flavor is nice and the brown sugar keeps them from tasting too much like saltines.  They are crunchy, but thin, so not like a cookie.  They are more like a hard Ritz cracker.  I did notice after swallowing an odd after-taste that I cannot quite place.  It tastes a little like the carroway seeds from rye bread.  It wasn't bad, though, and it was gone pretty quickly.A couple of these will tide you over between meals, and the nutritional value is pretty good for a treat.

column9: Deliciously crispy and tasty, but somewhat messy.
column10: Received my pack yesterday and couldn't wait to rip it open since I had just been contemplating what to eat to satisfy my sweet tooth. A number of thins didn't survive the shipping so lots of broken pieces, which were actually easier to eat than the full cookie. The actual thin itself is pretty hard and has a tendency to crack in several directions when you bite into it, which makes for a messy endeavor. I set it on my pant leg and was rewarded with lots of crumbs. But the taste is pleasing, nice blueberry hints and though I didn't get the brown sugar flavor as much as I wanted to, it's still sweet enough to satisfy a craving. Each thin is approximately 46 calories, which does seem a bit high given such a small snack, but I would definitely buy them as a nice cookie-alternative.

column9: Good cookies, but pretty high calorie for those watching their weight
column10: The cookies arrived, albeit a few more broken inside than I'd like, but I really enjoy them.  They are not overly sweet, have a nice buttery texture, and the dried bluberries offer a good contrast to the rest of the cookie.  However, I assumed (never do that...) that they were reasonably low calorie, but in fact the serving size is three cookies and the calorie count is well over 100 for that amount.  They are addictive, so watch out!  All in all, a good cookie with a nice flavor and no funky aftertaste.  Just break out the food scale or bag up 3 in your lunch box and leave the rest of the pack at home!

I got these for free off the Amazon Vine program ... at the time I was pretty pissed because all of the electronics and other cool free stuff were already gone, and the best thing left were these Newtons so I settled for them.  Well, they turned out to be pretty good.

column9: Actually is delicious and as good for you as a cookie can be!
column10: These cookies are crispy, lightly sweet and delicious.  They really do taste like real blueberries and brown sugar and make a great accompaniment to tea.  My husband who doesn't eat many sweets, picky 10 year old and 5 year old really enjoyed them, as well.  A big hit with this family!

These fruit thins have a wonderful fruit flavor.  You realy get a yummy burst of blueberry and some brown sugar.  However, the flax seed makes the texture a bit unexpected, and the soybean oil leaves a bit of aftertaste.  My children (5 and 7) liked the first bite or two, and then were done with them.  My husband does not really like them plain, but does like them with cheese (such as a brie).  I like the health value, but it is very crunchy with a slight aftertaste.  if you're looking for a healthy snack, however, these are worth trying.

We recently received a box of Newtons Fruit Thins from Amazon Vine and I have to say ... these are tasty little treats! My husband is a big fan of fig newtons and we usually keep those around for his lunches. Where a fig newton cookies is heavy - heavy cake-like cookie, thick spread of the fruit - these treats are very light and crispy. To me this is what makes the difference if you are the type of person that likes a snack with a crunch to it. The blueberry flavor just sent it over the top as well. A much lighter taste than with a regular fig newton - again, not a heavy cakey treat, but a light cracker-y/cookie. These would be wonderful as an afternoon snack or at a little girl's tea party.Two thumbs up!

These are crisp cookies with berries sprinkled through the cookie.  Not like the Newtons Fruit Crisps, or regular Newtons, which have a layer of fruit purée.  The cookie is 2.5 inches wide and about an eighth of an inch thick.I rarely buy packaged cookies, so I don't have a lot of points of comparison.  The texture of the cookie reminds me a little of a graham cracker, only denser.  There is a strong scent of blueberry and a distinct flavor of dried blueberries.  They are not very sweet, which I think is a good thing.They'd be tasty spread with a little soft mild cheese or peanut butter.  On their own, they're good; just not knock-your-socks-off good.  More of a pleasant snack.  It occurs to me, though, that they'd make an interesting pie crust; similar to the kind you make by crushing graham crackers or chocolate wafers and mixing with butter.  I'm thinking they could be very nice in a pie crust with a vanilla pudding filling.Here's the nutritional scoop:  There are three cookies in a serving size, which results in 140 calories, 5 grams of fat (1g saturated, 3g polyunsaturated, 1g monounsaturated), 90 mg of sodium, 50g of potassium, 21g total carbs, 2g dietary fiber, 8g sugars and 2g protein.  Not too bad as a snack from the nutritional standpoint, at least by comparison to most cookies.  From the ingredient list, they appear to be vegan.  Also, they are sweetened with brown sugar, not high fructose corn syrup.  They do contain wheat and soy products.I'd say go for it if you're looking for a packaged cookie that's on the healthier side.

This is a new product made with real fruit.  It is more of a cracker than a cookie and is thin and crispy.  Three cookies constitute a serving.  A serving  is only 140 calories and provides 8 grams of whole grain. The cookies contain no high fructose corn syrup and are a healthier alternative to similar products on the market.  Newton's Fruit Thins should be a popular snack or lunch box item.

The advertisement looked compelling so we bought a pachage. They taste like animal crackers with dried blueberry bits that stick between your teeth. After two or three crackers, the rest went into the garbage.Next time, try producing a cookie instead of a cracker.Chet

Not a fan.  There's really nothing good about these.  They only taste a little bit like blueberry, but what really gets me is that they are more like crackers.  I saw "newtons" and I assumed they would be soft and cake-like.  But no, they are hard and crunchy like crackers - and they kind of taste like cardboard.  Imagine eating Wheat Thins without any flavor at all (even the plain ones have some sort of spices on them) - that's what these remind me of.  My toddler also hated them, and so did my pregnant wife.  My dogs liked 'em, though!

column9: Ok, But Not Really What I Expected
column10: The Blueberry Brown Sugar Newtons Fruit Thins had a nice blueberry flavor with a slight hint of brown sugar and are a crisp cookie - unlike the historical "Newtons" brand which are soft and chewy.  They are also low in carbs and calories, giving you a somewhat healthy snake.However, I was not particularly fond of them.  To me the Newtons Fruit Thins tasted basically like a cookie-shaped, blueberry-flavored, graham cracker - dry, somewhat bland, and devoid of any real, enthusiastic flavor.  Obviously the packaging states that the cookies are "crispy cookies", but truthfully I was anticipating more of the "Fig Newton"-kind of texture rather than a hard cookie and was somewhat disappointed with the product out of the box (however this was due only to my preconceived notions).Upshot is since I rarely eat cookies and when I do, I enjoy something sweet and tasty, I doubt I will return to this product.  In my mind, if one is really looking for a thin, crispy, low fat treat, you might as well by some good old graham crackers - they are much cheaper.  The Newtons Fruit Thins just don't do it for me.  I also don't really understand the purpose of branching out the "Newtons" brand name into such a completely different product.  It's like coming out with a "Hummer" line of motor scooters - you think that the public wants a more economical vehicle, but tagging on such a dissimilar brand to the new product only confuses people.  Similarly, you see a public request for healthier snacks, but tagging the Newtons brand name does nothing but give people a false sense of what you are selling.  Seems to me that it would be better for Nabisco to just come out with a completely new line, but then that's just my opinion.

column9: The Blueberries Tasted Great, But That Was About It
column10: These are supposed to be a thin cookie that has real fruit and whole grains in it. They smell good and do taste of real blueberries. However, the taste tends to stick with you for quite awhile after you have eaten a cookie. The cookies themselves kind of remind me of a flat Pop-Tarts, Frosted Blueberry without the frosting, although they have the consistency more in line with a hard cookie, which I really don't like. I was not impressed at all with the overall taste of the cookie except for the blueberries.The healthy part of the cookie was real fruit, whole grains, and no high fructose corn syrup. The whole grains were in the middle of the ingredients with no corn syrup. The fruit part passes the taste bud test with a score of 100%. The whole grains look like they were just tossed into the mix for a selling point without really having enough to make a difference. Also, even though there was no corn syrup, there was still sugar, fructose, and brown sugar. Three cookies are considered a serving size for a total of 140 calories.When I saw that Amazon was selling them for $7 a bag that did it for me. I'm not impressed at all with these. I could chew on cardboard with jam on it and have a better snack that has more fiber in it. The only reason I gave it two stars is because they do know their fruit.Shawn KovacichCreator of numerous books and DVD's.

Newtons Fruit Thins Blueberry Brown Sugar, 10.5-Ounce (Pack of4)I have to say that I was very surprised by how good these cookies are, great tasting blueberries. When I had the opportunity to try out these snacks I jumped on it and ordered them. I am a big blueberry fan, not sure if I have ever said that in another review but I love em. So I was really interested in trying this healthier type snack out, I am glad I did.Like I usually do I shared this with my girl, bro, and a few others and we all agree they are good. To be honest they taste just like a blueberry graham cracker, wonderful. Now it says pack of four on here but it really means four rows of these cookies. So you do get a lot snacks here so it is worth the price that they ask. Add in that they are made with real fruit, blueberry, and wonderful brown sugar and you get a great snack.This is a low carb and low calorie snack, but don't over do it as with everything else. I do recommend this nice little snack since it does taste good. Every one that tasted these with me agrees that they are indeed good. Try them out if you are a blueberry fan, they are really good.

column9: Very Nice Light Snack-- I'm buying more as soon as I can find them!
column10: These were a lot like European "biscuits"-- they were hard, crunchy, and the dried fruit and brown sugar flavors were great. They made an excellent diet-size snack, too since the serving size isn't one tiny fleck and the calories aren't high.They have nothing to do with the original Fig Newton, though...so if you're expecting something like that, it will be different.Good, though...really good!

This was a tasty treat that was sort both a cracker and a cookie. The blueberry and brown sugar is tasty, and I like that it doesn't have high fructose corn syrup and a ton of additives, and has whole grain. I don't have a particular taste for cookie cracker type treats, but it is a good choice if you like them.
These can be very addictive! Nice texture, very full flavor and not too sweet. A few of these with a cup of tea (or coffee) makes for a nice afternoon break. Try them!

These cookies aren't like the traditional Fig Newtons/Fruit Newtonss I have bought in the past.  They look more like a thin cracker.  The cookies are also crunchy like a cracker, but definitely not as dry.  They are sweet but not too sweet, and very blueberry.  They remind me of the very top of a blueberry muffin, which is a good thing!  I'll definitely buy more of these for my family.

These are pretty good. They're a 2 inch in diameter round graham cracker-like cookie with blueberry bits in them. They're crunchy and sweet, and blueberry bits will get a little stuck in your molars. They're great with milk. Although they taste healthy, the serving size is pretty small- 3 cookies (about an ounce) has 140 calories. The package is easy to open and resealable.

They are very enjoyable. My 4 1/2 year old daughter enjoyed them as well. They are not really really sweet like some cookies. They are the thickness of a graham cracker. The flavor of blueberry is not overwhelmingly strong, I think the taste is just right. They are just right for a light snack. There are no where as many crumbs that seem to come with regular cookies, which is nice if you have kids, and like I said my daughter really enjoyed them as well.

Fig Newtons are some of my favorite cookies. I like them because of the nice balance between the fruity filling and the chewy cookie. When I ordered these thins I expected them to be similar in flavor to the other Newtons that I was familiar with, but they turned out to be an entirely different type of sweets. They are very similar to the other kinds of thins. The blueberry flavor is noticeable, but it's not overwhelming. I haven't been able to discern the brown sugar aroma, other than in terms of the general sweetness. I actually like these thins a lot, and I have to restrain myself from eating too many at a time. They make a great accompaniment for tea or coffee. Overall, these are very tasty thins.

I didn't really enjoy this product at all. I like the idea, but the actual product wasn't very good. The cookie crumbles all over the place making a big mess. The blueberries are hard little rocks with a strange texture that isn't very appetizing. The flavor of the cookie itself was alright, a definite brown sugar taste. The serving size is small, and not very satisfying for the calorie count. Overall I would try a different snack product over this one.

The first thing I did when I received this package was turn it over and give the ingredient list a quick browse.  NO High Fructose Corn Syrup!  Yay!I then passed a couple out to the kids for their opinions.  17 year old boy immediately scarfed his down and then made a grab for more.  He said they taste a little like graham crackers with blueberries mixed in.  He rated them a 9/10 (don't ask me why the 1 pt deduction) and agreed that he would recommend buying them and would pack them in his lunch.8 year old boy ate his a little slower and said that they were a little like a cookie but not as sugary.  When asked for a rating he replied "I dunno" but did say he wanted them in his lunchbox the next day.  He said that they are almost as good as cookies.  LOLI tried a few myself and agree with the graham cracker comparison, although they are not quite a crumbly.  The taste is quite pleasant and there is no aftertaste at all.  The brown sugar sweetens nicely and gives the cracker a pleasant taste.
This is exactly what I expected, a thin cracker like cookie filled with blueberries and not too sweet. I highly recommend this to anyone wanting a cookie that's semi-healthy

column9: not a good price, but excellent cookie!
column10: Personally I don't like a lot of filling sometimes. I like the fig newtons but these are very different because they have a lot less filling- more like a crispy biscuit with dried blueberries and an oat-y taste.However, this price is outrageous. At my local safeway, they oftentimes have a sale for Buy one get one Free, so the usual price of $4.50 is actually $2.25 per bag. For for bags that's only $10.I noticed they have cranberry oat for a little over $16. This is a decent price if there is no sale, and you like the your cookies with a slight citrus tang to it.

column9: Wife loves them, I can't stand them
column10: My wife likes these but for me, I feel like if you like smashed, dried Fig Newton flavor with less "filling material," minus a lot of the buttery richness of the soft original, these are for you. I would not buy these again.

column9: Addictive Wafer Variation on the Old Cookie Standby
column10: Fig Newton aficionados may pooh-pooh this textural variation on the old classic, but they may not even notice that this product is remotely related except for the name. Thin and crispy, this is a surprisingly tasty cookie that bears little resemblance to the original Fig Newton. The Fruit Thins are made with real fruit and contain eight grams of whole grain per serving. The blueberry and brown sugar combo is a good pairing of flavors. While they may look like a healthier snacking option, they are still cookies after all, an indulgence that will hopefully not be the subject of your bingeing. The serving size of Newtons Fruit Thins are three cookies, which equal 140 calories, five grams of total fat and 1 to 1.5 grams of saturated fat. Good luck with that.

column9: Not soft. Bland flavor. Went stale very quickly.
column10: Based on the write up, I expected something soft and chewy. More like a soft cookie. This wasn't it.In it's favor, it does have healthier ingredients than a lot of other "cookies" on the market.On the other hand, if it doesn't taste good, I'm still not going to eat it.We gave these to our 5, 3 and 1 year old kids, plus 2 adults. We all thought they were "okay" but no one finished them.No one went back for more.Every time I offered them again, they refused.After just a few days, they went stale in a plastic bag.These are more like a fruity cracker than a cookie.They are lightly sweet, if you like that kind of thing.There isn't much of a fruit flavor.I thought of trying other flavors to see if they were any better, but the texture was not pleasant, so I didn't bother. Not recommended.

column9: They have a lot of fiber...
column10: These are an "ok" substitute if you are looking to add fiber to your diet and don't mind a cookie that tastes like blueberry cardboard.Don't eat more than 4 at once if you don't know the location of your nearest potty.Kidding aside, I actually did go out & buy another box of these because they are not "terrible" with fruity tea in the evening.  But I did not buy again after that.  I would rather have a few more calories and eat something that is enjoyable and tasty.  These taste like artificial blueberry flavor and have the texture of hard crackers.

column9: YUM!  like the taste and texture
column10: I love these! Both taste and texture rank very high by my taste buds. The cookies are crispy,not too sweet, and the dried blueberries taste is very good.One warning, they are addictive, you can't stop at just one. The "thins" name might make you think that they are light on calories, but when I compared them with the old favorite Fig Newtons, these thins have 60% more fat!Fruit thins calories: 140Fig Newtons calories: 110Fruit thins total fat: 5 grams (3 cookies, 30 grams)Fig Newtons total fat: 2 grams (2 cookies, 31 grams)Fruit thins saturated fat: 1 gramFig Newtons saturated fat: 0 gramsOverall, very tasty cookie but don't let the "thin" name fool you into eating a lot of them at one time!Yeah, I know, easier to say than do! My trick is to take 1 out and put away the box before I eat it, it is easier to resist the temptation then.Ali Julia review

column9: A Tasty Alternative to Other Cookies
column10: These Newton Fruit Thins seems to be some sort of cookie / cracker combination, they are crunchier than most cookies but are sweeter than any cracker you may try.  The blueberry flavor is nice, but they are not as satisfying tasty as most other packaged cookies but are a bit healthier than most snacks like it making it a decent trade off if you are looking for a better food to snack on than most other foods in the cookie aisle.  One negative point to these fruit thins is you are going to be picking them out of your teeth after eating them.

This is obviously  a fine snack, and all the nutritional facts are printed on the box, so you know its value. Mighty tasty to boot...My small complaint is that they are slightly hard, and a bit rough on teeth like mine (almosy 60 years old, and not getting any better). Beyond that, a fine nutrional product

I saw the commercial for these & thought they looked good so I picked up a package to try. For some reason I thought they would be soft like regular fig newtons but they're hard. The taste is pretty bland. In fact, I didn't really taste anything blueberry at all. They actually reminded me of a childhood memory going over to a friend's house where the mom used to give us generic tasting cookies and watered down kool-aid. So I'll pass on these. I was pretty disappointed because I really love fig newtons in general.

I prefer crisp cookies over soft one.  So when I heard about this product, I had to give a try.  As they claimed, it was thin (could be thinner, in my opinion), crisp, and very fruity.My only complain about this product is its price.  At the local grocery store, it's sold less than $4 per pack.  How come the pack of 4 is here (Amazon.com) priced as over $20?

As other reviewers have also mentioned, this cookie is very crumbly.  A lot of them actually were broken upon receipt (which isn't Nabisco's problem).  When you actually start eating them, they crumble at the first bite and make quite the mess.  I wouldn't want my toddler to eat these in the living room, for example.  The Fruit Thins are a great alternative to a regular processed cookie, however, and are 140 calories and only 5 grams of fat for 3.  Compared to some others, this is quite a bit better nutritional profile.I wish they were a tad more moist and chewy, which I expected from a Newton cookie.  But overall these are still very enjoyable and a nice change of pace from other cookies.

These are very tasty crackers! They are about 3/16" thick with 2 1/2" diameter. They are sturdy enough to spread a decently thick cheese on, or can be topped with other items. I like how they are less likely to break than many other crackers intended for serving with cheese and other toppings.Normally when I see the name "Newtons" I think of the Fig Newtons, and expect a moist and soft snack. These are not soft & moist. The difference is comparable to the difference between soft cookies and the stiff ones. That was the main thing that was different from my mental image of what these thins would be like. However, they are not too dry. They have a bit of moisture content so they hold up quite well.These thins taste great! The brown sugar is more of the background base flavor that one would expect to taste, and the blueberry gives it the flavor mixture that really makes these a pleasure to eat! I have to say, this mixture is quite excellent! It is not too strong, so I could eat a whole package without getting tired of the flavor, and yet each cracker has enough flavor that I can eat just one and be pleased.Newton's Fruit Thins are a delightful snack, with a perfect blend of maple sugar and blueberry flavoring. They are nice and sturdy (not a single one arrived cracked) and the price is quite excellent! I find them great for snacking, and they are actually decent at curbing hunger. I was very hungry just a while ago, and snacked on a few and am fine now.

These flat cookies are tasty with a nice touch of dried bkueberries.The dried fruit bits are flavorful and natural tasting.If your thinking blueberry flavored fig bars, that's not it. More cookie than a fruit bar, but still delicious.

column4: Megan Bostic "I am Creative Chaos. I may have...
column10: I've never really been a fan of fig newtons, but thought I would try these new cookies anyway.  For cookies, first of all, these are pretty healthy. 140 calories, 5 grams of fat, and 2 grams of fiber. They're made with whole grains and real fruit.  No fake stuff here.And for something that's pretty good for you?  They tasted good too.  LOVE.
I'm a sucker for anything with bluberries in it and these made a nice snack. Would buy these for lunch snacks

column9: A bit too dry and crunchy
column10: The blueberry flavor was also probably not a good choice on my side. But perhaps I'm expecting too much from dried, baked blueberries. I can see having these with plenty of milk but not otherwise.

column9: Nice crisp cookie but too sweet
column10: I love the texture, crunch and lightness of these cookies. They remind me of English tea biscuits, which I love. However, After trying two of the flavors (blueberry and fig/honey), I find that they are just too sweet. I think they would be a much better (and probably healthier) cookie if the sugar was cut back. If you don't mind a very sweet cookie and a thin, crisp cookie appeals to you, you'll probably like them.
