But if, like me, you prefer a bigger dose of fruit and a smaller dose of sugar, you might be disappointed with these.

I like crisp cookies, and have been beaten down by the soft cookie movement (yuck).  These Fruit Thins are great!  Very light and crisp, with a bit of whole grain bits in the cookie for texture.  I tried the blueberry ones, and the blueberry flavoring was a little unbalanced, it overpowered the brown sugar flavor.  However, they are quite tasty, and more importantly, crisp.  I plan to try the cranberry ones and see if the fruit flavor is as strong.  Overall I recommend them!

I was quite wary. I've been a fan of their fig newton bars since I was a little girl, but I really wanted to see something different.My first taste and I was in love. I like how the blueberries are chewy.Even the children enjoyed them as well.I highly recommend them for a great snack by themselves or even with a sweet spread.

I took these to an office potluck so I could share more opinions of them--and wow, was that a good choice! Everyone loved them, and I got lots of compliments for a potluck offering I didn't even have to make myself!They're cookies, and they taste *really* good. What more review do you want than that?

The Newton Fruit Thins are about 3" thin, crisp cookie which is also similar to a cracker.  I tried the Blueberry Brown Sugar. They are flavorful and better for you than a traditional cookie.  They are a good alternative when your kids want high calorie cookies.  You can have 3 of these for 140 cal, 5 g fat, 1 sat. fat, and 8g sugar.  Usually you would only get 2 package-type cookies for the same calories and higher fat. My husband liked these as much as the kids, but because they are not as substantial as a cookie, he found himself wanting to eat more of them to be satisfied.  Everyone liked them and wanted them again.  I don't think they are for everybody but you won't know until you try.

These were on sale at my local grocery store so I decided to give them a try.  If you love blueberry muffins, you will like these cookies.  They taste just like the good old out-of-the-box blue berry muffin mix with real canned blueberries that mom used to make.  This is my new favorite cookie!

These are pretty good. They're bursting with blueberry flavor and the texture is interesting... sort of a chewy cracker.They're just the right amount of sweetness for snacking and have a lighter sort of 'feel' than junkier snacks.These are great with milk or coffee and are a healthier alternative to more conventional snack cookies / crackers.I don't usually buy snack foods but may be picking these up again.

Honestly I really didn't expect much from these fruit thins.  Boy was I surprised!  These are excellent!  They are thin and crispy and really do have the blueberry and brown sugar taste.  They are the perfect light snack either by themselves, after a meal, or with coffee.  My wife and I both loved them and would highly recommend them!

I picked these up on a whim. Something different to try. Boy, was I pleasantly surprised.I have been trying to think of a good way to describe these - but the best way I can say it is; they taste like a crunchy blueberry muffin. The blueberry does not over power this wafer it's just right.These are perfect for mornings, or in between meals. These are definitely something I will be buying more of in the future.

column9: Good Cookie, but a Little Sweet
column10: Recently, I tried Newtons Fruit Thins Fig and Honey cookies.  Then someone brought a package of the Cranberry Citrus Oats, type to work.  I liked the cranberry cookies better. Now I have also tried the Blueberry variety. My favorite is still the cranberry.The blueberry cookies themselves are good. They are thin, but that was the idea, wasn't it? The cookies have a nice texture. You can taste the blueberries, but the sugar makes them sweeter than the other varieties. The calorie count, 140 for three cookies, is about the same as the granola bars that I sometimes snack on. Just don't eat the whole box at once.The ingredients are also reasonable with the exception of the use of palm oil. As palm oil use has increased dramatically over the past ten years, commercial growers have been clearing rain forests in Indonesia and Malaysia to create palm oil plantations. The palm oil is used in food production, as in these cookies, and in the manufacture of bio-fuels. The result is a loss of endangered species and ironically increased carbon emission. There has been some movement to either reduce palm oil use or use only palm oil from sustainable sources. There have even been stories of girl scouts agitating to sell only palm-oil-free cookies.Kraft is aware of the palm oil situation. It is not clear that they are doing anything about it. This is from a July 15, 2009 Wall Street Journal article: "Kraft spokesman Richard D. Buino said that while the company supports the RSPO's [Roundtable for Sustainable Palm Oil] efforts, 'it is clear more work is needed to consolidate standards, enforce principles, verify traceability along the supply chain and ensure competitive pricing to bring certified palm oil to market. We're monitoring the RSPO process and actively engaging our suppliers to monitor their certification efforts to find viable options for sourcing sustainable palm oil.' Neither Nestlé nor Kraft directly addressed purchases of Malaysia's certified palm oil."

It's not really a "newton" at all.  More like a delicate French butter cookie with bits of chewy blueberries.  Quite nice actually but not what I was expecting. But very good nonetheless..the box lasted all of 2 nights.

These cookies are thin and crispy. They have a wonderful blueberry flavor that isn't artifical tasting. The sweetness is well balanced, not too sweet, but definitely not bland.  My husband didn't not really care one way or another for them. So, I was thinking I had finally found a treat for myself. This was not to be. My children actually enjoy these cookies. While this is great that they like a snack that is not so sweet, but bad, because I will not have my snack that they won't ask for ;)

You know the cookies or crackers that you simply cannot just eat one?  Newtons Fruit Thins are not this type of cookie.  That's not to say that they're not delicious because they really are!!!  Everyone in my family liked them, including kids and my hubby, but I noticed that nobody ever asked for them on their own volition.  It was simply a cookie they ate and liked if it was offered.One teensy, tiny complaint is that they're kind of high calorie.  There's really nothing healthy about them despite the picture of blueberries on the front.  I don't know why, but they just SEEM like they should be healthy cookies by the packaging.  Do not be mislead into thinking that they are.  Nabisco NEVER even hints that they might be healthy, but it's just a perception I get when I look at them.
When I crave something sweet, I want it to be great and sweetly delicious.  That is not the case here.  However, if you're on a diet, buy these cookies.They're good for you.

column9: Tastes good and healthy for you
column10: I was pleasantly surprised by how good the blueberry Newton thins tasted considering that it is a healthy snack. It is difficult to find the right healthy-tasty balance in snacks. I think they have struck the right chord with my taste buds and will definitely make this a regular in my grocery list. A great snack to keep at the work place too, when you are feeling pecky in the afternoon.

Just a warning to potential buyers of this product, Amazon itself is not currently carrying it, so it is only available from 3rd party sellers, which means no Prime shipping and no Suscribe and Save, so if you really want this product, wait until Amazon gets it back in stock.I guess some people will love this product, others will strongly dislike it.My personal impression was that I was eating a piece of artificial blueberry flavored cardboard, but 3 other people in my house raved about how good this "cookie" is.I felt it was too dry, the texture while crispy, was rough and not pleasingThe taste of blueberry was too faint and I could not taste the brown sugar at all.If my rating had been based only on my tasting of this product, I would have given it two stars at most, a serving is 3 of the thins for 140 calories, and the taste just wasn't enjoyable.However, since my daughter, grandson, and a guest raved about the taste, I upgraded my star rating to 3 1/2 stars, since it is a healthy enough treat to give to a toddler

column9: Amazon Rocks, but Still Can't Ship Snacks Without Breaking
column10: I've tried ordering several types of snacks from Amazon, and invariably the contents have more broken and crushed pieces than typical at a grocery store.  It's not really their fault--- package shippers just aren't designed to handle these items carefully enough to prevent breakage.As for the snack itself, it gets props for good taste, using some wheat flour and some real fruit, but still too much sugar, too little fiber, and unnecessary added fructose to have it rate as a healthy snack.

column9: Great snack - tasty and on the healthier side
column10: These have quickly become a family favorite for a quick after-work snack.  I found the Blueberry Brown Sugar to be the sweeter of the flavors offered in this line, but not in an over-powering way.  The serving size is adequate (3 large crackers) and the packaging holds them together well so that you don't end up with a crumbly mess.  I recommend them, they are more subtly flavored than similar cookies on the market and they are on the healthier end of the spectrum.

I love Fig Newtons and I love crisp cookies.  I really wanted to love these new cookies.Kudos to Nabisco for trying to make a healthier type cookie that uses real fruit, flax, natural flavoring and sugar instead of high fructose corn syrup.We are slowly eating these as they aren't bad, but they also aren't the cookie or snack we want or crave.As many others have noted they are a bit on the dry side.  They are visually appealing cookies and I actually like how thin they are.Overall, they are just a bit to bland and dry for me.  Hopefully Nabisco will look at all the feedback on this and make some tweaks to the "recipe" and re-release these.

I tried this in addtion to the cranberry Fruit Thins. The blueberry flavor really pops, but there's less texture than with the cranberry ( I liked the chewiness of the cranberries). On the plus side, the brown sugar is delicious. As with the cranberry product, this cookie is good on its own, but much better with a cup of coffee or tea.A serving of three is enough to satisfy. They're good, but filling, and you won't keep munching until you look at the package and realize--oops!--they're almost all gone.If you like blueberries and want to indulge yourself a little, try these.
These are a pretty healthy, tasty snack.  They are more like a cracker, with a bit of dried fruit baked into the product.  My kids loved them!

column9: Good, pricey and has been done before
column10: I shared these Fruit Thins in the Office and the response was 45% YUCK, 40% GOOD, and 15% Neutral.  The Yuck group complained that the cracker was too dry, fruit tasted like cough syrup, texture was too chewy.  The Good group liked the Fig and Honey flavor better, and like that this was at least nutrious compared to similar crackers.  I fell into the neutral group and my main opinion is that it is okay, this type of cracker has been done before, some have had baked better versions and the price is quite expensive for a bag of crackers.  One of the more colorful comments is that NEWTON'S are always characterized by a soft fruit filled cake and this product just does not come close to that description hence the comfort food factor which might have made this more acceptable is lost.  Good effort, bad execution.

column9: Take everything you knew about the Newton Line.....
column10: The usual cookie wrapped around the fig filling will not be found in these cookies or Thins as these are being called.  The cookies or thins are crunchy little cookies packed with blueberry flavor, and not just a hint of blueberry either.  The first bite of these you know you are eating a blueberry cookie!  These make a great alternative to the afternoon snack of chips, or cookies, etc.  Overall they are a great product, as for the price per bag that needs a little work.

These remind me of the English tea biscuits that are nearly impossible to find anddon't have this wonderful flavor.  Yeah, real blue berries in the cookies.And for those complaining that they are dry... no where does the descriptionsay this is a soft cookie, so you can't assume they wouldn't be what they are;a thin, crunchy, cookie.Excellent flavor and I hope these stay around for a long time.  I have also tried theChocolate/Raspberry and I think they go better with coffee or a dark hot chocolate,basically a stronger drink. But they are excellent, just not as delicate as the Blueberry,or the Cranberry/citrus which I find as tasty as the Blueberry.  The Fig is good, but I haveto be in the mood for them as their flavor is very unique.If you are looking for a Tea Biscuit these are excellent and they are great for milk dunking.These were easy to find locally as well and at a much lower price.

The Newtons Fruit Thins crackers are a nice snack.  My kids really like this Blueberry Brown Sugar flavor saying it tastes like a blueberry muffin.  Basically they are thick granola like crackers but are more on the soft than crunchy side.  Layered in is a slightly sticky fruit type filling.  So you've got a crackery texture with a more bready and fruity taste.  They are pretty good and make a good quick snack.

I brought these with me to work, and they were universally enjoyed. "Any more?" was the repeated request, and I was sorry myself when they were all gone.Nabisco Newtons Blueberry Fruit Thins are the perfect combination of just the right amount of blueberry coupled with a light, biscuity cookie that satisfys a snack jones and provides both pleasing flavor and texture. Not one person who tried them disliked them; I only had one neutral comment, and that did not dismiss them entirely. I could have, frankly, eaten the whole bag myself, if restraint had not stopped me.The next stop at the store will be involving a pursuit of the other flavors in the Newton Fruit Thins line. This one was a shot out of the park.

I can't exactly tell you what it was that I expected when I agreed to sample and review these, but they're definitely a lot better than I thought they would be. My reaction to things that are blueberry flavored varies a lot, and this is definitely one of the better products I've come across in that area.They're not a super health food, but they're not meant to be. They're pretty reasonable as treats go. The serving size of 3 fruit thins for 140 calories is satisfying, and it's nice that there's a bit of protein and fat in the mix to help keep you from being hungry again 5 minutes later.I liked these a lot and I expect to buy them from time to time in the future as a nice treat.

Nabisco's new snack cracker, Newtons Fruit Thins, is a good tasting snack that doesn't contain some of the worst ingredients found in many snacks.  I tried the Blueberry Brown Sugar kind, and enjoyed them, as did my wife and daughter.  They tasted good with a very blueberry taste.  While you shouldn't classify these as a health food, they are not as bad as many snacks.  I like that they are made with real fruit, whole grains, and no high fructose corn syrup.Three of the thin cookies add up to 140 calories, and it would be easy to eat many more than three, so a person dieting will have to control portion size.  Out of those 140 calories, 45 come from fat, and one of the 5 grams is from saturated fat.  However, no trans fats, which is good.  90 mg of sodium, so not too high.  The ingredient list has things you know, not a lot of man made things, so I like that.  It is a more natural snack.  Ingredients are: Unbleached Enriched Flour (Wheat Flour, Niacin, Reduced Iron, Thiamine Mononitrate (Vitamin B1), Riboflavin (Vitamin B2), Folic Acid), Whole Grain Wheat Flour, Soybean and/or Palm Oil, Sugar, Rolled Oats, Dried Blueberries, Brown Sugar, Flax Seeds, Fructose, Salt, Baking Soda, Soy Lecithin, Natural Flavor.For a thin, fruit flavored, cookie snack, Nabisco's new Newtons Fruit Thins are a good tasting crispy cookie.  We enjoy them, and I like that they are not as bad for you as many other snacks.  If you control how many you eat, these are great for those with a sweet tooth.

I am snacking on one of the Blueberry and Brown Sugar Newton's Fruit Thins as I am typing this review.  All I can say is Nabisco has created a winner with this snack.  These are not overly sweet, which I like, almost like a shortbread and they are full of real blueberries (dried blueberries) and also brown sugar.  Also they are crispy which I also like! A thin crispy and full of blueberries treat.These are very good with tea or with coffee whatever is your pleasure.  Also for those of you who are dieting, 3 of the cookies, which are a decent size have 140 calories or in Weight Watchers, 3 points, so not too bad on the calories or the points.I am enjoying them and will be buying more! These have no high fructose corn syrup and they are made with wheat flour so it is all good!

column9: More of a cracker than a cookie
column10: The Newton Blueberry Fruit Thins reminded me more of an English biscuit than a real cookie.  Great with tea.  Very intense blueberry flavor.  Although they have the Newton name, they are nothing like a fig newton.  They have the consistency of a cracker or a raisinette cookie (if those are still around).  Good product.

column9: I shall call these... crookers. That is, part cookie, part cracker.
column10: With the density and shape of a cookie and the fragility of a cracker, it's an interesting combination. They have a shortbread-like consistency, a dry blueberry taste, and a bit of oatmeal flavor as well. The brown sugar flavor is subtle at best. Each time I open the box (which has re-sealable tabs I've never seen before), I get a waft of fruitiness. I'm hooked!The ingredients aren't listed on the product page, so I had to seek them out elsewhere. These cookies are dairy-free, and it appears they may even be vegan.UNBLEACHED ENRICHED FLOUR (WHEAT FLOUR, NIACIN, REDUCED IRON, THIAMINE MONONITRATE (VITAMIN B1), RIBOFLAVIN (VITAMIN B2), FOLIC ACID), WHOLE GRAIN WHEAT FLOUR, SOYBEAN AND/OR PALM OIL, SUGAR, ROLLED OATS, DRIED BLUEBERRIES, BROWN SUGAR, FLAX SEEDS, FRUCTOSE, SALT, BAKING SODA, SOY LECITHIN, NATURAL FLAVOR.Allergens and Nutritional Considerations: Added Sugars, Gluten, Soy, Wheat

I found these cookies a breath of healthy fresh air in the typically over-sweet standard selection of American traditional cookies.  I never understood the fascination with the sweet, fatty, calorie-laden favorite cookie in this country - the chocolate chip.  The Newtons are very European, where  on my travels I discovered the idea of the light "biscuit" style cookie that people there snack on with tea or coffee.  It's not a coincidence that Europeans are not nearly as overweight or obesive as we are, and this type of cookie snack is a small part of why that is with their differences in diet and attitudes.I liked the Raspberry Chocolate very much, but thought the Blueberry was the best.  The latter has a delicious blueberry flavor with nice bits of dried fruit, along with a tastey and healthful flax seed crunch.  With my morning coffee, just fabulous.

A delicious, fresh-tasting cookie, with the real flavor of blueberry. If you could take the concentrated aromatic yumminess of the filling of a "blueberry newton" and spread it throughout a crispy wafer, this is what you'd expect. Definitely not a disappointment. I will order more!

column9: if you want healthier, these are good
column10: This package was delivered not long before the tornadoes struck so I had almost forgotten about them. This afternoon I was looking for a snack and remembered these cookies.They were very crunchy and crisp although a bit dry; solved that with a tall cold glass of milk. The blueberries tasted real although got a little gummy and stuck to my teeth. The brown sugar was very subtle - I definitely have a sweet tooth. These are nothing like Fig Newtons.If you are looking for a tasty healthier cookie with no HFCS, then Newtons Fruit Thins are what you want....

These are semi-thin, crunchy cookies with dried blueberries mixed in.The good:I loved the packaging and the fact that I could keep the contents fresh with the folding wire.I appreciate the lack of corn syrup and the whole grain %.They are low in sugar and even have some iron.I love that they have no cholesterol.My husband and son really liked their taste (very important to know when one craves junk food and the other has high cholesterol).The negative:I thought these would have a new kind of taste but they don't.Each cookie is about 45 calories.The fat content is quite high (8%).I didn't like the taste much.Would I buy them again? Not for me, but if I am filling up the pantry with food for others to snack on, I will definitely pick these over other cookies.

My children taste tested these and only one of them liked them.  The cookies were crisp, so if you envisioned these to be like a soft, chewy fig newton cookie, that is something that you should know.  The picture on the front makes the cookie look softer than it actually is.The child that did like them also loves blueberries.  He gobbled the cookies up and asked for more.  The fruit bits aren't microscopic; you can actually see them in the cookie.  The cookies are very thin though and I don't know that they hold up well in milk.  They are thin, as advertised!They have no High Fructose Corn Syrup in them.  One other thing I would like to note is that when you open the package up, you can definitely smell the blueberry flavor.  It is fairly strong too.

I love this cookie* and it's my husband's new favorite. It's crisp (sturdy, not delicate; great for dunking), not too sweet, and with blueberries that add a chewiness and a wonderful, natural flavor. The nutrition stats are decent (3 cookies = 140 calories/5g fat/2g fiber); 30+ cookies in a package and we're satisfied by 4-6 cookies. At a sitting, that is :) we like them so much that we've been back to the grocery store and are finishing up our third package.*Note: the "Newtons" name seems a branding/marketing tactic; these bear little resemblance to e.g. Fig Newtons other than being a less-sweet, more wholesome, fruit-oriented cookie.

I was really excited to try these because i love blueberries. I was very disappointed. The blueberry part was very tough. The worst part was the flax seeds. I was not expecting seeds in my cookie. I did not enjoy these and won't be buying them ever again. Who wants seeds in their cookies?

My initial impression of Newton's Blueberry Brown Sugar Fruit Thins was that they were too dry.  I confess that, at the bottom of the package, are the words "crispy cookies".  I had expected a chewy-like fig newton except with the more appetizing blueberry filling than the fig filling.  So I had started out with some false impressions.  I ate a few and my wife ate a few and then they sat on the shelf until last weekend when our fine Northern Plains community was struck with an awesome blizzard that left the whole county without electricity for three days.  We had food in the freezer and a gas grill on the snow-drift covered deck so we were able to survive.  One of the best treats we had during those cold, gloomy days was the rest of the Newtons Fruit Thins.  They were gone in a hurry.  Once I got away from the idea of a chewy blueberry bar, those crispy crackers weren't too bad.

My husband and I are not big fans of sugary sweets, so I hesitated at trying this product.  Well, bring them on!  This is a crispy, slightly sweet wafer filled with real blueberries!  The serving size is three cookies, and with their slightly oversized diameter of approximately three inches, I found just two to be more than satisfying.  These cookies are a natural for ice cream or fruit.  I would not, however, give these cookies to really young children because of the sticky dehydrated blueberries compressed into the cookie.  They stuck to my teeth, which was OK for me, but I'm not sure how a child under two would do with this product; maybe OK.  Overall, this is a very nice light dessert item.

Nabisco has done it again with this great new product. It is not exactly a cookie, and it is not exactly a cracker, but something in between.These Fruit Thins are called crispy cookies on the packaging, and they are crisp enough to seem like a cracker, but they are not dry like a cracker. They have a wonderful fruitiness about them. I had the blueberry and bown sugar version, and they had real pieces of chewy blueberry in the cookies.They are not heavy like some rich desserts, but have a rich flavor. I like that they are made with unbleached flour, which gives the cookies a warm brown color. I especially love them with hot tea; my husband likes his with coffee. These Fruit Thins make a great snack or a light after dinner dessert.Three cookies are only 140 calories, with 5 grams of fat, only 90 sodium, and only 8 sugar grams.The packaging is nice in that the cookies are not loose in the bag but set in a plastic tray. Now I know that environmentally, this is extra packaging, but I like the tray because it keeps the cookies from getting crushed in transport/shipping.Overall, this is an excellent snack or dessert.

These are some very tasty, crispy, blueberry cookies.  Their ingredient list is almost entirely pronounceable, and for cookies, they are relatively low calorie.  They have a nice crunch, and the flax seed adds to the overall taste.  If you like crunchy cookies and blueberries, you will appreciate this new offering from the Newton family of cookies.
These cookies were crispy and delicious.  Everyone in the family from tween to grandpa loved them.  This will definately become a staple in our house.

I wasn't sure what to expect when I ordered these new cookies, and to be honest, I have mixed feelings about them. They're thin and crunchy, much more like crackers than cookies. The texture is very similar to graham crackers, actually, and they're not very sweet. They have tiny dried blueberries in them, along with brown sugar for flavoring. I would not have called them "cookies", because they're much more like crackers. The flavor is a bit odd. I don't know how to describe it. Rather bland, actually. My favorite part is the dried blueberries, so it's a shame they're so tiny! These cookies make for a quick breakfast, or a mid-afternoon snack. Just make sure you have something to drink, as well, to wash them down.The ingredient list appears mostly "normal", without a lot of weird stuff: enriched flour, whole grain wheat flour, soybean and/or palm oil, sugar, rolled oats, dried blueberries, brown sugar, flax seeds, fructose, salt, baking soda, soy lecithin, and natural flavor. They're somewhat low in fat (5g) and they've got some fiber in them (2g), zero trans fat and zero cholesterol, and 8g of sugars.I would hesitantly recommend them, but I have a feeling that many people will be as ambivalent about them as I am. They're not great, they're not horrible. They're just sort of . . . eh. On the other hand, I do keep eating them. So perhaps they grow on you? I can't see kids enjoying them, it's definitely a more "mature" kind of cookie. My husband feels the same way--he doesn't love them, but doesn't hate them, either.

Wow, these are really good!  These are a thin, crispy cookie with bits of blueberry.  They're not too crisp, though -- not like a cracker -- they're more cookie-like than cracker-like.  They're also nothing like the Newton Fruit Crisps; they're much, much tastier.  You can taste the traditional Fig Newton flavor, but the blueberries really add a great twist, making it a totally different cookie.  If you're a Newton fan, you'll definitely want to try these.

Crispy, full of flavor without being too sweet, blueberry taste lingers deliciously on the tongue: I thoroughly enjoyed the Newtons Fruit Thins.  And--judging by how quickly they disappeared from the cookie jar--the rest of the family did also.The picture on the front of the package made it appear that the cookies were larger than they actually were.  A full serving is 3 cookies...that seems about right since the "cookies" are more like thin cracker wafers than actual cookies.  The manufacturer might want to consider placing a see-through celophane window on the package rather than the current picture.  Otherwise buyers might think they're purchasing one thing and would be getting something that looked quite different.

I love the soft and chewiness of a Fig Newton so I wanted to try Nabisco's newest product Newton's Fruit Thins with Blueberry and Brown Sugar.  It tastes like a blueberry muffin but in a thin crisp cookie reminiscent of shortbread.  My 5 year old saw that we had cookies and immediately asked for one.  But, she was expecting something soft and chewy and handed it back to me after one bite.  But my 3 year old appreciated the flavor and didn't mind the crispiness of the fruit thins.  It was hard to just eat one but be careful, it's easy to eat more than the suggest serving size of 3 cookies.  Here's the nutritional information:Serving Size: 3 cookies (30g) About 10 servings per containerCalories: 140Calories from fat: 45Total fat: 5gCholesterol: 0mgSodium: 90mgPotassium: 50mgTotal Carbs: 21gDietary Fiber: 2gSugars: 8gProtein: 2g

column4: Michael A. Saxton "Dark Lord of the Sith"
column10: So I brought this package into work and shared with a coworker and we both came up with the same conclusion. Yum.Of course, I will explain. These are thin, almost English tea-like cookie crackers. They're decent in the health department, with some fiber and 3 of them are 140 calories. What's nice is the balance of flavor. They are not overly sweat. They have a strong but not overpowering blueberry flavor. I'd definitely add these to my snack list.For those that are health conscious, there is fructose in these. It is one of the last ingredients. There is also wheat and soy for those of you with allergies. If you are not allergic, give them a try.

column4: ChibiNeko "Sooo many books, so little time!"
column9: Not too sweet, not too bland, just right.
column10: I received both this flavor as well as the cranberry citrus flavors to review, & I have to say that I prefer this flavor over the other one.PROS: The blueberry flavor is nicely done. While it doesn't taste exactly like a fresh blueberry it's still a pretty yummy flavor. It sort of reminds me of the blueberry compote you get on top of IHOP pancakes. (This is good for me since it's a good way to get the taste without the obscene amount of fat & calories that you get in IHOP pancakes.)CONS: While I got used to it after a while, I wasn't really expecting these to be thin & crispy. It's not a dealbreaker but I know I'm not the only one who was expecting a softer cookie.Over all, I'll be purchasing these again to eat. They make for a nice, relatively healthy treat to pack in my lunches.

column4: John Clark Craig "author of Sun Position - Hi...
column10: Somehow, I expected the Newtons Fruit Thins to be sort of soft and chewy, like a blueberry flavored fig newton I suppose. However, they're more like a cross between a thin, crisp, dryish blueberry-sprinkled cookie, and a graham cracker. The ingredients all sound healthy, and they are rather tasty, once you get used to what they are, so I did enjoy them, and the kids made them disappear overnight. They're just what they are, and not what I had expected them to be, but that's okay. Give 'em a try to see if they work for you.

Three people taste tested these.  All three reported favorable.Comments were, "mmm, it tastes like real blueberries"Teenager, "of course I like it, that's why I keep eating them"The cookie is called a thin, but won't help you get thin.One serving is three cookies, 140 calories, 5 fat, 21 carbs.It is roughly equivalent to a lower calories snack bar.I also like that there is no high fructose corn syrup in it.It's not as thin as a wafer, nor as thick as a home baked cookie, it's more like the thickness of a Ritz cracker, but wider.It has a nice brown sugar and blueberry taste and feels substantial.  I will buy them again.

This product -- two mugs and two filter cones -- is a great bargain. The red mugs are very attractive. They've redesigned the filter cone so you can see how much water you've already poured in. (This avoids the former "whoops" of overflowing the mug because you poured before checking.)  Also comes with a few filters to get you started. Highly recommended.
This is a quality product.  The cone is what you would expect. The mugs have a hard plastic top with a slider that covers the opening you would drink from.  This is a good deal.

The single cup coffee maker works well as advertized and makes great coffee. One of the two was damaged in shipment (box was squashed in the corner) but at this price it was not worth sending back.Two slight quibbles:1. The top piece was designed more for a 'sweeping' look than snugly fitting a #2 cone filter2. It would be great if someone could design one of these single coffee makers where one could pour in the full 6 / 8 ounces of hot water at one time and not have to hover over it to keep topping it off, at the same time worrying about over filling it.Note: the thermal carafe is the best portable hot travel mug I have used. It's deep lip keeps the hot liquid from spilling in the car.

This is a good deal.  Pack of 2, one for me and one to give as a gift.  Very easy to use.  I use it at night to make a cup of decaf.  Makes good coffee and you can make coffee your desired strength.  I use 1 scoop of coffee for every 5oz of water.

I have been a Melitta user for at least 5 years and could not be happier with the Ready Set Joe set. It works as it is suppose to and is an excellent value for your money. Get yours while the price is low!

I thought I would just google mushroom powder for the heck of it, and came across this.  Now, I have been grinding my own porcini powder for several years, it was very time consuming as well as expensive.  Messy, too.  But I love putting it on potatoes, in soup, on fish, just about everything I could think of.  I love mushrooms.  I had been out of powder for quite a while, and I could not really afford to buy any to grind.I saw this product, and thought it was too good to be true, there had to be a chemical or something in it, or a filler.  But I ordered a couple of containers anyway.  OMG, the stuff is the real deal.  Real porcini..nothing else.  And it is ground finer than the stuff I was making.  And smells fabulous.  It is a HUGE bargain compared to doing it myself.  I don't even have to be stingy with it.  I am overjoyed.  Sometimes I open the lid just to smell it.  It is amazing.  I couldn't be happier.  I will be a grateful customer as long as they carry this product.A few suggestions..in rice a roni, in gravy, in wild rice, in broth, on potatoes, sprinkle on fish with a little bit of garlic powder, seasoned breadcrumbs,and bake, added to cream of mushroom soup  for more flavor, a little in scrambled eggs, the possibilities are endless..

column9: Excellent porcini flavor from this powder
column10: Have used it in a rub for meat, and also mixed with flour in a roux. Even tried it in baking bread, but the overall effect wasn't good (the cook's fault!). Quite flavorful stuff. I've used it reasonably quickly so am not sure if it keeps the flavor for long. But I do have a large sealed bag of dried porcini mushrooms which has kept quite well for over a year (with a desiccant package inside).

I can't say I'm an expert at evaluating porcini powder, but I use it on grilled steaks.  The first time, I ground dried porcini mushrooms and that was a pain.  I decided to buy some, and compared to other merchants this was a great value, and both the shipping charges and expediency was very reasonable.
Arrived on time, but  jar was open, partially spilled  :(.  Taste is great. I wish I would get it in better condition, but the product itself - will order again.

This stuff is the shit. It is an easy way to add flavor and nobody will know where it is coming from. It doesn't taste "mushroomy" exactly, it just adds depth to any dish without additional salt!  YAY!

Add to food as a flavoring in place of the mushrooms and the earthy taste is amazing.  I love this.  Have used it in several dishes and it has made it's statement in each.  It has wonderful flavor and very easy to use.  Price is much better than many others I looked at.  I'm happy!
Great product!  I use it as part of a rub for veal chops, steak and tuna.  Nice not to have to grind up whole porcini mushrooms, and yet the flavor is very intense.

column9: I could take this, or leave it!
column10: It's okay a tasting but I'm not a real big fan of it. I've had Australian type licorice that tastes much better. This stuff to me just my opinion had a weird after taste to it! Somebody else might just absolutely love it though. It's soft and authentic Australian type licorice but I just didn't enjoy the taste of it as much as others I've tried.

My husband got me this gift basket for Mother's Day. At first sight, it was beautifully wrapped, and the lavender smell was soothingly lovely. However, once I opened it, the body lotion bottle and the shower gel bottle had clearly been tampered with. The seal on both bottles was broken, and the bottles themselves were not full.My husband and I were both enraged, especially after we learned from my mother-in-law that the Jasmine basket we sent her for Mother's Day had the same problem. Her package arrived collapsed, which damaged the potpourri inside. In addition, the safety foil around the body lotion was missing and the bottle was 1/2 empty and very clearly tampered with.NOT ONLY IS THIS A DISAPPOINTMENT, BUT ALSO A HYGIENE ISSUE!!! We have been using Amazon gift service for a very long time and had never had any problem until now. DO NOT ORDER PRODUCTS FROM ART OF APPRECIATION!!!

column9: Helps my dogs breath and hair
column10: I have a yorkie who even after having her teeth cleaned at the vet, use to have horrible breath and hair that matted very easily. Since changing her dog food, she no longer has the horrid breath and her hair looks and feels fantastic! I will definitely buy this repeatedly- worth every penny to us!!
I love canned guavas - I wish these were the pink variety because I love them more, but these are GOOD!

column9: I want them ALL, so don't buy 'em
column10: This is almost like sitting under my great-grandmother's guava tree hoping for a bumper crop so she would let me eat more than one (homemade jelly had first priority and I SWEAR she counted them). WONDERFUL taste and texture. So, please don't buy these so I don't have to share.
Mex grocer shipped my order fast a product widely unavailable in the US. The product tastes like a pear and the seeds are edible. I like the seller and product.

column9: Cinnamon good, Cherry Cough Syrup, Lemon Nice
column10: This is an interesting combination. The Cinnamon flavor is light so it doesn't bring tears to the eyes or burn the mouth. The Cherry tastes a bit like cough syrup. The Lemon flavor is very nice and just what one would expect for a Lemon hard candy.I won't buy the combination again as I prefer a much stronger cinnamon flavor. I avoid anything tasting like cough syrup and I can get the lemon drops separately.

column9: Don't waste your good money on the Godiva name
column10: Just got my order today.  Not nearly as good as I was thinking they were going to taste.  Trader Joe's sugar free milk chocolate bars are so much better and cheaper.  Will never buy these again.  They don't taste like real chocolate and leave a greasy coating on the tongue.  Yuck!
this is the most nasty low carb chocolate that i have tried and i have tried a lot.i will never get this again.

I will never pay that much for a canister of Hills Bro Capp.  I pay $3.28 per canister from Walmart.  I wasn't understanding what volume of product you were getting for the price, so I clicked on the 'More Info' link.  That's absurd!! The offer for $19 plus for 3 canisters is even more insulting.  I could easily purchase 2 cans for what they're asking for 1!!  Not a good deal...

Whew!I need to wipe my forehead.These are very fresh, flavorful chiles.They are not hot for heat's sake, they are actually tasty as well.My husband does most of our cooking and with these he has learned that less is actually better.Great price, good packaging and fast shipping.Kudos to the seller.

column9: Not as hot as I expected
column10: All of these peppers are fresh, but only one of them is hot (the habanero flakes). The other five choices are moderately hot and would be tolerable to most folks. I wish they were all as hot as I would expect Dave's brand to be.2 Flakes: Habanero, Chipotle4 Powders: Cayenne, Ancho, New Mexico, and De Arbol
If you love curry, these are the noddles for you!  They have 3 seperate flavor packs inside and are delicious!!!

These noodles taste great, but I would suggest adding the flavor packets in as soon as you start cooking, instead of pouring the noodles/water over the seasonings immediately before eating, as instructed. The latter leads to a far weaker flavor than Indomie noodles usually have. Adding the seasonings in at the same time as the noodles results in a much richer flavor.My only complaint is the noodles themselves aren't very good, even for instant noodles. This isn't a big deal, but it's more noticeable in their soups than in their Mi Goreng.

Excellent freshness and quick receipt of product.  A superb nutritional product that should replace much of coffee drinking.  The company INFUZION was easy to contact, very friendly, and very reliable, once it is realized the spelling is infuZion. Will always order from this vendor.
This tea has a very mild smooth flavor, best tea I have ever purchased. Would highly recommmend this tea, great with honey when nursing a cold.
Product was two months expired when I received it. I would have given it zero stars if possible since I wasn't even able to try it.
Masoor lentils are my favorite. They're quick and easy to prepare. Very easy to digest and delicious! Thanks Swad!
Used to make a brew and no effect: if even mild. Wouldn't waste $ on it even if it seems to be cost effective!

Ayahuasca Vine alone will not give any pleasant or interesting trip. But combined with mushrooms or DMT it will give an intense trip. This special combination is capable of inducing a powerful psychedelic experience because the MAO inhibitor present in the Ayahuasca preserves the DMT. DMT is a psychoactive chemical which produces intense visuals and strong psychedelic effects but is usually rendered ineffective when taken orally because it is easily broken down by the body's MAO enzyme.
Excellent heat though it has a bit too much smoke for my taste. Just a little dab will do ya when it comes to the heat. If you use too much the smoke flavor can be a bit overwhelming.
I make both chili and hot sauces and this powder takes it up a notch!!!!

If you are looking for a true hot chili pepper this is the one for you. However, not recommended for the average person. Even those of us that think the hot peppers that are avalible in the stores are like sweet peppers, we still only use very small amounts of this pepper to make dishes very hot to us.Few warnings though, do not get on skin, or in face it will hurt you a lot. Best used with eye protection, good venting, and gloves. If you get it on your skin wash it off as quickly as possible. If in face, flush with lots of water and seek medical help.

I orderd these lollipops for my daughter's birthday party. By far the best prices I could find and everyone said they were delicious. I liked them because they were small and most of the children at the party were younger. They come one a long stick but it is very easy to cut to whichever length you want.

I can't vouch personally for this product as I selected it to send as a gift to my brother-in-law for his birthday (he lives on the East Coast of the USA and I live in London).  It was delivered very quickly in plenty of time for the actual date I wanted it to arrive.  Brother-in-Law was thrilled as he's keen on BBQs, and enjoys good quality meat.  My sister and niece were also thrilled.  They celebrated Father's Day with the Birthday sausages and happy smiles all round.

This plant food is incredible. It's super-concentrated plant fuel. Whether you have a green thumb or not, I highly recommend Schultz. It's inexpensive and lasts forever (only 7 drops per quart of water). If you tend to notice last-minute that your plants are dying, this stuff will save the plant.It does promote incredible growth, though, so if your plants are healthy and you start using it every time you water, be prepared for that.I've never tried it on outdoor plants (I live in an apartment), but I've heard nothing but good from friends who also use Schultz.Bottom Line: Incredible value, Super-Concentrated, and definitely worth checking out.

What could be worse for your superstitious spouse than a dying "lucky" bamboo plant? Thankfully, a quick drop of this into some water and the plant perked right up within a week. Works great, and it looks like the bottle will last forever.

I purchased this product as I liked the all-in-one formulation and was inspired by others' comments about how it has successfully snatched their flora back from almost certain demise.  I haven't been disappointed.  I live in a shady area, but decided to try my hand at growing some potted herbs outdoors (basil, cilantro, catnip, catmint.)  Even with the limited amount of sun, the herbs are robust with the addition of this product.  True to other reviews, it also saved my droopy looking fuchsia which I thought I would lose.  In short, I'd definitely recommend this product.

Straight up love this fertilizer.  I use it every-other-day on my herbs, at either the prescribed "7 drops per quart" or half that, depending on how I feel my plants are doing.  Provides a perfect mix of nutrients for indoor plants.Every few weeks I like to spike my plants with a nitrogen-rich fertilizer, so you may want to pick up an small bottle of something else to complement Schultz.  The nitrogen-rich fertilizer will give your herbs a nice flush of leaves, but you don't want to do it too often or you'll have a lot of leaves with little flavor.

I have an umbrella tree at the office where I work. Though matter how much or little I watered it, the leaves would turn yellow and fall off. I gave it coffee grounds. I even transferred it to a larger pot with Miracle Grow soil. Nothing still. As a last resort, I bought this. I put a few drops of this into the water and not only did it stop dying, it actually has a lot of new growth. I'd recommend this product to anyone new to plants. This has the ideal ratio of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium so it'll bring most houseplants back to life in no time.
Very convenient, easy to use.  I keep my watering can full so I am always ready to water and fertilize.  Great for indoor plants
This product when used as instructed does not kill your plants and rarely causes nute burn with over application. This is a good product for a novice like me.

This is the only plant food I would use on my Norfolk Island Pine.  It has taken this plant from a baby to a tree and it is fabulous!  The dropper is very handy and easy to measure.  Can't always find it in stores, but I can always find it on Amazon!  Fast delivery.

I got a not-so-lucky bamboo that was trying to survive, but I have not really seen it  thriving -- it's not drying up but there aren't any noticeable changes, either. I had another stalk that had the top half died and I had to cut off that portion to try to salvage the bottom stalk as the roots still seem healthy. I read the reviews of this product, and they seem promising, so I decided to get it and see what happens, because I really wanted to prove that I have some green thumb in me.So far my bamboo are starting to show some positive results. The little stalk that I salvaged is now sprouting new roots, and it's now got a leaf stalk growing within a few weeks of the food solution, which I never thought would happen (I was almost ready to give up on that piece). I see the leaf stalk growing every day. The other stalk didn't have much progress, though, at least on its existing leaves, but I am noticing a little leaf bump on one of its sections (plus a set of new roots) so I still think it's surviving.I'll take pictures when it starts looking less sad (when it's leafed up a bit more). I can't really say I still have a green thumb in me, but I am happy that at least I can keep my lucky bamboo alive (considering it's one of the more resilient and easy-to-care plants, it would be embarrassing if I still manage to kill it).
I recommend this, the 10-15-10 formula seems to be what finally turned the corner on my house plants. They were yellow and nothing else would change that until this 10-15-10 came along.

This brand name product has been around for quite some time and this product grade 10-15-10 is perfect. This has just the right amounts of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Just gives houseplants that little extra zing. I would definitely recommend this product.
my blooms have doubled in size, my baskets and tubs are the envy of the street,i will definitly be using this product again

i started using it right away and at first couldn't tell. I then used it again a few days later, then stopped for a week and the plants looked as if they were dying, but they weren't, just growing slower. This stuff really boosts growth and makes plants look more lively!

column9: My Favorite Tonic For House Plants
column10: This is an excellent product.  As the previous reviewer said, it does last forever.  I use 28 drops per gallon of water plus a dab of "Super Thrive" and it is the bomb!  It is far superior to Miracle Grow.  I tried to buy this locally both at Walmart and Lowes without success.  Came home, Googled and here I am.  Very happy to find it on Amazon.  Going to order some for myself and my florist friend.  She has noticed a definite improvement in her plants that she has for sale.  That says a lot for a product.  I'm the "Church Lady" and I bring peace lilies home to baby them for the week in between.  They are in absolute gorgeous bloom!  I actually saw a lady today touch the plant to see if it was real or not!

Schultz All Purpose cibi vegetariani più 10-15-10, 4 Fl. Oz. 1011è un ottimo prodotto per nutrire con equilibrio le piante in vasola crescita delle piante è più velocele foglie saranno di un bellissimo verdela pianta risulterà più sana
easy to order-arrived quickly. I ordered 2 bottles of it and they came separately on different days, (??) but they came! Am happy with that.
I really don't think people need this, but if you find it as your only hope, then why not? I used it once and I can't say there was a wow reaction.

I bought this bread to try as a cheaper alternative to Mestemacher's -- the sort of dense, moist rye bread commonly sold in packets in Europe, especially Germany.  Lowell seems to be an importer of various European foods, so I was hoping for quality similar to that of Mestemacher.  But this bread is definitely less flavorful and falls apart more easily.  Moreover, it's not truly whole rye, but "whole grain rye" -- i.e., contains wheat, which noticeably dilutes the rye goodness.  Unfortunately Amazon doesn't show the ingredients list.  Packaging suggests it's a product of Poland.

Be careful!  After trying this wonderful blend of spices, with great complexity of flavor, that they say is made with 35 ingredients, I found ras el hanout in my local grocery store.  When I tried it alongside this one, there was no comparison.  Then I checked the label--the local one had only 8 ingredients!  It went into the trash and another order was placed to Zamouri.Ras el hanout can be used in a number of Moroccan dishes that are fabulous, although they tend to be complex to prepare--although if you're in the mood they are worth the effort.  But I also use it in tomato soup to give an amazing richness of flavor to it, transforming an everyday dish to a company dish.  Today I'm braising short ribs, and when I've cooked down the braising liquid I'll add ras el hanout to provide a symphony of flavor to it.  I haven't tried it with tomatoes and cheese on an omelet, but it's the sort of thing that's likely to be fabulous.  With a little experimentation, you'll find your own favorite uses for it.

About ten years ago a friend made amazing Algerian couscous for us in which she used a bottle of ras-el-hanout purchased in France under the Ducros brand name.  It was fabulous and for years I tried finding the same spice/flavor/scent in hopes of duplicating our unforgettable feast - with repeated disappointments.  I read the reviews for the Zamouri ras-el-hanout and decided to take a chance, even though I was about to give up hope. And what do you know, this IS the real thing - just incredible. Do yourself a favor and saute some crushed garlic and onion in olive oil, add some diced assorted vegetables (peppers, tomatoes, zucchini, eggplant etc.), throw in some raisins, garbanzo beans, 1T cumin and 3T of this wonderful ras-el-hanout... serve over couscous and you're off to a very happy evening!
This is great for Couscous sauce and other red sauces! I would recommend making it at home then buying it, but if you don't know how or don't have the opportunity to do it this is the brand to buy!

Most Ras al Hanout contains only a few ingredients. This one, with over 20, is the real stuff one might get in a Maghreb spice shop as the "top of the line" (literally 'top of the shop') secret family mixture.

This spice blend means we give you the best we got.  Zamouri is one of the most reliable and expert of shops on the web.  I usually try to make my own blends, but for tagine, I let these folks do the work.  My job is not letting it get stale.  Four ounces is plenty.  But I am a somewhat heavy user.  Go with two ounces.  The shelf life is about six months in the cool and dark before the power starts to fall off.They have cute little spice tagines like the one pictured, and many more in a variety of colors and styles.  But I am not good at presentation and I am happy with the jar it comes in.  Fish, chicken, cauliflower, turnip -- all good!  And you can go to the red side as well.  But I could not resist their large tagine, charcoal burner and bellows to do some outdoors.  High quality, tasty and fragrant.  I cannot find or produce the equal. Surrender.

This Ras El Hanout is a wonderful, authentic  spice that is difficult to recreate yourself.  It's hard to find and really enhances Middle Eastern cuisine.  This blend  includes lavender and roses, as well as more common cinnamon and cumin. Ras El Hanout gives a distinctive Middle Eastern flavor to a dish.  I use it in my Moroccan chicken, which I prepare in a crock pot.  A tagine would of course be even better!  For my recipe, I use organic  boneless chicken, a few tablespoons of high quality extra virgin olive oil,  potatoes or sweet potatoes,  quartered onions, lots of "baby" carrots, chick peas, cans of whole or diced tomatoes, diced garlic, honey, diced/chopped dried fruit such as apricots and/or prunes, chopped preserved lemon (you can buy or very easy to make), and then some  additional cinnamon and cumin, plus black pepper in addition to Ras Al Hanout to taste.  You do want to add enough to really flavor the "stew."  Moroccan chicken is very healthy and  fantastic served over whole wheat couscous.  For a lower carb version, you can omit the potatoes and serve over greens.  My kids love it, but it's also special enough for company.  If you enjoy Moroccan food or experimenting with spices, it's a great addition to your pantry!

column9: Ras El Hanout - more curry-like than I'd anticipated
column10: I love Morrocan chicken and a good Ras El Hanout spice is essential for this dish.  I was suprised at this blend, it differs significantly in the balance of flavors from the one I was originally introduced to.  This is a much more savory - curry-like spice than the more sweetly cinammon-heavy original I started with.  I'll have to try others to understand better if there is a 'standard' for Ras El Hanout!

column9: I can't get enough of it!!!
column10: I love Middle Eastern spices and foods, so I look for fresh spices all the time. I stumbled on this and used it the other day in  Black-eyed peas with green peppers, garlic, and onions...oh my goodness AMAZING!  I have used it with extra Lean ground beef to make meatballs and gravy YUM!  The combination is amazingly well blended.  IF you have ever eaten at a real Moroccan restaurant and loved it...you'll love this.  If you like Eastern Indian food, Dahl etc, you'll love this spice in your lentils and stews!!

'Ras El Hanout' means 'top of the shop', indicating a blend of many spices (in some instances, more than 100) as favoured by whatever spice merchant happens to be selling it to you.  Thus, it varies greatly in composition from one merchant to another.  Some are more 'traditional' blends than others, and some are just lazy Westernised versions about as exotic as K-Mart Curry Powder.This is not a 'lazy' Ras El Hanout.Coming in at a reasonable 35 spices (including Rose Powder, Lavender Powder, Grains Of Paradise, and 32 others), this lovely blend strikes just the right balance of spicy, sweet, floral, and savoury.  I use it with Couscous, Hummus, Tabouli, Kebabs, Chicken Bastila - really anything North African or Middle Eastern.  Hell, I'll even dust some Naan lightly with it prior to heating in my oven; I'm not some xenophobic Food Purist!Try it, you'll like it...

column9: A very authentic Moroccan spice blend
column10: As with many ethnic spice mixtures, there is no one recipe for Ras el Hanout.  Each family and spice merchant has their own, highly treasured and guarded version of this traditional blend.  This particular product is of high quality and arrived fresh (which isn't always the case with spices that I have purchased on-line).Ras el Hanout starts off with strong, curry-like flavors that betrays it's Indian origins followed by subtle, traditional African flavors such as nigella and rosebuds.  Although I was very pleased with this blend I do think that it is over-priced.  I shop for most of my spices at ethnic markets (mostly Indian and Middle Eastern) and find their mixtures to be not only fresh but REALLY affordable.  I am using this mixture with my new tagine and if I use it often enough I will seek out an African grocery store that has a similar product at a price that Moroccan expatriates will be willing to pay. If you don't live near a city that is large enough to have that type of store, then I think that this is the best Ras el Hanout available on-line.  As a matter of fact, a tangine cookbook that I bought recently singled out Zamouri as THE source for this delicious, exotic blend.Tagines & Couscous: Delicious Recipes for Moroccan One-pot CookingEmile Henry Flame Top 2.6-Quart Tagine RedHarissa Paste 8.0 Oz By Zamouri Spices

column9: Great to have on hand: they keep for ever and are very tasty!
column10: I grew up up in a family that loved mushrooms, so I love using them in my cooking. Dried mushrooms are convenient because they keep so well! I like the flavor of Oyster mushrooms and JR Mushrooms brand has an excellent quality.To reconstitute them I put them in water and then put them into the microwave for 4 minutes to get the water boiling. Then let them cool. If some of them are still hard to cut I repeat the process on the ones that are still not soft. Then I cook with them like I would with fresh mushrooms.They are easy to use in many different ways. They taste great sauteed in butter. I like adding them to stews or as ingredient for any sauce I make for cooking chicken. I also found they go great with any Indian sauce, like Pataks: Pataks Vindaloo Curry Paste 10 OzMushrooms, what do they taste like:* OYSTER - mild, slightly nutty* PORCINI - sweet, nutty flavor reminds me of hazelnut* CHANTERELLES - sweet mushrooms with flavors that make me think of corn* BLACK TRYMPETS - smokey flavor* CREMENI - more flavorful than button mushrooms, but not as strong as shiitake or portobellos* ENOKI - very delicate flavor, slightly crunchy if fried* PORTOBELLOS - meaty flavor* SHIITAKES - rich, almost beefy flavorJR Mushrooms offer great quality at reasonable price. I recommend them!Ali Julia review

You'll really have to taste it yourself.Hotness: mild or roughly like TABASCO brand Pepper Sauce - Original Red 12 oz.Saltyness: none!  It's just pepper.Absorption: v.high, v.finely ground; unable to observe any small flecks after cooking into my standard spice test: Top Ramen Variety Pack 48ct (24-3oz Beef-24-3oz Chicken)It has a very clean smooth taste, almost like adding pure "hotness" to food without the smoky overtone of Tobasco, the roughness of black pepper, or the cumin of chili sauces. column9: Best litterbox I have used hands down.
column10: I have owned 3 of these with 4 different large (up to 16 lbs) cats and a variety of litter types.  I would like to echo Esther G.'s review - this box is amazing if used "correctly"!!I'll try and explain another way for the sake of repetition.This system comes with 2 bottoms: at any time one bottom contains the litter (let's call this the "active box") and the other is empty (the "standby box").  The boxes fit inside of eachother so the standby is stored below the active box.  In fact, the lid won't seal properly unless the boxes and sifter are all stacked together in a nice package.There are two major ways to use the system - the NASTY WAY and the AWESOME WAY:********NASTY WAY (most people do this):Most everyone leaves the sifter inside the active box so that the litter itself is sitting inside the sifter.  The sifter, in turn, sits inside the active box.  From top to bottom we have:SIFTER (contains litter)ACTIVESTANDBYWhen it's time to change the litter, people simply pull the sifter out and dump the contents into the trash.  The sifter then goes into the standby box and the (cleaned) litter is dumped from one box to the other.  What was previously the active box is now the standby box and everything gets re-stacked like before.This is the most obvious way and I think the product literature even suggests this.  However, there is a small gap between the sifter and active box which leaves room for liquid to gather below (and around) the sifter.  Clumping litter will clump *around* the holes in the sifter and create clogs.  This also allows for some small clumps to gather on the inside walls of the box - these get smeared over time.  After a week or two, you're left with a messy, stinky box and a sifter that needs lots of attention.****************AWESOME WAY (everyone should do this):You can eliminate the clumping inside the sifter if you don't leave the sifter sitting in the litter!!You can order the boxes like this:ACTIVE (contains litter)SIFTERSTANDBYWhen it's time to clean, you simply pull the active box out and pour its contents (including clumped waste) into the sifter (which is sitting inside the standby box).  Next, you pull the sifter out like you would have done for the NASTY WAY.  The sifter now contains all the waste but, since it hasn't been sitting in the waste, doesn't have any clumps or clogs!!  Throw away the waste, put the sifter into the empty box, and stack everything up.  Voila!  You're done.********I have 2 cats sharing 1 of these boxes.  I can completely clean the box in less than 1 minute using this method.  This allows me to clean the box every day without trouble.  I change out the litter once every few weeks, rub down the insides every few months and do a deep clean maybe twice a year.That's seriously low maintenance and I have the cleanest box of anyone I know!! That includes those with fancy auto-cleaning systems!

column9: a must have for owners of many cats
column10: I love this litter box.  It lets me finish my most dreaded chore (cleaning six litter boxes for four cats) in only a few minutes.  And since the chore now has less dread associated with it, I'm likely to do it more often (like I'm supposed to), which makes it easier still (and makes for happier kitties!).  I dread cleaning every litter box other than these, so I'm in the process of replacing all of our litter boxes with this type.My only major complaint is that I can't find it (or something like it) in an extra large size, and one of our cats really needs an extra large litter box (he sometimes misses when he uses the smaller boxes).Is it something you should buy?  I don't know.  Please read the other (less positive) reviews.  The complaints that others have are real.  My wife has similar complaints, and doesn't really like these boxes.  But it's my job to clean the kitty litter, so this is my review.  ;-)  I've dealt with a couple of mechanical self-cleaning litter boxes in the past, and keeping them clean was far more of a hassle than this litter box.One reviewer mentioned that "tipping it over even a large trash receptacle is awkward and messy."  I have a different approach: once the litter has been sifted, I place the tray (with the waste) into the empty pan, and place the entire thing into the mouth of a large garbage bag before pouring it out.  There's no mess at all with this strategy.The slots in the sifting pan *do* get clogged if your cat pees a lot.  I solve this by banging the tray and empty pan against the wall or floor a couple of times (while inside the garbage bag), and it always gets out the wet litter.  It also helps if you put a thin layer of baking soda on the bottom after most cleanings (before adding back the litter).  Since the large clumps wet litter is less likely break up while sifting with this tray than when sifting with a scoop, the litter also stays cleaner for longer.A minor complaint: the swinging door is flimsy and was both too stiff (so the cats tended to avoid that box) and it kept falling off, so I just pulled it off.I haven't used the "Omega Paw Self Cleaning Litter Box" (probably linked under "What Do Customers Ultimately Buy After Viewing This Item?"). column9: Works great if you use it right
column10: I'm buying a second of these boxes, as we've added another cat to our family.  My 11-year-old son is in charge of keeping the boxes clean, and this box makes it easy for him.  As other reviewers have said, the clumps do tend to get stuck in the sifter, and it can be messy to dispose of the waste.  However, after some experimentation, we have found the solution to both problems.  First, store the sifter in the empty pan, and NOT in the pan with the litter (when stacked, the sifter should always be in the center of the stack).  When it is time to clean the box (preferably not when there are fresh clumps, as they will break if you don't give them a little time to harden), dump all the soiled litter into the second pan with the sifter in it (if any clumps are stuck to the bottom, it is easy to knock them off).  Then, lift the sifter to remove all the waste.  Slip the whole sifter directly into a cheap 10-gallon wastebasket liner, and dump the waste into the bag.  Finally, remove the sifter from the bag, put it into the newly empty pan, and place under the pan that now contains the litter.  The whole process takes my son about two minutes, and he has no problems.  He's used the scooping method before, and much prefers this box.

This method prevents the sifter from getting clogged and it also saves you money on clumping litter. It works flawlessly! I've cleaned it every morning since I bought it and it only takes me 1 minute and I don't even have to use the scooper.I recommend this product to anyone with a cat or kitten. It's very reasonably priced, it's good quality material, and it's super easy to maintain. Even the filters are only $1 and are changed every 3 months

ANY BODY WHO IS THINKING ABOUT BUYING THIS BOX SHOULD READ THE FOLLOWING POSTED ON 1/4/2011 BY BOBAROO, IT SAYS IT ALL, HANDS DOWN!5.0 out of 5 stars Best litterbox I have used hands down., January 4, 2011By bobaroo - See all my reviewsThis review is from: Van Ness CP66 Enclosed Sifting Cat Pan/Litter Box, Large (Misc.)I have owned 3 of these with 4 different large (up to 16 lbs) cats and a variety of litter types. I would like to echo Esther G.'s review - this box is amazing if used "correctly"!!I'll try and explain another way for the sake of repetition.This system comes with 2 bottoms: at any time one bottom contains the litter (let's call this the "active box") and the other is empty (the "standby box"). The boxes fit inside of eachother so the standby is stored below the active box. In fact, the lid won't seal properly unless the boxes and sifter are all stacked together in a nice package.There are two major ways to use the system - the NASTY WAY and the AWESOME WAY:********NASTY WAY (most people do this):Most everyone leaves the sifter inside the active box so that the litter itself is sitting inside the sifter. The sifter, in turn, sits inside the active box. From top to bottom we have:SIFTER (contains litter)ACTIVESTANDBYWhen it's time to change the litter, people simply pull the sifter out and dump the contents into the trash. The sifter then goes into the standby box and the (cleaned) litter is dumped from one box to the other. What was previously the active box is now the standby box and everything gets re-stacked like before.This is the most obvious way and I think the product literature even suggests this. However, there is a small gap between the sifter and active box which leaves room for liquid to gather below (and around) the sifter. Clumping litter will clump *around* the holes in the sifter and create clogs. This also allows for some small clumps to gather on the inside walls of the box - these get smeared over time. After a week or two, you're left with a messy, stinky box and a sifter that needs lots of attention.****************AWESOME WAY (everyone should do this):You can eliminate the clumping inside the sifter if you don't leave the sifter sitting in the litter!!You can order the boxes like this:ACTIVE (contains litter)SIFTERSTANDBYWhen it's time to clean, you simply pull the active box out and pour its contents (including clumped waste) into the sifter (which is sitting inside the standby box). Next, you pull the sifter out like you would have done for the NASTY WAY. The sifter now contains all the waste but, since it hasn't been sitting in the waste, doesn't have any clumps or clogs!! Throw away the waste, put the sifter into the empty box, and stack everything up. Voila! You're done.********I have 2 cats sharing 1 of these boxes. I can completely clean the box in less than 1 minute using this method. This allows me to clean the box every day without trouble. I change out the litter once every few weeks, rub down the insides every few months and do a deep clean maybe twice a year.That's seriously low maintenance and I have the cleanest box of anyone I know!! That includes those with fancy auto-cleaning systems!

I followed the advice of another Amazon user by using the litter pan without the sift sitting in the active litter tray. That way, the holes on the sift won't get gummed up with litter and urine. When you're ready to clean, pour that active tray into the sift and let the "clean" litter fall into the 2nd pan.It's brilliant!! column9: Sifter doesn't work with wet clumps, takes MORE time to use.
column10: I like the concept this box is going for, but it isn't effective. The sifter does a great job with poop clumps but wet clumps just stay stuck. Even with vigorous shaking sometimes the holes stayed plugged with wet, clumped litter. And if you have a large, wet clump stuck to the side, forget about easy removal! You still need a scoop to make this box work. I stopped using the sifter pretty quick and eventually just tossed it. I do LOVE having two bottom halves. Every three months or so I clean out the box and let it soak in a bleach/water mix for a few hours. Then I pop the clean half on the bottom and swap out when needed. It makes keeps the box clean and sanitary much easier not having to wash it right away and worry about an accident in-between. If you are a 1 box household like me that feature may be helpful but not for the listed price. I bought this box in a store for about $20. It has held up really well and is about 3 years old. The clasps are in great shape and the handle is still sturdy. I can fasten the lid and carry a fully loaded box outside for easy clean up without worrying about anything breaking. I don't use the swing panel door though, my cat never could get used to it. Overall this has been a good litter box and is very sturdy, but don't but it thinking the sifter will be of any help. If anything it took me MORE time to clean the box out than scooping by hand. I do love having the 2nd bottom half and it has held up amazingly, hence the 3 stars.

So far, I like it. I keep the sifting pan in the box that doesn't have litter in it. Then I pour the whole mess into the sifting pan and unused box. Lift, and pour the clumps into my Litter Locker. Easier than scooping, in my opinion.Unfortunately, my wheat litter sticks to the side of the box I just emptied, forcing me to get that cement loose. However, I recently read that spraying non-stick cooking spray inside the box before adding litter helps prevent clumps from sticking to the side of the box.My only concern is that it's only available in the one size. At least that I've found. And it's a bit small for my 17 pound (mostly muscle, but is a bit over-weight) cat. I would purchase a larger size if it became available, or easier to find on Amazon.

column9: Does the job well, but needs regular maintenance
column10: We use this box with two cats...one a large tabby (18lbs). What the others note about the clumping litter getting stuck in the sifter is true... urine clumps can get stuck. However, with a little bit of banging against the edge of the garbage can, most of the clumps come loose. The key to using this pan is regular maintenance. Be sure you do your sifting at least once a day, and before reassembling the unit, make sure to rinse and sanitize the spare pan. I've found that I need to hose down and sanitize the black sifter pan and the lid one a week. This keeps the odors down and the pans in good shape. Now, I say all this as somebody who HATES litter pans and for years would not touch them (made my husband do it). With this new set, I've found it takes a few minutes each day and about 10 minutes on the weekend to maintain. No problem at all.I do find that the latches on the lid aren't that great... before lifting the unit, be sure the latches are secure. As cats use the pan, they do come loose. Also, the sifter allows some of the smaller clumps to get through. When you sift, you might consider using a scoop or smaller strainer to lift out those smaller clumps out of the "clean" litter. If you leave them, the odor will get fairly strong.I also suggest that when you reassemble the unit, sprinkle some baking soda in the bottom of the spare pan, and on the bottom of the sifter itself before re-filling the sifted litter. This will help with clumping issues as well as odor.We've tried many different cat pans, and this one seems to be the best so far. Yes, it involves some work... but if you do it regularly, the effort is minimal, and most of it can be done during a commercial break of a TV show.

column9: Great to have on hand: they keep for ever and are very tasty!

Then let them cool. If some of them are still hard to cut I repeat the process on the ones that are still not soft. Then I cook with them like I would with fresh mushrooms.They are easy to use in many different ways. They taste great sauteed in butter. I like adding them to stews or as ingredient for any sauce I make for cooking chicken. I also found they go great with any Indian sauce, like Pataks: Pataks Vindaloo Curry Paste 10 OzMushrooms, what do they taste like:* OYSTER - mild, slightly nutty* PORCINI - sweet, nutty flavor reminds me of hazelnut* CHANTERELLES - sweet mushrooms with flavors that make me think of corn* BLACK TRYMPETS - smokey flavor* CREMENI - more flavorful than button mushrooms, but not as strong as shiitake or portobellos* ENOKI - very delicate flavor, slightly crunchy if fried* PORTOBELLOS - meaty flavor* SHIITAKES - rich, almost beefy flavorJR Mushrooms offer great quality at reasonable price. I recommend them!Ali Julia review

column9: A saving grace for Green Mountain Coffee...
column10: When we received our Keurig Elite for Christmas, we were so excited to break open the sample pack of pods to try out different blends and flavors. Of the 12 pods we had in the box, four were Green Mountain Coffee brand. I'd never tried anything from this company before, but from what I had researched online, they have the largest range of Keurig pods and have even bought out competitors to produce coffee under their brand names as well.Unfortunately, I was immediately disappointed by the quality of the coffee. We tried their Dark Magic, Decaf and Breakfast Blend and all were underwhelming, to say the least. I was almost completely set on writing off Green Mountain altogther.We had one GM pod left and being of the mindset of waste-not-want-not, I figured I'd give it one last go around before forgetting about them completely. And I'm glad I did.The Nantucket Blend is a perfectly pleasing cup of coffee. It is nice and flavorful without being thick and pungent (unlike some of the other GM blends we tried). I added some flavored creamer to it and it almost measures up to our go-to Caribou Blend pods. Almost. All in all, this is a very standard cup of coffee which, while it isn't anything new or exciting, is very pleasing and definitely one of the better Keurig options we've been able to test out. When we run out of all the pods we've accumulated, I'll probably pick up a box of these as well.Now that I know Green Mountain isn't completely disappointing I'll definitely be open to trying a few more of their coffees (with our promotion for getting the bewer we ordered Green Mountain Coffee Golden French Toast,  K-Cup Portion Pack for Keurig K-Cup Brewers, 24-Count to try as well) and see how it goes from there.If you're looking for a go-to choice, this is your cup!

I just like the flavor of bacon.I'd recommend this soup to anyone who likes corn, chowder, and a rich tasty soup.

column9: Frontier Soups Hearty Meals Illinoise Prairie Corn Chowder
column10: My family loves this soup.  It is so quick and easy to prepare.  It tastes like I cooked it all day, but of course I did not.  I just added a few ingredients listed on the package.  I even added a few more ingredients I thought might be good.  The first time I purchased it, I found it at a local craft show and wanted more so where did I look for it, on Amazon of course?
