I shipped a case of this stuff to the girlfriend when she was sick and stuck at home. She thought it was really good. She wasn't able to taste much of anything else but she said she was able to taste this and thought it was really good,  I don't know if it means that this was really salty or what....
Um.... These are. $1-$1.89 per pouch in stores, or $7-8 per 6 pack. Where do you off selling a 6 pack for $24.99???
Great gift basket except most everything in it was the same - different size packets of Irish creme coffees - needed more variety

column9: Not like anything I've ever had before
column10: I truly expected these to be thin & crispy cookies, I suppose this was due to the use of cocoa in the product & description.  I could not have been more wrong!The texture reminds me of a club cracker or puffed cereal of some sort, light and airy but crunchy at the same time.  They are not at all flat & thin like Wheat Thins.  They are also not very big - I'm adding a photo to the product photos above so you can see them in perspective with my hand.I did NOT find the taste to be chocolate-y, at least not at first.  Rather it begins tasting like a rice & sesame blend.  The finishing flavor is that of chocolate for sure, but it is not a sweet chocolate taste - definitely more subtle - all about the cocoa itself instead of sugary.  I'm not sure where the sea salt comes in, I don't really pick up on any saltiness.There are 130 calories in 46 pieces - that's a lot of pieces without breaking my snack calorie count (I try to keep it at 150 calories for a between-meals snack).  Plus with the levels of calcium (10%DV), Vit.E (4%DV), Iron (4%DV), and Fiber (2g, 8%DV), I find this to be a better option than crackers.This is not a super-sweet snack, but it does satisfy my love of chocolate in a surprising way.  I definitely enjoyed these after getting used to the subtle flavors.

column9: Subtle cocoa goodness - but not to everyone's taste
column10: I'm guessing that the "Eat.Think.Smile" name is a tie in to the trend toward "slow foods" in cooking and "mindful eating" in dieting.  As in, do not grab the bag of cheetos and just start gobbling.These crackers do fit that bill, but taste is subjective.  I had to hold back from the gobbling, being a fan of subtle cocoa-y flavors (such as in chili or mole) and mildly salty snacks. My picky middle kid also liked these:  "Weird, but good!"  But the rest of the family ranged from "Huh?" to "Please never give me this again!"  Forever the optimist, I may yet try to introduce these as toppings for a fruity salad or ice cream or something.Health digression:  much is made on the packaging here of the benefits of whole grains (brown rice, oats, sesame seed) and the antioxidant power of cocoa.  I'm with food author Michael Pollen here - "superfood" claims are marketing, pure and simple, and processed "super" snacks can't begin to compare - healthwise - to fresh, unprocessed foods.  Still, these crisps beat the heck out of most packaged snacks, and I'd gladly recommend them for toddlers over the usual cheerios, except for one timely caution:  at this writing, recent news reports have raised alarms over the (trace) arsenic levels in brown rice products - flour, syrup, etc. - with an emphasis on the concern over brown rice syrup in infant formulas.  This, as the rice plant has a natural affinity for arsenic and takes up that dangerous metal along with the chemically similar silica that rice requires for growth.  (White rice, which is simply hulled brown, retains less - but some - of this trace metal.)  Arsenic based pesticides - used for decades - can persist in the soil even where long discontinued, so experts addressing the arsenic-in-rice issue have recommended looking for organic brown rices.It doesn't look to me like Apure Foods (maker of Eat.Think.Smile) sources organic rice, or other organic ingredients, for that matter.  I'm pretty sure they'd tout it on their packaging and website, were that so. But really, if ordinary rice is a normal part of your diet, there's no point in getting worked up over a more occasional snack source.But why, oh why are these crackers called "thins"?  They are small and "puffed out", much like the kitty treats in our household.  (Note to self: Do not mix up.)  They are also MINE.  I guess if you like these, you really do.

I am not a nutritionist so I can not evaluate or judge beyond very general knowledge the claims made on the pouch about the natural antioxidant power of cocoa. Therefore, my review is purely about the product itself.I find this to be a surprisingly interesting and different snack. The pieces are roughly triangular and the longest side is about 1" long, so these are fairly small. According to the package, the serving size is 46 pieces which come in at 130 calories. Of these, 45 are fat calories. The pieces are crispy-crunchy but "airy", almost like toasted cereal but again - surprisingly satisfying (and quite filling!).I do not taste much of the cocoa, and the snack is also not overly sweet, which is probably why the manufacturer suggests such varied use such as in salads, with wine, or as a treat all by itself. I find the balance between sweet and salty quite well done. The ingredient I can taste the most is the sesame seed but it is not overbearing, just adds a nice hearty something to the snack experience.For those of you who are interested in the nutritional information, here goes:Total Fat 5 gSaturated Fat 1 gTrans Fat 0 gCholesterol 0 mgSodium 135 mgTotal Carbs 19 gDietary Fiber 2 gSugars 6 gProtein 3 gVitamins: No A and C, Vitamin E 4 %; Calcium 10 %, Iron 4 %, Magnesium 8 %Ingredients (listed already in the product description but...):Brown rice flour; sun flower seed butter (sunflower seeds, sugar, salt, mono and diglycerides, natural mixed tocopherols, to preserve freshness); dried cane syrup; rice flour, cocoa, sesame seeds; whole oat flour; whole grain yellow corn flower; wheat flour; sea salt; calcium carbonate; monoglycerides; natural flavor (milk).I actually did not expect this to be very good and stand corrected. I like it quite a bit and will buy again.

These snacks are basically a triangular puffed grain mixed with cocoa, then covered with sesame seeds and sea salt.  The chocolate sea salt mix sounded intriguing, so I decided to give these a try.  The taste is definitely unusual.  I ate the first few and thought they were unusual and tasty.  After the first few, however, I got sick of these really quickly.  There's just too much chocolate in these snacks for my taste.  They're sweet, but not in a good way.  I could eat a few of these (about three), but beyond that I just couldn't handle any more.  Interesting idea, for sure, but they weren't very good in the execution.

column9: I really like the IDEA of these, I just didn't really enjoy them
column10: I like the idea of making more foods with chocolate - I like chocolate and cocoa has some healthy properties. I also like salty foods. I'm always looking for healthy snack choices and these have whole grain oats and whole brown rice, as well as sesame seeds.As a result, I was excited to try these "crispy thins." They have a chocolate taste, and are crunchy, but aren't very salty though that is probably a good thing as a lot of people are trying to limit their sodium.  I couldn't distinguish the taste of the sesame seeds in them and found that when I poured them out of the bag the crisps had a lot less sesame seeds on the surface than the ones in the photograph on the bag.Because I received several bags I shared some with a guest visiting me and asked her impression. She thought they had a bit of a burnt taste to them.As the title of my review indicates, these aren't something that I would be interested in buying for myself or to serve to guests. However, I encourage people to give them a try and see for themselves - there wasn't anything that I found objectionable about the flavor.One interesting thing about them is that both I and my guest initially mis-read the package as "FAT. THINK. Smile." When it actually reads "EAT. THINK. Smile."  To me that's an indication that the seller should change the font on the package - or maybe just an odd coincidence.

From the name of this product: "Crispy Thins, Savory Sea Salt", I thought these would be thin crackers, with a savory (not sweet) taste. Not. At. All.  They are not thin, they are puffy little nuggets.  They are not crackers (i.e. that one could put cheese on), they are more like a bite-sized cereal.  AND they are sweet like a cereal... not savory at all.  I taste no sea salt- which is too bad because I like a salty-sweet.  They're like... triangular Cocoa Krispies with a few sesame seeds.  WAY too sweet, like a kids' cereal.They are tasty, I'll give you that.  In moderation because they are sickeningly sweet after more than a few.  But a handful can be a nice chocolate fix.  Sometimes.Bottom Line: Tasty, but badly mis-named.  Not a savory cracker; more of sweet cereal-like snack.  Oh, and if you read the label you can see that while they do have some good healthy ingredients (brown rice flour, sesame seeds), they are still a processed snack, NOT a health food.

These are quite different than what I expected. I've kept a bag at home in the pantry, and a bag at work in my desk drawer. Whether I like them at any given moment "depends".Each piece is a triangle, roughly the size of a dime. They're a bit puffed, and contain chocolate. Some of the pieces contain enough chocolate to provide a creamy consistency. Surprisingly, a serving is 46 pieces, which ends up being a really good fulfilling snack. From a nutritional perspective, it's better than what I thought, but not stellar. A serving is only 130 calories, with a 45 of those from fat -- 5g of fat, 1g of saturated fat. While it provides 2g of fiber, sugar is 6g. Sodium comes in at 135g -- but these don't necessarily taste salty; in fact, the "sea salt" is quite subtle and works well with the chocolate.They are made with cocoa, whole grain oats, sesame seeds (as a topping), and brown rice. The only way to describe them is "cereal-like". I tend to grab these, while at work, as a mid-morning snack. They are easy to count-out and track calorie-wise.At home, though, I never reach for them, even on days when I'm home. Maybe it's because I have other options available, but they don't "call to me" -- they aren't something I crave. Therefore, given all the choices out there, this isn't something I'm likely to pick-up againSomething great to try, but not compelling enough to buy again.

column9: Like dog food, but not in a bad way
column10: On first bite, I thought these tasted like Rice Chex. But everyone else who's tried them has said, "Hm, they taste like dog food. But not in a bad way."They're light, cocoa-y but not sweet, with just a hint of salt. They feel like they keep me going until my next regularly scheduled meal without causing sugar or sodium shock, and they feel relatively wholesome -- not, like, kale or sprouted almond wholesome, but wholesome for an easy snack.Overall, they're not blow-your-mind delicious or anything, but they're pleasant, and way more appealing than doritos or oreos. If you like (or don't mind) rice and sesame, and don't need or want something with a plethora of artificial flavors, then these are a nice choice.

I was excited about these, I like "salty" style snacks, and I thought the combination of cocoa and sea salt would be interesting.Out of the packet, first impression is breakfast cereal, in size and shape, not unlike one of the many chocolate square styles around. These are small, don't expect nice big chip size pieces.Taste was eclectic, first crunchy, nutty, and sesame come through strongly, similar to a Japanese rice cracker. Slowly, and with subsequent bites, you get a chocolate cocoa secondary taste. It may sound weird but there's a sort of chocolate "oil" taste, that's not unpleasant, but gives a cocoa taste linger.Overall I wasn't impressed, yes they're pretty low on the calorie counter, but that's the point isn't it? - if we are eating this stuff as it's better for us than potato chips or chocolate, the least it can do is taste really good.Too many flavors going on for my choice, and too much with the sesame seed coating, without that these might have tasted more like a chocolate snack, and less like muddled mix of flavors.

column9: An interesting combination of flavors unlike anything I've ever tried
column10: I tried the Eat, Think, Smile crispy thins, and it was an interesting journey for my taste buds. I was expecting a primarily cocoa/chocolate taste from these thins, but the cocoa flavor was subtle and mixed with rice and sunflower seeds (cocoa is only the fifth ingredient behind brown rice flour, sunflower seed butter, cane syrup and rice flour).  I even tasted sesame seeds and yellow corn in these chips, and that is alot of different flavors for one snack crisp.  The product is all natural and relatively low in sugar (only 6 grams per serving).  I don't mind some combination of tastes (chocolate and peanut butter are great combinations) but cocoa, sesame, sunflower seeds, yellow corn and brown rice?  This product uses quality ingredients, but the wide variety of tastes mixed into one crispy thin was too odd for me. Then again, taste is subjective, so someone else may appreciate the wide variety of flavors in one crispy thin. Just know what you are getting yourself into before you buy.

column9: Very tasty morsels but they are not a health snack in my opinion
column10: I really like the flavor of these Savory Sea Salt Crispy Thins.  They definitely have a strong cocoa taste to them. These thins are more like morsels and look like large-size triangular-shaped hard cat food.Each bag is 6 ounces. There are 6 one-ounce servings per bag at 130 calories (45 from fat) per serving.  The first three ingredients are brown rice flour, sunflower seed butter, and sugar which in my opinion makes them closer to dessert than healthy eating. Despite this I really enjoy the instense cocoa flavor with a hint of salt.  I find it very hard to stop eating them.

column9: Tiny bites with lots of chocolate flavor
column10: Not quite 5 stars as I agree with other reviewer, they're a lot like a cereal.  I think would be great with milk, but as just a snack, they're too much hassle to eat one after another.They have a strong sesame flavor.  I'm a fan of sesame seeds, but something about mixing them with cocoa just doesn't feel right for this American meat & potatoes stomach.

These reasonably healthy snacks got a thumbs up from my husband and four-year-old. I found them, well, different, in terms of snack food. Slightly sweet, but not overly so, with a hint of salt and sesame. These reminded me most of snacking on dry breakfast cereal. The chips/thins themselves are also about the same size as Frosted Flakes-size cereal bites. Not bad, but not exactly what I was expecting, based on the product photos and advertising. I was thinking they would be thinner, based on description, and more chip-like. (Maybe something in the rice cracker family? These are much denser than that.I can see how they'd be tasty on salads as a crouton replacement, though I haven't tried them that way yet, but can't see myself eating them out of hand all that often; though my son asked for more. These are just a little too dry and bland for my tastes and the sweetness, which lingers long after you eat them, kind of threw me off ... And this is from someone who regularly eats organic blue corn flax seed chips, not Lays or Doritos. (Just to give you an idea of where I'm coming from, taste-wise.)Though you're kidding yourself if you think these are health food, they are definitely a better option than regular chips at 130 calories for a good-sized serving, with only 45 of those calories coming from fat, though the sodium content is pretty high (135 mg/serving).Honestly, I was done after less than half a full serving (which the bag defines as about 46 chips), so these could be a fairly low-cal snack option, IF they fit your flavor profile. Though the marketing boast buzz is all about cocoa and its antioxidant properties, cocoa is at least halfway down the ingredient list, well behind two kinds of rice flour, which is mainly what you're eating here. (Brown rice flour is ingredient number one, followed by sunflower seed butter and I think regular rice flour is No. 3 or 4 on the list.)All in all, just so-so for me, and I don't think I'd go out and buy them again for myself, though they are far from terrible, and I will use the remainder on salads. But, given the flavor profile, if you're someone who likes to snack on dry cereal, you'll probably enjoy them BUT just buying the cereal will likely be a more cost effective, and likely calorie equivalent, option.

My friend bought a bag at the Hershey Chocolate Factory last month and we haven't been able to find them anywhere! I asked the company when Amazon would carry them and they said in June!!! Yes!!!  These yummy little crisps are the perfect snack. You have to eat few of them before you "get it". The cocoa taste IS there-I'm not sure how anyone could miss it. They are not a super sweet candy type snack. My friend and I both agree they are yummy and I am so happy that Amazon is now carrying them.

These snacks were just okay, nothing special. I wish they had been organic or at least, non GMO. This was like combining chocolate with a crunchy, salty snack. Normally I love that, bt this was pretty bland. I will go back to dark chocolate and hummus or lentil chips when I want a snack or salad topping.

column9: Never one to shy away from trying something new... :)
column10: Eat. Think. Smile. Crispy Thins, Savory Sea SaltNever one to shy away from trying something new, if a snack product boasts of being all natural and antioxidant -- on the front of the package --, it usually ends up in my shopping cart, especially of late, 'cuz that's the way I roll. :)Eat. Think. Smile. Crispy Thins, Savory Sea Salt was an especially nice surprise, as I found it to be crispy, crunchy, not messy, with an extraordinarily satisfying cocoa/light sea salt taste -- that did not leave me feeling bloated/over stuffed, if ya know what I mean.  The extra thick zip-lock like re sealable bag really came in handy, as I was tempted to eat more than one of the 6 portions contained in the bag.  It is that good!  :)You might also like to try, as I did, Eat. Think. Smile. Crispy Thins, Sweet Cinnamon.  I can't make up my mind which variety I enjoy more...  Highly Recommended!  --Katharena Eiermann, 2012

column9: Is it illegal to taste this good?
column10: Eat. Think. Smile. has me wrapped around their finger. After trying the dark cherry chocolate bars and the berry nut ones, I tried out their take on what are essentially chips. I have to say, these are the best thing by the company that I've had so far. If you like chocolate at all, then you'd be doing yourself a huge favor by ordering some of these. Each bite is better than the last, and I actually got disappointed each time I was finished with a bag, knowing that I'd reached the end.Not only are these Crispy Thins not very bad for you, they're the perfect snack time food. Each bag is a decent size, and if you happen to go through a whole bag in one sitting, it isn't going to make you feel horrible. Low in calories and fat, it's absurd how low in calories and fat these are. The sea salt flavor is very faint, which is a 50/50 thing for me. On one hand, I love salt, but on the other, it's a health-thing and it's good that they didn't go overboard in this category. These snacks would be perfect packed in paper bag lunches or thrown into a bowl on the counter for all to enjoy. Even better? Throwing a bag of these into a bowl and adding milk, making for a cereal that'll blow your mind. Trust me.I'm not this enthusiastic about many foods, but these babies came out of nowhere and caught me by surprise. The only problem? The price is a bit high for how much you're getting. If you get as hooked as I did, one bag isn't going to last very long, unless you're a calorie counter. I don't eat much at all, but this is the kind of thing I can go nuts with and not feel guilty. Get a bag and see how it fares with you.

column9: Try them first before you commit to buying six bags!
column10: These lightly salted, dark cocoa tidbits are the kind of snack that you're likely to eat by the handful -- IF you like them.  I like the flavor combination (I've eaten sea salt dark chocolate bars, and the flavor is similar); these have just enough salt to bring out the not-too-sweet chocolate flavor and a hint of sesame.  My husband, though, sampled a handful and wasn't impressed.  He didn't like the size (he would have preferred a chip or cracker size), and he found the flavor bland.  If you, like me, enjoy dark chocolate -- that is, cocoa flavor without a lot of sweetness -- you have a decent chance of liking these.The description suggested eating these with wine, and, since I know dark chocolate goes with red wine, I sampled some of them that way.  While the cocoa brought out the taste of the wine a bit, I'd rather have cheese or fruit with my wine.  Yeah, it was interesting to sample, but it wasn't good enough for me to plan on bringing the crisps out the next time I open a bottle.I don't know why the manufacturer calls these "thins" because they are basically little puffed, crunchy triangles -- about the size of Wheat Chex. I found the mouth-feel odd as well:  they turn kinda gummy and fudgy when you start to chew them.  I found it disconcerting that something crunchy would end up stuck to my teeth.  At least I like the flavor!The package says that these crisps contain a lot of antioxidants.  If I want a boost of antioxidants, I'll eat a square of dark chocolate or a no-calorie mug of green tea.  But these are good for more filling snacking.  The bag uses a serving size of 46 pieces for 130 Calories -- that's a little less than 1/2 cup.  The only notable nutrients in a serving are 3g of protein and 10% of the RDA for calcium.  A serving also contains 6g of sugar.These come in resealable bags, six servings per bag.  While the thins are probably more healthy than potato chips, don't confuse them with health food.  They are sweet snacks that, if you like the flavor, can become addictive.-- Debbie Lee Wesselmann

column9: Surprising! Chocolate undertones, but sunflower flavor and crunch predominate.
column10: A great crunch!  It took me a moment to identify the predominant taste as sunflower seeds. The cocoa gives a rich undertone, but without the sweetness, the taste is not what I would usually describe as chocolatey.  I need to pour a half-cup or so out of the bag and put it away; otherwise, I eat too many of these!  They really are nice with red wine.  I haven't tried them on a salad yet, but that sounds like a good idea!

all I can taste is the dry cocoa powder. Really disappointing. Are you familiar with the Hershey's Cocoa powder you buy in the can for baking? Well if you have some, open the can and smell it. That's what these taste like. I don't know what you would use these for. I thought about maybe in a dry pie crust like the cookie crusts but the after taste is bitter so I wouldn't use it that way either. This item, to me anyway, is a bust...

column9: Wow, Surprisingly Tasty, Rich and Satisfying
column10: When I tried Eat Think Smile I had that very reaction. I ate it and thought, "wow, that's very different tasting, what is that?" I quickly realized that it is different in a good way. Tthe dominant flavor was unusual to me because it seemed nutty (but there are no nuts listed) but what I was really tasting was the sunflower seed butter and sesame seeds, which in my opinion are "nutty" tasting even though not nuts. Combined with the light taste of cocoa and a little salt, its a very unique combination that did make me smile! The suggested serving size is the right size and satisfying in my opinion; its very rich tasting to me and does have 5 grams of fat per serving (although there is no cholesterol) so its best not to exceed the serving size or exceed it by much. Its crunchy and a couple handfuls is a nice snack that satsfies a sweet tooth (6 grams of sugar) for only 130 calories. And it does seem reasonably nutritious, consisting of a lightly sweetened mix of whole grains and seeds with some cocoa. The texture is kind of like cereal, but what seems different to me is the sunflower seed butter and the whole sesame seeds give it a different taste and texture than cereal I have tried. This may sound strange (because there are no nuts and the grains appear to have been ground together and shaped into airy little pillows) but it reminds me tastewise of snacking on pieces of a Nature Valley peanut butter granola bar and probably falls into the same category of snack food for me.

I got a couple of bags of these snacks at a 5K expo, and thought, since they were free, I'd give them a try. I'm now addicted. They're the perfect snack: lightly salted, slightly chocolaty, and, my favorite part, sesame seeds. Unfortunately, they don't sell them anywhere near me. Fortunately, Amazon does.
I don't like the taste and I love sea salt products. This stuff is light on sea salt and heavy on the chocolate.  That suits my husband. Weird looking too.

I was surprised at the taste of chocolate and sea salt in this crispy treat.  I was also thrilled with the portion size that allowed me to munch it like popcorn while watching a movie.  It is a total win where I am concerned.  It has the antioxidant properties of chocolate along with the benefits of of mineral rich sea salt.  This is a terrific snack that is healthy as well.

I didn't expect much of this item, but decided to try anyways. I was extremely surprise with how awesome this product is.Good:- Has a tasty combination of salty and sweet- Crunchy and fun to nosh on- Provides a feeling of a filling (though I don't think there is one really)- 46 pieces for only 130 calories- Tested on 7 different people and everyone LOVED it and couldn't stop eatingBad:- Leaves a black residue on your fingers- 16.6% fat- Once you pop, you can't stopBottom line: buy, but split to 46 pieces Ziploc bags to avoid eating the whole thing :)

column9: A HUGE hit at our house!
column10: As a working mom healthy snacks are important in my house. I don't always have time for cooking full on healthy meals - which often translates to my daughter eating less-than-ideal foods in a pinch. I am the low fat, low sodium, healthy food option person -- and my teen is the whatever-I-can-find-to-sate-my-hunger option. Sometimes that is an issue.These are like a cross between a cereal (that you can eat as a snack) and a cracker. They have a good flavor and are pretty robust for being so little. They are kind of rich (probably the cocoa) so, for us, it was hard to eat more than a small toddler type bowl full which is great as that's the serving size. The crackers stayed crisp in the bag and really just have a very nice flavor. They are very good with coffee and tea as well.They are easy to take with you as the bag is not heavy and fits in (well in my anyway) purse. These will be a purchase for us when our supply runs out!

column9: Strangest snack you will ever LOVE!
column10: Our palates are very "American" & salt and chocolate just never mixed on anything we enjoyed--until now!These aren't like chips at all...kind of like Golden Yangles for those of you who remember them...only chocolaty instead of cheesy. There is NOT a lot of sodium in them (great!) But there isn't a lot of anything else either. They are good to satisfy your mouth's need to crunch and taste without being too bad for you.This company is my new faviorite snack company and I plan to work my way through their oeuvre. You should too!I have to be honest and they smell a bit like paste, but they sure don't taste like it! (Not that I've had it since preschool...)

column9: Chocolaty Crunchy Triangle Puffs. Not Too Salty, Not Too Sweet. A Decent Alternative to Satisfy the Afternoon Snack Cravings.
column10: Like others, I was expecting a crisp, flat salty cocoa cracker covered with sesame seeds.  What is in the bag looks more like Chex Mix Puppy Chow without the powder sugar coating.  But, while Puppy Chow is very sweet & not chock full of "healthy" ingredients, Eat Think Smile Savory Sea Salt bites are chocolaty (some bites seem to have a soft chocolate middle), not overly sweet and contain healthier ingredients.The Savory Sea Salt flavor is a confusing flavor description.  The bites are predominately chocolate flavored.  There is a bit of sweet flavor & a touch of salt flavor and a bit of sesame seed on top of some of the bites, the overall flavor is not what I would define as "savory".So, what to do with these bites?  I would use them as a snack alternative to chocolate.  I think they work best as snack to satisfy a sweet tooth, but they could also be used as part of an h'orderve tray, or to slightly crush & put on ice cream.  I would not use them as croutons, but I am not enough of a chocolate fan to want chocolate on my salad.If you are in a "healthier" mode, but realistic enough to know that you aren't going to completely give up on crunchy snacks, these bites are worth trying.  They have a not so ordinary taste that it is difficult to describe, but it is a taste that will likely grow on you with each bite.  They are worth a shot.

How to describe it - it is like cocoa puffs with more oat and in square shapes. And of course the ingredient list seems to suggest better nurition and healthier dosage of fiber. My 4-year old likes it very much. He could eat a handful at each sitting.The rest of us used it as a great substitude of cereal.

Eat, Think, Smile Crispy Thins are small little crisps with a taste that would best be enjoyed by adults. It's a combination of sesame and chocolate taste, and it's not really sweet at all. It's the kind of thing to savor while eating slowly. It's not a chip. It's not a cookie. But it is somewhat like both.If you are in for a new kind of snack that is more subtle than anything else, give these a try.

I saw the Just Add Juice advertised and wanted to give it a try.  BBQ sauce is so loaded with sugar that our family can no longer eat it due to dietary restrictions.  This is a wonderful alternative.  We found a lower sugar apple juice and used that in conjunction with the packet, following the instructions.  Our first attempt we marinaded for only about 30 minutes.  It had a very light flavor.  The second attempt we marinaded for around 5-6 hours and it was just right.  We have also tried the tequilla-lime flavor which is outstanding.  I'd give this one 4 stars and the tequilla-lime 5 stars.  I'd definately buy this product again.

I have been buying Emerald Deluxe Mixed Nuts for quite a while now and have never encountered a bad or a stale nut. I buy the 10 oz size because it's just right to pour into a bowl when company comes. If they aren't all eaten, just pour back into the container and they'll stay fresh for quite a while. I love Emerald's mixture of walnuts, almonds, cashews, pecans--AND NO PEANUTS! Peanuts are legumes, not true nuts, and don't belong in a cocktail nut mixture. To me, they overwhelm the taste of "real" nuts. Sure, these cost a little more, but aren't you worth it? I know I am!

column9: My New Favorite Nut Mix - Mystery Nut is the Marcona Almond
column10: I LOVE this Deluxe Nut Mix!  I happened to make the purchase because I had a $1.00 coupon.  Better than Planters and - yaaay!  No peanuts! As others have mentioned, I did notice the "mystery" nut - yummy and not hard like the roasted almonds in other mixes.  Since there was a review which expressed concern that it was an apricot kernal, I called Diamond Foods today. The mystery nut is a Marcona Almond. (If you google Marcona almond, you'll see pics as well). Donna in Consumer Relations told me they used to just have the marconas, but they are a more expensive gourmet nut so now they have two types of almonds. She also noted that they receive lots of calls regarding the "mystery" nut.I did suggest that given that so many consumers have noticed it and it seems to really make this type of impression, perhaps they should specifically list it in the ingredients or just note it in the description on the label somewhere.So no apricot kernals. :)
Excellent service - 1 week before Christmas and ON TIME! Best mixed nuts - bar NONE.

I had been buying these from the grocery store when they went on sale, but Amazon has them at my price all the time. All four cans arrived exactly as expected. The nuts are delicious and fresh, as I have grown accustomed to. Really guys, these are GOOD. My consistent snack go-to.

I buy a lot of nuts, but I only repurchase those that are fresh & flavorful.  Emerald Nuts Deluxe Mixed nuts are fabulous.  A fresh, crisp, lightly salted flavorful bite every time.  I also liked that this came in four 10 ounce containers allowing you to maintain their freshness to the last bite.  I signed up for the subscribe & save in order for them to just keep on coming.

This was an outstanding price when I bought it. It's gone up $2 but is still cheaper with subscribe and save than buying the same product at the grocery store or even THE big box discount store. (Shipping will drastically change that equation, so ymmv if you aren't a prime member or subscribe and save buyer.)The product. Great mixed nuts without peanuts. They include walnuts, which are the best nut source of Omega-3 fatty acids, and brazil nuts, which are a top source of selenium. The 4-pack split up into plastic snack bags makes a heart healthy snack for every day of the month. My problem? They're too good, so I open the containers and finish all 4 in about a week and a half.This is one of the deals that makes Amazon worth visiting.
the price was cheap, and it was high quality product. Great nuts, im satisfied. i would recommend this ,and would be buying it again soon.

I strongly recommend this product... The perfect mixture of nuts with a perfect touch of salt in them... I have only 2 left... Every body says I'll just have one or two... That's a lie... I need mooooooooore!!!!

I love these nuts. I have been eating the Cocoa ones. Tried these for the first time this week. I found all five nuts, cashews, almonds, walnuts, pecans, & brazil nuts. But there also is another nut in the mixture not listed. Looks like a macadamia nut. But doesn't seem to taste like one. So we really have six nuts in our canisters.  LOL  Great not have the peanuts.

Anyone who'd order quadruplet cannisters of Emerald Mixed Nuts must really like them. I just received my first order of the four cannister set from Amazon, and in cashew you were wondering, I love these things. An almost empty container of Emerald Mixed nuts sits before me for inspiration. Inside is a delightful mix of cashews, almonds,walnuts,  pecans and brazil nuts. I especially like that cashews and almonds dominate the mix and that there is nary a peanut to be found. Yes, they're salted, but not overly so, and oily fingers don't go hand in hand with the Emerald mix as they do with other brands.Nuts are healthy in moderation so I eat a handful or so a day. This mix is so good, that self control isn't always easy. As for price, I'm certainly satisfied. Around these parts the Emerald selections go for $6.50 a container in most stores, and I'm getting them for half that from Amazon with free shipping and a scheduled shipment every four months.The Emerald Mixed Nuts are great tasting treats with a long shelf life.

column9: 2 packs of 4?  or two individual canisters?
column10: I just received two individual canisters of Emerald Deluxe Mixed Nuts.  I thought I was buying two packs of 4!!!!  I would never order nuts at this price if it meant only a total of 20 ounces.The order shipped from Sam's Club, yet I ordered it through Amazon.What is going on???

This mix is wonderful. I do not snack. I just consume for the health properties that the nuts generally offer. So I eat just a little but everyday. I like the composition of the mix and they taste absolutely fresh too. There are no peanuts so does not feel cheap. I would perhaps have been happier with a little more walnuts. I think the nuts are also priced just right too although Amazon raised the price lately.
Emerald always puts out quality nuts, far superior to Planters imo. The price is on par with other brands, but the quality exceeds them.5 stars.

We love mixed nuts and are always open to trying a different brand. The Emerald mixed nuts looked good on line--good selection, good price. Well, we found them to be unimpressive--not tasty, very small size, and generally a flop. We would rather pay more for a different brand and have nuts that are delicious.
They come in a pack of four. There are four of us in our family. I sat one container beside each of lounge chairs. They lasted about 5 days. Mmmmmm I am ordering more... lol

I purchased these as a healthy choice.  I'm concerned about the last ingredient "natural flavoring." I don't need natural flavoring on my nuts.  I wouldn't have purchased them if I had known this prior to making the purchase.  Initially I was thinking that these were the most delicous nuts on earth now I know why, they are altered by something they call natural.  There's no phone number on the container?  but there is an email address.  I will update this after I hear from them.
... because to me, all of these nuts had the same flavor and nearly the same texture.  The local grocer was happy to issue me a store credit...

If there is such a thing, I am a connisseur of mixed nuts, and no doubt these are the best Deluxe Mixed nut assortment I have found both for quality and value.  But they can be purchased at excellent prices in the Supermarket - Until recently, I was paying $2.99 for the 10oz container at Market Basket - they just raised it to $3.49.  But to pay over $6 here plus shipping is absurd ! !

column4: John Paul R. Jones "Star, Saeco,Fitz Grips"
column9: Bought for sprouting but they refused to sprout
column10: The Amaranth we wanted to sprout then dry the sprouts, grind to flour, add them to our sprouted wheat flour, to add extra protein to our sprouted whole wheat bread.  We tried and tried but they refused to sprout.  We have three kinds of sprouting methods. And wanted the burst of extra nutrition that grains gain from being sprouted. The the third kind of three seed shown and ordered K???? sprouted fine and tastes good.The Amaranth would probably be best cooked for breakfast.The supplier was fine and gave us a refund to our Amazon card.

I used to make fun of my ex for liking Folgers, but now it has become one of my favorite coffees.However, I haven't tried the regular Folgers yet only this ground Special Roast, and the whole bean Special Roast, I must admit that I like both.However, for the difference in price between this and the whole bean, this ground to me is the best deal.This is so funny because for years I refused to drink Folgers, I was a real coffee snob and would buy exotic green beans to roast.I would also buy 100% Jamaican Blue Mountain, 100% Kona, etc., and even though I have seven different exotic coffees right now, I find myself reaching for Folgers more than any other coffee I have.

Personally, I don't care if my escargot are in shells or some fancy dish so these are perfect for me.  Keep in mind that if you put a stick of butter, garlic and salt on a brick it would taste good too.

I love these escargot.  Nice, juicy, large size...just right for escargot with butter/garlic sauce...as well as nice for a favorite escargot and mushroom soup.  The smaller size is OK, but these larger ones are nice to bite into and give you a flavorable taste.  The price is great.  I buy only this product if I want escargot.

My husband bought these snails from Amazon.  I thought they were very tender and tasty.  He thought same, except they are "too big".  We served on escargots plates from Williams-Sonoma rather than in the shell.  I would order these again, although my husband would probably look for smaller ones.  They work well in a pinch when you are not in France (ha)....
I was very happy with the quality, price, and speed of delivery!!!! Will buy again next Christmas.
Great product.  My favorite snails.  My local supermarkets do not normally have this brand in stock, so I was happy to find this source.
For canned escargot this is awfully tasty. About half the price of the ones that have the empty shells enclosed in a plastic tube. Good price here at Amazon and a very good product.

column9: I would rate a 5 Star if......
column10: RE: Reese Maurice canned snails: I would rate a 5 Star "if" they put a easily translatable code ("Expiration date" )  on the can or a table  the marketing sites. I am looking at a12078 and below it 28 1dzh l2413302  {??} Anybody speak shortmouth code and know what this means?  Thanks~
Exactly what I need mid afternoon. This is the best tasting of the low carb sugar free energy drinks out there.
With the subscription program I have these delivered once a month.  I can rock until they drop... them at my door.

I love Rockstar energy drink.  Even though it has hardly any calories, it does not taste like it is artificially sweetened.  It gives me a nice afternoon pick-me-up and I love the fruity taste.  The drink is augmented with ginseng, guarana, B vitamins, and other good stuff.  While it's probably not the healthiest drink on the market, I love the taste.  I'm one of those people who can't drink water and need to find other sources for hydration especially since I live in Florida where it's very hot.  Rockstar and Blackberry Ice are my drinks of choice.

column9: Doesn't taste like toothpaste or cough syrup. All right.
column10: By the grace of God, unlike Monster or almost any energy drink (including those horrifyingly disgusting and extraordinarily expensive shots of caffeine which carry the not-so-happy side-effect of making you get hot flashes and flush like it's a freaking rash on your face), this actually tastes palatable. Alas, this week when I purchased a new case of what is advertised as Rockstar Juiced Guava with 50% juice, I discovered that the product has been reformulated to be only 10% juice.  They have reduced the juice, but added sugar and sodium and increased the calories.  The result is a terrible-tasting beverage that is NOT what is described on their web site.  This is a classic case of bait and switch.  Rockstar is trying to increase profits by selling a watered down, awful-tasting drink.  What a slap in the face to their customers.  It reminds me of the New Coke disaster a few years back.  At least Coca Cola admitted their mistake and went back to their classic formula.  Will Rockstar be that smart?  I'm not optimistic, but until and unless they do, I will not purchase any more of their products.

Great coffee at a decent price. Cheaper than my local grocery and it comes to my door....without dents!............what more can ya ask for... Thanks Amazon!!

column9: Outstanding coffee with the smoothest of flavor
column10: After having experienced the varied, horrible dark...and even darker roasts of coffee that are now widely popular because of Starbucks, I thought I had somehow lost my taste for coffee over the years. Literally, many of the iced coffees at Starbucks taste what I imagine dirty sink water would taste like with all the fermentation and settling. In a nutshell, it seemed like every cup I experienced was more and more bitter with headache-inducing, cringe-worthy bite upon each sip-----the kind of bite that no amount of cream or sweetener can undo.Well, lo' and behold, my grandmother had spoken of how great coffee/chicory blends taste.  Having never experienced chicory or a coffee/chicory blend for that matter, I dismissed  the suggestion as yet another bizarre coffee variation a la the many flavored roasts that are so popular these days. While at my local grocery store, I decided to take the plunge and venture away from the Folger's, Dunkin' Donuts, and Starbucks varieties. Upon the first taste of this coffee, I was hooked.  It is as smooth as can be with no bitterness whatsoever. It is as if someone took the smoothness of hot cocoa and infused it with the best elements of coffee flavor.  Taken black or with milk and sweetener, the flavor handily beats any of the overpriced competitors. And, in all of this, you will find no sharpness, bitterness or ripe bluntness that is so evident in many of today's "scorched" roasts.Please try this if you yearn for good coffee.  This product will reacquaint you with what your taste buds have been missing for so long.  Luzianne makes an excellent iced tea, and this product is proof that they can do equally as well with coffee.Try it!!:)  You won't regret it.

I have been drinking chickory coffee for years and this is some really good coffee at a good price. The real bargain is that you only have to use half the amount that you would normally use to make a full pot and still have the full strength. Glad I bought it.

The chickory removes all the "bite" from the coffee.  The result is you can make a strong, robust cup of coffee rich in flavor without any bitterness.  Great stuff.  My local grocery stopped carrying this product years ago.  I was glad to find it on Amazon.
the coffee got here within 7 days, and I* have been enjoying it since, I would not hesitate to order from these folks again

My local supermarket no longer carries Luzianne coffee. I am glad to purchase it from Amazon. Very convenient shipping.  This is the only canned coffee that has flavor. It stays fresh and flavorful to the end.  I use this coffee to make boiled coffee on my electric stove.  I combine cold filtered water and coffee together(6 oz. water per cup to one measure of coffee) into a pot. I use an old stove-top percolator without the inside strainer assembly. Bring to a boil. When the coffee boils take the pot off the burner and turn off the heat. This is to prevent the coffee from boiling over the pot onto the stovetop. Put pot back on the burner and let simmer slowly for at least 3 minutes. An electric burner stays hot even after it is turned off and that's how you "simmer" a pot of coffee. The coffee can simmer for 5 minutes for a stronger brew. Take coffee off the stove. It is ready to serve but I strain it first to get out the coffee grounds. Old-time recipes call for an egg shell to be added to hold back the coffee grounds but I omit the egg shell. You can then pour the brewed coffee into a carafe or put it back into a cleaned out pot and leave it on the stove on a warm setting.  Boiling for a short time really brings out the flavor. Great for camping too.Hope Amazon will continue to sell this brand of coffee.
I love the coffee, light full taste, goes a long way, chicory has health benefits for you so it is not just coffee. Great taste, fullness and lovely flavor.Thank you

These potato chips rock.  I've been looking for a low-fat real potato baked chip for a long time and I finally found it.  What's even better, it tastes like a real potato chip.  Not those other baked chips that taste like a salted piece of dried plastic potato mush.  Love these chips.

Well, baked potato chips have finally gone mainstream after years of being some obscure brand in the store that you bring home and just try to eat while they crumble in your hand and taste bland while they're doing it.Now some of the big national snack companies have "baked" chips, but why are they shaped like hexagons? These are great chips, relatively low in fat and calories. A great snack when you have the craving for something slightly salty.Glad they have these on Amazon. Can't find this inexpensively anywhere else, when you can find them at all.

These Kettle Bakes potato chips are incredibly good.  They have a more intense potato taste, and they are not too salty like a lot of other baked chips.  If you open the bag, heaven help you because you are probably going to eat the whole thing.  Luckily, the bags only contain 4 oz.

(For example, any product with sucralose/Splenda in it makes me extremely ill!)However, with Kettle's chips, consumers can easily identify all of the ingredients in the package, and in the baked chips, you can essentially eat an entire bag for about the same amount of fat you'll find in a single serving of most other brands of chips. Even better, the BBQ flavor is really great in these chips, ensuring that your snack is really satisfying and truly filling your cravings. I love the fact that more salty snack options are appearing on the market, and I hope that Kettle continues its trend of producing simple, healthy, and absolutely tasty products. I guarantee that chip lovers will not be disappointed by this yummy offering...

column9: Weird after-taste for me (try one bag before you buy a box)
column10: I bought a box of these baked barbeque Kettle brand chips from Amazon in somewhat larger-sized bags, because they came so highly recommended by other reviewers, but I really don't care for them at all (though other people to whom I've offered them  munch through them quite happily, and are pleased to take the rest of the bag home with them when I make the offer). column4: R. W. Taylor "Wil O' The Wisp"
column10: I hope that one day this snack can reach the point where it is truly healthy and consistently good.A) Claiming to be healthy, at least - last bag I munched on had nutrition info that would in one serving give you the bare minimum healthy cholesterol score (<300) for an entire DAY. Many snacks do this. Like peanuts. Or popcorn. The idea is that since the products are from 'natural' sources, there is less control over the batch. But seriously - less than 300mg per serving? Give me a break. This gives no one trying to help themselves in this area any hope of control. It's almost like writing a blank check. To yourself. To state that your product's single serving falls less than the daily total max recommended is garbage. Read the label.B) The batches may be uneven in cholesterol, and they may avoid legal issues by setting it at the 'max'. But the uneven textures and flavors you may get (I consumed, along with family and friends, several cases of these over 2 years or so) don't add up, either. I had burnt tones, teeth-cracking textures at times.I used to love these chips, much as the majority of the reviews portray. I thought I was enjoying at the least a fair product, staying healthy, keeping the fat away. But - they are simply simple carbs with a little twist of fat that get you by in the place of their higher-fat brethren. In case you are not sure of where I stand, I am one of those people who think carb-laden chips are not a great food. You don't miss health until you lose it. These chips will not help your health. They might, at best, make it slightly less worse than everyday chips - at twice or more the price.A leading non-profit consumer org concluded this was 'junk health food'. They cited other causes, as well. I wholeheartedly concur that this is not a healthy food. It is a junk food that is masquerading as one.ADDENDUM:Just got around to adding this. My wife purchased a bag of the "Hickory Honey BBQ" at the beginning of July. They were real dental-rattlers, uneven but thick-cut and baked into seriously hard material. column9: Tea is so good that the annoying packaging is worth it
column10: Pros:1. Black tea with peppermint flavor (not herbal tea)2. I assume it's caffeinated (though it doesn't actually say so on the packaging as far as I can tell).3. Great price in bulk on Amazon.Cons:1. Packaging is annoying -- Each tea bag is individually wrapped and there is a perforated line indicating where to tear open each package. Unless you are very careful it is easy to tear off the top of the tea bag. This happens to me about 1/3 of the time and is mildly annoying.

This is a good peppermint tea.  The peppermint does not overwhelm the taste of the tea.  It is a black tea with peppermint, not an herbal tea.  There is no spearmint added as some "peppermint" teas are flavored with.  I drink this tea all day long.  Since another tea company stopped making their peppermint flavored black tea years ago, I have been searching for another peppermint tea and I have been disappointed with every one I tried until this one.

The tea is delicious.  The packaging is totally obnoxious.  First, each tea bag comes in a sealed packet with a perforated line across the top where you tear off the top to free the bag.  It doesn't always tear on the perforation and often causes the top of the tea bag to be torn off.  Then the teabag string is wound under the tea and exits at the top of the bag only slightly, so that if you threw it in the hot water, you'd have the little paper tag in your tea.  On four occasions, in trying to gently tug the string through, the tea bag ripped, spilling tea leaves all over my kitchen. Tired of microwave popcorn that is all greasy and chewey?  Jiffy Pop makes it easier to make stovetop popcorn.  No pans to clean, no need to keep oil around.  All you need is a stove!  People are always talking about how hard this stuff is to cook, but if you are able to carefully follow the instructions, you will get it perfect.  Remember, it's the same prinicpal as cooking a steak.  If you have the heat too high, you sear it and the inside is raw.  What you have to do is keep the heat on medium, and keep shaking to move the unpopped kernals to the bottom.  When the popping slows, pull it off and enjoy!

When I was a little girl my mom would get this for us.  My Uncle was the only one with the skill to sit over the burner  and cook this popcorn without scorching it!  I purchased a case for his birthday, as kind of a joke (because I knew how much he loved popcorn and always said Jiffy Pop was the best.)  Well, he LOVED it!  He said it is exactly the same as it was twenty years ago.  When microwave popcorn became the norm,  Jiffy Pop seemed to disappear from the grocery stores, but since my Uncle loved popcorn so much he would just make what was available.  After making the Jiffy Pop for the first time after having microwave popcorn for all these years, he declared it the best.  So much tastier than the nuked kind!!  I am so glad I am able to find it for him!!
What a flash back.  It is amazing how many people have never seen this before.  Well worth buying, especially for a conversation piece.  Great tasting popcorn!

Was anything more of a childhood treat than Jiffy Pop? Watching that tinfoil mushroom covering rise up, and knowing there was hot, fresh popcorn inside was just perfect! La Victoria is at least as hot and the thickness does not change as it is heated.  Excellent flavor.  What I ended up doing is splitting it into freezer-type zip lock bags - roughly 14 oz each - and freezing them flat with no air inside.  They thaw in 10 minutes in the sink.  Then I clip one of the bottom corners off and squeeze out what I need and then fold the corner back up with no air and put a spring-loaded clip on it (a chip clip or binder clip works) and keep it in the fridge while I'm using it.  Opening and closing the zipper is asking for mold issues.I also tried vacuum sealing in glass mason jars and keeping them all in the fridge, but that didn't prevent mold.  The zip-lock bags work great and the flavor and consistency of this cheese is the best!  It is worth the repackaging effort.

If you didn't grow up eating these, you may wonder why anyone would like them.  These fall into the category of "comfort food".  I think for many of us, these were one of the options our fathers cooked for us when we were either in a hurry to go out sportsfishing etc. (breakfast, with a side of eggs), or conversely exhausted after a day hiking the desert or some other such outdoorsy activity.  Indeed, you can pack and eat these cold on the trail.These are not unhealthy whatsoever.  They can't qualify as "Mexican" food really, but on the other hand, I do recall having fresh tamales very much like these, from remote villages and homes in Baja etc. where my father used to fly to go fishing and visiting friends.  So I guess on some level they really could be called authentic....I admire these because they are the kind of thing you can keep in the cupboard and heat up rapidly for a very satisfying meal when you are famished but otherwise don't want to cook or stop somewhere for fast food.  Believe it or not, they go down well when you are home sick with the flu or other ailments.  When I was living an extremely active lifestyle (walking everywhere, martial arts, tennis, racquetball, etc. constantly), these were one of the truly best things to have on hand when I came home late, ravenous and needing a quick and easy meal before bed, or a rapid lunch between engagements, or a breakfast when I knew I wouldn't likely eat anything for the rest of the day.  They have a sort of balanced quality in terms of answering one's hunger without leaving you too full or still hungry, or like you're missing something.  Of course, you can use them as part of a meal with other foods as well (as mentioned above, these are really great with eggs for breakfast).They are also awesome for times when you've been drinking or after parties etc.  They won't upset your stomach but will make you feel like you ate a full meal, and you can then crash in bed right after eating them, without any digestive problems.I also used to keep these as a standard in my emergency supplies (I need to re-stock!); again because you can eat them without heating up and they will make you feel satiated without any stomach/digestive issues.  You could also in an emergency take advantage of the liquid in the can for flavoring rice etc. (or well you can do that anytime of course if you want).You can doctor them up in multiple ways.  Cheese is a good option, as are sour cream, and/or lots of freshly diced scallions (or shallots if you have them).  You can cut these into chunks and add to other things, like soup.  I suppose you could even deep fry them (without papers obviously) but I never tried that.  For normal cooking in a pot, keep the wrappers on, all the way until you plate them; then pull off wrappers with tongs.
