This is a delightful beverage.  The mild green tea allows for the full flavor of the honey and orange slices to be experienced.  This last cup of tea is the one I recommend.
Actually a great tasting green tea. I first found it at Jason's Deli, and knew that it must be good then. Its much better than the stuff you find in most grocery stores.

column9: I wouldnt buy it in this large amounts but...
column10: This is really good tea..and unless you drink several cups a day I dont suggest buying this much! It's really a clean taste, not bitter or grassy and is healthy.

This is good tasting tea at a decent price.  My only problem is not really with the tea but probably me, if I drink green tea on an empty stomach, sometimes I turn green myself.  Nausea eventually goes away, just have to remember not to drink it on an empty stomach.

column9: Doesn't taste at all like green tea
column10: Did I get a bad batch?  People here seemed to rate it so highly?  Very bland taste for me.  Strangely enough, whatever aroma is there almost more of chamomile or peppermint than actual tea.  Yes I tried a few different times -- steeping longer, less water, different temperatures.  Does a better job at replicating the color of tea than the flavor.  Don't know what else to say.

I was looking for an organic green tea for the health benefits and natural source of caffeine.  I found this tea at Vitamin Shoppe, although I'm pretty sure I've seen it in most super markets.  This is one of the best tasting green teas I've ever had.  I steeped two bags in about 12 oz of boiled water for 3 minutes.  A little while after drinking the tea, I got really relaxed, almost tired, but my brain felt more alert.
This has got to be the best green tea on the market today.  Excellent flavor and a bargain thru Amazon.com.
A mistake was made in the order, but it was quickly rectified.  So I give you folks a B+ for your delivery.

We were having a terrible time finding a food that our little shihtzu, Sheldon liked and liked him back.  I tried a few of the Castor & Pollux foods and he loved them all!  Plus, there wasn't any adjustment time with his system.  Within 2 days he was eating it completely without any digestion problems.  I have found that to be true with finding pets the food that agrees with them...if it does, it does quickly and if it doesn't, it never will.  At least that has been my experience.  This one and the turkey vegetable flavor are a firmer consistency that make it easier for me to cut up and for him to eat.  I tried Wellness and Natural Balance as well as Nature's Variety Instinct and Blue Buffalo and none of those agreed with him and even a small amount (a tablespoon) added to his regular food made his stool soft.  Not so with these foods.  I have talked with Debra Guenther at Castor & Pollux too and the company has excellent customer service.  This is a keeper in his rotation.
Both my chihuahua love this...they are so excited every morning when its breakfast time...This is a great product, and the price is great too :)

column9: Very picky dog likes it and so does the cat!
column10: Our dog is very picky when it comes to dog food. I have bought cases in the past that she wouldn't even touch. So glad that she liked this brand and that I have it on subscription. The cat even tried to snake it from the dog! Will check to see if they make cat food.LOL.
Best Instant Coffee. These are great when served hot or as iced Latte.But I find much better prices for this product on eBay.

Never had a problem with this seller. I love this coffee. I don't have time to wait for a coffee pot or for a barista to make my coffee.this little package was the perfect fix. Try it you will like it..its a little strong for instant coffee.

I love Krinos Taramosalata and we buy it often. So when I saw it at Whole Foods I grabbed a jar. Later, eating it on some French bread something seemed horribly wrong. I looked at the jar and it turned out to be this awful "Lite" version. Tastes nothing like the real thing. Tastes like nothing at all, and there is an unpleasant aftertaste.

This is a very excellent mildly-fiery addition to just about anything. Sprinkle it over traditional Japanese fare such as udon, omurice, or okonomiyaki - or on such treats as hamburgers, salmon steaks, or BLTs! It gives a wee 'kick' to just about anything savoury, and in the econo-pack available from amazon you can have a bottle about as ubiquitously as in any Japanese diner.

I love Arizona iced tea, especially this flavor, which offers the perfect combination of lemony sweetness.This review is specific to the product, not the price, but this product usually retails for three to four dollars at my local store so the price is reasonable . . . one would just need to decide if the shipping costs made it worthwhile.

I'm just finishing up my first three boxes of these and ordered three more. (I had to order directly from Melitta because for some reason these folks won't ship to Hawai'i. This little snub took away one star.)Personally I think the bamboo filters impart less of a taste to the coffee than the wood-based paper, especially the brown paper. I haven't had any trouble with my filters coming apart or grounds spilling over the top.

At first I hesitated buying these because of the negative reviews.  However, supporting a sustainable fiber product motivated me to at least give it a try.  I was very impressed and you will be too!The filters are solid and I have not noticed any filters breaking.  I have even tried to damage these and make coffee and surprisingly I found they withstood the damage better than regular paper filters!  As for the taste I find that there is a small improvement in taste, but that might also be caused by the special Melitta style of filter (small pips throughout the filter that increase the filter surface area).When it comes to a name brand like Melitta's, you really cannot go wrong.  I am very happy with these filters and I am certain you will be happy as well!

column9: Looks, feels, and works as well or better than the paper ones.
column10: I initially purchased these bamboo filters while trying to order in quantity for my office. Amazon was out of stock on the regular paper filters, so I crossed my fingers, and tried these instead.  I was immediately impressed by their performance, and received not a single complaint from the dozen or so fussy coffee-drinkers in our little club.  I have since purchased two more of the six-packs for the coffeemaker here at the office.  We easily brew 6 pots a day in our Krups dual-carafe machine, and have never had a problem.They work just like the "real" thing, and are made of sustainable fibers.  These *are* the filters you are looking for.

I bought these thinking that using bamboo was a great idea as it's highly renewable.  But these filters do not do a good job at keeping the grounds in the filter, which obviously is all important.  I tried using these four separate times and each time the filter leaked at the seam.  And it wasn't just the seam splitting.  They actually deteriorated at the seam's edges.  The combination of bamboo and paper pulp does not seem to be able to withstand the flow of hot water.  I use a pour-over method when making coffee, and I never have a problem with paper filters, so I'm confident that it's not what I'm doing.  It's the composition of the filters.  Maybe I got a bum batch, but maybe not.  I won't be using the 76 filters that I have left.  It's back to all paper for me.
these coffee filters are very good. and they are 100% sustainable made with 60% bamboo makes an excellent cup of coffee buy it you'll love it.

On my second box. No problems. They filter as hoped. I also use them to filter my red wines (no, even my most discriminating wine-loving friends do not know that my wine has been filtered) and they work great for that also.

column9: What can you say about coffee filters?
column10: I bought this product due to its eco friendly paper.  Big time coffee drinker so I could be a big source of deforestation if I don't watch it.  It does the job it is intended to do.  Have to say I noticed some crumpling at top edges that I need to smooth before brewing.  A few times coffee has leaked over the sides of the filter resulting in grounds getting in the pour and leaking.  Making sure the paper is open all the way and smooth around the top edges has taken care of the problem.  Can recommend bamboo based paper vs white chemically treated paper!

This is a pretty nice mole.  In comparison to restaurant moles, it will work.  We don't know how to make mole, and we live in a remote location so having this makes us happy.  I disagree with the other reviewer about taste.  It has a lovely, rich taste that adds a lot of flavor to enchiladas.
The color is right.  It's wet and the texture is rich.  Utterly devoid of taste.  Adds nothing to any dish except moisture.

column4: William D. Bailey "Friend of the Great Khan"
column9: Super seasoning for plenty of different foods.
column10: Don't be fooled by the simple packaging of this mixed spice. This is not a simple flavor.If you like the steaks served at a certain "Australian" styled steak house you may well like this seasoning. A friend of mine introduced it to me at a little cook out, where he rubbed a generous amount on some new york strip cuts and grilled, and I fell in love. He then told me that this was the above mentioned steak house's secret seasoning for it's steaks, him claiming to know this by having worked their for a time. I know he had worked at just about every chain restaurant at some point, but that's about all I can confirm in regards to this rumor one way or the other as I've never had a steak there, nor worked at one. Regardless of the truthfullness of that statement, I can firmly attest to fact that this is an excellent mixed spice.I've used it on just about every type of meat except sea food, though I suspect it would be good on that too, with a noteable preformance on eggs. It is mildly spicey and fairly salty, but not overpowering unless you really load up.Reminds me of cajun seasonings in simular packaging, but is not as "hot". I highly recommend a good cut of beef, pan fried in olive oil with a generous amount of Cavender's Greek Seasoning rubbed in.It is also priced very well, and one container is more then enough to last a while. If you for some reason don't love it, you won't be out very much money and if you end up loving it as much as I do, you'll have plenty of it to last you a long time. A seasoning every kitchen should have!

You can create your own secret recipe with this seasoning and make people think you are a true grilling champ.  Wonderful flavor and just the right amount of spice on grilled chicken.  I ordered from the company because I could no longer find this product at my local grocery store.  I was absolutely amazed at how quickly the company shipped my package.  Won't hesitate to order from them again!
Purchased this product to make "Gumbo" for the first time. The flavor I had been looking for was there. Perfect!

This spice blend is very useful in all sorts of situations, not many of them "Greek."  It is easily added to steak, chicken, spaghetti sauce, burgers, etc.  I've used it when I did not have pepper.  I've used it when I did not have garlic (in fact, it has both).  It is never a terribly overpowering blend, which is why it can be used anywhere, and (for some reason) wherever it is used, it seems to yield success.  It's very cheap, so it is advisable to keep it around...it's advisable to keep it around anyway, since it will do you wonders, when you are in a bind.  This is an ideal product.

Very good seasoning blend, but sooooooooooooooooo salty!!! Way over the top salty for my tastes. And the salt free version uses something in place of the salt which seems to make it really bitter. Apparently no happy medium. Make your own greek seasoning, lots of recipes all over the web.

Have been putting this on any beet whether i grill or fry and it is amazing. Took to deer camp last week and put on some fresh deer steaks and wow it was amazing!!!  Even better when you sprinkle a little bit over your salads!
Sprinkle on both sides and fry in high heat w butter...an instant gourmet meal! I tried it on dolphin fish but choose your own

I sprinkle a little on my broccoli after steaming it and my entire family loves it.I've also used it on stir fry, sauteed chicken, and hamburgers.I've talked a lot of people into buying this product and they love it!I'll definitely buy it again.

This is made locally at a near by town, and everyone around here always uses it, so I was surprised to find out that a lot of people have never heard of it. It's a great seasoning for just about everything and can definitely make your barbecue much better.
This a great spice for salads-- especially for one that involves, feta, tomatoes, green peppers and olive oil.  Add a couple tablespoons of this and it's a delicious dip. It adds such great flavor!

column9: No kitchen should be without this.
column10: First of all, to the fraidycats that say this contain a "dangerous neurotoxin"....thatshilarious. Most people are smart enough to do their own research on MSG if they have anyconcerns, and they will find that is a pure myth and all this MSG hysteria is nothing buta manifestation of gastronomic xenophobia. Glutamate is naturally occurring in dozens offoods, the list is long and also includes breast milk. Yes, you heard me.Anyway, I've used Cavenders for years and its my secret weapon for boiled shrimp and alsoLow Country Boils. Its great on steaks and pork, and also perks up any green veggies. Itdoes contain salt so if you're sensitive to that then be judicious with its use.This is the original and its still the best from all the copycats out there from Konrikoand others. You wont regret having a can of this in the pantry. Now I'm off to write areview for Morton's Salt...my header is going to be "Too Salty!" LOL
I can't get the greek flavor to the food because it would be too salty. I combined it with other spices, but what's the sense if you can't use a lot?

column9: BEWARE!  This contains MSG a dangerous neurotoxin!
column10: I bought this product and was very happy with it until I realized that it contains MSG a very dangerous neurotoxin.  Please check this out before using it again, you may want to find something safer.  [...]

column9: Not for the faint of heart!
column10: This is something that my husband LOVES (which is too hot and weird for my taste.) First discovered by him in Indian restaurants, it has been a quest to always have some around the house. We can't buy it locally any more.

I started using this years ago when it was in the condiment section of our health food stores. Having had Indian mixed pickle, lime and mango pickle in India, I was happy to find this in the states. My favorite by far is this Chili Pickle, now called relish. I add it to lots of quick meals for a taste treat. At some point the stores gradually stopped selling it and I assumed others did not share the delight (we have found it in Indian groceries in large city areas).  Anyway, even as my mouth waters in anticipation, I am grateful for the internet for helping me find a way to bring it home.

column9: Addictive, perks up dull dishes, not just for Indian food
column10: Simple ingredients combine for a mouth-watering, spicy condiment that I keep finding more and more excuses to use.This is not just for Indian food. In fact, I don't eat a lot of Indian food. But I find myself putting it on pasta, Mexican dishes, salads, stir fries, fried rice, pizza, anything with tofu, vegetables, omelettes, etc.I'm a vegetarian these days, but I literally salivate remembering what it tasted like on a turkey sub. Luckily for me, this condiment also makes it easier to remain a vegetarian.The ingredients are simple -- Chile Peppers, Canola Oil, Salt, Ginger, Mustard, Fenugreek, Spices, Acetic Acid, Citric Acid -- but the blend is perfect. The heat isn't overbearing and there's no unwanted sugary taste, which ruins so many relishes for me.Everyone's tastes are different, but you should give it a try.I'm so happy I've found Patak's Chile Relish.
This fantastic hot chile relish is comprised of pickled string beans mixed with chiles. If you want to liven up a sandwich then its for you. Be careful though, since a little goes a long way.

We were introduced to Robby's pancake mix by a friend several years ago.  Of all the many prepared and scratch mixes we have tried in the past, Robby's is by far the best we have ever had.  Although when prepared with milk Robby's tastes excellent, it is by far better when prepared with buttermilk! We use the same Robby's mix (prepared with buttermilk, of course) for waffles with the same wonderful taste experience.  You will not be disappointed.

If you love having those famous pancake house pancakes but don't always feel like leaving home early on a weekend morning, this is the answer.  Easy to make and so delicious, there is no comparison to the store  mixes.  All you need is some buttermilk, an egg and cooking oil and you're ready to have the pancake house in your own kitchen. My kids always make sure I'm well stocked on my Robby's.

I just tried this mix for the first time today, as it took awhile for me to remember to buy buttermilk. It's quite tasty, but you can really taste the salt! I made it on my Villaware Belgian wafflemaker on setting 6, using 1/8 cup butter and 1/8 cup oil (recipe calls for 1/4 oil), and it came out dark-brown and crispy on outside and very moist on the inside - just delicious. Using two cups of the mix, I got about 5 waffles.I've also purchased the Carbon's Golden Malted waffle mix, which I've like, but I prefer Robby's because it's so much more flavorful - perhaps I should try buttermilk with the Golden Malted as well. The downside is Robby's calls for 1/4 cup of oil, while Golden Malted requires 2 tbs of butter - so if you're looking for something lower fat, you may want to look at the Golden Malted. By the way, I was surprised to see that the folks who make Carbon's Golden Malted make the Robby's mix as well.Tip: You can freeze buttermilk (just measure the correct amount and put in ziplock bags for the next go-around) to avoid wasting the leftover buttermilk....

These are by far the best pancakes I've ever made at home.  The whole family loves them.  Our weekend tradition is to have these with maple syrup, warm strawberry sauce and whipped cream.  The buttermilk lends a tangy delicious flavor to the pancakes.These are great for snacking from the fridge, too.  They are great without syrup or whipped cream.
The pancakes are light and delicious. Ever since I discovered Robby's pancakes I don't buy anything else.  Amazon offers a great price for the set of 3 or 6 cans.

I love this product. I used to go to the Robby's Pancake Houses in Florida where I grew up as from teen to my adult years and even up to a few years ago when they closed. I'm glad I am able to purchase this and continue to enjoy my favorite pancake.
Our family has tried many pancake mixes and this BY FAR makes the best tasting pancakes.  You hardly need butter and syrup.

column9: Hands down, THE BEST pancake mix on the planet.
column10: This makes the best pancakes in the world - better than my Mom's pancakes from scratch. Seriously, and sorry, Mom. I bought this mix as a stocking stuffer for Christmas from Williams Sonoma (impulse purchase), and I will forever buy these with buttermilk and blueberries. Awesome awesome awesome!

column9: Robby's buttermilk pancakes, breakfast worth waking up to
column10: I have bought several of these pancake mixes to share with my friends after I got to taste them. They all agreed that this is the best pancake they have ever tasted. There were times when this item was  not available due to demand. That shows how convinced the consumers are about the quality of this product.

column4: Mrs. Carol R. Deegan "love to eat"
column10: I first found this product at a small grocery store and thought the ingredients were healthy.  Our family has made wonderful buttermilk pancakes every Sunday since my initial purchase.  Adding buttermilk to the mix increases the buttermilk flavor.  The pancakes are light and fluffy.  No heavy, fat belly after eating.  Have had to search high and low for this product until I found it on Amazon.
I've used this pancake mix for some time and with good reason. When used with buttermilk, these pancakes are the yummiest!

column9: Not what we expected in taste.
column10: When we tried Carbons Malted Pancake and Waffle mix, we were pleasantly surprised. The waffles are great, crisp and tasty just like the reviews stated. We always keep the waffle mix in stock. We tried making pancakes with the waffle mix and didn't like the results.That led us to try Robby's buttermilk pancake mix. What a disappointment. Now it could be us as we are used to Aunt Jemima and those are hard to beat. Robby's was definitely saltier, flat and had a strange taste. They seemed to be oily too, which the 1/4 cup of oil might be the cause I guess. We used real buttermilk but milk can be substituted. On the can, it's not recommended.I wouldn't steer anyone away from giving Robby's a try but I wouldn't order a 3-pack just in case.
This mix is one of the best recipes for pancakes.  Have to try!  Cook it slowly so the texture will be soft and moist.
I have to admit it is a pain having to buy buttermilk but this is a great mix! The pancakes come out light and fluffy and taste amazing. Highly recommended.

column9: Too bad I can't ask Amazon for Tokyo delivery
column10: This makes really very good pancakes.  It is a favorite of my youngest son who currently lives in Tokyo.  Now, I either have to ship it to him, or he takes some home with him when he comes to the US in the summer or for Christmas.  It would be nice if Amazon could ship this to Tokyo for me.One of my daughters  has a very good recipe to make pancakes from scratch but I haven't yet  persuaded her to share it with me.  However in any event it is probably more time consuming and would not beat having the ingredients already mixed except for the egg, oil and buttermilk that one adds to this product.  I try to avoid using low fat buttermilk but nowadays all you often can find is those tasteless low fat or no fat products that serve to increase your appetite.  No wonder we are turning into an obese society.

After trying unsuccessfully to buy commercial mixes from pancake houses whose pancakes were superb, I tracked down the miller of Robby's mix who originally sold only to institutional customers. I bought directly from the miller in bulk until they decided to outsource their direct-buyers to worldpantry.com who now sells Robby's for more $. That's when I started buying from Amazon for less.Be careful not to over-mix the batter. It's better to FOLD the dry ingredients gently into the liquid ingredients rather than mix vigorously -- it's ok to leave small pockets of undissolved solids. Then let it sit for at least 15 minutes to allow the reaction of the ingredients to generate bubbles. Resist breaking the bubbles and dissolving every small pocket of powdery mix. Leave some lumps.This will ensure a light fluffy pancake.Breaking all the bubbles and dissolving all the solids completely, so that the batter is completely smooth like frosting, will cause thin, heavy pancakes.To the 3 out of 16 people who hated the taste, all I can say is that you may have developed a taste for blander, less authentic batters in childhood, which has become your standard. There's nothing wrong with that, any more than those who grew up on Vermont Maid imitation maple syrup who still prefer it to pure 100% maple syrup.But for those who know and appreciate the more complex flavor profile of the real deal (a bit salty, light and fluffy with a buttermilk tang, a bit yeasty), then Robby's will probably exceed your expectations.I noticed that some are reporting good results using the mix for waffles. Years ago, I asked the miller why it's not called "pancake and waffle mix." His answer: "We don't recommend it for waffles. It's a pancake mix."
The absolute best. Has no biscute (bisquick) after taste.  It is made with buttermilk and is wonderful and light.More like desert!

I got this pancake mix in time for Jan 1st brunch. I did like the other reviewers advised and used buttermilk. We made plain, blueberry, and chocolate pancakes. They were tasty, fluffy and just plain YUM. My mom made pancakes from scratch (even sifting the flour) every Sunday morning for as long as I can remember - and Robby's are better!!!

We love this brand!  We use it to make waffles - they turn out slightly crunchy on the outside and fluffy inside.  The flavor is excellent.  We like it so much we are on auto-order refill!!  FYI - fresh buttermilk is needed in order to make them.

very disappointed with this brand and was indeed shocked to see some of the raving reviews turn out to be sooo wrong. Makes me want to believe that reviews are not really written by real people. Where can I start? it is a very dry and bland recipe with no taste, that did not cook right at all. We used to purchase and cook Flappin Jack Pancakes, and it was wonderful. This thing just tasted downright horribly bland. Our first attempt of following directions and using Buttermilk yielded nothing shy of gross pancakes - we tried it with regular milk and butter and that was not much better. I am sad to say that I bought 3 of these and should have never wasted my money. So, if you like fluffy, buttery taste pancakes that melts in your mouth, do not waste money on this piece of junk recipe.

We had Robby's pancakes at the restaurant near St Petersburg, some years ago.  We were disappointed to find out the restaurant had closed, but then we found that the pancake mix was still available, from "Golden Malted".  This is our second order, and the pancakes are almost as good as if we were at Robby's Pancake house.  Of course,there's more work involved.  The order was easy to deal with, and delivered quickly.  What more could we ask?

I was really looking forword trying this batter.All the local store brands ARE OF THE JUST ADD WATER TYPE.READ THE REVIEWS WERE GOOD.the day it arrived tried cutting the receipty in half,the pancakes came out thin and silthery.so next time I tried the full receipty.same result.I like my pancakes to be soft and fluffy.
I thought this sounded like a good mix.I made a batch & it was great.Do your self a favor & buy this you won't be sorry.I eat these every weekend will buy more.

column9: Not the BEST $$ can buy but the best all-over Bittersweet Chocolate in THIS price range: Great for Cooking & Snacking
column10: While it is certainly true that there are other superb Bitterwseet chocolates out there that can outshine Scharffen Berger in a one on one taste test, I have yet to find one that could consistantly deliver this same level of quality at this price point and still achieve all the things we look for in a very, very dark chocolate.  One would have to have access to a dependable Artisanal Chocolatier to find that and even then, I doubt they could came in at even less than twice the price.This is why Sharffen berger is the preferred chocolate of both home and professional bakers at this busy time of year.  We know it will deliver to us a nice evenly noted Bittwersweet taste not too waxy nor overly creamy in texture and that this 70% Cacao bar can be easily incorporated into ganaches, used to melt and then coat dried fruits for Holiday platters, serve as the basis of a decadedent Southern Chocolate layer cake 6 layers high or, be snapped off into the scored triangles and enjoyed by the cook as a not-too-guilty indulgence full of flavinoids and anti-oxidants your store-bought candybar has long abandoned in the name of cheap, artificial vanillas and tropical fats to replace to Coco butter.Some people I tried to tempt with a small serving of the bar, snapped off and offered as the perfect marriage of bitter and sweet just couldn't get over their love of rich Milk Chocolate but if you make sure the bar is warmed to at least 78 to 80 degrees, very gently on a plate, it melts a little eaiser in the mouth as it warms up to body temperature and loses the waxy sensation that people eating it at a colder 65 degrees tend to report.  So if you plan to serve the bar or eat the bar on it's own, respect the coco butter's richeness and the fact that there is less of it in this dark bar.  Give the bar the time and environment it needs to warm up.  I put my oven on 100 degrees, open the door until the interior temp goes down to 80 and then slide the prepared triangles on a serving plate onto the top rack sitting on a cookie rack and leave them there until I can see the chocolate loosen up just a bit.. maybe 10 minutes at best.For cooking, well - you simply can't beat this bar.  it grates well with a microplane, easier if warmed a little, and it incorporates well into nbatters.  it melts well but make sure your recipe actually CALLS FOR a 70% Cacao bar or you may need to add some fat to get the correct texture.  Use a reliable recipe or recipe book author and do a test run if you've never cooked with this before.  I would say to save this deliciously bittersweet chocolate for your company who know a good brand when they taste it and incoprate it into the frosting of a centerpiece cake or use it in one of my favorite recipes, the Wlanut Dark Chocolate Bourbon Pie , also known as the Kentucky Derby Pie or a Christmas Chocolate Bourbon Pecan Pie.  The intesnity of the chocolate matches up well with a good aged Bourbon in a dessert.  In fact a good, rich yellow caked soaked with bourbon, layered with wet walnuts ( or candied Black Walnuts) between and then spread with a Bittersweet Chocolate frosting  is a grandstanding finish to any Holiday party.Viva le Sharffen Berger!  An indulgence we can all afford.  You can find a decent recipefor the aforementioned Derby Pie in Desserts from the Famous Loveless Cafe: Simple Southern Pies, Puddings, Cakes, and Cobblers from Nashville's Landmark Restaurant and find excellent Bittersweet chocolate dessrt recipes that uses this kind of quality chocolate in The Bittersweet World of Chocolate: Sumptuous recipes using fair trade chocolate.  Enjoy the Holidays and any time of the year, really.  The nice thing about 70% Cacao Chocolate bars is that they do not melt quite so easily as Milk Chocolate so they work well in the summer recipes as well.

If your taste runs to dark chocolate without filling, then this is the bar for you.  It has a rich very "cacao" flavour with a nice snap and smooth  mouth feel. There's also  slight notes of fruitiness.This would actually be good for those on a diet. The flavour is so rich, intense and satisfying, that I can only eat a little at a time, whereas I can (and have) easily consume a entire milk chocolate bar in a manner of mere minutes.And, on that note- dark chocolate actually has health benefits!

Today three of us (all of whom believe that we love dark, bittersweet chocolate) taste-tested Sharffen Berger Bittersweet Dark Chocolate against Lindt bittersweet, Ritter Sport Dark Chocolate a la Mousse au Chocolate, Krause's dark chocolate (from a local handmade chocolate shop), and Trader Joe's dark chocolate.  Trader Joe's failed -- it had no vanilla or other flavorings and was hard, almost crunchy, seemingly lacking in sufficient cocoa butter.  The Lindt chocolate was fine-textured, full-flavored, and somewhat creamy.  It contained vanillin, an artificial vanilla flavoring, rather than real vanilla.  The Scharffen Berger was less sweet, but also creamy, smooth, with a nice color and sheen, broke nicely, and was rich and full-flavored, with notes of vanilla (it has the real thing) and citrus.  The Ritter was very creamy and much sweeter and much less complex in flavor.  The Krause's was also quite sweet, full-flavored, smooth, and creamy.All three of us liked the Krause's chocolate best, then the Lindt, then the Scharffen Berger, then the Ritter, and none of us liked the Trader Joe's.  I've always thought I liked chocolate just as bitter as possible without being hard like unsweetened baker's chocolate, but this taste test suggests that Sharffen Berger's was perhaps not sweet enough for us, although it was excellent in texture and had a complex flavor.The Sharffen Berger's claimed to be gluten-free.  Only the Ritter claimed to contact milk products.I plan to repeat this process, adding Godiva and chocolate fromHotel Chocolat.  I'll report back.

This sleek, thin chocolate bar has a strong bouquet and is fairly complex. Most notable are the vivid berry and earthy notes. The chocolate is smooth with just the right amount of sweetness to temper the cacao's bitterness. Only a small quantity is necessary, as this one packs a great punch and lingers long in the mouth. Highly recommended.

column9: who's going to complain about chocolate?
column10: Not me. This wasn't overly strong, for being a 70% bar, frankly I expected more. It was pleasantly fruity-flavored, but that's where it ended. I've had 70% bars that had a much brighter, sharper flavor, and that's what I happen to like in chocolate. This was kind of chalky and dull. Perhaps the 80% is a better option.

After reading all of these positive reviews, I thought the Amazon Gold Box deal on these bars of chocolate would be a winner! Boy, was I wrong!For one as myself, who enjoys dark chocolate taste, one bite into this chocolate and all I could taste was SUGAR. Yes, SUGAR taste with 70%??Looking at the ingredients, and the amount of sugar and fats looks comparable to my other 70% chocolate bars, but the taste is far off.  If I were to guess the percentage, I would guess 50-55%.  This tastes much more like semi-sweet chocolate chips than fine chocolate... and chocolate chips are MUCH cheaper!Don't waste your time with this brand of chocolate.... unless you are used to Hershey's style and want something only slightly higher in quality.

column9: I Love Dark Chocolate and This Chocolate Is Excellent!
column10: This is an excellent chocolate. It isn't too sweet as many are for me.I like the idea of eating the 70% Cacao dark chocolate, which is supposed to be healthy for us, as long as we don't eat too much of it. Speaking of which, you will definitely not need more than a fraction of a bar at one sitting. As a chocolate fanatic, I could eat the whole bar, but I really don't 'require' it with this. A moderate piece works just fine, a little bit like an after-dinner chocolate. You don't have to eat the whole thing at once. After thinking about it, I think I may chop up a little and put it over ice cream. Yum!Moderation in all things, right?

column9: Not too bittter. Not too Sweet.
column10: Scharffen Berger Bittersweet Dark Chocolate Bar, 70% Cacao is one of the better dark chocolates I've tried. It's not too bitter, and not too sweet. My normal preference is "semi-sweet" chocolate containing around 60% Cacao, but I enjoyed the 70% "bittersweet". It was just sweet enough for me. The chocolate is definitely better quality than the average mass market store shelf brands, and I recommend it.

I am, undoubtedly, a lover of dark chocolate, and I am known to try any dark chocolate bar in any variation/concoction I can get my hands on, regardless of the brand, so long as it does not have high fructose corn syrup in its ingredients. Having never tried Scharffen Berger chocolate products before, I was unsure what to expect. I tend to purchase and quickly consume Green & Black's organic brand as my preferred choice, even if it is slightly pricey. To me, dark chocolate is just dark chocolate, and although I will eat any dark chocolate, I still have expectations, and I was certainly pleased with Scharffen Berger's fine dark chocolate. This bar contains 70% and it's labeled as bittersweet, which is exactly what it tastes like, bittersweet. I never mind a bitter taste, but the sweetness to this bar makes the taste perfectly neutral, which was the taste I was looking for after drinking coffee. Needless to say, if you are a lover of dark chocolate and enjoy a touch of sweetness, this bar is perfect for you. This pack of 6 makes a great gift, especially a stocking stuffer now that the holidays are around, for any dark chocolate lover. Lastly, I have to admit that if you buy the pack of 2 (for 9.7 ounces worth of chocolate) versus this pack (18 ounces of chocolate), you might be saving yourself a few dollars for a little more of chocolate, but that's for the merchant to decide. I definitely recommend this chocolate!

To me, balanced usually means boring, and this chocolate could easily have been that. Fortunately, it has a lot going for it. It smells complex. It snaps cleanly, but not in a brittle way. The surface has a matte sheen. It melts to a very smooth and rich texture in the mouth. There is only a moderate amount of chocolate flavor (for a dark chocolate), but it's accentuated by flavors of dark raisin and enough bright notes (floral?) to make it interesting. It's not too sweet with only a hint of bitterness (I could have used more). Wonderful for a mass-produced bar.

This is very yummy dark chocolate that you sure can't confuse with milk chocolate! It is rich and smooth and without excessive bite or bitterness. It is much more satisfying and truly higher quality than Hershey's for instance. It is easy to get just enough to be satisfied - it breaks into chunks that go down good. It's not too bitter, yet not too sweet.I have taste-tested this against the Ghirardelli and Lindt bars of the same cacao content, and the SB bar is better

I love dark chocolate, and the Scharffen Bergen is a yummy treat and a great bar of bittersweet dark chocolate. I have not heard of this USA based company and would highly recommend trying this brand of chocolate. Nice smooth bar that melts in your mouth with a delicious floral flavor and just the right amount of bittersweetness. It's right up there with the more upscale brands and does not have a lot of sugar, junk or additives. They even designed the breaks triangularly, so it's easy to snap off a piece. Overall, a great product at a price of around $2.60 a bar with the $5.00 coupon Amazon is offering as of today.

I received these and the Scherffen Berger Papua New Guinea 68% series. Both are outstanding chocolate bars. This 70% percent bar doesn't quite have the readily apparent complex flavor of the 68% bar, but you can discern slight hints that they are there. The ingredient list between the two bars is identical (although different bean stock is likely used) with slightly more fat in this bar and a bit less sugar. What you would expect though as you get a higher percentage bar.I am a bit of a cheapskate when actually faced with bars on the store shelf and will tend to pick up what is on sale or lower priced. When I ordered these I wasn't expecting to taste a big difference over the lower priced offerings. These bars do taste better then most I have tried though. I won't rate my sense of taste as being refined enough to threaten anyones wine or chocolate tasting job anytime soon, but even I can pick up on the different flavors as I am eating these. They are great tasting and I would recommend.

To say I love chocolate is an understatement.  And oh by the way, did you know 70% cacao dark chocolate is supposed to be good for you so naturally I won't hesitate to eat this chocolate, knowing I'm getting my antioxidants in.  Many dark chocolates with higher cacao content can be less sweet but this one is just right.  You can also use it in baking too, if you can have enough willpower not to eat it on the spot!

Various health benefits have been ascribed to dark chocolate, and I hope they're correct, because there's no more delightful and not-very-fattening treat than a small piece (or maybe two) of this 70% cacao chocolate.  As another reviewer has observed, it's unlikely one would or could eat a whole bar, and even the "serving size" of one-half a bar is, surprisingly, an overstatement of what a typical person's intake, in one sitting, would be. It is said that Julia Child once claimed that Scharffen Berger was "America's finest dark chocolate", and while I'm willing to keep sampling until I taste them all, I wouldn't doubt it.

According to Wiki, Scharffen Berger was an independent chocolate producer in the San Fransisco Bay area that was acquired by the Hershey Company in 2005.  Scharffen Berger continues to produce chocolate under this name, now at a plant in Illinois.  Its products include the Bittersweet Dark Chocolate Bar reviewed here.Scharffen Berger Bittersweet Dark Chocolate is 70% cocoa and is considered "bittersweet", with a much stronger chocolate taste than milk chocolate that most Americans consume.  Though this is definitely a rich dark chocolate, I was actually a bit surprised by how smooth the Scharffen Berger chocolate was; though there is the slightest hint of bitterness, it is less than other 70% chocolate bars I have tried before.  If anything, as person who admires dark chocolate I wish that the Scharffen Berger had a bit more character; it is very good and very smooth but isn't memorable to me like their Scharffen Berger Mocha (Dark Chocolate with Freshly Roasted Coffee) Chocolate Bar (62% Cacao) is.In any event, Scharffen Berger Bittersweet Dark Chocolate is still a fine product that I will enjoy whenever I have the chance to have some.

Scharffen Berger is really good chocolate.  This bittersweet dark has a nice flavor, but is your pure bittersweet chocolate with no aftertaste, no waxy taste.  Not exceptionally flavorful (unfortunately I tried this right after trying the Limited Edition Markham Valley chocolate which knocked my socks off!), but a nice straightforward chocolate.

Scharffen Berger used to be a local (SF) chocolate factory.  Now that they have moved half way across the country, I'm not as enthralled with them.  It seems that freshness is a factor in dark chocolate flavor after all.  (Dark chocolates last at least a year, longer in my experience.) Or perhaps SB is not quite as good as it was before.70% chocolate is the level where dark chocolate becomes truly dark, in my opinion.  Below that percentage, there are some fine chocolates, but not ones that I buy. 72% Guittard dark chocolate is my favorite for chocolates in the 70s.The SB 70% has the crisp snap when you break it.  And it melts nicely in your mouth, if you let it linger. And it has some nice complexities in the after-taste. If you are moving from 55%-65% chocolate to the true dark chocolates, then this is a nice introduction. But I do not recommend buying six bars if you have never tasted it.Go to a brick&mortar sweets store and buy an assortment of bars. If you are lucky enough to have Eastern European grocery stores in your area, try some of the Russian chocolates. Some have honey for sweetener, which I personally don't like, but might be wonderful to you.  Some have brandy, which I do like.  Also Cost Plus has a fabulous selection of chocolates, including a 99%. One tiny square of that goes a long way.As far as pricing goes, I see these bars in our groceries for under $4.00, but only by pennies.  Cost Plus has the best prices, at least around here.  So if you know you like this chocolate and you live somewhere that does not have gourmet chocolate bars, then this is a reasonable deal.One last comment: The bar is scored in large triangles.  Most bars have smaller rectangles, three or four across. I prefer the smaller rectangles because it helps me regulate how much I eat at a time. And one of these triangles is more than my regular portion. What can I say, I'm a unit eater.

Scharffen Berger chocolate is made in Robinson, Illinois on vintage European equipment.  I received 6 bars of bittersweet dark chocolate that measured about 6 inches by 3.5 inches.  Each bar is 220 calories.  They were wrapped in foil then wrapped in a paper wrapper.  The wrapper says that the bar is 70% cacao.  Cacao is everything that comes from the cocoa bean.  Knowing how much cacao there is usually helps you know how concentrated the chocolate taste will be.I compared this bar to many of the other common and not so common chocolate bars made in North America.  This chocolate broke easily and melted in your mouth smoothly.  The taste was excellent.  These bars of chocolate were easily as good or better than the famous big name chocolate bars.  It is very rich even if there are only a few calories in each bar.  The six bars lasted a long time.

I eat a lot of dark chocolate, I have slowly climbed the ladder and gotten to the darker the better, I also prefer organic, and environmentally friendly. While our house hold found this to be tasty it doesn't quite has the cacao taste we have grown to love, I would defiantly try their darker versions.  Now if you're new to dark cacao I think this is a perfect starter, I had people that normally curl their noses at my normal bitter offerings and they happy gulped this Scharffen Berger down. I found the history of the name interesting if you're interested at all in companies and where your food comes from Google it.

The Scharffen Berger Bittersweet Dark Chocolate Bar is a delicious, delightful chocolate bar.  It's semi-sweet, without really any noticeable bitter taste, and has a smooth, soft texture (at moderate room temperature).  I've enjoyed a lot of chocolate, often from Switzerland where we have friends, and the Scharffen Berger bar compares favorably with their best.  This is high quality chocolate, not your typical mass-produced candy of dubious ingredients.  My only complaint, and it is minor, is that bars are not scored, so breaking off uniformly-sized pieces is difficult.  As an added bonus, I also very much like that the product is American-made.

This is still the same amazing quality chocolate, the one that cooks and bakers all over the San Francisco Bay area and then all over the country started raving about back in the 1990s:  U.S. produced gourmet grade to go up against anything from the European market.  On top of that, this chocolate is affordable - priced similar to many "gourmet" chocolate brands of good to indifferent quality such as the Newman's organic line (which I recently tasted for another review.)  Okay, I'm cheap, and completely unimpressed by advertising embellishment or slick packaging - Scharffen Berger is great chocolate without the "ooooo, how exclusive!" baggage.I'm San Francisco born, and will admit that when Hershey bought out the late Dr. Steinberg's startup back in 2005, I was saddened and predicted the worst; that the company would be out of San Francisco (probably outsourcing production to some overseas factory) and that the quality would go down.  I'm happy to say today that I am -- so far, knock wood -- mostly wrong.Mostly because Schaffen Berger *did* leave San Francisco, closing the Bay Area factories and moving production of the bars to Illinois.  Certainly disappointing, but at least production stayed in the U.S.  And whatever the backlash, it certainly wasn't the media circus attending Marshall Field's Frangomints leaving Chicago in 1999, after 70 years of production there.  I lived in Chicago for 3 years around that time, and can tell you that the public outcry/anatagonism against Marshall  Field's/Macy's was unfading and of astonishing proportions!In any case: Scharffen Berger chocolate, to me, today tastes the same as it ever did.  If you love chocolate for it's complexity, depth, and even it's bitter bite, if you're not just into the smooth and the sweet, if one little wedge of the good stuff beats a truckload of - sorry - Hershey bars, for you, then this is the stuff you'll dream of, forever after you first try it.  Even my children have preferred the high cacao product from early on, and likely your kids will love it too...assuming you're willing to spoil them for the "cheap stuff".But heck, Chocolate is healthier as a not-everyday indulgence is the first place, right? Or...at least not much, everyday...

I've always preferred dark chocolate. (Not surprisingly, I don't care for chocolate made with Dutched -- alkalai-treated -- cocoa. Bleh.) In college, I used to go out after dinner for a Hershey's Bittersweet bar. (It was more bitter than the current Special Dark bar.)I was expecting something spectacular from Scharffen Berger's 70%-cacao bar, and was (sorry) bitterly disappointed. Their description -- "bright fruitiness and a long, smooth finish" -- is accurate. (The lingering bitter taste is especially pleasing.) But there's insufficient "complexity" to justify a $5 price. The taste isn't sufficiently "better" (or more-adult, if you like) than a much-less expensive Hershey bar. Definitely /not/ a treat to be savored, one small bite at a time.A "good" chocolate bar, but of questionable value. See if a friend will give you a bite before you commit to buying.

Can't go wrong choosing this 70% for, at least for snacking.  It has a deep chocolate flavor with minimal bitterness and minimal fruitiness.  Eating it by the square (or triangle) is a pleasure.  1 or 2 pieces satisfies.  While this bittersweet bar is certainly a great bittersweet dark chocolate, my favorite in this category is the Valrhona 71%; but I have a hard time finding it.One note:  Hershey bought Scharffen Berger in 2006.  Hershey closed Scharffen Berger's San Francisco Bay area plant and layed off most, if not all, of the workers.  SB is still made in the USA but in Robinson, IL.

If you're looking to treat yourself with a delectable dark chocolate then look no farther than the Scharffen Berger brand. Made of fine, quality ingredients, the 70% cacao bars are smooth and rich, definitely bittersweet, and with a slight fruitiness to its flavor (as described on the wrapper rather accurately) and without the waxiness that can be found on some inferior chocolates. Since there is such a large percentage of cacao in the bar, making the taste stronger than most, I find I only need a tiny piece of the three ounce bar to curb any chocolate urge I have and far from half a bar they have as a serving (220 calories per serving, 440 for the whole bar). This is a great choice to get the health benefits dark chocolate provides. It would also make a great gift for any chocoholic in your life or be used decoratively on various desserts. A very nice dark chocolate that more than satisfies and is sure to please most anybody's dark chocolate craving.

I already reviewed 62% chocolate of the same brand, so it is going to be basically the same review. I mean, this one is obviously a bit more bitter, but still for me not too bitter, texture is just right and very very enjoyable.

I need to accept the fact that I am somewhat of a dark chocolate snob. I am not proud of it, but I have found myself time and time again disappointed by brands that many people like and seem to have no problems with. There are two main flaws that I have found in these products that do not fulfill my expectations: some have a noticeable bitter aftertaste that ruins the experience, and others have a huge problem with texture, and you feel like you are chewing powder or a dried out version of what the product is supposed to be.I am happy to report that this chocolate passes both those tests with flying colors. It has a smoothness that blew me away, it almost reached the levels of the smoothness you may find on milk chocolate. You can definitely identify the bittersweet taste when you are eating it, and the flavor remains constant in after it's out of your mouth. There is not a hint of the dreaded bitter aftertaste here.If you, like me, have struggled to find affordable high quality dark chocolate, look no further, this is where it's at!

I've been a fan of dark chocolate way before it was considered healthier than milk chocolate.  This is my first time trying this brand and couldn't be any more satisfied.  I'd like to eat an entire bar at once, but at more than 400 calories I cannot afford it.  Just like other reviewers have said, it is nice and smooth, creamy and almost fruity.  Nice chocolate flavor.  It is great for baking as it makes some of the best chocolate ganache I have ever tasted.  In two words: "Just excellent!"

Scharffen Berger is known for being high quality chocolate, preferred by some chefs for baking.  Although some of the very dark chocolates can not only be bitter but one-dimensional and chalky, this one has a nice balance of bitterness and sweetness and also a fruitiness that I enjoy.  If you're used to Hershey's, you'll be surprised that chocolate has a lot more complexity than emerges from any of the mass-produced, very sweet, waxy candy bar-style chocolates. Although I won't deny I love the taste, I eat as much chocolate as I do these days mostly for its purported health benefits, so I usually eat unsweetened (or baking) chocolate.  70% cacao is actually at the sweeter end of the spectrum for me, but I know some people who wrinkle their nose at it as "too bitter."  I find it great for munching or cooking, and it's a good choice for those who are looking for the health benefits but don't find the super dark variety palatable.

Suprisingly listed as a later division of Kraft foods in the USA, this Artisan Confection has a rewarding taste with cacao's natural health benefits wrapped inside.Scharffen Berger Bittersweet Dark Chocolate bar probably comes close to  having similar nutrients found in the darkest berries; yet, it's rich, smooth, and perfectly balanced with sweetness that's not too bitter.  In addition, mixing a piece with hot water and/or milk makes a tastety indulgence.

This bittersweet "dark" chocolate is unremarkable, but fine. I generally like dark chocolate at 80% or higher. These bars are 70% cacao. I think that is the minimum percentage to be called dark chocolate.It tastes similar to other chocolate bars with 70% cacao, so why pay more (and deal with the absurdly long name)?There isn't much more to say. It's just a barely-dark chocolate bar. If you want something more interesting, try their 68% bar from Papua New Guinea. That has a unique fruity flavor (without any fruit in it).

I agree with the other reviewers about the Scharffen Berger Bittersweet Dark Chocolate Bar, at 70% cacao.  It's chocolatey yet it manages to be both bitter and sweet at the same time, which is a good combination if you like your chocolate to taste of chocolate and not so much of sugar.  I think it's an acquired taste, like espresso or a single-malt Scotch or a fine cigar or a six-month-old chunk of Limburger cheese.Because I am as big a fan of high-octane cacaoa -- and 70% is high indeed -- as so many other reviewers are, I appreciate the deep flavor of the bean as it resonates through the remaining 30%.  To my palate there's the slightest nuance of coffee and perhaps an insouciance of lignin, and just maybe the tiniest tincture of acetic acid and vanilla.  Altogether it works well, at least for me, as a chocolate bar to nibble at from time to time.I have to point out that, based on numerous experiments I conducted over the last couple weeks, the Scharffen Berger Bittersweet Dark Chocolate Bar at 70% cacao is at best neutral and is at worst positively disgusting when added as an ingredient -- in various concentrations and whether melted or not -- to certain recipes such as onion soup, ranch dressing, potatoes au gratin, and steak tartare.  Also, don't waste your time melting a bunch of this chocolate bar in a double-boiler and dipping the guts of a McDonald's fish fillet sandwich into it and letting it cool and then expecting it not to surprise you with just exactly how awful it is.The bar does not serve well as an eraser for errant pencil marks; it just leaves behind a waxy brown blob that's even uglier and harder to remove than the original mistake.  I'm not sure which reviewer said it would make a good eraser, but it doesn't.Also contrary to a reviewer's assertion, I did not find any GPS transmitter hidden in any of the wrappings or in the product itself, and I looked pretty hard.For these reasons, including the cons, I still have to rate this product at 5 stars.

If you like Caramels, this is the only PERFECT Caramel IN THE WORLD. Nothing else comes close to comparing. The most expensive and worth every penny.Anything else is a PRACTICAL JOKE - This is Caramel the way it should be. the balance between sweet and salty - hard and soft - is just... simply... PERFECT. It really does not get any better than that - Tasted the original Caramel from Turin, Italy - not even close to the French's Caramel. If you want the best - THIS IS IT !

These Stauffer's Original Animal Crackers are a real treat.  My kids love them.  They are crispy and not too sweet with a hint of nutmeg.  Only 120 Calories per 16 crackers, 15 Calories are from fat.  Yum.  They make a great snack, and the kids don't beg for anything sweeter.

This is a comfort snack for me. These cookies have a great, simple taste-exactly what you expect animal crackers to taste like. Not exactly health food but low in fat and not excessively sugary. Better than the "brand name" animal crackers/cookies.You may want to try a small bag first before getting this huge tub but I love em.

Like most of us I have been eating animal crackers since I was a kid.  Nothing seemed to go with the TV westerns of my childhood like animal crackers and milk.  I don't really think this Stauffers brand was around back then.  Only that familiar other brand with the circus animal on the box.  I have to say that taking a chance on this big container of them didn't disappoint.  They are just as tasty and look just as much like zoo animals as any other.  I keep them around all the time for the kids and grand-kids, and for myself, (with or without a western).  This large container is very easy to store them in an keep them fresh.  For one thing about animals crackers, (which are really little cookies) is that they get really soft and stale rather quickly if not kept sealed.  The big Stauffers jar is handy and makes sense.  And they are a downright bargain when you order two or more at once and save on shipping.  Oh and one last thing.  These cookies are a great take along when visiting one of those petting zoos where you get to feed the animals.  (Although check with the zoo first just to make sure).  The animals love the cookie critters, and the kids get a kick out of feeding them animal crackers.  Order some and enjoy with a big glass of fresh milk... : )

I was shopping at my local drug store late one Saturday night and I stumbled across this brand of animal crackers. I've tried Barnum and Keebler before but not this brand so I wanted to get it. These Stauffer's Animal Crackers are a lighter version of both the Barnum and Keebler. They have less fat and calories and taste more like a cracker whereas the other 2 are more like cookies. So I guess you can eat more of these without feeling as guilty. One aspect of these Animal Crackers that really stood out for me is that they have amazing shelf life. The package I bought is not the same as this one on Amazon - it more resembled a potato chip package. So I opened it and ate some and then closed it with a clip and then I forgot about it for a while. It must have been sitting there for about 2 months before I remembered I had it. So I tried it and it was as good and as fresh as new. I was amazed. Would definitely buy these again.

We always keep a package of these handy.  They make great snacks when you aren't really hungry but have the "the munchies", grab a handful and you're all set.They have the classic Animal Cracker flavor.  We've had a container for as long as 2 months without going stale.The container also makes a great change jar when the crackers are gone.  The only problem may be finding a cabinet tall enough to hold it unless you have a pantry.  It is as tall as a large cereal box.[...]
I mailed this to Afghanistan for my husband....and he and his Marines LOVED them! Free shipping is always nice too!!!

Someone left these crackers on our break room table at work.  Since then this brand has become my favorite.  I like them so much I searched for them online when I couldn't find them locally.  I was elated to find them on Amazon.  I have gone through half of this HUGE container all by myself and I have yet to become tired of them.  They do not have an artificial taste like other animal crackers I've had.
We use a lot of animal crackers so this size is perfect!  I like that we don't have to buy many of the small bags or smaller tubs.
These cookies make a great snack,or a light treat instead of dessert. It is a fun gift to give, the size and the animal crackers always bring a big smile.

column9: Great snack, cheaper at Sam's Club
column10: You can buy these at Sam's club for around $5 for the 4-pound tub.Crackers are great, fresh taste, sealed for freshness, great container for other things when you are done with the crackers.

column9: Tasty and low-calorie, but more broken than whole crackers
column10: These animal crackers are low-calorie, low-mess standby for the office.  Just wish the tub contained more whole crackers than piecy bits to pick through.
Stauffer's Original Animal Crackers - 78oz. What a great buy! Loads of animal crackers to snack on! Recommend the vendor and the product highly! Thanks!

These are very good tasting animal crackers (I've encountered plenty of bad ones). The container is HUGE - there are tons of animal crackers here, which I suppose for the price it better be. We've been eating out of this for a month now and they are still very fresh.

low fat and tastes great and not too sweet!the other brand zoo animal crackers is way too sweet!honestly, not many food products like thiswish i had found out about it lot lot soonergreat for health, convenient, delicious - need i say more!
I love blueberry anything, for the most part; but this coffee is excellent.  It is a mild coffee with just a hint of blueberry flavor so it is not overwhelming.  A great anytime coffee!
Generous amount of raisins, but I found it too sweet.Liked the mix of different types of cereal flakes.Having some almonds would make it perfect though
Would purchase this again, Good cereal for the value. Like the bigger boxes. Not a real fan of raisins, but this was good.

I love Honey Bunches of Oats cereal. This raisin medley is no exception. It is loved by everyone in the family. The combination of flavors is fantastic. I just wish the price was a bit lower for so many boxes ordered at a time. Mostly because the cereal doesn't last us very long! Will order again.
Best gum ever. To bad you have to pay so much for it and order it online. It should be in stores.

column9: AMAZING JERKY and SERVICE IS TOP NOTCH
column10: I am somewhat of a jerky fanatic due to its great protein vs calorie content, and the flavor is pretty helpful as well.FIRST OFF, the service was awesome[not the shipping, but I am in Iraq...sooooo that probably had something to do with the time :)]  The reason I say the service was so good was due to my inspection of the package.  Upon opening I see not only my bag that I ordered, but there are also 3 other packages(samples, of which two were a fairly large amount) of different flavor/cuts of jerky.  So, not only do I get the Cajun Western Cut, I now know that the Maple Jerky is AMAZING, the Chipotle Habanero is RIDICULOUSLY FLAVORFUL(I really like hot stuff.  Not to say that this was hot, but the flavor was amazing.), and I haven't tried the spicy sample (but I am sure it is nothing short of the previous reviews)The original purchase is pretty tasty, but I will likely be reordering the habanero.  The cajun is lackin on the spicy side, has a decent flavor, and the cut/quality of meat is superb for all of the above.
I tried this jerky and it is fabulous!!!  Its spicy but not so hot you can't enjoy it and it has a great flavor.  Definitely a big winner- will get it again for sure!

I've had a ton of jerky's and order them all the time.  This one I won't order again and will probably give away.  It's too tough, and it tastes good but not great.I'm adding a star to this review not for the product itself, but for the company selling them.  When they saw the mediocre review, they immediately offered a refund or to try something else.  You can't find better customer service.

I've been eating a lot of jerky lately, this one takes the cake! The pieces are a little on the tough side, but since it's quality meat it wasn't a problem at all. The flavor starts out immediately being sweet, but after a few seconds a nice medium heat comes in. I would not have guessed the flavor was cajun if I didn't know, but don't let that stop you. This is the best sweet/hot jerky I've ever tasted. What a wonderful unique flavor. I will definitely order this again.

column9: Way too sweet to be Cajun.
column10: I had high hopes for this jerky based on the other review I read.  However I think they need to rename this product. It is described as Cajun and hot.  It was sweet like candy and had absolutely no heat to it.  I would say more like sweet Teriyaki.I think this recipe needs a redo.  Jerky should not be this sweet.  The bag of jerky I bought was passed around to 5 other people who all said it was too sweet.  I spent 8 dollars on a bag and threw it in the trash.  Very disappointed.  If I could give you zero stars I certainly would.I cannot recommend this to anyone and will not buy any of your products.

Like the Rosebud Powder found here: Rosebud - Powder - 1.3 OZ , I purchased this for incorporation into homemade Ras El Hanout.  Since the floral component of this Multi-Spice is quite small (floral powders easily overwhelming other flavours if overused), I ended up with quite a bit left over for use in my perfume-making hobby or in sachets, etc.I found this to be a high-grade powdered lavender, the floral 'nose' being greater than the (wholly expected and natural) bitterness of it.
I found that Timothy's Columbian Decaf k-cups to have the flavor of regular coffee. Economical in 50-cup pack - along with free shipping. Makes it competitive with retail store items on sale.

I have this item on a recurring order and I am very happy I don't have to go to the store for this it.  It is the most practical way for me to purchase coffee.  The taste also is fine and compares to anything else I have sipped in the past.

column9: A bargain that is not a bargain!
column10: One of the worse tasting coffee we ever had since we brought our Kurig. Leaves a bitter after taste and would not use again. A good price but a awful product.
Excellent coffee at an excellent price.  The ease in dealing with making a simple cup of coffee, an excellent cup of coffee, is made simple withthis product.  Hurrah.
Product flavor is superb.  Product delivered on time.  Bulk pack made price economical and best price found for identical product offered elsewhere.  Will continue to purchase the pack offering.

column9: defective k-cups - coffee grounds explode into machine
column10: most of the reviews that said that these cups explode were written a few years ago, so i took a chance and bought them, hoping timothy solved this problem. he did not. 3 out of 4 of these k-cups explode into the machine, filling all the nooks with coffee grounds. i have found that if i run just half a cup of water there are less explosions (but half a cup of coffee is not very satisfying). a full cup of water will always produce an explosion and coffee grounds are just everywhere. WTF, Timothy?
This decaf is so good that I can't tell it from regular coffee.  Would give it 5 stars but it tends to clog my brewer.  Easy to unclog but still a problem.

column9: Timothy's Decaff Coffee for the Keurig Brewer
column10: We got a Keurig K-Cup brewer about a year ago and found that we were spending far too much locally buying the coffee in small quantities.  I checked on Amazon, and found the Timothy's World Coffee and have been purchasing it every since.  We only drink decaffeinated coffee and found it hard to find sometimes locally, but with Amazon, as always, it was available.  We got delivery in a timely manner and will continue to purchase Timothy's World Coffee.  It is such a pleasure to be able to have a "fresh" cup of coffee when you want one instead of depending on a full pot to stay fresh all day.  We put confidence in Amazon to always furnish the best available.

Timothoy's Columbian decafe is a full bodied and delicious tasting coffee.  When the doctor told me Ihad to drink decafe, I thought to myself that I would never enjoy a cup of coffee again.  It took muchserching and many disappointing cups before I found Timothy's.  I can honestly say that I really doenjoy my morning coffee once again. At Amazon I found that the price was managable and the delivery issupurb.

Timothy's Colombian Decaf is about as close to full flavored caffeinated coffee that I have found. If I liked a normal roast then this would be 5 stars since it takes like a great cup of regular coffee. The issue is that I like extra bold and dark roasts and this tends to be a little on the weak side for me. If it's too late for caffeine though, this is my go-to decaf!Bottom line: If you are looking for a great cup of coffee and decaf is your only option, go with this. You won't regret it (at least not in my opinion).

I love Timothy's Columbian Decaf coffee, and the fact that I can get 50 K-cups per order from them is great!  I save money and I have a perfect cup of flavorful coffee every time I make a cup. Many people claim they don't like decaf coffee because it doesn't taste like regular coffee, but I challenge anyone to taste Timothy's Columbian Decaf and then tell me that it isn't a great tasting cup of coffee.

There are several older complaints in this and other forums about defective Timothy's K-Cups.  We purchased the 50 unit multi-pack recently and 30%+ are defective.  When making coffee the drinking cup is filled with grounds and the machine is contaminated with loose grounds requiring a thorough clearing before another use.  We carefully removed the top from a defective K-cup and found the filter pulled loose from the K-Cup rim and folded down on itself.  This allows grounds to wash over the loose filter edge and into the machine and drinking cup.  Timothy Coffee has not addressed this quality control issue for many months and continues to sell defective K-Cups with current lot dates.

Thanks to all that took the time to write reviews of this product. My doctor told me I had to give up caffeine, which devistated me because I hate the taste of decaf coffee. After reading tons of reviews on various decaf coffees for sale on Amazon.com, I decided to try this one. I am so glad that I did. This coffee tastes great! It's a nice medium blend coffee and the best part is that there is no funny after taste. Plus you can't beat the price. I am highly satisfied with this coffee and will definitely buy it again.

column9: Wish it was a bit stronger but good enough.
column10: Wish it was a bit stronger but good enough. Best for its price. Bought it many times before. Works for our home.

Some of the best decaf coffee I've ever had.  Compares well with Keurig Donut House coffee.  Rich, full taste with no bitterness.  Pretty good price also (although all Keurig coffee is fairly expensive).

column9: made with methylene chloride for your enjoyment
column10: This product boldly mentions on the package that it is "Decaffeinated using methylene chloride". Read on to learn more about the process.  Coffee beans are decaffeinated by softening the beans with water and using a substance to extract the caffeine. Water alone cannot be used because it strips away too much of the flavor. The water containing the caffeine (and the flavor from the beans) is treated with a solvent, heated to remove the solvent and caffeine, and then returned to the beans. The flavors in the water are reabsorbed by the beans, which are then dried. This process is referred to as "indirect decaffeination," because the beans never touch the solvent themselves. The most widely used solvent today is ethyl acetate, a substance found in many fruits. When your coffee label states that the beans are "naturally decaffeinated," it is referring to this process, specifically using ethyl acetate. Although it doesn't sound like a natural process, it can be labeled as such because the solvent occurs in nature. Other solvents have been used, some of which have been shown to be harmful. One, methylene chloride, has been alleged to cause cancer in humans and therefore is not often used. Back in the 1970s, another solvent, trichloroethylene, was found to be carcinogenic and is no longer used.

First of all, my favorite K Cup is the Timothy's Colombian Decaffeinated.  If you are looking for an excellent cup of coffee, I highly recommend Timothy's.  Secondly, it is my understanding that Timothy's is packaged by Green Mountain Coffee. Again, I have never been disappointed by Green Mountain products.  Unfortunately, there comes a time that something goes wrong in the process and you just have to get it off your chest.This package of 50 was not typical.  I have had others in the past and they were neatly packaged in a Timothy's box.  In this case, the package was simply a cardboard box with 50 K cups inside.  What's really different about this order is the incredible poor quality of the K Cups.  It's like they bundled all of the bad production products and stuck then in box to sell on Amazon.We've all heard of the exploding K Cups, but what's really happening is that the small filter inside the K Cup is not bonded properly to the side of the K Cup, and the coffee flows into the bottom of the K Cup and into your cup.  The coffee is not drinkable and you have to pour it out and waste another K Cup.  At today's prices, that's a problem.  I have had a few of these in the past, but this batch is particularly bad.  I have gone through 20 of the 50 K Cups now, and 10 have been defective. Every time, I carefully remove the foil top to find the filters are not properly attached to the side of the plastic K Cup.  What's really bad, is I have 30 of these left.My advice to you is stay away from these 50 packs if you can.  I have not had any real problems when purchasing 2 24 count boxes, but I think these are factory rejects, which are costing me double the price I had expected to pay.

The tomatoes make for incredible sauce.  I always heard about them on food network, cooking channel, etc. I never thought there would be this much difference until I tried them. You have to be sure to use the San Marzano D.O.P Certified (they actually have a unique number on each can).  I can also tell you that cooking them on very high heat with some good olive oil will yield a very nice tasting sauce.  We add only salt, black pepper and a bit of red pepper flakes.  Then when the sauce is cooked down and the oil incorporated (does not take long, maybe 20-25 min at most)  add you spaghetti to the pan with the sauce and add some fresh grated Parmigiano-Reggiano some good quality butter, fresh  cut basil and you have a great meal.

column9: one of the best tsating hot sauces in my life.
column10: I am of korean descent, and have had my share of spicy food. Korean food as you know has varying degrees of spicy foods that also taste amazing.The 357 pure ghost hot sauce by mad dog, is the best hot sauce I have had in a very long time, as far as the balance of flavor and heat is concerned. Its not hot at all in my opinion but it does have that bite that lingers nicely after consumption [not overbearing]. I can see why others have commented that this and the other non pure version were considered great flavor enhancers.I am a little disappointed as far as the heat level is concerned. I was hoping to experience more of the bhut jolokia, but over all I am very happy with experimenting with this brand. Mad Dog you have 1 more fan to add to your list of many. I will definitely be buying more hot sauces from this company, and very soon too.I highly recommend this hot sauce, to anyone who wants a step up from the bull sh-t you find at your local grocery store. This brand by far, beats out tobasco, franks red hot, red devil, and the other run of the mill brands u see in stores, in both heat content and flavor.Note: I have purchased from amazon a lot in the past, and this is the first time I felt a product was necessary/worthy of a review.

This sauce isn't for some one who thinks red peper flakes is way too hot. I was highly excited about this. Da' Bomb Beyond Insanity sauce is way hotter. Meaning , I was expecting this to throttle me. Wow, this is the first hot sauce that I can honestly say is hot! You only need a dash of it to give a kick to anything.

After all of the hype about how wonderfully hot and flavorful ghost peppers are; all i can say is - meh, average, mediocre, nothing much to get excited about. I have to say that i was disappointed with this product.I have previously had the Mad Dog 6M scoville - it was much hotter and much better tasting than the pure ghost.In comparison the pure ghost sauce is honestly no hotter than a bottle of habanero Tabasco; although it does have better flavor than the Tabasco.Save your money - buy the Mad Dog 6m Scoville sauce instead if you're looking for something with really good heat and flavor.3 out of 5 for this product as hot sauces go and that's being a little generous cause I like this brand.

"this sauce delivers hauntingly pure heat with a killer sting" ... yeah, right ... more like a 3-legged mule in a wheel chair trying to sting you with a sugar cane.This sauce tickles at best, it definitely is everything but hot.
